   The primary procedure is the pilot-trained calendar score because its functional, learning
error and financial covariance can all be derived for this information regime. Direct residual
regression with the same frozen pilot and Bartlett rule is a computational comparator: it
solves precisely the same score. An outcome regression fitted jointly on evaluation data can
be more efficient in the correctly specified finite basis, but is a different fitted experiment.
External-IV projections become the primary alternative when the price innovation is privately
confounded and a valid instrument is available; their weak normalization needs the set-valued
inference already derived. Lag-augmented innovation projections do not by themselves solve
that IV problem.
   A short bank panel with endogenous lagged balances calls for the separate initial-law and lag-
moment analysis, not multiplication of the calendar sample size. A mixed-frequency analysis
can retain daily prices and monthly stock measurements, but must specify whether the monthly
stock sees the last daily action, its path or an integral. A MIDAS distributed-lag restriction
reduces coefficients only after that observation equation is fixed. Synthetic controls address a
sustained unit intervention under donor restrictions; they do not automatically recover this
one-month innovation response. Each is a substantive alternative when its observation and
assignment premises match the bank’s question.
   If evaluation outcomes suggest a break, choosing the favorable subperiod and reusing this
interval is invalid. The result must become exploratory, or the bank must define a new
regime-specific target and obtain independent evaluation information. The public operation
binds the pilot, calendar, bandwidth, observation mapping, price normalization and financial
weights to its inference identity. This is a necessary consequence of the derivation, not merely
a software cache preference.


9.13     A dependent learner with a public scientific contract
The separated-block construction of Section 9.7 can support an operation only if its learning
and calendar assumptions survive the interface. The target remains the partially linear IV
coefficient with score (Z − m(C)){Y − ℓ(C) − θ(D − r(C))}. Its population slope must be
nonzero; controls and the instrument must satisfy the substantive restrictions before any
nuisance prediction. The product does not infer those restrictions from a high validation score.
  The request names a bounded geometrically absolutely regular calendar law, a lower
bound c on the exponential decay rate, feature-lag and outcome-horizon spans, a separation
gap, a nuisance-rate statement and one of the implemented learners. The two evaluation
blocks are separated after expanding their full lag/outcome windows. The operational check
9.13. A dependent learner with a public scientific contract                                    97


requires g ≥ ⌈3 log n/c⌉ + H + LC . The supplied c is a population assumption; an empirical
autocorrelation plot does not establish it. Arbitrary user estimator objects are not accepted as
qualified learners.
   Each block is evaluated using nuisance fits trained on the other block. Lasso tuning uses
only a further separated training/validation
                            p                 split inside that training block. Three prespecified
penalties share the order log n log(np)/n; predictions are clipped to the declared known
envelope. The fixed-dictionary challenger uses ordinary least squares on the same controls.
The fitted score retains the exact product remainder derived earlier, and the covariance still
requires Ln δn = o(1) in addition to the orthogonality product condition. The operation uses
Ln = ⌊n.2 ⌋. With a fixed correct sparse dictionary these conditions follow from the earlier
sufficient rate construction; accepting a learner name alone does not establish approximation
error or restricted curvature. The general score conditions of Chernozhukov et al. (2018,
Assumptions 3.1–3.2) remain conditions, not an automatic dependent-data theorem.
  Scores use one global centering mean. Their Bartlett lag products are summed within
each evaluation block with the total retained sample as denominator; the deleted gap is
not collapsed into adjacency. The weak-IV extension is a different inference operation. A
numerically nonzero sample slope does not prove the fixed nonzero population slope required
by this regular method.
   The executed example uses 3,000 dates, 20 bounded controls and a 90-date gap. Across
200 independent simulations, nominal 95% coverage is 187/200 = .935 for the sparse learner,
.930 for the fixed basis and .940 for an oracle with the true conditional means. The sparse
coverage Monte Carlo interval is [.8914, .9649]; the experiment is not precise evidence for exact
calibration. The intercept-only challenger covers in none of the 200 draws. When both outcome
and instrument nuisance functions omit a common nonlinear interaction, both fitted learners
again cover in none of the draws, while the oracle covers in 187/200. This is the consequence
of a persistent product remainder, not an error corrected by adding a HAC covariance after a
misspecified fit.
   A bank can therefore reuse this selected learning route with an explicit dictionary, causal
information and rate argument. It cannot substitute a different learner on the strength of a
common method signature. Nor can the independent-pair audit result be attached to this
calendar score without a joint sampling derivation.
Chapter 10

Discovery, graph uncertainty and
identification across models

10.1      The scientific object comes before the search algorithm
A bank might supply monthly balances, offered rates, accepted products, customer contacts and
arrears to a discovery procedure. A graph over these columns is not yet a graph over economic
mechanisms. The offer precedes acceptance, balances are stocks measured at particular
dates, arrears affect eligibility, and a relationship manager may use private information. The
same table can therefore be compatible with several latent-variable and observation models.
Chapter 1.3’s construction of nodes, clocks and interventions precedes the statistical search.
   The output to be learned must also be specified. A DAG with no hidden common causes,
a Markov equivalence class of such DAGs, a latent projection, and an equivalence class
of ancestral graphs encode different information. Changing a graph’s serialization without
preserving its class can change the identification argument even when its visible arrows look
identical. Discovery is useful because it can reject some scientific specifications, suggest missing
variables and narrow intervention questions. Its strongest conclusion remains conditional on
the model class and discovery assumptions.


10.2      From a full DAG to observed mixed graphs
Let the full acyclic causal graph have observed vertices V and hidden vertices U . One observed-
variable representation is an acyclic directed mixed graph (ADMG). A directed edge X → Y
in a latent projection can summarize a directed path with hidden internal vertices; a bidirected
edge X ↔ Y can summarize a path with arrowheads at both observed endpoints and hidden
noncolliders internally. Directed cycles remain excluded, but a directed and bidirected edge can
coexist between the same pair. For example, A → Y together with A ← U → Y gives the bow
A → Y , A ↔ Y . Its two marks retain both causal transmission and confounding. Districts
connected by bidirected edges are the objects used by the ID decomposition of Section 1.5.3
(Shpitser and Pearl, 2006).
   A maximal ancestral graph (MAG) used for conditional-independence discovery is a different
representation. In the no-selection setting, it has directed and bidirected edges, no directed or
almost-directed cycles, and every nonadjacent pair can be separated by other observed vertices.
An arrowhead at X on an edge to Y rules out X being an ancestor of Y . The bow above is
therefore not an ancestral graph. Its MAG on just A, Y is A → Y , which records ancestry but


                                                98
10.3. Conditional independence: oracle logic and finite information                           99


can still represent hidden confounding. Interpreting that MAG as a causally sufficient DAG
would incorrectly license adjustment by the empty set.
   Zhang (2008, Section 3, Definitions 1–3) gives the construction. Join two observed vertices if
there is an inducing path in the full DAG: every observed internal vertex is a collider and every
collider is an ancestor of an endpoint. Hidden internal noncolliders are allowed. Orient the
resulting adjacency by ancestry in the original DAG: a tail at an ancestor and an arrowhead
at a nonancestor. If neither endpoint is an ancestor of the other, use two arrowheads. This
construction preserves the marginal conditional independences and observed ancestry; it does
not uniquely recover the latent DAG or every intervention law.


10.2.1    Separation and endpoint semantics

On a mixed-graph path, a collider has two incident arrowheads pointing into it. A path is
m-connecting given Z if each noncollider is outside Z and each collider is an ancestor of a
member of Z, including itself. The endpoints are m-separated if there is no such path. This
extends d-separation without changing the reason conditioning on a collider can open a path
(Zhang, 2008, Definition 2).
   A completed partially directed acyclic graph (CPDAG) represents a DAG Markov equivalence
class. Its directed edges have that direction in every member; its undirected edges can vary
across compatible DAGs. DAGs are Markov equivalent exactly when they share a skeleton
and unshielded colliders (Peters et al., 2017, Definition 6.24, Lemma 6.25). A partial ancestral
graph (PAG) represents a MAG equivalence class. An invariant arrowhead or tail appears
at the corresponding endpoint; a circle means that endpoint mark varies across represented
MAGs. For example, A ◦→ Y establishes that Y is not an ancestor of A, but leaves the status
at A unresolved. It does not say that A is definitely a cause of Y . Nor do endpoint circles vary
independently: allowed completions must satisfy the whole graph’s ancestral and equivalence
constraints (Zhang, 2008, Definition 3).
   These definitions exclude selection variables. General ancestral graphs can also contain
undirected edges encoding selection structure. A bank sample restricted to approved borrowers
or surviving accounts cannot inherit a no-selection theorem merely by removing the selection
column. An ADMG causal model may also imply observable restrictions beyond conditional
independence; learning its MAG does not preserve all of that structural information. This is
one reason to retain an assumed economic model alongside, and separately from, a discovered
equivalence graph.


10.3      Conditional independence: oracle logic and finite infor-
          mation
Under causal sufficiency, the causal Markov property makes graphical separation imply inde-
pendence. Faithfulness supplies the converse. With a perfect conditional-independence oracle,
the PC procedure starts with a complete undirected graph and removes X − Y when it finds
X ⊥ Y | S. Searching growing subsets of current neighbors uses the fact that nonadjacent
DAG vertices can be separated by the parents of one endpoint. It stores each separating set.
For an unshielded triple X − M − Y with X, Y nonadjacent, M ∈     / SXY identifies the collider
X → M ← Y under the oracle assumptions. Orientation rules then avoid new unshielded
colliders and directed cycles and propagate compelled directions (Kalisch and Bühlmann, 2007,
Sections 2.2–2.3).
  With latent variables, observed parents need not supply all required separators. FCI adds
100                                                          Causal analysis for a universal bank


searches over possible separating sets and uses ancestral-graph orientation rules, returning
a PAG under its assumptions. Simply relabelling PC’s undirected output a PAG does not
perform that search. The latent and time-window issues in Gerhardus and Runge (2020,
Section 2) build on this distinction; the MAG/PAG semantics and oracle interpretation are
made explicit in Zhang (2008, Section 3).
   The oracle argument is not finite-sample certification. Failing to reject a conditional-
independence null does not establish independence. Testing many adaptively selected condi-
tioning sets can create incompatible separating statements. Sparse graphs reduce the number
and size of the sets, but variables that are almost deterministically related can make both
estimation and testing unstable.


10.3.1    The signal restriction behind high-dimensional recovery

Theorems 1–2 of Kalisch and Bühlmann (2007) concern independent Gaussian vectors, not
arbitrary nonlinear time series. Their assumptions allow pn = O(na ) variables and maximum
degree qn = O(n1−b ), with 0 < b ≤ 1. Nonzero relevant partial correlations have magnitude
at least cn , where c−1        d
                     n = O(n ) for 0 < d < b/2; absolute partial correlations are uniformly
below some M < 1. With a suitable vanishing test level, the recovered CPDAG is correct with
probability 1 − O{exp(−Cn1−2d )}. The lower signal bound is a substantive restriction on how
rapidly an apparent independence may be approached. The result is not a guarantee for a
fixed test threshold on millions of weakly dependent banking variables.
  To see the issue without asymptotics, take independent centered Gaussian noise and the
SCM
                A = ϵA ,    M = A + ϵM ,      Y = M − A + ϵY = ϵM + ϵY .
The graph contains A → M , M → Y and A → Y , but A ⊥ Y . The direct and indirect
paths cancel. Replacing the direct coefficient −1 by −1 + δ makes their marginal covariance
arbitrarily small. More data helps distinguish a fixed nonzero δ; it does not give a uniform
separation guarantee over arbitrarily small signals. A stability frequency from resampling is
useful evidence about this algorithm and data regime, but is not a posterior probability that a
causal arrow exists.


10.4     Scores and functional restrictions supply different infor-
         mation
A score-based search minimizes a penalized negative log-likelihood over graphs. If the score is
equivalent across Markov-equivalent DAGs, the likelihood cannot choose their directions. A
Bayesian prior or a deterministic tie-break can choose a representative, but that choice must
not be presented as observational identification.
  For a linear coefficient matrix W , the NOTEARS constraint is

                              h(W ) = tr{exp(W ◦ W )} − d = 0,                            (10.1)

where ◦ denotes elementwise multiplication. Write B = W ◦ W . The series h(W ) =
P          k
  k≥1 tr(B )/k! has nonnegative terms; a directed cycle contributes a positive product to
a diagonal entry of one power. Conversely, a DAG can be permuted to strict triangular
form, so every power has zero diagonal. This proves the acyclicity equivalence in Zheng et al.
(2018, Theorem 1). It proves a property of the feasible matrix, not causal sufficiency, global
optimization, or uniqueness of the causal graph. A loss based on unweighted squared residuals
10.5. Temporal discovery must preserve the clock and hidden history                            101


additionally privileges a noise scale; rescaling currency and ratio variables can change that
comparison.
   Functional-model methods restrict mechanisms more strongly than Markov and faithfulness
assumptions. For Y = f (X) + ϵY with ϵY ⊥ X, a reverse additive-noise representation need not
exist. But both directions do exist in the bivariate linear Gaussian case: each regression residual
is Gaussian and independent of its regressor. Non-Gaussian independent noise with an acyclic
linear system supplies additional information through ICA; the structural VAR construction
in Chapter 9 uses that information (Hyvärinen et al., 2010, Sections 2.2–2.3). Nonlinear
additive-noise identification also needs restrictions excluding its exceptional reversible cases
(Peters et al., 2017, Sections 7.1.2–7.1.5).
   The tradeoff is practical. A conditional-independence method may leave an equivalence class,
while a restricted functional model identifies a direction if its noise and function assumptions
are appropriate. Neither a neural function approximator nor a small acyclicity loss can
supply evidence for independent disturbances. Residual independence, sensitivity to variable
transformations, held-out model adequacy and alternate graph classes are therefore relevant
diagnostics. Passing them leaves the substantive assumptions conditional.


10.5      Temporal discovery must preserve the clock and hidden
          history
For an unrolled process graph, time order can exclude arrows from a future decision into
an earlier outcome. A cycle in the summary graph, such as balance affecting next month’s
offer and offer affecting next month’s balance, is compatible with an acyclic unrolled graph.
Instantaneous cycles at the observation scale need a different model; forcing an arbitrary
within-month ordering imposes a restriction.
   PCMCI-type methods reduce conditioning sets and test lagged links with conditions chosen
to control autocorrelation and common parents. PCMCI+ also treats contemporaneous
structure. Runge (2020, Assumptions 1 and Theorems 1–2) requires causal sufficiency, Markov
and adjacency-faithfulness conditions, consistent CI decisions, stationarity, time order and
a maximum lag covering the true parent lags. Its stated setting excludes selection and
measurement error. Collider-rule choices determine the corresponding completeness claim.
These conditions explain both its usefulness for repeated mechanisms and why it cannot
automatically certify effects from a monthly table of selected accounts.
   LPCMCI permits latent confounders but changes the graph object and conditioning problem
(Gerhardus and Runge, 2020, Sections 2.1–2.3). When only a finite lag window is retained,
earlier observed variables are themselves marginalized. Increasing the window can remove
edges inside the old window because a previously hidden separator becomes observed. Thus a
maximum-lag choice is partly a scientific observation choice, not merely a hyperparameter.
The primary paper also distinguishes how stationarity constrains repeating adjacencies and
orientations. Its stationary, acyclic, no-selection model is not a general theorem for arbitrary
missing or irregular event histories.
   Chapter 9.4’s subsampling example makes this restriction concrete: a two-day series cannot
distinguish daily coefficients 0.7 and −0.7. Temporal order does not restore the lost daily
response. Aggregated flows can additionally induce dependent innovations and change the
conditional-independence structure. A discovery operation must therefore record the obser-
vation operator, lag window, contemporaneous rules and stationarity regime alongside the
returned endpoints.
102                                                                 Causal analysis for a universal bank


10.6      A graph and effect confidence construction on the same
          data
The preceding equivalence-class argument concerns a population law. A finite-sample construc-
tion can preserve that ambiguity without assuming that a selected graph is correct. Consider
independent observations of three jointly Gaussian variables (X, A, Y ), a positive-definite
covariance Σ, and the class of linear acyclic structural equations with independent disturbances.
The mean is unrestricted. A supplied ordering may restrict this class; causal sufficiency is a
substantive assumption. We give a deliberately small, conservative reference construction. It
provides a standard against which faster discovery proposals can be judged.
   Use the nine directions V = {ei : 1 ≤ i ≤ 3} ∪ {ei + ej , ei − ej : i < j}. For each v, the sample
variance s2v has pivot (n − 1)s2v /(v ′ Σv) ∼ χ2n−1 . Give each variance a two-sided interval with
error α/9. The union bound shows that all nine intervals contain their population quantities
with probability at least 1 − α, without independence between pivots. Diagonal entries follow
directly, and
                           Σij = {Var(Xi + Xj ) − Var(Xi − Xj )}/4
gives interval bounds for off-diagonal entries. The resulting entrywise box is an outer region: it
ignores some joint restrictions and may include non-positive-definite matrices. Keeping these
extra matrices can enlarge the answer but cannot remove the true covariance on the coverage
event.
   Enumerate the 25 labeled three-vertex DAGs, or the subset respecting a declared time
order. For each graph, list its d-separations. In three variables these require either Σij = 0
or Σij Σkk − Σik Σjk = 0. Discard a graph only if interval evaluation of one required equality
excludes zero. This is an outer feasibility test, not proof that every retained graph has a
compatible covariance in the region. It needs the Markov property, but no lower bound
on nonzero partial correlations and no faithfulness assumption. The true graph cannot be
discarded when its covariance is inside the region.
   For a retained graph G, regress every node on its parents: βj,pa(j) = Σ−1 pa,pa Σpa,j . With
one parent this is a variance ratio. With two parents it is a two-by-two inverse, evaluated by
interval sums, products and quotients. If the denominator interval reaches zero, return an
unbounded coefficient interval. Multiply coefficients along every directed path from A to Y
and add the products. Their interval sum IG encloses the total intervention derivative for
every feasible covariance in that graph. Return
                                                   [
                                        CAY =                IG .                                (10.2)
                                                G retained

On the single simultaneous covariance event, the true graph is retained and its true effect
belongs to its interval. Therefore P (θAY ∈ CAY ) ≥ 1 − α. This proves finite-sample coverage
under the stipulated Gaussian structural class in exact arithmetic. There is no additional
selection penalty because the same joint event covers all the subsequent transformations. The
union is an outer confidence set, not the sharp population identified set or a collection of
posterior arrow probabilities.
   The implementation rounds interval additions, products and reciprocals outward. Sample
variances and chi-square quantiles remain ordinary floating-point numerical calculations. Thus
the program approximates the mathematical construction; it does not supply formally certified
numerical enclosures of transcendental quantiles. Repeated interval occurrences also lose
dependence and can yield very wide bounds. Semialgebraic optimization over positive-definite
covariances and compatible structural equations could tighten the result, at a substantially
larger computational cost.
10.7. A supported temporal class and its intervention image                                      103


10.6.1    What the construction teaches a banking decision

In a Gaussian chain X → A → Y with action coefficient 0.7, the unordered population law
permits effects {0, 0.7} in this class. Across 500 samples of size 600, the outer effect set contains
the true effect in all samples, but also contains both zero and 0.7 in all samples. Its median
width is 21.13, and 1.8% of runs have an unbounded set. A supplied order X ≺ A ≺ Y
identifies 0.7 in the population; even then the conservative finite-sample set contains both zero
and 0.7 in 83% of samples, with median width 10.69. Tightening computation or gathering
more information has economic value when these alternatives lead to different decisions.
   A hidden-common-cause experiment is more revealing. Its true action effect is zero, but its
observational covariance admits a sufficient ordered model with effect 0.4. The returned set
misses zero in all 500 runs, even though the covariance region covers the actual covariance
in 94.4% of samples. Coverage of the observed law cannot validate the causal model class.
For 500 successes or failures, a two-sided 95% Wilson interval has an endpoint about 0.9924
or 0.0076; the zero plug-in Monte Carlo standard error at these extremes is not certainty. A
measured common cause, a credible instrument, or randomized assignment would change the
information available for this query. A larger observational sample alone would not identify
which class is appropriate.


10.7      A supported temporal class and its intervention image
For a distinct temporal route, stipulate a stable observed Gaussian VAR(1), Xt = F Xt−1 + ut ,
with independent innovations across dates and coordinates, no contemporaneous causal edges,
and a known lag bound of one. Each nonzero Fij is a directed lagged edge in the unrolled graph.
These are much stronger structural restrictions than those used by PCMCI+ or LPCMCI. In
particular, diagonal innovation covariance is partly testable, but its observed fit does not rule
out every hidden causal explanation.
                                  ′ Q−1 , with Q = E[X
   OLS has influence matrix ut Xt−1                          ′
                                                        t−1 Xt−1 ]. These scores are martingale
differences because ut is independent of the past. Ergodicity gives convergence of their condi-
tional variance and the Gaussian moments give the Lindeberg condition, so their normalized
sum has a multivariate CLT. Sample outer products of the fitted scores consistently estimate
its covariance; a serial HAC correction is unnecessary in this specified model. Bonferroni
marginal intervals for the p2 coefficients form an asymptotic joint box BF with coverage at
least 1 − α. Do not set a coefficient to zero merely because its interval includes zero. Label
that edge “zero or nonzero”; an interval excluding zero supports a present edge conditional on
this class.
   An additive intervention raising coordinate j at date zero by one unit has response e′i F h ej .
For fixed H, interval matrix multiplication maps BF through F 0 , . . . , F H , retaining a simul-
taneous outer band for all these responses. If the true F belongs to the box, every true
response belongs to its image, irrespective of thresholded edge selections. The box may include
unstable matrices, which can widen long-horizon bounds. Intersecting with a justified stability
restriction is allowed; merely clipping a fitted eigenvalue changes the procedure.
   With 1,000 dates and 500 replications, the correctly specified three-variable experiment
has whole-response coverage 0.954 (Monte Carlo standard error 0.0094). An omitted second
lag gives zero coverage. Its failure does not recommend a better confidence threshold: it
invalidates the lag-one structural equation and hence its intervention map. Screening, lag
choice and an observation aggregation must be qualified before this operation is used. General
PCMCI/LPCMCI results remain exploratory in the initial product unless a separate graph-
confidence and effect argument is supplied. Functional-model discovery can orient additional
104                                                               Causal analysis for a universal bank


edges only by adding the noise/mechanism restrictions discussed above; this small construction
does not turn their optimization output into a confidence set.


10.8      Adjustment over an equivalence class
Suppose the graph is a DAG, CPDAG, or a no-selection MAG/PAG, and the target is the
total effect of A on Y . An adjustment set must make
                                                   Z
                             p(y | do(A = a)) =        p(y | a, z)p(z) dz

hold for every compatible causal model, not just for a conveniently oriented representative.
Generalized adjustment makes this requirement precise (Perković et al., 2018, Definitions 1–4,
Theorem 5).
   A possibly directed path has no arrowhead pointing backward along its direction of traversal.
It is proper relative to an exposure set if only its first vertex is an exposure. An edge A → B
is visible in a MAG/PAG if graph structure certifies that the relevant latent confounding
explanation is absent. A sufficient configuration is V ∗ → A → B with V not adjacent to B;
the full definition also permits a collider path into A whose internal vertices are parents of B.
All directed DAG/CPDAG edges are visible by convention. The criterion has three parts:
1. Every proper possibly directed path from the exposure to the outcome starts with a visible
   edge out of the exposure (amenability).
2. The adjustment variables avoid every possible descendant of a non-exposure vertex on such
   a path (the forbidden set).
3. They block every proper definite-status noncausal path from exposure to outcome. A
   definite noncollider has an incident tail, or is the middle of the appropriate unshielded
   circle-marked triple; colliders have two incident arrowheads.
The cited theorem is sound and complete for adjustment in its stated graph classes. Failure
can mean that a front-door or other identifying functional is needed, or that the target is not
identified. It does not by itself choose between those conclusions. The visible-edge condition
also explains why the two-node MAG A → Y cannot be treated as the corresponding causally
sufficient DAG.


10.9      From unresolved graphs to effects and useful experiments
Let G be the allowed graph class and M(G, P ) the structural models with graph G that
produce observed law P . The causal identified set is
                                        [
                            Θ(P, G) =         {θ(M ) : M ∈ M(G, P )}.                          (10.3)
                                        G∈G

If each graph identifies a functional θG (P ), this reduces to a union of functionals. If some
graph does not identify the target, replacing its inner set by a regression coefficient is invalid.
The union need not be an interval; reporting its convex hull is a conservative summary that
can conceal gaps.
   For an exact Gaussian example, let (A, M, Y ) have unit variances and covariances
(ΣAM , ΣM Y , ΣAY ) = (1/2, 1/2, 1/4). It has A ⊥ Y | M and no other pairwise conditional
independence. The CPDAG is A − M − Y . The three compatible DAGs are A → M → Y ,
A ← M → Y , and A ← M ← Y . Gaussian regressions supply independent structural errors
for each. The total effect of A on Y is 1/4 in the first model and zero in the other two. The
10.10. The resulting discovery operation                                                       105


observed law therefore identifies the set {0, 1/4} within this causally sufficient linear class. An
arbitrarily accurate estimate of its covariance does not decide whether an offer changes the
eventual financial outcome. A credible decision-clock restriction that A precedes M would
orient the first edge; an experiment on A would distinguish these effect hypotheses. These are
additional sources of information.
   Sampling error is separate from this structural set. If a graph-set procedure contains the
true graph with probability at least 1 − α, and a confidence set valid for that true graph
misses its target with probability at most β, their union construction can have coverage at
least 1 − α − β by the union bound. Obtaining those two properties is the hard part. In
particular, post-selection confidence intervals for a chosen graph do not supply the second
property without an appropriate uniform or independent-sample argument. A bank report
should distinguish graph uncertainty, nuisance/parameter uncertainty and uncertainty about
the substantive model class.
  The useful next experiment is one that changes the decision-relevant identified set. Resolving
an edge that all admissible policies ignore can have little value. In contrast, a randomized
encouragement, a new predecision proxy, finer timing or a deliberately held-out intervention
environment may distinguish the causal explanations that lead to different banking actions.
The scientific request should name that distinction and its expected value before a discovery
engine ranks variables solely by edge confidence.


10.10      The resulting discovery operation
A reusable discovery result contains its graph class, endpoint marks, background restrictions,
CI or likelihood assumptions, observation and time-window definition, statistical tuning and
unresolved alternatives. It can feed adjustment/identification queries over a bounded supported
class. It should return a common functional, a set of candidate effects, or an explicit unresolved
query. These are distinct from returning a best-fitting DAG. Automated data organization
must next preserve the variables and information sets on which these conclusions depend.


10.11      From multivariate temporal search to a conditional effect
           query
For deposit pricing, balances, lending and market conditions, a useful discovery workflow
must allow lagged and contemporaneous relations. PCMCI+ uses time order and parent
selection to address autocorrelation under causal sufficiency; its contemporaneous output
can retain unoriented edges (Runge, 2020). LPCMCI allows hidden common causes within
its stated time-series graphical model. A partial-correlation test supplies a linear Gaussian
conditional-independence test, not generic nonlinear independence. Stationarity, causal Markov,
faithfulness, a sufficient lag window and test validity remain separate premises. Choosing a
flexible test changes sample requirements and computation as well as the null it tests.
   The graphical target is itself a method choice. The temporal ancestral-graph characterization
distinguishes the latent projection on a finite window from its stationarified representation,
with potentially different orientation information (Gerhardus, 2021, Sections 4.5–4.6 and
Propositions 5.2–5.7). Its conceptual complete enumeration may be computationally infeasible,
and the inspected 2021 preprint explains why then-current LPCMCI does not recover every
invariant of the stronger time-series graph class. This is not a claim about every later
version. TS-ICD supplies a distinct ordering of temporal and contemporaneous search under
its stationary SVAR/oracle assumptions (Rohekar et al., 2023). Faster orientation under one
106                                                               Causal analysis for a universal bank


graph class is not evidence of completeness under another. The preserved author versions and
later journal identities are recorded separately.
   The selected runtime comparison uses Tigramite 5.2.10.1, PCMCI+ and LPCMCI, with
α = .01, six variables, 1,600 dates and a maximum lag of two (tigramite contributors, 2026).
LPCMCI’s conditioning search is capped at three; this is an explicit computational restriction,
so no unrestricted oracle-completeness claim is made. The generator has stable lagged effects,
two contemporaneous triangular relations and independent Gaussian innovations. A challenger
adds an unobserved autocorrelated common cause of two series. Another searches only lag one
while the true mechanism retains lag two. All graph endpoint strings, conditional-independence
statistics, p-matrices and timings are preserved over 20 repetitions.

                                             PCMCI+           LPCMCI
                   Regime                 Precision Recall Precision Recall
                   Sufficient, lag two          .993     1.000         .971   1.000
                   Hidden common cause          .865     1.000         .815   1.000
                   Omitted second lag           .980      .929         .917    .929

These are descriptive adjacency comparisons with the observed structural DAG. In the hidden
case that DAG adjacency is not the PAG target, so the numbers must not be read as PAG
accuracy or a ranking of latent discovery correctness. Recall counts true edges outside the
requested lag window; in-window recall alone is one and conceals the omitted-lag defect. Finite
p-values and edge-selection frequencies are not graph-confidence levels.


10.11.1    A supported transformation and its preserved uncertainty

The local effect adapter accepts a supplied sufficient temporal graph with directed lagged
edges and directed or unoriented contemporaneous edges. For at most seven variables it
enumerates contemporaneous topological orders that preserve directed edges and introduce
no unrepresented unshielded collider, including colliders involving lagged parents. It refuses
conflicting, bidirected and partially ancestral endpoints. This is a bounded sufficient graph
operation, not a general PAG completion algorithm.
   For each permitted order fit the declared linear structural equations on a fresh independent
3,000-date sample:
                                                p
                                                X
                                (I − B0 )Xt =         Bℓ Xt−ℓ + εt .
                                                ℓ=1
Only parents present in that candidate graph enter each equation. The companion matrix built
from (I − B0 )−1 Bℓ propagates an additive equation impulse (I − B0 )−1 ea . Query outcome j
at horizon h gives the corresponding coordinate of the propagated vector. The result contains
each order, stability diagnostic and curve, plus a pointwise envelope. The tested PCMCI+
sufficient graph admits 180 compatible orders, many differing only in the order of unrelated
variables; these are not 180 distinct causal models. LPCMCI output retaining richer marks is
refused by this adapter. The hidden-cause case is outside its sufficiency model, not proof that
every hidden-variable effect is unidentified.
   The output is conditional on the selected graph and linear structural restrictions. A fresh
estimation sample prevents reusing search noise in the coefficient fit, but does not guarantee
the selected graph contains the truth. Consequently the displayed envelope is structural-
order sensitivity, not a confidence band. The earlier finite covariance-region construction in
Section 10.6 provides a distinct confidence route under its own bounded model; its guarantee
cannot be attached to this search.

   A two-series example makes the remaining decision ambiguity material. Let reduced-

a contemporaneous price-to-balance coefficient .6; a reverse recursive model fits the same

With 8,000 simulated observations the supported order envelope at impact is [0, .6096], with

decision needs a response above .3, the existing evidence does not make it robust across the two
models. This is an actionable request for additional information, not a decorative ambiguity
label.
   The practical hierarchy is therefore PCMCI+ for a defensible sufficient stationary temporal
model, LPCMCI as a hidden-confounding challenger with retained endpoint semantics, and
structural identification/effect sets only where the query’s premises justify them. Increasing
lag windows can add identifying information at the population level but increases finite-sample
conditioning cost. Interventions, reliable prior ordering and additional measurements should
be chosen for the effect ambiguity they resolve. A large discovery runtime cannot by itself
convert a search graph into a bank policy recommendation.


10.12      Evaluate the observed margin, then ask a causal question
Hidden common causes can create adjacencies absent from the observed portion of a structural
DAG. Consequently precision against that structural portion is not a measure of recovering
the hidden-variable method’s target. A finite-window construction makes the distinction exact.
Observe price, uptake and balance at dates 0 and 1. At each date an unobserved liquidity
state causes price and balance; price causes uptake, which causes balance. Each variable and
the liquidity state have a persistence edge to date 1. Independent initial innovations define
the beginning of the experiment. There is no silently discarded infinite past.
   For this finite DAG D and observed set O, join observed nodes i, j if no subset of O \ {i, j}
d-separates them in D. This gives the adjacency of its maximal ancestral margin. Put a tail at
i when i is an ancestor of j in D, and an arrowhead otherwise. There are no selection variables,
so no undirected selection edges are required. An adjacency with a tail may represent an
inducing path, not a directly observed structural coefficient. A bidirected edge records neither
endpoint being an ancestor of the other. The relation to latent projection, ancestral graphs
and window boundaries is developed in Zhang (2008); Gerhardus (2021).
  This example has six observed nodes and twelve marginal adjacencies. The oracle checks
every one of the 240 pair/conditioning-set queries twice, using independent NetworkX and
Tigramite d-separation implementations (NetworkX and Tigramite contributors, 2026). They
agree on all queries. With the resulting population independence oracle, LPCMCI recovers all
twelve adjacencies and makes twelve correct definite endpoint claims, leaving twelve circles.
Those circles are not errors against a fully oriented generating MAG: a PAG describes an
equivalence class, and unidentifiable orientations must remain unresolved. The comparison
measures correctness of definite ancestry claims and their informativeness separately. It does
not assert completeness of every orientation under additional temporal background knowledge.
   The finite-data experiment uses 2,500 independent two-period episodes per replication and
unrolls their six nodes into columns. LPCMCI is called with maximum lag zero on these
episode rows; this isolates its latent graph operation without asserting stationarity across the
finite window. The earlier stationary time-series runs remain separate evidence. Treating
this episode construction as an infinite time-series oracle would be wrong: longer unobserved
108                                                                 Causal analysis for a universal bank


history can alter its marginal adjacencies, as the time-series ancestral-graph analysis explains
(Gerhardus, 2021).
   With partial-correlation tests, fixed significance .01 and conditioning cap four, forty repe-
titions give mean adjacency precision .9977 and recall .8313, but mean accuracy of definite
endpoint claims only .6605. Conflicting marks are retained as conflicts, not silently converted
to arrowheads or tails. The strong adjacency precision therefore does not qualify a causal
ordering. In the exact population covariance, some genuinely adjacent pairs have partial
correlations as small as .00123 and .00869 under allowed conditioning sets. Finite testing
can remove such edges and then misorient others. This supplies a concrete weak-faithfulness
difficulty; the oracle comparison shows that changing the target definition alone does not fix
statistical graph recovery. No favorable significance threshold is selected after these results.
Learned endpoints remain exploratory unless supported by additional scientific information.


10.12.1     An identifiable hidden-variable query

Take the first-date price A, uptake M and balance outcome Y under the substantive front-door
graph A → M → Y , A ↔ Y . Assume no direct price-to-outcome path, no unblocked back-door
path from A to M , and all back-door paths from M to Y blocked by A. These are stronger
restrictions than an arbitrary LPCMCI output. Graphical identification gives (Pearl, 2009;
Shpitser and Pearl, 2006)

                                                               E[Y | m, a′ ]P (a′ ).
                                          X               X
                     E[Y | do(A = a)] =       P (m | a)                                          (10.4)
                                          m               a′

The first factor identifies the action’s effect on the mediator. Conditioning on A closes the
mediator/outcome back door, allowing the second factor to average the mediator intervention
over the original action distribution. The outer sum composes these interventions because the
mediator intercepts every directed path from A to Y . An arbitrary adjustment regression on
M would instead remove the mediated effect.
  For an exact binary check, let U be fair binary, P (A = 1 | U ) = .2 + .6U , P (M = 1 |
A) = .15 + .6A and P (Y = 1 | M, U ) = .1 + .3M + .4U , with independent assignment noises.
The observed 2 × 2 × 2 probability table is enumerated, not fitted. Equation (10.4) recovers
the structural contrast .6 × .3 = .18, while the unadjusted association is .42. A servicing or
deposit application must justify that all relevant pathways truly pass through the measured
uptake variable; a price’s direct cash cost would violate that exclusion if it were included in Y .
Financial accounting can add a known direct cost separately, as in the funding dossier, but
cannot wish away an unknown direct behavioral pathway.


10.12.2     An unresolved query and its information requirement

For an action/outcome pair with unrestricted hidden confounding, compare two SCMs: U ∼
Bernoulli(1/2) and A = U in both, with Y = A in one and Y = U in the other. Both produce
P (A = Y = 0) = P (A = Y = 1) = 1/2. Their average action effects are 1 and 0. Thus even
an exactly known observed distribution and adjacency do not identify this query. A larger
sample or a preferred completion cannot distinguish the two models.
   Additional feasible randomization, observed action-relevant confounders with support, a
defensible instrument with its own target, or validated front-door restrictions may resolve a
suitably redesigned question. Without such information the product returns the ambiguity
and the requested additional evidence. It does not turn circles into a recursive order. Fresh
estimation data address reuse of outcomes after graph selection; they do not make the
10.13. From an observed-law region to a latent temporal effect set                           109


selected graph causally correct. The hidden-variable query operation therefore records whether
identification comes from an asserted scientific graph, an invariant equivalence-class conclusion
or an unresolved discovery result.


10.13       From an observed-law region to a latent temporal effect
            set
A selected ancestral graph does not by itself justify intervention confidence. The alternative
developed here retains a whole declared structural class. Consider three time-ordered variables:
an encouragement Z, a later action A and a subsequent financial outcome Y . Independent
Gaussian episodes repeat this finite window. The order is scientific information, not an
orientation learned from the same sample. A longer hidden past, selection or dependence
across episodes requires a new observation-law argument.
  For graph G, write

X = BG X +ℓG U +ξ,         ΣG = (I −BG )−1 (ℓG ℓ′G +DG )(I −BG )−T ,     θG = [(I −BG )−1 ]Y,A .
                                                                                          (10.5)
U is a standard Gaussian latent root, DG is positive diagonal, and the time-respecting BG has
possible edges Z → A, Z → Y , A → Y . The broad class enumerates all eight edge subsets and
five latent supports: none, ZA, ZY , AY and ZAY . Loadings and coefficients have no artificial
finite bounds. The 40 descriptions overlap when coefficients vanish; overlap is harmless for a
union and is not counted as 40 distinct data-generating laws. Here θG is the coefficient of A in
the equation for Y because there is no later intermediate observed variable in this window.


10.13.1     A simultaneous covariance region with a finite-sample argument

For n independent Gaussian episodes, the variance estimate of a scalar normal contrast
Q = v ′ X satisfies (n − 1)vdar(Q)/ var(Q) ∼ χ2n−1 . The unknown mean disappears through
centering. Use the three coordinate contrasts and both signs of each of the three coordinate
pairs, nine contrasts in total. A two-sided variance interval with error α/9 for each contrast
gives simultaneous coverage at least 1 − α without assuming independence between the nine
statistics. Polarization then yields, for j ̸= k,

                            Σjk = 14 {var(Xj + Xk ) − var(Xj − Xk )}.

The resulting coordinate rectangle CΣ contains the true covariance on that event. It also
contains impossible or non-positive-definite matrices; retaining them is conservative.
   The ideal confidence image is G {θG (p) : ΣG (p) ∈ CΣ }. The implemented image enlarges
                                   S

structural feasibility to analytically tractable necessary restrictions. On the coverage event,
the true structure and parameter remain in this larger set if they belong to the declared class.
This proves outer coverage without claiming sharp identification. A graph is not removed
merely because a local optimizer could not find its parameters.


10.13.2     Why an unrestricted latent answer can be the whole line

There is a constructive witness, not just a numerical timeout. For any observed positive definite
covariance, regress A and Y on Z and let their residual variance/covariance be vA , vY , c. For
any proposed effect b ∈ R, choose BA,Z = ΣZA /ΣZZ and BY,Z = ΣZY /ΣZZ − bBA,Z . The two
110                                                              Causal analysis for a universal bank


structural residuals then have covariance w = c − bvA and variances vA and v = vY − 2bc + b2 vA .
Their determinant is vA v − w2 = vA vY − c2 > 0. Set

             ℓ2A = 21 (vA + w2 /v),   ℓY = w/ℓA ,   DA = vA − ℓ2A ,     DY = v − ℓ2Y .

Both error variances are positive, and a single latent root shared by A, Y reproduces the
covariance for every b. The broad class therefore contains observationally equivalent models
with every effect value. The implementation checks this equality for several widely separated
values; the algebra, rather than the grid of checked values, establishes the unrestricted witness.


10.13.3     What additional information buys

A validated randomized encouragement declares Z independent of the latent root and excludes
its direct edge to Y . For every retained model,

                                            θΣZA = ΣZY .                                      (10.6)

Project the two covariance bands through this equation over all eight allowed edge/latent-
support descriptions. If denominator and numerator bands both contain zero, retain the whole
line; if the denominator crosses zero but the numerator does not, retain the corresponding two
rays. A nonzero denominator interval yields a bounded outer ratio interval. These are global
interval calculations. Exclusion came from the added experiment, not discovery.
  With observed sufficiency instead, adjustment for the prior Z gives the coefficient
                                           ΣAY ΣZZ − ΣAZ ΣZY
                                      θ=                     .
                                            ΣAA ΣZZ − Σ2AZ

Interval arithmetic on CΣ gives an outer image. It can be very loose: if its denominator
enclosure includes zero, the implementation retains the whole line even when the observed
covariance is well conditioned. This is a conservative numerical relaxation, not population non-
identification. A sharper positive-definite covariance or structural optimization is a legitimate
next improvement, with its own global retention argument.
   In 2,000 repetitions of 600 episodes with hidden A–Y confounding and a strong valid
encouragement, the encouragement set is bounded in every draw, covers in every draw and
has median width 1.282 response units. The unrestricted latent set is always the whole line.
A sufficient-regression challenger that ignores the hidden cause covers in none of the 2,000
draws. With weak encouragement, the valid outer set is the whole line in 1,999 draws. Falsely
asserting exclusion in the direct-effect arm reduces coverage to 127/2000 = .0635, with Monte
Carlo interval [.0532, .0751].
  The supplied-sufficiency interval relaxation is sometimes extremely wide, including whole-line
output in most draws of one sufficient design. Accidental coverage under a false premise is not
evidence for that premise. The omitted prior-path stress arm represents an exclusion failure
through its reduced-form direct path; a full dependent-history extension remains separate.
This selected construction consequently closes a bounded observation-law-to-effect argument,
while useful arbitrary learned-PAG confidence and scalable sharp optimization remain open.
Chapter 11

Observation processes and automatic
organization of banking data

11.1      The data product is part of the statistical experiment
A causal estimator sees records, while the intervention acts on customers, contracts and markets.
Let X ∗ denote the scientific variables, R their observation indicators, L an entity-linkage
assignment, and O the stored records. An observation kernel K maps the full law into the
recorded law:                     Z
                          pO (o) = K(o | x∗ , r, l) p(x∗ , r, l) d(x∗ , r, l).            (11.1)

The target θ may depend on interventions in the law of X ∗ , not merely on the distribution of
O. Identification therefore asks whether all admissible full models with the same pO give the
same θ. A cleaning transformation T (O) cannot distinguish full models that already agree
on O: their pushforward laws under T also agree. This elementary argument explains why a
more complete-looking table cannot by itself resolve missingness, measurement error or causal
ambiguity.
   Useful automation instead makes the observation assumptions explicit, checks their ob-
servable implications and preserves information for an appropriate estimator. The aim is to
automate reproducible construction of an analysis view while retaining a scientific record of
what that view means. Data lineage proves how a variable was computed; it does not prove
that the variable blocks a confounding path.


11.2      Event, availability and revision clocks
For a decision at time t, let Ft−bank be the information actually available immediately before

assignment. A deployable policy gt and its inputs must be measurable with respect to that
information. This is different from having an event timestamp earlier than t. A January income
field entered in March may describe January but was unavailable to a February decision. A
revised arrears balance may replace an older value in today’s warehouse while the historical
policy acted on the older version.
   Represent a record by its entity, event time, availability time, validity interval, revision
identity, value, unit and source. An as-of view at t first restricts records to availability before
t, then chooses the applicable version for the scientific event interval. For example, a deposit
balance dated 31 January, posted on 2 February and corrected on 10 February supplies no
input to a 1 February offer; it supplies its initial value on 5 February and its corrected value

                                               111
112                                                          Causal analysis for a universal bank


on 12 February. Whether the outcome should use the eventually reconciled balance or the
historical published balance is a separate estimand choice.
   There are also two scientifically different uses of retrospectively measured variables. An
eventual audit can validly measure a truly predecision confounder for an explanatory analysis
under its measurement model, even if that measurement was unavailable to the historical
policy. It cannot then be used as a prospective policy feature. Conversely, a postdecision
credit score that incorporates the offered credit limit is a descendant of treatment; its event
label does not make it a valid baseline adjustment variable. The product must preserve both
causal time and available information.
   For longitudinal evaluation, rolling outcomes extend beyond their origin. If Yt,h aggregates
cash flows through t + h, training rows with earlier origins can still use outcomes that occur
after an evaluation decision. A prospective split needs outcome availability as well as feature
availability. An offline estimator of a stationary law may use a different split justified by
dependence assumptions, but it answers a different validation question.

First isolate missingness from treatment assignment. Suppose X is fully observed, Y is a
