   A symmetric example cannot detect a transpose. The proposed acceptance fixtures therefore
include a named directed chain and a named collider, each under every permutation of its three
columns. An independently written decoder was checked on 54 representation/fixture/permu-
tation combinations, and 36 deliberate transposes of directed fixtures changed the expected
answer. These checks establish the small reference examples. They do not establish that an
installed R serializer preserves them; that is the later adapter test (Causal proposal project,
2026b).
  The response should retain the original representation, node order, exact accessor and
package revisions alongside named edges. A display may render the graph more conveniently,
but an unresolved edge must stay unresolved. The importer must also retain the origin of
exceptional marks. A pair of twos can encode an orientation conflict in PC and a bidirected
edge in a PAG; equal integers do not establish equal scientific meaning.

Failures must be caught before they are hidden

The selected source makes three failure boundaries especially consequential. First, with
solve.confl=false, relaxed PC can overwrite an earlier edge direction when another collider
or orientation rule conflicts with it. With solve.confl=true, it can preserve conflicting
directions using reciprocal entries of two. The proposed profile therefore uses conservative
PC, stable skeleton search, relaxed orientation and conflict preservation. Such a result may
still fail to be a valid CPDAG. The discovery result can retain this diagnostic, while the
effect calculation must refuse it. The conflict is not evidence of a latent common cause (pcalg
contributors; CRAN source mirror, 2024).
   Second, a finite conditional-independence p value need not show that every preceding
numerical operation was valid. The inspected pcorOrder uses a pseudoinverse for conditioning
sets of size at least two, replaces a missing partial correlation by zero, and clips its result.
zStat likewise replaces a missing statistic by zero; gaussCItest then evaluates a two-sided
Gaussian tail probability. Disabling NAdelete acts later in the skeleton routine and cannot
recover a failure already replaced inside these functions (pcalg contributors; CRAN source
mirror, 2024).
  For example, in the invalid correlation matrix with every entry equal to one, the one-variable
conditioning formula gives
                                                1−1·1          0
                                 r12|3 = p         2       2
                                                              = .
                                             (1 − 1 )(1 − 1 )  0

Replacing this undefined value by zero yields a finite p value of one. An independently written
base-R scalar trace reproduces this arithmetic; it also verifies that positive-definite factorization
rejects the input. A separate invalid-degrees-of-freedom example reaches the same finite p
value through the statistic fallback. These are intentionally invalid inputs, already excluded
by a correctly enforced preflight. They demonstrate why checking only the final p value is
insufficient, without establishing a failure for valid, well-conditioned package inputs (Causal
proposal project, 2026b).
   The proposed initial path instead supplies a strict Gaussian test callback through PC’s exist-
ing independence-test interface. It uses checked positive definite submatrices and factorization
solves, preserves degrees of freedom, and refuses rank loss, nonpositive residual variances, non-
finite arithmetic or unacceptable conditioning. It does not silently substitute a pseudoinverse,
clip a failed calculation or choose a new regularization parameter. Numerical tolerances must
be fixed before adapter qualification. This callback is a proposed project component with
its own comparison obligation, rather than a description of unmodified gaussCItest. The
compiled fast skeleton path is outside the initial profile so that it cannot bypass this callback.
   Third, the inspected IDA code replaces all nonzero graph weights by one before checking
graph validity. If validity fails, it emits a message without an immediate stop. A conflict
pair (2, 2) can therefore lose its distinction from an undirected pair (1, 1) before that check.
The proposed adapter must inspect the untouched graph, reject conflict codes, and enforce
a strict CPDAG/extension gate before calling IDA. It must not treat a warning stream as a
structured failure response, or silently orient an edge to make an invalid request calculable
(pcalg contributors; CRAN source mirror, 2024).


Reuse choice, operating cost and the next experiment

An isolated local R process is the preferred implementation boundary. The request would
contain an operation name, named data or a checked summary, units, sampling assump-
23.6. Selecting Tetrad without adopting an unrestricted discovery service                     211


tions, resource limits and expected source revision. It would not contain arbitrary R ex-
pressions. The initial effect call uses the singleton local method on a verified CPDAG, with
y.notparent=false. The result preserves the multiset and labels graph ambiguity separately
from sampling uncertainty. Broader PDAG constraints, optimal adjustment, joint interventions,
PAG effects and dependent observations require their own contracts. This restriction makes
the first experiment interpretable.
   The package declares GPL version 2 or later, R at least 3.5.0, seventeen imports and
three LinkingTo dependencies. It requires compilation; the selected build file links LAPACK,
BLAS and Fortran libraries. These are dependency declarations, not a resolved runtime
inventory. Separating R into a process helps isolate versions and failures, but does not waive
applicable source, notice or distribution obligations. The actual dependency versions, build
flags, numerical libraries and third-party rights must be recorded for the artifact selected for
distribution (pcalg contributors; CRAN source mirror, 2024).
   The inspected source includes PC and IDA regression examples, including comparisons
across local/global methods, but some examples are conditional on an extra-tests switch. Their
presence supplies useful candidate fixtures; it is not a passing test receipt. The inspected
NEWS begins with an older 2.7-8 section, and the separate ChangeLog begins in 2010. Neither
provides a complete explanation of the selected release. The build owner should therefore
retain compatibility tests and a revision-change review rather than treating the package date
as a support guarantee. The local inventory contains R 4.1.2 but no installed pcalg or the
inspected key graph/build packages; no package benchmark is claimed here.

expensive bank records. First build the isolated dependency set and record its complete

23.7     A restricted pgmpy integration: verify the candidate,
         preserve the question
The proposal selects a narrow pgmpy integration for generating an adjustment candidate
from a supplied, fully observed causal DAG. The project must then verify that candidate
independently before reporting it. This choice reuses a permissively licensed graph library while
preserving a scientific boundary: a successful method call does not prove that the supplied
graph describes the bank, that the requested adjustment identifies the intended effect, or that
a numerical estimator has valid uncertainty. The selection authorizes development of this
limited prototype path; it is not evidence that an adapter has been implemented or executed
pgmpy contributors (2026a); Causal banking research project (2026ac).
   The source is pinned to the repository revision beginning 1f6296fc2606, committed on 5
October 2026 and selected by the cutoff-bounded history query. Its project metadata declares
version 1.1.2. Fifteen inspected source, guide, test and licensing files match the selected Git
tree, in addition to their local SHA-256 identities. Source acquisition occurred after the 7
October cutoff. The pin establishes which implementation is discussed; neither a late repository
snapshot nor a recent commit measures maintainer responsiveness or long-term support pgmpy
contributors (2026a).


23.7.1    A guide, a graph type and an implemented method are separate
          evidence

The identification guide presents minimal, variance-optimal and all-set adjustment routes.
The pinned implementation gives a more qualified picture. Its minimal-variance branch raises
NotImplementedError. The minimal branch explicitly requires a single exposure and outcome,
constructs a proper backdoor graph, then obtains a minimal separator. The all-set branch
enumerates subsets of an ancestor candidate set after removing specified causal-path and latent
variables. These operations cannot be combined into a claim that every documented graph
class and every advertised adjustment variant is implemented with the same semantics pgmpy
contributors (2026a).
  The distinction between minimal and minimum matters even without statistical estimation.
A set is inclusion-minimal when no proper subset remains valid. It is minimum-cardinality
23.7. A restricted pgmpy integration: verify the candidate, preserve the question               213


when no valid set has fewer elements. The inspected separator routine greedily removes
dispensable members of an initial set; that does not establish a global cardinality minimum.
Nor does cardinality alone determine estimator variance, data acquisition cost or missingness.
A front end should not translate the option name into the promise “the cheapest or most
precise set of controls” pgmpy contributors (2026a).
   An exact graph illustrates the difference. Let C cause A, B and Y ; let A and B cause X; and
include X → Y . The two inclusion-minimal backdoor sets are {C} and {A, B}. Conditioning
on C blocks both forks; without C, both A and B are needed. A project reference that deletes
dispensable variables from {A, B, C} obtains either answer depending on deletion order. That
computation describes the semantics of greedy minimality; it is not a measured pgmpy output.
For a lending example, one verified common driver may be cheaper to collect than two separate
proxies, but its actual measurement quality and availability still determine whether the smaller
set is useful Causal banking research project (2026ac).
   The package’s all-set path is also a bounded algorithmic choice. Enumerating subsets can
require work exponential in the candidate count. Restricting the candidates to ancestors is
meaningful, but a consumer must retain that domain rather than describe the output as all
imaginable observed-variable sets. Variables irrelevant to the target, descendant restrictions and
generalized adjustment criteria introduce different enumeration questions. The first proposed
wrapper therefore excludes both all-set enumeration and the unimplemented minimum-variance
option. It asks for one candidate and checks its stated sufficient criterion pgmpy contributors
(2026a).


23.7.2    A total-effect validator must reject the wrong question

The inspected public validation call first checks the supported graph type and invokes a
graph-role check. The latter checks the presence of exposure and outcome roles. The adjust-
ment validator then tests whether parents of the exposure remain connected to the outcome
conditional on the exposure and proposed adjustment variables. This particular call path does
not independently exclude descendants of the exposure pgmpy contributors (2026a).
   Consider the supplied DAG X → M → Y with X a root. Its exposure has no parents, so
the inspected parent’s-connection predicate is an empty conjunction and evaluates to true,
even if the proposed adjustment variable is the mediator M . The role-presence check does not
reject that assignment. This is a static trace through authentic source, not an installed-engine
experiment. It suffices to show why the project cannot adopt that validation call alone as
its total-effect admission rule. The finding concerns this specific validator and pin; it does
not assert that every identification method returns an invalid set pgmpy contributors (2026a);
Causal banking research project (2026ac).
   The financial significance can be derived exactly. Let independent, zero-mean, unit-variance
errors generate
                        X = UX ,     M = 2X + UM ,         Y = 3M + UY .
Under an intervention on X, the derivative of expected Y is 6. The covariance entries are

    Var(X) = 1,      Var(M ) = 5,    Cov(X, M ) = 2,      Cov(X, Y ) = 6,    Cov(M, Y ) = 15.

The coefficient of X in the population regression on (X, M ) is
                                         6 · 5 − 2 · 15
                                                        = 0.
                                           1 · 5 − 22
Conditioning on the mediator has removed the mediated path. Reporting that coefficient as
the total effect would change the causal question. If X is a one-unit service intensity, Y is
214                                                           Causal analysis for a universal bank


dollars over the agreed horizon and the common linear law is stipulated for 1,000 accounts, the
authored gross response scenario is 6,000 dollars, compared with zero under the misreported
coefficient. This is generated arithmetic, not bank ROI, a binary-treatment guarantee or a
measured customer response Causal banking research project (2026ac).
   The proposed first path consequently requires a conservative pre-action backdoor contract.
A candidate set must contain observed variables distinct from exposure and outcome, include
no descendants of the exposure, and d-separate exposure and outcome in the graph with
outgoing exposure edges removed. This is a sufficient contract for the selected DAG setting.
It is intentionally narrower than generalized adjustment over all supported graph classes. An
otherwise useful generalized set outside the contract receives an unsupported-scope disposition;
it is not declared scientifically impossible. The separation between a restricted sufficient
criterion and complete identification is part of the result’s meaning.
   Two project-owned graph calculations support the proposed verification boundary. One
tests separation after ancestral moralization. The other enumerates simple skeleton paths,
checks noncollider conditioning and checks whether colliders have conditioned descendants.
They agree on 26,064 queries across all 543 labeled DAGs on four nodes, including every
ordered exposure–outcome pair and every subset of the remaining nodes. The check helps
detect mistakes in the small reference implementation; it is not a proof for arbitrary graph size,
an upstream pgmpy test run or a statement about statistical discovery from finite samples
Causal banking research project (2026ac).


23.7.3    A selected DAG can conceal unresolved direction or a failed extension

Static discovery remains a separate reuse decision. The pinned PC class supports original,
stable and parallel variants; its defaults include parallel execution, test level .01, a maximum
conditioning-set size of five and a partially directed return. In the fitted method, the names
pdag and cpdag follow the same return branch. The dag option calls a conversion selecting
one orientation. The option spelling alone cannot establish a complete equivalence class,
whole-graph confidence or causal identification under hidden confounding. The source declares
causal sufficiency, acyclicity and faithfulness; particular conditional-independence tests add
their own assumptions pgmpy contributors (2026a).
   The default conditioning cap can stop search before all possible separating sets have been
considered. Test selection, data types and expert constraints must therefore be retained
alongside the graph. A per-test threshold of .01 is not a .99 confidence level for every edge or
the downstream effect. Required and forbidden edges introduce external information; their
provenance must survive any business-language or agent-assisted formulation step. A graph’s
attractive rendering cannot supply that provenance pgmpy contributors (2026a).
   The PDAG implementation contains a particularly clear conversion boundary. Its to_dag
routine warns when it cannot find a consistent extension preserving directed edges and v-
structures, then orients remaining edges arbitrarily while avoiding cycles. The result can
therefore be an acyclic graph with different v-structures. The to_cpdag route first obtains an
extension when undirected edges exist, so it cannot be used as an independent certificate that
the input represented a valid equivalence class pgmpy contributors (2026a).
   A four-node chordless undirected cycle supplies an exact refusal fixture. There are sixteen
orientations of its four edges; two form directed cycles and fourteen are acyclic. Every acyclic
orientation has a sink with two nonadjacent parents and therefore introduces an unshielded
collider. Consequently none preserves the undirected graph’s absence of specified colliders.
The project enumerates all fourteen acyclic cases to check this small argument. An arbitrary
DAG returned after a warning would answer a different graphical question; simply confirming
23.7. A restricted pgmpy integration: verify the candidate, preserve the question              215


acyclicity would miss the change Causal banking research project (2026ac).
   The initial integration therefore consumes an already supplied DAG rather than an automat-
ically completed discovered graph. Future discovery integration must preserve typed directed
and undirected edges, isolates, separating sets, constraints, warnings and the exact selection
procedure. Named-edge conversion is preferable to guessing direction from an unlabeled
binary matrix. An incomplete or nonextendible graph must remain an explicit scientific or
computational limitation, with no fallback to a conveniently oriented causal story.


23.7.4    The permitted prototype path and its failure contract

The proposed operation accepts one exposure and one outcome in a fully observed acyclic
graph, with unique string node identifiers and an explicit node list. It initially caps the graph
at twelve nodes as a conservative wrapper design choice; that number is not measured engine
capacity. Latent, bidirected, selection, undirected and ambiguous-edge inputs are outside
this path. It constructs a fresh pinned DAG with explicit roles and requests the minimal
adjustment candidate. The original graph remains available for comparison Causal banking
research project (2026ac).
   After a successful return, the wrapper must verify unchanged nodes, edges, exposure and
outcome roles; validate candidate membership and timing; exclude exposure descendants; and
run the independent graphical check. Success then means a candidate satisfying the specified
criterion relative to the supplied graph. It carries no numerical effect, confidence interval or
certification of the graph’s real-world truth. An empty valid set is a meaningful result, whereas
a null or failed return is a different disposition. A failure to find a set by this method must not
become a claim of global causal nonidentifiability Causal banking research project (2026ac).
   Exceptions, warnings, unsupported variants, altered graph structure and resource limits
are retained with their causes. They do not become an empty adjustment set or zero effect.
The same graph, target identity and disposition must cross library, CLI and MCP boundaries.
Implementation acceptance will require actual pinned-engine calls on named confounder,
mediator, collider, isolate and permutation fixtures, together with invalid graph and failure
cases. The exact references developed here provide oracles for that work; no pgmpy runtime
or adapter call was performed Causal banking research project (2026ac).
   The minimal path’s attraction is limited but practical: pgmpy can propose a graph-based
candidate while the project’s independent sufficient check guards its meaning. It is not
necessary to copy the whole library or port its graph stack to another language to obtain
this benefit. A reference-only role remains appropriate for presently unverified discovery and
estimation branches. Minimum-variance adjustment is rejected at this pin because the branch
is unimplemented. Generalized adjustment, latent graphs and data-driven direction selection
are deferred to separate source and semantic reviews pgmpy contributors (2026a).


23.7.5    Licensing, dependencies and ownership make reuse concrete

The pinned MIT license permits use, modification and distribution subject to preservation
of its copyright and permission notice and contains a warranty disclaimer. That permission
does not replace dependency-license review. Project metadata requires Python from 3.10 up
to but excluding 3.15 and declares twelve mandatory dependencies, including NumPy, SciPy,
NetworkX, pandas, scikit-learn, statsmodels, scikit-base and Hugging Face Hub. Optional
groups separately include Torch, graphical tools and LiteLLM. Declared version floors are not
a resolved reproducible environment pgmpy contributors (2026a).
  The proposed graph service should use an isolated, locked environment and only the necessary
216                                                          Causal analysis for a universal bank


path. Owners must retain source and dependency identities, notices, conversion fixtures and
resource measurements. An upgrade requires rechecking API names, graph representations
and failure behavior as well as rerunning accepted fixtures. The inspected revision includes
adjustment tests for observed, latent and M-graph cases, which are useful maintenance evidence;
their presence does not imply that those tests were executed here or that all targets and graph
classes are qualified pgmpy contributors (2026a).
   The LLM pairwise class is also a separate capability within the same repository. Its
description states that it uses variable names and text descriptions, not the observed data
values, and its source includes an optional provider-call path. Such suggestions can inform
a reviewable business formulation but do not inherit the evidence of a CI-based discovery
algorithm. This selected graph operation has no live-model dependency. A future language-
model path would need its own custody, ambiguity, source-grounding and held-out evaluation
contract pgmpy contributors (2026a).
   Costs therefore include graph elicitation, controls and timing review, dependency main-
tenance, integration fixtures and adjudication of failures, even though the selected source
license has no purchase price. No monetary maintenance estimate is supplied without workload
evidence. Research owners must justify the assumed graph and target; adapter owners must
enforce the conversion and failure contract; reviewers must verify executed results before
runtime qualification. The concrete revisit trigger is a new pin, graph class or method path,
followed by source inspection and matched behavioral tests. This division gives pgmpy a useful,
limited place in the proposal while keeping the unimplemented and scientifically unsupported
extensions visible.


23.8     Native discovery software and the meaning of a C++
         boundary
A bank may choose a native library because it must fit a larger numerical system, reduce data
movement or control deployment dependencies. Those are reasonable engineering motives, but
they do not select a causal model. A fast graph search can still answer the wrong question,
discard the direction ambiguity that matters to a rate decision, or reinterpret a repeated
customer history as independent observations. The useful comparison therefore starts with
the statistical object and only then asks which implementation can preserve it.
   Four roles need separate treatment. A native discovery engine takes data and method
assumptions to a graph or graph class. An R or Python package with a C++ backend supplies
that engine through a host-language contract, including coercion, missingness and graph
conversion. A graphical-model inference library evaluates a model already supplied to it. A
research demonstrator may expose a valuable search idea without distributing a complete
reusable implementation. Counting all four as interchangeable “C++ causal libraries” would
obscure the investment choice.
   The bounded comparison uses two repository-search routes, for causal discovery and Bayesian-
network structure learning, together with known engines and direct upstream references. All
eleven returned candidates are represented below, with four known leads and two direct
upstream leads. This is a seventeen-candidate comparison of inspected releases, not an
exhaustive catalogue of every native implementation. The searches used a current index with
a creation-date filter; selected commit snapshots separately enforce the 7 October 2026 cutoff.
Repository language metadata identifies a lead. The implementation files, release terms and
mathematical contract determine its role. For example, the selected SVI-DAG model imports
JAX and Flax and is implemented in Python, although its repository was returned by the
23.8. Native discovery software and the meaning of a C++ boundary                              217


C++ query (SVI-DAG contributors, 2026).

explicitly reject missing values. The presence of parameter-learning EM elsewhere in the
library does not remove that structural restriction. A first adapter should therefore expose a
declared discrete-data route and preserve the rejection. Discretizing continuous bank covariates
or imputing missing histories requires a separate scientific argument, not merely a conversion
function.
  OpenBNSL supplies a second explicit native boundary. Its selected build uses C++20,
Python, pybind11, OpenMP and Boost, with optional CUDA detection. The documentation
specifies categorical variables. The inspected PC routine freezes neighbor information for a
conditioning level, distributes tests and then applies the collected edge removals. The CI
implementation dispatches Chi-square, G-square or an oracle graph, calculates contingency-
table statistics within observed strata, and returns an independence decision. It also applies
a Yates adjustment in one-degree-of-freedom strata, including before the G-square branch.
A comparison against another implementation must reproduce that convention or explicitly
compare different tests (OpenBNSL contributors, 2026).
   The build’s CUDA option is not evidence that GPU-PC is implemented. The selected
feature list separately leaves that item unchecked. Similarly, its published timing examples
remain the authors’ reported benchmarks, not measurements of the proposed bank workflow.
The proposal would measure the complete path from categorical encoding through CI tests,
graph conversion and a meaningful result, with timeouts and unsupported requests retained.
Neither a worker count nor a short kernel time measures that path by itself.


23.8.2    Scores, conditional independence and functional assumptions

The native implementations also show why a common parameter name is not a common
statistical interface. In PC-style search, α commonly controls the rejection threshold of an
individual conditional-independence test. In the inspected XGES command line, alpha defaults
to two and multiplies the BIC complexity penalty. In ccdr.run, alpha limits the number
of edges relative to the number of variables. Mapping all three to a generic “confidence”
setting would change the method (aGrUM contributors, 2026a; Achille Nazaret and XGES
contributors, 2026; Bryon Aragam and Dacheng Zhang, 2026).
   For a target variable j and candidate parents P , the inspected XGES scorer computes
centered empirical covariance, solves the parent regression using an LLT factorization, and
forms residual variance
                                         b jj − Σ
                                 vbj|P = Σ           b −1 Σ
                                                       PP Pj.
                                                b jP Σ    b

Its local score, when these operations are well defined, is
                                    n                   α log n
                        s(j, P ) = − {1 + log vbj|P } −         (|P | + 1).                  (23.1)
                                    2                      2
This equation describes the selected implementation; it is not a new consistency theorem. The
centered covariance uses divisor n, and the residual variance, factorization status and finite
logarithm need explicit checks in a prospective numerical comparison. The inspected overload
that accepts intervention indices computes the same covariance without using those indices.
Its signature alone therefore does not establish an interventional score (Achille Nazaret and
XGES contributors, 2026).
23.8. Native discovery software and the meaning of a C++ boundary                             219


  By contrast, ccdrAlgorithm follows a regularization path rather than returning one universal
best graph. Its documented gamma chooses MCP or L1 regularization; its sigmas argument
can fix conditional variances; and its input must be numeric without missing values. These
decisions affect the family of fitted models. The path should be retained with its tuning
and stopping information, while a later selection rule is evaluated separately. BNSL likewise
exposes a criterion choice and a parent-set bound. A fast search over a restricted family should
be described as such, rather than as an unrestricted optimum or a calibrated causal answer
(Bryon Aragam and Dacheng Zhang, 2026; Joe Suzuki and Jun Kawahara, 2026).
   Constraint, score and functional methods should consequently remain separate comparison
families. Constraint methods require a suitable CI test and the graphical assumptions that
make its independence information meaningful. Score methods require a score model, search
space and declared regularization or prior. Functional approaches add restrictions on structural
functions and noise that may orient edges left ambiguous by a Gaussian independence model.
The earlier Python comparison supplies selected functional and continuous optimization
alternatives. The C++ search does not establish their absence from every native ecosystem. It
does reveal that neither a nonlinear experiment’s title nor a repository language label supplies
a reviewed native contract.
   The selected rCausalMGM route illustrates the host-language issue. Its pcStable docu-
mentation distinguishes numeric and categorical variables, drops missing rows, accepts an
optional initial skeleton and returns a CPDAG under causal sufficiency. The native path calls
its stable skeleton search, regression-based CI machinery and orientation routines. A sparse
initial skeleton can prevent consideration of an omitted adjacency; missing-row deletion can
change the population. Both need to appear in the scientific contract. Its adjMat2Graph
documentation defaults directed to false and does not fully specify endpoint orientation.
The selected evidence supports an integration candidate, while the exact converter still needs
delegated-source inspection and a runtime fixture (Tyler C Lovelace, Max Dudek, Jack Fiore
and Panayiotis V Benos, 2026).


23.8.3    A funding calculation that detects a reversed matrix

Consider a synthetic structural model for a bank offer. Let A denote an administered-rate
offer measured in ten-basis-point increments, M retained deposits measured in USD 10 million
units, and Y annual contribution measured in USD 1 million units. Take independent centered
structural errors and stipulate

            A = εA ,              M = 12 A + εM ,                  1
                                                            Y = − 10 A + 25 M + εY .        (23.2)

The negative direct coefficient represents the modeled cost of the higher offered rate. The
mediated route represents the modeled contribution of retained balances. These amounts are
a transparent synthetic accounting example, not bank estimates (Causal banking proposal
project, 2026h).
  Define Wij as the coefficient from source i to target j, in node order (A, M, Y ). Then
                                               
                             0 1/2 −1/10
                        W = 0 0    2/5  ,             X = W T X + ε.
                                       
                             0 0     0

For this acyclic system, W 3 = 0, and the total effect of a unit offer on contribution is

                         θA→Y = [(I − W T )−1 ]Y,A = − 10
                                                        1
                                                          + 21 25 = 10
                                                                    1
                                                                       .                    (23.3)
220                                                           Causal analysis for a universal bank


It corresponds to USD 100,000 annually. Direct substitution after do(A = 1) gives the same
result. An adapter that instead interprets the same bytes as X = W X + ε reverses the
direction convention and returns zero for this query. Dropping the negative direct coefficient
while preserving the positive route returns USD 200,000. Both errors can survive a check that
only counts nonzero entries or compares absolute weights.
   This example requires a coefficient matrix, not an unweighted adjacency matrix. A graph
alone cannot supply the monetary calculation. In addition, units must transform with the
coefficients. For X ′ = DX, with diagonal positive unit-conversion matrix D, the row-source
coefficient convention requires W ′ = D−1 W D. The effect in the new units is (DY Y /DAA )θA→Y .
Converting only the displayed output label would leave the arithmetic wrong. Exact rational
calculations verify this transformation, all six permutations of the three named nodes and an
independent topological substitution (Causal banking proposal project, 2026h).
   The selected OpenBNSL header provides a concrete reason to test storage and meaning
separately. Its directed-edge query accepts (u, v) in source-to-target order, while its packed
storage looks up the bit for u inside the parent array indexed by v. Copying rows of that
parent array into a public source-row matrix would transpose the relationship. The proposed
adapter must decode the public graph semantics rather than infer them from a memory
layout (OpenBNSL contributors, 2026). The exact bitmap exercise in the project checks this
distinction; it does not execute OpenBNSL.
   Undirected edges need a different check. In the inspected header, two potential arcs represent
one undirected edge, while one arc represents a directed edge. A generic directed graph with
both arcs would instead contain a two-cycle. A correct boundary therefore carries an explicit
graph type, endpoint marks and node identity. It cannot infer causal cycles from the number
of bits, or erase the marks to satisfy a DAG-only downstream API.


23.8.4    A correct orientation can still leave an effect unidentified

Byte-faithful conversion is necessary, but scientific ambiguity remains even after it succeeds.
Consider a different, standardized Gaussian example with covariance
                                                         
                                          1 1/2 1/5
                                    Σ = 1/2 1 2/5 .
                                                   
                                         1/5 2/5 1

The partial covariance of A and Y given M is zero. A forward chain with coefficients 1/2, 2/5
and error variances 1, 3/4, 21/25 generates this law. So does a fork A ← M → Y , with
coefficients 1/2, 2/5 and variances (3/4, 1, 21/25) in (A, M, Y ) order. A reverse chain also
generates it, with variances (3/4, 21/25, 1). Each variance is positive. Exact covariance
reconstruction checks equality for all three systems (Causal banking proposal project, 2026h).
   Their offer effects are 1/5, 0, 0, respectively. If one outcome unit is USD 1 million, the
structural alternatives allow USD 200,000 or zero for a unit action. Choosing an arbitrary
DAG extension from a PDAG would choose one answer without evidence for that choice.
Averaging extensions would add a distribution over graphs that the observed covariance does
not provide. The useful output is a graph class and its justified effect alternatives, with any
sampling uncertainty handled separately. This is the same reason the pcalg integration retains
an effect multiset rather than presenting its mean as an identified monetary answer (pcalg
contributors; CRAN source mirror, 2024).
  Native score search may be the appropriate computational component for that workflow. It
does not, by itself, supply the identification layer, a confidence region over graphs, a decision-
23.8. Native discovery software and the meaning of a C++ boundary                           221


useful effect set or banking validation. The proposal should budget separately for each missing
component instead of treating an executable graph search as the complete causal product.


23.8.5    Why categorical encoding and predictive rules need their own review

Categorical support does not imply that an arbitrary discretization preserves the required
adjustment information. Let a binary risk state R have probability one half, and suppose A
and Y are independent given R, each having success probability 1/5 when R = 0 and 4/5 when
R = 1. There is no structural arrow from A to Y ; changing A does not change Y . Treatment
probabilities are positive in both strata. Nevertheless, exact enumeration gives

    E[Y | A = 1] = 17/25,    E[Y | A = 0] = 8/25,    E[Y | A = 1] − E[Y | A = 0] = 9/25.

Collapsing the two risk categories into one bin destroys the conditioning information and
retains that spurious association. The population contrast within each original stratum is
zero (Causal banking proposal project, 2026h). A finer encoding also has a cost: conditioning
on five binary variables creates up to thirty-two strata before the two tested variables are
cross-classified. Cell sparsity, omitted combinations and test approximations consequently
belong in the proposed evaluation. More bins do not automatically improve inference at a
fixed sample size.
  A second example addresses the conditional-entropy lead in the finite search. Its README
describes low conditional entropy as a causal rule. Let U ∼ Bernoulli(1/2). In one structural
model take A = U, Y = A; in another take A = U, Y = U . Both models have identical
observed atoms (0, 0), (1, 1), each with probability one half, and both have H(Y | A) = 0.
Their intervention contrasts are one and zero. Thus even perfect prediction does not establish
an offer’s causal effect. This exact counterexample concerns the claimed inferential rule; it is
not a benchmark of the downloaded program (Causal banking proposal project, 2026h; Named
repository contributors, 2026).
   The inspected COJEC implementation creates an additional, narrower concern: its
selected rule uses the expression p(x, y) log p(x, y)/ log p(x), a threshold of 0.08 and a
count condition above nine. That expression is different from the full conditional entropy
− x,y p(x, y) log{p(x, y)/p(x)}. The source observation and the identification counterexample
  P

justify declining this rule as a causal-effect contract. They do not establish that association
screening has no useful exploratory role (Named repository contributors, 2026).

and nested GES contributors, 2026; Named repository contributors, 2026; libDAI and OpenGM
contributors, 2026). Old mirrors do not establish the status of every current upstream version.
An inaccessible license endpoint likewise does not prove that no license exists. For XGES, the
inspected cutoff tree and failed license retrieval leave the grant unresolved. For LGES, an
available nested GES license does not settle the root grant. For the incremental and COJEC
leads, a new source-and-rights review is needed before copying or redistributing code. These are
reasons to choose an already documented alternative for the first prototype, while preserving
the technical leads.
  The selected aGrUM headers identify an LGPL-3.0-or-later or MIT choice, and both texts
are saved. OpenBNSL supplies MIT terms. rCausalMGM declares GPL-3; the selected
ccdrAlgorithm and BNSL packages declare GPL version two or later. The Breaking Bad root
has a customized BSD-derived license and a separate notice collection. A top-level declaration
cannot silently replace the terms of an omitted scorer, a nested dependency or another project’s
code (aGrUM contributors, 2026a; OpenBNSL contributors, 2026; Tyler C Lovelace, Max
Dudek, Jack Fiore and Panayiotis V Benos, 2026; Bryon Aragam and Dacheng Zhang, 2026;
Joe Suzuki and Jun Kawahara, 2026; LG AI Research, 2026). The prototype choice must
name the distributed components and preserve the applicable notices; a process boundary is
an engineering choice, not an automatic answer to every licensing question.
   The resulting proposal is concrete. Begin with a restricted aGrUM native discrete-discovery
path and an OpenBNSL categorical comparator. Preserve the selected R packages behind
their public contracts when their assumptions fit. Keep XGES as a Gaussian score-search
comparator pending resolution of its pinned-release grant. Defer the incomplete Breaking
Bad assembly until the missing implementation and its rights can be established. Use libDAI
or OpenGM only where an already justified model needs their inference role. Do not port
23.9. Discovery beyond the principal language interfaces                                           223


the whole library merely to remove a host language: a port also assumes responsibility for
numerical failure, graph semantics and future maintenance.
  The first prototype should exercise named-node permutation, signed coefficient and unit
conversions, directed/undirected endpoints, missing rows, empty or sparse strata, singular
covariance and resource limits. It should compare like statistical procedures before comparing
speed, and retain every rejected or timed-out request in its report. A subsequent registered
public or generated study can measure graph recovery, effect-set retention and resource use
under declared models. Source inspection and the exact examples above justify this experiment
and explain how to interpret failure. They do not yet demonstrate native runtime performance,
general calibration or a validated bank capability.


23.9       Discovery beyond the principal language interfaces
A causal library can gain useful capabilities from Julia, Rust, MATLAB and JavaScript
without treating the programming language as evidence for a scientific claim. Julia offers
composable graph and independence-test interfaces. Rust can supply numerical search behind
an existing R or Python interface. MATLAB contains influential reference implementations
and older toolboxes whose mathematical ideas remain useful even when their deployment or
licensing conditions are unsuitable. JavaScript can connect graph construction to an analyst’s
conversation. These contributions belong at different points in the proposed system.
   The comparison develops eleven selected implementation families from source revisions
dated no later than 7 October 2026. It distinguishes algorithm source, interface documentation
and author performance claims. Broader language and package-registry coverage remains
incomplete: neither a missing search result nor an uninspected repository establishes that an
implementation does not exist. The numerical examples below are exact project constructions,
not executions of the surveyed engines. Their purpose is to specify what a future adapter must
preserve before a speed or accuracy comparison would be meaningful.


23.9.1     The useful unit of comparison is the mathematical operation

Table 23.5 gives the proposed disposition of each selected family. Integration means retaining
an engine behind a reviewed input and result contract. Porting means taking responsibility for
a new implementation, including its numerical behavior, dependencies and applicable terms.
Adoption means making the dependency part of a supported product path. A favorable source
comparison can justify an integration experiment; it does not complete any of these engineering
obligations.

23.9.2     A funding example distinguishes ambiguity from a matrix error

Consider three jointly recorded quantities: a funding-pressure score U , a quoted-rate change Q
in percentage points, and retained funding F in millions of US dollars. The score is a summary
measured over the observation window; its name alone does not establish that it precedes the
quote. The following centered linear Gaussian constructions stipulate three different causal
explanations. Disturbances are mutually independent within each construction, with variances
23.9. Discovery beyond the principal language interfaces                                     225


stated explicitly:

                       M1 : U = ϵU ,      Q = 12 U + ϵQ ,       F = 2Q + ϵF ,             (23.4)
                       M2 : Q = η Q ,     U = 12 Q + ηU ,       F = 2Q + ηF ,             (23.5)
                       M3 : F = ξF ,      Q = 25 F + ξQ ,       U = 12 Q + ξU .           (23.6)

In variable order (U, Q, F ), the disturbance variances are respectively (1, 3/4, 1), (3/4, 1, 1)
and (3/4, 1/5, 5). Each construction induces the same covariance in variable order (U, Q, F ):
                                                           
                                            1 1/2 1
                                      Σ = 1/2 1 2 .
                                                   
                                            1  2 5

For example, under M1 , var(Q) = 1/4 + 3/4 = 1, cov(U, F ) = 2(1/2) = 1, and var(F ) =
4 + 1 = 5. Under M3 , var(Q) = 4(5)/25 + 1/5 = 1 and cov(Q, F ) = 2. The other entries
follow directly. Because the laws are centered Gaussian, equal covariance here implies equal
observational distributions. Also
                                                     (1/2)(2)
                               cov(U, F | Q) = 1 −            = 0.
                                                        1
The three graphs have the same undirected chain and no unshielded collider. They differ in
what a quote intervention does.
   Replacing the equation for Q with a value increased by 1/4 changes expected F by 1/2
in M1 and M2 , and by zero in M3 . Thus the intervention response belongs to {0, 1/2}
million dollars in this declared three-model family. This is a finite ambiguity set, not a
confidence interval and not a claim about every possible causal model for the observations. A
justified observation clock could exclude some of these explanations; the statistical column
label cannot do so by itself. Exact rational covariance and intervention calculations reproduce
the construction(Causal banking proposal project, 2026o).
  Now write a supplied structural model as x = Bx + e, so that Bij is the coefficient from
variable j to variable i. For M1 ,
                                                          
                                             0 0 0
                                       B = 1/2 0 0 .
                                                  
                                             0 2 0

The total Q → F slope is two. If an adapter transposes this matrix while keeping the variable
order and column-vector convention, the displayed graph is still acyclic but its Q → F slope is
zero. This is a conversion error in a supplied model. It differs from the legitimate ambiguity
across the three observationally equivalent models: one should repair the conversion error and
preserve the genuine ambiguity.
   Unresolved edges introduce another representation problem. A Julia DiGraph may store
both i → j and j → i to represent one undirected edge. It is then a container for a partially
directed graph, not a claim that the causal system has a two-way feedback loop. A generic
acyclicity check applied before decoding will incorrectly reject that representation. A generic
linear-system solver applied to its zero-one adjacency will invent coefficients and feedback.
Both failures can occur without changing a single stored byte.
  These conventions are documented or implemented in the inspected versions (mschauer/-
CausalInference.jl contributors, 2026; JuliaDynamics/Associations.jl contributors, 2026;
sepehr78/RecursiveCausalDiscovery.jl contributors, 2025; CausalDisco/flopsearch contributors,
2026; Biwei-Huang/Generalized-Score-Functions-for-Causal-Discovery contributors, 2020;
226                                                               Causal analysis for a universal bank


                    Selected representation          i → j: (Gij , Gji ) i − j
                    Julia reciprocal-arc container   (1, 0)              (1, 1)
                    FLOP documented CPDAG            (1, 0)              (2, 2)
                    Generalized-score GES            (1, 0)              (−1, −1)
                    BNT selected PC function         (−1, 0)             (1, 1)

coefficient.

bayesnet/bnt contributors, 2019). The table does not define a universal convention for every
function in a package. For example, BNT’s K2 routine returns a selected DAG with a different
contract from its PC routine. The proposed interchange object must therefore carry method,
version, graph class, variable identities and endpoint meaning. It must distinguish a weighted
structural model from an unweighted graph even when their matrix dimensions agree.


23.9.3    Julia: composability requires checking the actual dispatch

CausalInference.jl 0.19.4 provides a useful starting point for a Julia backend. Its inspected
PC entrypoint accepts a conditional-independence callback and defaults to the stable skeleton
path. It returns a CPDAG in the reciprocal-arc representation. Gaussian GES exposes
a different computation: forward insertion and backward deletion continue while a score
improvement is available. The selected function returns a graph, score improvement relative
to the empty graph, and timing information. Its default penalty is 0.5, which should not be
confused with the explicit values used in examples or with another library’s score normalization
(mschauer/CausalInference.jl contributors, 2026).
  The covariance-based local score makes this distinction precise. With n rows, k parents,
penalty multiplier λ, and residual variance Cp , the inspected expression is

                       s = − 12 {n[1 + log(max(0, Cp ))] + λ(1 + k) log n}.

For a nonsingular parent covariance block, Cp is computed by subtracting the explained
covariance contribution. A larger value is preferred by the search. If Cp = 0, however, the
displayed logarithm is not a finite number; the zero clamp is not a positive numerical floor.
The adapter should diagnose constant variables, deterministic relationships, singular parent
systems and nonfinite scores before using a chosen graph in a funding decision. A perfect
numerical fit can signal degeneracy, not overwhelming causal evidence. Score comparison
across engines also requires matching centering, penalties, constants and the exact returned
quantity.
  Associations.jl offers a broader composition of association measures, independence tests and
graph algorithms. That flexibility is useful when the banking variables are nonlinear, but it does
not make arbitrary compositions valid. The PC documentation requires nondirectional pairwise
and conditional measures and specifically warns against inserting transfer entropy into this
generic symmetric skeleton procedure. The selected check_input contains the direction check
only as commented code. The proposed wrapper must enforce the compatibility condition itself
and record which measure and test were admitted(JuliaDynamics/Associations.jl contributors,
2026).
   Defaults also need source-level attention. The PC constructor uses maxdepth, while the
docstring presents max_depth. The local-permutation constructor defaults to ten neighbors,
although its documented signature says five. It exposes the number of shuffles, random
generator and a temporal exclusion window. These are concrete parameters of the proposed
23.9. Discovery beyond the principal language interfaces                                      227


statistical experiment. A temporal window alone does not prove that a resampling scheme
gives valid uncertainty for repeated accounts, common market shocks or a changing assignment
process. The parameter, sampling unit and relevant null law must be reviewed together.
   The selected skeleton removes an edge when the returned p-value exceeds α. This is a
procedural choice made by the algorithm. Failure to reject independence is not proof that
the variables are independent, especially with small samples or high-dimensional conditioning
sets. Likewise a finite orientation-sweep limit can leave the graph less fully oriented than an
unrestricted run. A result should disclose the restriction and retain the partially resolved
object, rather than infer a unique graph from the fact that an execution completed.
   RecursiveCausalDiscovery.jl 0.2.0 gives a narrower alternative. Its README lists RSL-D as
implemented while marking MARVEL, L-MARVEL and ROL as future work. Its boundary
initialization tests every pair conditional on all other variables. That initial conditioning
problem can be statistically difficult even when a later recursive search reduces the number of
tests. The selected implementation also falls back to a smallest-boundary variable when it
finds no removable variable. The output alone does not reveal that the intended removability
condition was successfully established (sepehr78/RecursiveCausalDiscovery.jl contributors,
2025).
   A specific dispatch issue must be resolved before relying on separate boundary and search
tests. The matrix overload accepts a distinct mkbd_ci_test argument but forwards ci_test
in its place when converting to the table path. Source inspection therefore does not support
the claim that both overloads honor the supplied boundary test. The README’s Julia
requirement and the broader manifest declaration also differ. These findings justify retaining
the package as an experimental comparison, with explicit overload and environment checks.
They do not establish that recursive methods in general are unsuitable.
   The three Julia families have inspected MIT grants. That makes a proposed integration
easier to pursue subject to the notices and dependency terms, but creates no statistical warranty.
The preferred first step is a restricted Julia process with a frozen package environment, explicit
table orientation and graph decoder. Reimplementing every graph method in the common
library would add mathematical and maintenance obligations before demonstrating a consumer
need for the port.


23.9.4    Rust: a native implementation still needs a statistical contract

FLOP/flopsearch 0.3.0 already connects a Rust numerical search to Python and R. Its selected
interface accepts observations by rows, a BIC penalty and a termination choice. It documents
a CPDAG matrix with directed entries one and unresolved entries two. This offers a plausible
alternative to building a new Rust foreign-function interface merely because the core is native
(CausalDisco/flopsearch contributors, 2026).
   The stopping contract needs closer treatment than the word “timeout” suggests. The
selected configuration requires exactly one of a restart count, a timeout or manual termination.
The Python stub states that at least one local search runs to a local optimum. In the inspected
Rust loop, the shown abort check is conditional on being beyond the first restart; it exits an
inner search loop. The surrounding restart loop and delegated numerical calls require further
qualification before the product can promise a strict elapsed deadline. A proposal adapter can
impose an outer worker deadline, but must then say whether interruption returns a validated
best-so-far graph, a checkpoint or only a failed request. It cannot imply that the library’s
timer already provides the desired service guarantee.
  The same entrypoint uses a thread-local random generator, while the selected public
configuration exposes no seed. This limits the replay contract that can be promised from that
228                                                           Causal analysis for a universal bank


interface alone. A frozen binary and dataset are insufficient to establish identical stochastic
output. Before a matched benchmark, decide whether the adapter can bind the random state
or must compare declared output distributions over registered repeated runs. The inspected
MPL-2.0 grant also requires a distribution-specific review of covered source and notices; using
an existing wrapper does not remove that obligation.
  The static DirectLiNGAM path in varlingam-rs 0.1.0 presents a different issue. Its coefficient
assignment is explicitly B[target, predictor], consistent with the column-vector convention
used above. It selects an ordering, uses a sparse predictor-selection step, and refits retained
predictors on their original scale. The README advertises matching accuracy and substantial
speedups, but those statements are not independent evidence for the proposed banking
workload(edy-os/varlingam-rs contributors, 2026).
   The inspected ordering optimization constructs entropy summaries once. Subsequent itera-
tions update residual data, yet the root-scoring helper ignores its data argument and uses the
cached summaries. There may be a mathematical argument for a particular cached formula-
tion, but it has not been established by reading the performance claim or this helper alone.
The appropriate next comparison freezes the intended algorithm, inspects the optimization
argument and delegated numerical helpers, and tests matched cases where the evolving residual
distribution matters. It would be premature either to assert algorithmic equivalence or to
declare every cached strategy incorrect. The recommendation is to defer default adoption and
retain this as a candidate for focused review. Its inspected MIT or Apache-2.0 choice resolves
one part of reuse, not the algorithmic question.
   why-rs 0.2.1 supplies a particularly clear reason to inspect code beneath an algorithm name.
Its selected PC propagation method implements one rule and explicitly leaves the second and
third rules for future addition. Its independence calculation has hardcoded normal critical
values for α = 0.01, 0.05, 0.10; every other supplied value receives 1.960. The recursive partial-
correlation calculation returns zero when its denominator is zero. These are source-level findings
about the pinned path, not claims derived from executing a Rust benchmark(jwhogg/why-rs
contributors, 2025).
   For example, a two-sided normal reference test at α = 0.02 would use Φ−1 (0.99) ≃ 2.32635.
At a stipulated statistic of 2.2, that reference does not reject independence, whereas the
inspected fallback 1.960 does. Under an exactly standard normal reference law, the latter
threshold has rejection probability approximately 0.05, not 0.02. This scalar calculation
demonstrates a parameter mismatch; it does not estimate an empirical false-positive rate for a
whole discovery procedure (Causal banking proposal project, 2026o). Returning zero for a
degenerate partial correlation can similarly turn an undefined calculation into an independence
decision. The proposed common adapter should preserve numerical failure as a distinct
outcome.
   Together these findings justify rejecting this particular PC implementation as the reference
discovery engine. They do not require rejecting its graph modeling or structural simulation
ideas, which would need their own inspection. A language with strong memory-safety features
does not supply missing orientation rules or validate a statistical reference law.


23.9.5    MATLAB: reference value and reuse rights are separate

Causal Explorer 1.5 documents a broad family of discovery and variable-selection methods.
Its PC manual specifies variables by columns, domain counts for discrete variables, and
mutual-information, G2 or Fisher-z choices. The saved release states P-code compatibility
with MATLAB R2017b. These details make it a useful documented comparator, but neither
they nor a public repository establish an unrestricted source-code dependency (mensxmachi-
23.9. Discovery beyond the principal language interfaces                                     229


na/CausalExplorer_1.5 contributors, 2019).
   The accompanying license restricts the grant to noncommercial educational and research
use by an academic recipient on a single-user system, without permission to redistribute or
create derivative works. The manual’s “public domain” wording cannot by itself resolve this
conflict. Under the saved grant, the proposed commercial library should reject direct adoption
and porting of this distribution. Separately obtained rights could change a later decision. The
proposal can already compare the documented capability against alternatives whose reuse
terms support the intended route. No MATLAB execution, current platform compatibility or
agreement to those terms is implied by this comparison.
   The generalized-score GES reference provides readable MATLAB search and scoring code.
Its selected criteria are negative cross-validated likelihood or negative marginal likelihood,
with separate paths for multidimensional variables. The search seeks decreases in this criterion.
This differs in sign and meaning from the maximized Gaussian score described for Julia; the
raw numerical values are not a common ranking of engines. Its output uses one for a directed
edge and minus one for an unresolved edge, adding another reason to decode by method
identity (Biwei-Huang/Generalized-Score-Functions-for-Causal-Discovery contributors, 2020).
   The inspected cross-validation score forms dense T × T kernel and centering arrays for T
observations, computes data-dependent bandwidths, and slices contiguous validation folds.
One dense double-precision array alone takes approximately 8T 2 bytes before workspace,
copies and other arrays. This storage account follows from the array dimensions; it is not a
measured peak-memory benchmark. Contiguous slices do not automatically constitute a valid
forward-in-time banking evaluation. Training can include observations later than the held-out
block, and the displayed preprocessing is computed before that block is sliced. A proposed
dependent-data study must explicitly decide what is known when, how kernels are constructed
and what the score is intended to validate.
   The top-level GES rights also remain unresolved. The saved repository tree contains a
redistribution notice for an embedded kernel-test component, but that grant does not establish
permission for all surrounding code. The immediate choice is to retain this methodological
comparison and defer redistribution or porting. A clean new implementation would still require
an inspected mathematical specification, independent verification and a reason to maintain
it alongside existing engines. Merely translating MATLAB syntax would not resolve those
obligations.
   Bayes Net Toolbox provides a useful older reference for how distinct search contracts coexist
inside one toolbox. Its K2 entrypoint places variables in rows and observations in columns.
It greedily adds parents from predecessors in a user-supplied ordering, with Bayesian or BIC
score options. Thus the ordering supplies directional restrictions that the procedure does not
learn. If a funding analyst orders quoted rate before retained funding, the algorithm’s inability
to return a reverse parent is partly a consequence of that input, not evidence against the
reverse causal explanation (bayesnet/bnt contributors, 2019).
   The selected BNT PC function instead accepts a conditional-independence callback and
returns a partially directed adjacency with negative one for a directed edge and symmetric
positive ones for an unresolved edge. Data orientation, algorithm output and coefficient
interpretation are three separate conversions. Tests that verify only the number of rows or
edges will miss a semantic reversal. Its BNT license file explicitly uses the GNU Library
General Public License version 2; its name ending in license.gpl.txt is insufficient to
characterize every component of the larger collection. Preserve the actual grant, review
bundled components, and test a selected modern environment before recommending adoption.
An old documentation date establishes neither current maintenance nor current failure, and
historical price references should not enter the investment account as contemporary quotations.
230                                                             Causal analysis for a universal bank


23.9.6    JavaScript: support the analyst without inventing an effect

DAGitty’s JavaScript core is a plausible component for constructing and analyzing a proposed
banking graph. Its selected adjustment interface accepts DAG, PDAG, MAG and PAG types,
reads source and target nodes, and handles adjustment and selection information. The browser
interface and R frontend expose the same underlying family of graph operations (jtextor/dagitty
contributors, 2024). This is valuable for reviewing a claim such as “adjust for the customer’s
prior relationship score.” It does not prove that the supplied arrows correspond to the bank’s
assignment process.
   The intended integration therefore keeps graph authoring, graph analysis and data-based
discovery separate. An analyst can propose alternative diagrams, attach an observation clock
and identify whether an adjustment query has an answer under each diagram. The proposed
numerical service can then report what estimation would require. The JavaScript graph must
retain its class and endpoint marks through those steps. Rendering a PAG as a DAG to simplify
an interface would give the analyst a stronger assumption than the source result supports. The
inspected GPL-v2 terms and dependency notices require an appropriate distribution design;
process separation alone does not establish exemption from those terms.
   The selected expert-in-loop JavaScript demo illustrates a more subtle boundary. Its
pillai_test fits random forests for two variables on the conditioning variables, predicts on
those same rows, computes residuals, and obtains canonical correlations. Its effectSize field
is the sum of squared canonical correlations, followed by an F -reference calculation. The display
logic can combine that statistic with an arrow from the supplied graph(ankurankan/2025-
causal-discovery-webapp contributors, 2025).
   A squared canonical correlation is an association statistic. It is dimensionless and does not
provide the sign or monetary units of the funding response above. Attaching an arrow to it
does not turn it into ∂E[F | do(Q)]/∂Q. Nor does the inspected formula establish a calibrated
null distribution after fitting flexible residual models on the same rows. A serious integration
would need a stated statistical target, an argument or measured calibration for the actual
fitting procedure, and appropriate held-out or cross-fitted alternatives. The product can use
the interface idea for discussing disagreements while declining to display the statistic as a
banking treatment effect.
   The package metadata declares ISC, while the selected tree does not supply a complete top-
level grant sufficient for this review. Its test command is a placeholder that exits unsuccessfully.
Neither fact proves that the interaction idea is unusable; both prevent treating a successful
package installation or a license field as a completed adoption assessment. The recommended
next use is a separately designed graph-review interaction, with any numerical comparison
delegated to an admitted scientific method.


23.9.7    An integration sequence that preserves useful alternatives

The proposed first implementation should admit a small set of mathematical operations. One
Julia PC/GES path can test the independence and score-search boundary; FLOP can test
an existing native engine behind an R/Python interface; DAGitty can test graph review
and adjustment. Each has a concrete reason to be considered. The unqualified Rust paths,
unresolved MATLAB rights and browser residual statistic need not block those independent
experiments. They remain explicit alternatives or rejected current choices, with the condition
that would change the decision.
  A common adverse-fixture suite should verify both input and result meaning. The funding
construction supplies a weighted DAG whose transpose changes the effect, an unresolved
23.10. Commercial discovery: compare the retained graph before the interface                 231


chain with several compatible effects, and graph mark conventions that cannot be read as
coefficients. Other fixtures should include constant variables, singular covariance, a caller-
supplied nondefault significance level, changed variable order, a limited conditioning depth and
an interrupted search. Each engine must preserve an undefined calculation or unsupported
request as such. Agreement on a convenient regular dataset is inadequate if the adapter silently
turns these cases into a definite causal answer.
   Matched comparison must then separate four families of assumptions. Constraint methods
depend on their selected independence tests and graph premises. Score methods depend on
likelihood or surrogate criterion, penalties and search restrictions. Functional methods rely on
the declared structural and disturbance restrictions, including the non-Gaussian conditions
developed earlier. Continuous optimization methods impose a numerical acyclicity condition in
addition to their statistical objective. The selected other-language sources do not complete the
census of functional or continuous methods; the earlier Python comparison supplies concrete
alternatives without implying that a Julia or Rust equivalent is absent. No implementation
family should inherit another’s causal qualification solely because both return a matrix.
   Only after these semantic checks should a bounded prototype compare runtime, memory,
failed requests and the consequences for an actual decision rule. Freeze the source and
environment identities, data units, baselines, stopping criteria and failure account before final
evaluation. These requirements define a proposed comparison; the source inspections and exact
examples here do not claim to have executed it. The investment choice is therefore specific:
integrate a few well-understood paths, preserve useful alternatives, and spend on porting
only when an identified consumer or measured bottleneck makes that additional responsibility
worthwhile.


23.10      Commercial discovery: compare the retained graph be-
           fore the interface
Commercial Bayesian-network systems already address substantial parts of the workflow that
a new causal product would have to build. The relevant comparison includes interactive model
construction, structure and parameter learning, background restrictions, model exchange and
programmatic inference. The proposal should specify which of these services it would reuse
and which scientific contract it would add. A common command-line or MCP interface alone
would not establish an advantage over an existing modeling environment.
  The following comparison uses inspected vendor technical documentation. The GeNIe
manual declares version 5.0.R2, built on 23 November 2024; the SMILE programmer’s manual
declares version 2.2.4.R1, built on 27 April 2024. The public URLs were retrieved after the 7
October 2026 literature cutoff, so those headers identify the declared manuals without proving
their exact historical bytes at the cutoff. The inspected BayesiaLab pages are mutable and
do not consistently pin the technical discussion to a numbered release. Their findings are
consequently dated documentation observations. No vendor executable, commercial trial or
paid service was run for this comparison (BayesFusion, LLC, 2024g,j; Bayesia, 2026d).
   GeNIe exposes both a PC route and a Bayesian Search route. The PC manual documents
a default significance level of 0.05, maximum adjacency of eight, and no time limit by
default. It allows continuous data under a multivariate Gaussian assumption and returns a
pattern for further inspection. The manual’s suggested histogram and scatterplot checks are
useful exploratory diagnostics; they cannot establish the full joint distribution or the causal
assumptions. Its Bayesian Search discussion instead describes score-guided hill climbing with
restarts, a BDeu-related sample-size parameter and a structural prior. A seed of zero uses
232                                                           Causal analysis for a universal bank


the processor clock, so it is not a fixed reproducibility seed. These are different procedures to
configure and compare, even though they share a graphical application (BayesFusion, LLC,
2024f,d).
   The pattern editor is a particularly important capability. Its documentation explicitly
discusses an equivalence class and permits inspection of unresolved arcs. It also documents a
Create DAG command that randomly chooses directions for unresolved arcs while producing an
acyclic graph. That command can be useful for constructing a representative Bayesian network,
but the choice does not add observational evidence for the selected directions. The proposed
product must preserve the pre-conversion pattern and label any selected representative. It
should not describe GeNIe as necessarily forcing a single graph: the documented pattern
workflow is itself a useful alternative (BayesFusion, LLC, 2024e).
   Consider the funding law in Section 18. Its three Gaussian models share the same covariance
but imply effects of either zero or 0.48 thousand currency units per percentage point. A
proposed interface that keeps only a randomly chosen representative could report either zero or
120 currency units per customer for the 25 basis point action. The difference would come from
the extra orientation choice. This is a project counterexample to a lossy integration design; it
is not an observed GeNIe estimate or a claim that the vendor’s documented interface conceals
that choice. A matched trial should inspect the pattern, the conversion and the returned effect
separately (Causal banking research project, 2026g).
   BayesiaLab supplies another relevant alternative. Its structural-learning overview describes
heuristic search and an MDL score used to compare learned networks. The EQ page explicitly
describes search over equivalence classes. That makes class-aware search a documented
competitor capability, rather than a novelty the proposed library can claim simply by retaining
ambiguous graphs. A score optimized over graph structures still does not validate the banking
assignment mechanism or supply an intervention-effect confidence region. Those are additional
scientific questions (Bayesia, 2026d,b).
   The EQ page also documents a consequential distinction among restrictions: fixed arcs
are treated as ordinary arcs, whereas forbidden arcs and temporal indices are taken into
account. A workflow that marks a bank-supplied edge as fixed must therefore inspect the
selected algorithm’s actual meaning for that setting. A generic required_edges field cannot
be mapped to a similarly named graphical control without a behavioral check. The same
page’s description of efficiency is a vendor claim, not a measured runtime result or a proof of
finding the global optimum in this proposal (Bayesia, 2026b).


23.11      What a commercial engine boundary would have to
           preserve
SMILE is the proprietary C++ engine underlying GeNIe. Its programmer’s manual describes
compiled platform distributions and wrappers for Java, Python, R, .NET and COM. These are
access paths to an engine, not independent discoveries of five competing causal implementations.
Their individual interoperability still needs review. The C++ manual does not, by itself, verify
that every wrapper exposes every endpoint type and error state (BayesFusion, LLC, 2024j).
   The DSL_pc::Learn reference returns a DSL_pattern and a success or error code. A progress
callback can interrupt learning, in which case the documented return is DSL_INTERRUPTED.
The time limit is checked after an iteration, so the documented setting is not evidence of a
strict external wall-time guarantee. A resource-bounded wrapper should retain interruption
as an incomplete computation and enforce its own lifecycle contract if a hard deadline is
required. Stopping the process cannot make the unfinished graph a completed scientific answer
23.12. Capabilities to reuse and capabilities the proposal still lacks                          233


(BayesFusion, LLC, 2024m).
   Graph conversion also requires care. The DSL_pattern reference declares absent, undirected
and directed edge types, indexed by the dataset’s variable order. Its conversion to a network
assumes that the dataset and pattern coordinates correspond. GeNIe’s graphical pattern
documentation uses a richer visual description, including colored and double-headed arcs.
These pages alone do not establish a complete equivalence between every graphical mark and
the C++ representation, or a standard CPDAG/PAG serialization. Before reuse, the adapter

REST service performs structural discovery. The overview also describes Java configurations

location. An integration proposal must select the actual interface and operation before
estimating deployment cost or data movement. A label such as “Bayesia API” is too broad for
either conclusion (Bayesia, 2026a).
