28.5      Orthogonality isolates a rate obligation
Let Z be an instrument, D an action, Y an outcome and X measured pre-action information.
Write m(X) = E(Z | X), r(X) = E(D | X) and ℓ(X) = E(Y | X). Suppose the declared
causal model identifies θ0 through

                        E[(Z − m(X)){Y − ℓ(X) − θ0 (D − r(X))}] = 0.

This is an assumption about an identified model; the existence of these conditional means does
not establish a valid instrument.
  Condition on nuisance functions trained on an independent pilot with the same target law.
Denote their errors by δm , δr , δℓ . Expanding the fitted score and using the zero conditional
means of the centered variables gives the exact remainder
                                                                                             
        R(θ0 ) = E[δm (X){δℓ (X) − θ0 δr (X)}],        |R(θ0 )| ≤ ∥δm ∥2 ∥δℓ ∥2 + |θ0 |∥δr ∥2 .

The inequality follows from Cauchy–Schwarz and the triangle inequality. It exposes exactly
what must be bounded for this score. In a two-stratum arithmetic example with equal stratum
probabilities, errors (0.1, 0.2, 0.05) and (−0.1, 0.1, −0.05), ordered as (δm , δℓ , δr ), and θ0 = 2,
the remainder is −0.005.Causal banking research project (2026ar)
   The identity provides no convergence rate for a particular learner. Reusing dependent
observations for training and evaluation also invalidates the simple conditioning argument unless
additional separation or dependence control is proved. Support failures and misspecification can
prevent the errors from shrinking. For weak instrument relevance, even a well-controlled score
may yield an unbounded effect set under test inversion. This is why source-level availability of
flexible learners and sandwich calculations cannot settle the unresolved research on dependent
learning and useful precision.
Chapter 29

Histories, forest targets and the
units of causal calculations

29.1      Resampling a sequence requires a sampling model
Consider a bank evaluating a sequence of servicing decisions over twelve months. The data
contain repeated observations of each borrower, interventions that depend on previous balances
and competing events such as account closure. The statistical unit might be a borrower history,
a household, a branch or an independent economic calendar. These choices imply different
resampling laws. A routine with “bootstrap” in its name does not determine the appropriate
law.
   LiNGAM’s generic bootstrap resamples rows and refits the model. VARLiNGAM has a
distinct path: it fits a lag model, applies a contemporaneous LiNGAM model to the residuals,
resamples residual vectors and reconstructs a sequence using the fitted autoregressive coefficients.
The inspected loop temporarily sets the lag-selection criterion to None. Consequently, one
must inspect the initial lag/coefficient settings and the loop’s refit behavior before claiming
that it propagates model-selection uncertainty.LiNGAM project (2026a)
   Residual resampling can be a sensible candidate under an appropriate innovation law. It
does not automatically preserve persistent residual dependence, unmodeled common shocks or
a different sampling calendar. Row resampling is a different candidate suitable for a different
observational unit. A banking comparison should include a correctly specified innovation
model and an adverse case with persistent residuals, preserving the uncertainty target and
failures in both. Bootstrap edge frequencies should not be reported as a calibrated effect
confidence region without an additional argument.
   pygformula’s inspected bootstrap draws observed subject identifiers with replacement, copies
each subject’s complete history and assigns a fresh replicate identifier to each draw. It updates
histories and refits covariate and outcome models. Expanding to the requested simulation
population occurs in a separate step. These operations distinguish the observed sampling unit
from the Monte Carlo population used to evaluate a fitted regime.pygformula project (2026a)
   The fresh identifiers matter. Drawing borrower 17 twice should produce two bootstrap
histories, not concatenate them into one impossible person with two records at every date. An
integration test needs duplicate draws, unequal history lengths and multiple interventions. It
must also preserve the original calendar when that calendar is part of the estimand. Subject
resampling alone does not account for a market shock shared by every subject on the same
date.



                                               282
29.2. The intervention clock and competing-event target                                      283


   Failed fits require equally explicit handling. The inspected bootstrap helper catches an
exception, warns and returns a dictionary whose boot_results is None. The caller filters such
entries when assembling one result list, but subsequently constructs bootests by indexing
every original entry. A failed entry therefore exposes a static inconsistency in that caller
path. This observation requires reproduction in the pinned runtime before attributing an
observed frequency or impact to it. The integration must count attempted, successful and
failed replications and preserve the failure reason, irrespective of whether the eventual repair
aborts, returns an explicit unavailable interval or uses a preregistered rule. pygformula project
(2026b,a)


29.2      The intervention clock and competing-event target
The inspected simulation path applies an intervention to the current simulated frame and then
refreshes history variables before outcome prediction. Static schedules index their values by
the absolute time index int_values[t]. Threshold interventions bound the current action
between the supplied limits. Custom interventions receive the current frame, available pool
and time index. The API permits useful regimes, but does not itself certify that a custom
function uses only information available at the decision time. pygformula project (2026a)
   For example, “contact once delinquency has persisted for two months” refers to the observed
history before the action, whereas “contact borrowers who will be delinquent next month” uses
future information. Both can be expressed as executable code if future fields have been made
available. A valid interface must enforce the declared information clock and treat prohibited
reads as a contract violation. Thresholds should also retain their monetary units and whether
they change an action, a measurement or an eligibility condition.
   Competing events alter the target even when the same outcome model is used. In a stipulated
discrete-time model, let dt be the probability of a competing event in period t among those
still at risk, and let yt be the outcome hazard conditional on avoiding that competing event. If
competing events occur before outcomes within a period, the cumulative incidence through T
is
                                     T
                                       (                    )
                                     X     Y
                         FY (T ) =             (1 − ds )(1 − ys ) (1 − dt )yt .
                                     t=1   s<t

This formula follows by partitioning on the period of the first outcome event. It differs from a
hypothetical law that eliminates the competing event.
   For two periods with y = (0.1, 0.2) and d = (0.05, 0.1), the first contribution is 0.095 and
the second is 0.9(0.95)(0.9)(0.2) = 0.1539. Total incidence is 0.2489. Removing competing
events while holding these outcome hazards fixed gives 1 − (0.9)(0.8) = 0.28. At a stipulated
10,000 accounts and CNY 100 per event, the corresponding expected-loss difference is CNY
31,100. This is exact illustrative arithmetic. It does not identify the effect of eliminating a
real bank’s competing event or establish that the outcome hazard would remain fixed under
that intervention.Causal banking research project (2026ar)
   The inspected pygformula source separately computes survival risks with and without a
competing-event path, using subject-level cumulative products and then population means.
That code provides a concrete place to check the within-period ordering, history alignment and
target definition. It does not settle whether observed censoring or competing-event assumptions
are valid in the proposed banking application.pygformula project (2026a)
284                                                           Causal analysis for a universal bank


29.3     Following an R forest operation into its C++ implemen-
         tation
For grf, the causal-forest binding assigns the same variable index to treatment and
instrument, then calls an instrumental predictor. The predictor factory constructs
InstrumentalPredictionStrategy. The native prediction uses a ratio of centered outcome–
instrument and treatment–instrument moments. When instrument and treatment coincide,
this corresponds to a weighted local covariance divided by a weighted local treatment variance.
This traced route supports the interpretation of continuous-treatment output as a local slope
under its functional assumptions.grf project (2026a)
   It does not identify an arbitrary finite change in a nonlinear dose-response curve. A change
from an offer rate of one unit to two units needs the appropriate counterfactual contrast and
exposure support. A slope, an average slope and a finite contrast can coincide in a linear
model and diverge otherwise. The bank must choose the target before comparing software
outputs.
  The native variance routine forms influence-like quantities across tree groups, separates
between-group variation from group noise and calls a Bayes debiaser. These groups concern
the forest’s computation. They are distinct from the observed borrower clusters used by the R
average-effect calculation. Inspecting both paths avoids the false inference that a tree-group
variance option automatically accounts for a persistent banking calendar. The debiaser, forest
sampling, serialization and numerical safeguards require additional review before a direct
native interface is qualified.grf project (2026a)
   The maintained R interface is therefore a reasonable first integration candidate, subject
to a complete license/dependency and behavioral review. A direct C++ port would have to
preserve the forest representation, prediction strategy, variance method, randomization and
exceptional outcomes across version changes. Avoiding one language boundary does not by
itself justify that maintenance commitment. The open-source decision should compare the
operational cost of an R process or library bridge with the full scientific and technical cost of
a maintained port.


29.4     Population averaging, support and unavailable combina-
         tions
In grf’s inspected all-population AIPW path, the mean is a weighted average of get_scores
output. The variance calculation sums centered weighted scores within the declared clusters,
squares these group contributions and applies a group-count correction. For binary treatment,
the score uses the usual propensity residual divided by eb(1 − eb). For continuous treatment, an
auxiliary regression forest estimates the conditional variance of the treatment; the debiasing
weight divides the treatment residual by that estimate.grf project (2026a)
   Small conditional variance is an information problem. Borrowers with essentially one
available offer rate do not support precise estimation of a local rate response simply because a
forest can fit the outcome. Qualification should retain weak-support cases and identify whether
the operation returns a warning, an extreme weight, an unavailable result or a misleading
finite value. The inspected formula alone supplies no finite-sample guarantee for such cases.
  The all, treated, control and overlap populations must remain distinct. In the overlap
path the code fits a residualized outcome on a residualized treatment and uses cluster or
heteroskedastic covariance as applicable. Moving to an overlap target may improve stability
29.5. A generalized propensity score has physical units                                         285


while changing which banking population the result describes. A wrapper must not silently
make that choice on the analyst’s behalf.grf project (2026a)
   Option support must be determined from reachable control flow. The inspected average-
effect routine rejects TMLE when clusters or sample weights are supplied before reaching later
formulas that contain cluster-related expressions. Seeing those later formulas would not justify
advertising clustered TMLE at this entry point. Likewise, only specified combinations support
continuous treatment. The adapter’s capability matrix needs explicit accepted combinations
and typed refusal for the others.grf project (2026a)


29.5      A generalized propensity score has physical units
Let a continuous exposure follow a location-scale law A = µ(X) + s(X)R, with s(X) > 0.
Conditional change of variables gives

                                             1             a − µ(x)
                                                                   
                             fA|X (a | x) =     f                   x .
                                            s(x) R|X         s(x)

The Jacobian 1/s(x) is necessary for a density with respect to the original exposure measure.
If a common residual density is used instead of fR|X , an additional residual-distribution
assumption is being made.
   CausalGPS’s inspected compute_resid returns the standardized residual (a − b)/c. Its
compute_density helper calls R’s density estimate and interpolates it with rule=2. In the
inspected kernel branch of estimate_gps, the standardized-residual density is assigned to the
GPS field without division by the predicted scale in that branch. The normal branch instead
evaluates a normal density using its fitted mean and scale. These observations establish a
concrete scale question for downstream matching, weighting and dose-response construction.
They do not establish the behavior of every downstream operation.CausalGPS project (2026b,a)
   At a standardized residual of zero, a standard normal density is about 0.3989423. Two
strata with scales one and two have original-exposure densities 0.3989423 and 0.1994711 at
their respective means. Retaining only the common standardized-residual value loses that
difference. If the exposure is measured in units one hundred times smaller, its numerical
value is multiplied by one hundred and the corresponding density must be divided by one
hundred. The probability of any physical exposure interval remains unchanged. These exact
transformations provide a reference for a future unit-consistency test. Causal banking research
project (2026ar)
  Some downstream procedures might deliberately use a transformed balancing quantity, while
others require a density in the original units. The integration decision therefore remains deferred
until each use of the returned field is traced and the intended quantity is established. Silently
changing the helper could alter package behavior without resolving the scientific contract. A
matched comparison should examine heterogeneous scales, near-zero scales, counterfactual
dose evaluation and an explicit unit conversion, retaining any unsupported cases.
   The causaldrf comparison has a separate source obligation. Its accompanying license notice
identifies the year and copyright holder, supplementing the package’s license declaration. That
resolves the availability of that notice; it does not settle transitive licensing or the statistical
behavior of its interval routines. Source availability, permission to distribute and justified
uncertainty remain separate questions.causaldrf project (2026a)

29.6     Implications for reusable causal operations
These examples support a common semantic contract with explicit graph orientation, query/-
failure type, independent observational unit, decision clock, target population, dose units
and uncertainty construction. A business-facing assistant can elicit these fields and explain
unresolved choices, while a deterministic validator checks the declared operation against its
supported combinations. An LLM’s plausible description is not evidence that a package uses
the intended covariance or intervention target.
   The relevant next qualification compares complete causal requests. It retains the same
estimand and information across packages, separates sampling from Monte Carlo error, includes
failed fits and preserves unbounded sets. Numerical agreement in a benign case is useful
evidence about implementation, but cannot establish assignment truth, identification or useful
precision in adverse banking regimes. Those remain scientific and institutional requirements.
Chapter 30

What language models contribute to
causal knowledge

30.1     Four different objects called causal reasoning
A banker asking why deposit balances fell can be asking for an explanation of a recorded event,
an estimate of a feasible rate intervention, a prediction of next month’s balance, or a diagnosis
of an observation error. A fluent answer can move between these objects without announcing
the change. The useful starting point for evaluating language assistance is therefore the object
being produced: a proposed scientific question, evidence about a causal model, a formal
calculation conditional on that model, or a recommendation under a specified loss. Success at
one object supplies no automatic guarantee for the others.
   The early frontier argument proposes using language models to organize domain knowledge,
draft graphs, critique assumptions and suggest robustness analyses. It also records the ability
to reproduce recognizable public data and distinguishes transforming known information
from discovering a new causal structure.Kıcıman et al. (2023) This distinction is particularly
consequential in banking. A familiar statement about interest rates can be useful prior
knowledge, but the effect of a particular bank’s deposit offer depends on its population,
competitors, eligibility rules and information clock. A remembered relationship does not
determine that intervention effect.
   Formal benchmarks introduce a second object. CLadder constructs questions from known
causal structures with different verbalizations. Its results concern answers to those generated
questions, including historically specified models and prompting methods.Jin et al. (2023)
Such a benchmark can reveal failures to distinguish observation from intervention. It cannot
establish that a model elicits the right variables from an unfamiliar bank process, measures
them correctly, or returns calibrated uncertainty after fitting to dependent data. These are
additional stages of the proposed product.
   Third, a language model can propose a causal mechanism for numerical analysis. Model
Discovery Agent illustrates a separation between executable mechanism proposals and numerical
fitting, evidence approximation and experiment design. Its finite predictive evaluations
explicitly do not establish causal identification.Murphy (2026) A mechanism may predict well
because several observationally equivalent models predict equally well. The bank must still
justify which intervention the model represents and which new experiment would distinguish
economically different mechanisms.
  Finally, workflow assistance concerns selection and coordination of established operations.
Causal-learn+ describes assistance with diagnosis, assumptions, method selection and inter-

                                              287
288                                                           Causal analysis for a universal bank


pretation while retaining algorithm outputs and graph ambiguity.Zheng (2026) This is a useful
architectural direction. It changes the analyst’s interaction with numerical tools; it does not
make a method’s premises true. The following chapters keep these four contributions separate
while studying how they can work together.


30.2      Text supplies a different information channel
Write D for the observed numerical records, K for inspected documentary or expert evidence,
and M(D, K) for the models consistent with the declared interpretation of both. For target
ψ, a set-valued answer is

                             Ψ(D, K) = {ψ(M ) : M ∈ M(D, K)}.

This notation does not assert that finite data identify the population law or that a statistical
confidence procedure has been supplied. It describes which models the analysis intends to
consider. Statistical uncertainty about the law must subsequently be propagated through the
model set.
  Additional reliable knowledge may exclude a model that the observed distribution alone
cannot exclude. A contract establishing that an invitation was randomized, for example,
has a different evidential role from a predictive correlation. But a model-generated sentence
repeating that randomization is common practice does not establish what happened in the
bank’s historical process. The analysis must identify the original source, the relevant population
and dates, the interpretation of its claim, and the person or measurement that supports it.
   This also explains why retrieving more documents need not improve discovery. LACR
combines background knowledge, retrieved documents and optional numerical information,
and includes an UNKNOWN response. Its reported retrieval effects differ across benchmarks,
with adverse as well as favorable outcomes. Zhang et al. (2024) Retrieval changes K; it does
not certify K. Documents may concern a different treatment definition, contain an association
stated as a cause, or duplicate the same original assertion. Ten repeated documents are not
ten independent confirmations of an edge.
   An appropriate evidence object therefore retains the claim, source passage, date, domain,
units and proposed role. A passage may justify a variable definition without justifying an
arrow. A process document may establish that one action occurs before another without
excluding a common cause. A source about another bank may suggest a hypothesis while
leaving transport assumptions unresolved. These roles determine the strength with which K
can restrict the model class.


30.3     Discovery methods use language judgments in different
         ways
Three broad routes recur in the inspected literature: direct graph or relation prediction,
refinement of numerical discoveries, and priors or constraints used within a search.Wan et al.
(2024) The distinction matters because it locates where a wrong assertion enters the calculation.
   In direct conditional-independence elicitation, chatPC obtains language-model judgments
from descriptions and context. Its statistical calculation concerns the proportion of YES/NO
model responses.Cohrs et al. (2024) Repeated answers can measure response variability under
a prompt. Without a separate argument, they are not repeated draws of the bank variables
30.4. Temporal discovery is not a change of vocabulary                                       289


and do not yield a sampling test of independence in the bank population. A highly stable
wrong answer can therefore be more dangerous than a visibly variable one.
   Soft guidance provides a different failure boundary. The inspected CD-UCT method
combines language and mutual-information scores to guide graph search without excluding
otherwise valid DAGs. Language-only priors are not uniformly beneficial in its reported
comparisons.Darvariu et al. (2024) Ancestral-path constraints can likewise enter through a
soft log-prior penalty, with reported degradation under inaccurate prior information.Ban et al.
(2023) Softness leaves room for the numerical criterion to resist the suggestion, but it does not
establish that the final graph probabilities are calibrated.
   Hard restrictions can be scientifically appropriate when backed by a genuine design fact.
They are more consequential when inferred from prose: deleting a candidate model deletes
every effect value that only that model permits. Statistical Causal Prompting converts model
outputs into forced, forbidden or unknown prior knowledge using method-specific mappings.
The inspected examples include failures as well as improvements.Takayama et al. (2024) The
interface must expose both the original assertion and the conversion rule, so a reviewer can
determine whether a numerical threshold has quietly become a scientific exclusion.
   Noisy language priors can also guide a sequential allocation of questions over edges while
retaining PAG representations.Verma et al. (2025) This is closer to a budgeted information
problem than to asking for a finished graph in one prompt. Its relevance to a bank still depends
on whether the supplied knowledge applies to the observed regime, whether latent structure is
represented correctly, and whether the retained ambiguity survives into the effect query.


30.4      Temporal discovery is not a change of vocabulary
A statement that collections activity affects arrears omits the action time, available history,
response horizon and possible feedback. Expanding a variable name into a paragraph does not
supply these missing indices. A temporal graph needs explicit time labels and a rule governing
contemporaneous edges, lag limits, hidden histories, stationarity and interventions.
   RealTCD combines a language-derived initial adjacency with numerical score optimization
over temporal graphs and intervention targets. Its setup includes causal sufficiency, a known
observational regime, finite lag and a DAG on unrolled variables; its identification statement
has further stated premises. The inspected real-system assessment lacks a ground-truth DAG
and evaluates selected relationships through expert rules.Li (2024) These qualifications prevent
a graph score from being read as a general guarantee for a bank’s latent, irregularly observed
time series.
   The Large Causal Models work is an adjacent numerical foundation-model route, not
simply a conversational language-model interface. The inspected model assumes additive
noise, stationarity, no latent confounders and no contemporaneous effects, and does not detect
or correct violations of these assumptions.Kougioulis et al. (2026) Distinguishing the two
routes avoids treating the shared word “model” as a common scientific contract. One supplies
semantic proposals; the other learns a temporal mapping under a training distribution and
structural restrictions. Either can be useful within its declared regime.
   For sequential servicing, a credible workflow starts with the decision history and feasible
intervention. It then asks whether the discovery output expresses the required variables and
whether a policy effect is identified over every retained graph. An automatically generated
lagged graph cannot resolve unrecorded private information merely by assigning it a latent-node
name.
290                                                          Causal analysis for a universal bank


30.5     Interactive systems and agents add a review problem
CausalChat combines graph suggestions, user editing and numerical updates. Its small nonex-
pert study uses a fixed sequence of interfaces. Zhang (2024) Such evidence can motivate better
interfaces, but it does not isolate every learning, ordering or expertise effect. The proposed
bank evaluation needs qualified reviewers, an explicit task distribution and a comparison that
records the time and information supplied by people.
  Debating agents provide another review structure. MAC uses affirmative, negative and
judge roles; its inspected comparisons also report a competitive single-agent route for simpler
graphs at lower cost.Le et al. (2024) Several personas can share the same mistaken premise or
model knowledge. Agreement among them is not automatically independent corroboration.
Their usefulness should be measured through detected errors, retained correct alternatives,
decision consequences and total cost.
   The oci-agent study instead emphasizes an accountable human principal over actor/critic
workflows and deterministic causal libraries. Its critic can decline analyses with poor over-
lap.Chou et al. (2026) The relevant outcome then includes correct refusal and what remains
possible for the requested population. Reporting only completed analyses would hide precisely
the difficult cases in which an agent’s judgment matters most.
   An evidence-auditing agent faces a similar boundary. ARGUS audits reported support
for assumptions rather than adjudicating their truth. Its retrieval and abstention tradeoffs
and small human-label pilot leave substantial generalization questions.Zhang et al. (2026)
In banking, an omitted document, a contradicted assumption and an assumption whose
truth is unknown require different responses. A documentation score should not become an
identification certificate.


30.6     An evidence standard for the proposed banking product
The synthesis supports a modular research program. Language assistance proposes questions,
variables, graph alternatives and evidence links. Formal operations check declared structures
and calculate identified functionals or sets in supported regimes. Numerical procedures estimate
those objects with their own sampling and approximation arguments. Human and institutional
evidence supply facts about assignment, ownership and feasibility that neither interface can
manufacture.
   Each interface needs an explicit refusal or unknown state. A retrieved passage with the
wrong unit should fail target review. A graph class outside a backend’s domain should return
unsupported. A valid but uninformative effect set should remain visible. A conflict between
textual and numerical evidence should retain both sources for investigation instead of selecting
whichever yields a cleaner answer.
   CausalDS makes narrated mechanisms, observations and private scoring objects separate
parts of a benchmark, and its results distinguish symbolic answers, uncertainty, abstention
and cost.Leban and Sun (2026) The proposed evaluation adopts that separation as a design
principle. It does not borrow a published model score as evidence for the local prototype. The
next chapters develop the translation, diagram, discovery, workflow and economic consequences
of this architecture; its empirical value still requires independent mechanisms and an actual
declared backend.
30.7. From a frontier result to a banking capability                                           291


30.7      From a frontier result to a banking capability
The inspected literature gives reasons to invest in better assistance, but it does not yield a
single ranking of causal systems. A system that extracts relations from documents, a system
that answers a supplied structural-model question and a system that chooses a treatment
policy may all receive a score called causal accuracy. Their inputs, permissible assumptions
and correct outputs differ. A product proposal must recover these differences before it uses an
experimental result to select software or allocate development effort.
  For this purpose, describe an evaluation claim by

                                      E = (T , I, A, O, B, L),                              (30.1)

where T is the task distribution, I the information supplied to the system, A its scientific
assumptions, O the oracle or adjudication rule, B the tool, repair and human budget, and L
the loss used to score its output. This is a proposed comparison vocabulary, not a theorem
that these quantities are observed without error. It asks a practical question: which parts of
the published experiment would remain the same in the proposed banking use? A change in
any component requires an argument or a new experiment before the original score can carry
the same interpretation.
   For example, a graph provided in the prompt belongs to I. Correctly calculating a back-door
formula from it tests conditional reasoning. Inferring that graph from account and contact
records is a different task with different assumptions. Likewise, a human who repairs a mistaken
join changes the combined workflow’s information and cost. The repaired answer can be
valuable, but attributing its correctness entirely to the model would misdescribe the product
being evaluated. This motivates an explicit comparison of the strongest available alternatives
rather than an agent-only leaderboard.


30.7.1     Favorable and adverse results locate different opportunities

The earliest broad frontier analysis treats language models as a channel for domain knowledge
and a possible aid to graph construction, critique and robustness analysis. It also probes
memorization and prompt sensitivity. These observations motivate assistance with familiar
concepts while warning that a recognizable public dataset can supply information absent
from a fresh bank problem. Neither renaming a variable nor recalling a benchmark answer
establishes a new identification result Kıcıman et al. (2023).
   CLadder gives a more controlled formal task: generated questions from specified causal
structures with alternative verbalizations. That design isolates important distinctions among
association, intervention and counterfactual reasoning. The supplied structure and generator,
however, are part of the experimental information. A bank workflow must also determine
whether its variable, treatment and population definitions support that structure. The paper’s
remaining language-to-formal-tool problem is therefore central to the proposed product, not
an incidental user-interface issue Jin et al. (2023).
   Two comparisons show why the proposal should retain nonagent and smaller-model baselines.
In CausalEval, adding function calls improves the reported GPT-4o CLADDER point score
from 69 to 76 relative to ordinary chain-of-thought, but reduces its e-CARE score from 90 to 73.
These are outcomes from the named historical configurations and samples. They demonstrate
variation across tasks, not a general tool penalty or benefit. In the inspected relation-extraction
study, the DDI F1 values for Single-Prompt C and PubMedBERT are 67.4 and 87.9. The
task concerns binary pairwise relations and the fine-tuned system receives labeled training
examples. The result supports considering supervised extraction where the document domain
292                                                            Causal analysis for a universal bank


and annotation budget are suitable; it does not compare whole causal pipelines at equal total
cost Longxuan Yu, Delin Chen, Siheng Xiong, Qingyang Wu, Qingzhen Liu, Dawei Li, Zhikai
Chen, Xiaoze Liu and Liangming Pan (2025); Yuni Susanti and Nina Holsmoelle (2025).
   Retrieval has similarly mixed consequences. LACR combines background knowledge, docu-
ments and optional numerical information. Its ASIA skeleton F1 falls from 1 to approximately
.73 when documents are added, while other reported cases benefit. Documents can add an
applicable mechanism, introduce a conflicting definition or repeat the same unsupported
assertion. The scientific question is which information changed and why it was relevant, rather
than how many documents entered the prompt Zhang et al. (2024).
   Auditing assumptions is another promising but restricted task. ARGUS assesses the reported
support for difference-in-differences assumptions, uses injected flaws as local ground truth and
explicitly avoids adjudicating causal truth. Its five-paper human-label pilot and in-sample
calibration do not establish the error rate on a new collection of studies. A bank can use such
an assistant to find missing discussion or contradictory passages while keeping assignment,
parallel trends and measurement facts open to scientific assessment Zhang et al. (2026).
   CausalCollab makes the longitudinal issue concrete. It defines an incremental stylistic effect
in sequential human–model interactions under explicit positivity and sequential exchangeability
premises. Its intervention mixes text versions through a specified functional construction. A
proposed collections-message rewriting policy is not automatically that intervention: it must
define which actual messages are delivered, to whom, and after which history. Model-generated
counterfactual edits or outcome labels in an evaluation remain generated evidence. The
theorem’s premises, the estimator’s approximation and the operational rewriting policy must
be reviewed separately Bohan Zhang, Yixin Wang and Paramveer S. Dhillon (2024).
  These results favor a portfolio of bounded roles. Template-driven formalization, supervised
extraction, retrieved evidence, formal graph algorithms and numerical causal estimators can
each be a baseline or component. A language model is valuable where it reduces a measured
bottleneck while preserving the meaning of the task. Its presence is not a requirement for every
component. The architecture chapter develops how to enforce those boundaries in handoffs;
the question here is what evidence can justify selecting them.


30.7.2    Task composition can reverse a published ranking

Let sak be method a’s success probability on task stratum k and wk the proportion of eligible
                               P
requests in that stratum, with k wk = 1. Under a common success definition, the overall
probability is                                X
                                    Sa (w) =     wk sak .                             (30.2)
                                                 k

Even when every sak is known, ranking methods requires w. A pooled score from one benchmark
mixture is not a mixture-free property of a system. When the strata use incompatible outcomes,
they should first remain separate rather than be forced into this formula.
   As an arithmetic illustration, use the two reported CausalEval point-score pairs just discussed.
Give CLADDER weight w and e-CARE weight 1−w. The FunctionCall-minus-chain-of-thought
difference is
                            ∆(w) = .07w − .17(1 − w) = .24w − .17.                           (30.3)
It changes sign at w = 17/24 ≃ .7083. At equal weights the difference is −.05; at w = .8 it is
.022. This reweighting uses published point scores solely to illustrate composition. It supplies
neither their sampling uncertainty nor a bank’s task mix. The original paired outcomes and
mechanism-level dependence would be needed for an uncertainty calculation Longxuan Yu,
30.7. From a frontier result to a banking capability                                               293


Delin Chen, Siheng Xiong, Qingyang Wu, Qingzhen Liu, Dawei Li, Zhikai Chen, Xiaoze Liu
and Liangming Pan (2025); Causal banking proposal project (2026i).
   The same principle applies to missing tasks. If all evaluated requests assume an observed
confounder set, the experiment cannot establish performance on latent-confounding requests,
whatever their future bank frequency. If the support and weights of the intended workload are
unknown, report stratum-level results and plausible planning mixtures. A later public or bank
intake sample can estimate the mix. Changing the weighting after observing which method
wins would instead change the decision rule being evaluated.
  The task family should be the meaningful sampling unit. Paraphrases from the same
mechanism, multiple prompt seeds and repeated tool calls share information. The repeated-call
variance example in the evaluation chapter explains why their count cannot simply replace
the count of independent mechanisms. For a matched comparison, pair methods on the
same held-out mechanisms, preserve all retries and report uncertainty at the level where the
evaluation law supplies independence. No variance estimate can be recovered from a published
average alone.


30.7.3     Component correctness must compose through conditional events

Suppose a request passes five stages: correct formulation E1 , observation construction E2 ,
identification E3 , numerical execution E4 and reporting E5 . By the chain rule,
                                                                                
                                   5
                                   \                    5
                                                        Y                 \
                            P         Ej  = P (E1 )         P Ej |         Ek  .            (30.4)
                                j=1                     j=2             k<j

This identity does not require independent stages. It does require that each factor refer to the
same workflow and condition on all relevant preceding successes. Marginal accuracies reported
in five unrelated papers are not those conditional probabilities. They may concern different
data, expert information and definitions of success. Multiplying them would manufacture an
end-to-end claim from incompatible experiments.
    For an exact planning example, conditional probabilities (.96, .95, .90, .97, .98) yield .78025248.
If these numbers are instead only marginal success probabilities in a common request population,
the joint success is bounded by
                                                                   
                                       5
                                       X                       5
                                                               \
                      max0, 1 −             P (Ejc ) ≤ P         Ej  ≤ min P (Ej ),         (30.5)
                                                                               j
                                       j=1                    j=1

giving .76 to .90. The lower bound follows from the union bound for failures; the upper
follows because joint success implies every individual success. Two authored populations of
100 requests attain the endpoints. In one, failure sets of sizes 4, 5, 10, 3 and 2 are disjoint,
leaving 76 complete successes. In the other the failure sets are nested inside the ten largest
failures, leaving 90. Both have exactly the same stage marginals Causal banking proposal
project (2026i).
   For the proposal, this means stage tests diagnose where to improve, while a separate
composition test measures the completed request. A syntactically valid graph can propagate a
wrong population through every later stage. A correct estimator may precisely calculate the
wrong target. Conversely, several stages can fail on the same small subset, so adding their
failure counts overstates the number of affected requests. Record per-request transitions and
preserve the joint history needed to distinguish these cases.

30.7.4    An answer key is another measured object

Let Z be a benchmark’s recorded label, T the scientifically intended answer and Tb the system
output. For exact-match correctness,

                             1{Tb = T } − 1{Tb = Z} ≤ 1{T ̸= Z}.                           (30.6)

Whenever the label is correct, both correctness indicators are equal; otherwise their difference
is at most one. Taking expectations therefore bounds the difference between scientific accuracy
and label agreement by the answer-key error probability. If a defensible upper bound is ϵ,
reported agreement a implies only max(0, a − ϵ) ≤ P (Tb = T ) ≤ min(1, a + ϵ). This statement
assumes a meaningful common answer space; set-valued and ambiguous tasks require an
explicitly defined acceptance relation.
   With agreement .9 and a stipulated label error .1, truth accuracy can be .8 or 1 in two
simple 100-case constructions. Errors in the key can either conceal wrong outputs or penalize
correct ones. This is an exact example, not an allegation that any inspected benchmark has
a ten-percent error rate Causal banking proposal project (2026i). The practical lesson is to
audit the generator, label rule and edge cases before using a score as product evidence. An
incorrect IV-to-population-ATE oracle cannot be repaired by making an agent match that
oracle more reliably. Likewise, model-generated labels and model-generated answers can share
errors even when their agreement is high.
   For public observations without known causal truth, use the information that is actually
available: variable definitions, temporal admissibility, numerical reproduction, sensitivity to
assumptions and agreement with a justified design. Do not silently promote a published
observational point estimate into ground truth. For generated mechanisms, keep generator
truth outside the analysis interface and verify the reference calculation independently. An
intentional nonidentified case must accept appropriate refusal or a valid set, rather than reward
a precise but unjustified number.


30.7.5    Causal uncertainty matters through the decision

Return to a bank choosing an action a ∈ {0, 1}. Let V (a, M ) be its net value under causal
model M . When the evidence retains class M, one way to display the decision consequence is
regret
                         R(a, M ) = max V (b, M ) − V (a, M ).                        (30.7)
                                        b∈{0,1}

A model’s graph accuracy and its decision regret can order systems differently. An edge
irrelevant to the intervention query may contribute graph loss without changing the decision;
a single uncertain edge on the treatment-outcome path can reverse the preferred action. A
credible evaluation reports both the scientific object and the loss appropriate to the decision.
  The architecture chapter gives two Gaussian worlds with an identical observed distribution
but effects of 0 and1/2. Rescale the effect to dollars so that the two candidate gains from
acting are 0 and 500, and set action cost to 250. Not acting has value zero in both worlds.
Acting has value −250 or 250. Because the available information has the same law in both
worlds, any randomized rule acts with the same marginal probability p. Its expected regrets
are 250p and 250(1 − p), so

                               inf max{250p, 250(1 − p)} = 125.                            (30.8)
                             0≤p≤1

Equality holds at p = 1/2; either deterministic rule has worst regret 250. This restricted
two-world calculation illustrates the cost of unresolved information. It is not a recommendation
30.7. From a frontier result to a banking capability                                         295


to randomize real banking actions, and the world class and loss are authored. It explains why
a request for an informative experiment can be more valuable than another confident narrative
Causal banking proposal project (2026c,i).
   The next experiment should target information capable of distinguishing models with
different preferred actions. A public simulator can check that the proposed procedure chooses
such an experiment under known truth. Public observations can establish feasibility of a
data pipeline or stress an assumption. Neither proves that the same model class, costs or
experiment availability holds at a particular bank. Those transport questions belong to a later
study justified by the prototype’s findings.


30.7.6     A public-evidence portfolio with explicit transfer limits

An affordable portfolio follows the four banking journeys already developed. For funding,
public panel and macro records support data-clock, aggregation and reproducibility checks,
while declared generated laws supply causal truth for uncertainty tests. For servicing, a
controlled history/action generator tests positivity failures, feedback, policy definitions and
the effect of withheld state information. For discovery, known mechanisms should include
observationally equivalent graphs whose effects differ, so a confident single graph is not always
rewarded. For observation construction, public or generated documents can test extraction
and linkage while preserving the difference between a faithfully extracted assertion and a true
causal statement.
   Each journey should compare a deterministic reference, an established statistical route
and the proposed assistance where its role is relevant. Give all arms the same admissible
information and account separately for training labels, retrieval, tool use and human repair.
Freeze mechanisms, splits, budgets and scoring before final evaluation. A fixed held-out set
can be used for that registered comparison; repeated development against its answers creates
a new dependence and requires a new final evaluation design. An unavailable or malformed
answer remains in the assigned-request denominator.
   The interpretation should stay attached to the actual evidence. A document review can
justify an integration candidate. A local exact example can expose a failure mechanism. A
controlled prototype study can compare methods under its declared law. A live-model study
adds evidence about a particular model revision and task distribution. A bank study adds
evidence about the target process and its decision consequences. These are useful, different
claims; their separation allows the proposal to advance now without purchasing an expensive
experiment merely to satisfy a deployment gate.
   The current research frontier therefore supports a concrete proposal: build typed formulation
and evidence assistance around an auditable causal core; retain supervised, deterministic
and formal alternatives; measure composition and review costs; and direct new information
acquisition toward consequential ambiguity. It leaves open the reliability of language-mediated
assumptions, performance outside benchmark support, annotation validity and the economics
of sustained human review. Those are falsifiable next questions. A count of papers, agents or
completed reports does not answer them.
Chapter 31

Translating a banking decision into a
causal question

31.1      A business sentence can contain several questions
“Should we increase the deposit offer?” sounds like a single question, but it leaves several
choices unresolved. The intended action could be a change in the quoted rate, the eligibility
rule, the message shown to a customer or the allocation of a fixed promotional budget. The
outcome could be a new deposit, retained balances, funding cost or total relationship value.
The population could be existing customers, applicants who received an offer or everyone
eligible under a proposed rule. Each choice defines a different causal problem.
   A language assistant can expose these alternatives and organize the evidence needed to
resolve them. It should not choose the easiest target to estimate and silently treat that target
as the owner’s decision. In the project funding case, the response of balances to a 25-basis-point
increase and the change in net funding cost over thirty days are retained as separate candidates.
Their business motivation is shared; their outcomes and decision consequences are not identical.
The unresolved choice is useful information, not a failure that must be hidden by returning a
number.
   The co-pilot roadmap discussed by Alaa and colleagues motivates this progression from a
scientific question through assumptions, statistical targets and interpretation. Their illustrative
medical examples attend to eligibility, baseline time, treatment and follow-up. The inspected
paper also reports that generic uncued answers can omit relevant design concerns. Applying
those principles to banking is a project proposal; the medical examples do not validate banking
clocks or interventions.Alaa et al. (2024)


31.2      A question as a collection of commitments
The project represents a question as

                                Q = (U, P, A, π, π0 , Y, H, ν, ℓ, I).                        (31.1)

Here U is the unit of analysis; P is the target population; A is the feasible action set; π and
π0 are the policy and comparator; Y is the outcome; H is the horizon; ν is the measure used
to average over the population; ℓ is the loss, including its units; and I specifies information
available at each action. This notation defines the project’s declaration contract. It is not an
identification theorem.

                                                296
31.3. Changing a population measure changes the answer                                        297


   The unit needs particular care. An account can be an observation while a customer is the
decision unit and a household is the unit within which actions interact. An assistant can ask
which role each identifier plays, but a column called customer ID does not certify ownership or
stable linkage. If several accounts share a budget or pricing rule, an account-level action may
also be an infeasible description of the intervention. The feasible action set should reflect what
the responsible institution can actually change.
   The comparator must be as explicit as the intervention. “No treatment” might mean no
new contact, continuation of the current contact policy, no rate increase, or a different offer
under a fixed budget. A dynamic policy can include future actions conditional on history, so
its comparator is also a history-dependent rule. An effect relative to one comparator cannot
be reused for another solely because the same treatment variable appears in the dataset.
  The outcome and loss should also remain separate. A change in balances has units of
currency held over a horizon; funding expense combines balances, rates and time. A larger
deposit balance can have a positive acquisition interpretation and an unfavorable net-cost
implication. If g(a) is a specified gross benefit and c(a) is a specified cost, the decision may
depend on E[g(a) − c(a)], not on E[g(a)] alone. The definitions and valuation assumptions
must be supplied before that subtraction is meaningful. The assistant should make missing
costs visible rather than invent prices.


31.3      Changing a population measure changes the answer
Let X denote baseline features and let τ (x) = E[Y (1) − Y (0) | X = x]. A weighted target can
be written
                                 E[w(X)τ (X)]
                           θw =                ,     E[w(X)] > 0.                       (31.2)
                                   E[w(X)]
Uniform, treated-population, overlap and trimmed targets use different weights. Under the
conditions that make a propensity e(x) = Pr(A = 1 | X = x) appropriate for the intended
population, familiar choices are 1, e(x), e(x)(1 − e(x)) and 1{a ≤ e(x) ≤ b}, respectively.
The formula records which average is wanted. It does not establish exchangeability, support,
estimation rates or coverage.
  An exact project example makes the distinction visible. Let two strata have equal population
probability, with propensities 0.2 and 0.5, and effects 0 and 10. Trimming to [0.1, 0.9] keeps
both strata, so the trimmed-population effect is 5. Overlap weights are 0.16 and 0.25, giving
                                   0.16(0) + 0.25(10)   250
                      θoverlap =                      =     = 6.09756 . . . .
                                       0.16 + 0.25      41
Both calculations can be exact and still answer different questions. A label such as “overlap
population” is insufficient if its underlying weighting rule is not retained.
   This issue is directly relevant to the inspected OCI agent paper. Chou and colleagues
describe a principal/actor/critic workflow, reproducible notebooks, point-in-time estimation
and overlap diagnostics. The inspected trimming passage uses a target label that must be
reconciled with the actual weighting rule before mapping it to conventional overlap weighting.
The proposed architecture is informative, but an assistant should not inherit a target label
without checking its definition.Chou et al. (2026)
   Changing the target to remove unsupported accounts can be scientifically reasonable, but it
is a new decision question. A bank owner may care about precisely those accounts for which
treatment support is weak. An honest report can say that a narrower target is estimable under
the supplied assumptions while the original target remains unresolved. It should show the
excluded population, the new averaging rule and the implications for the decision.

31.4     Information is governed by an availability clock
The date on which an event occurred differs from the date on which an analyst or policy could
observe it. For a recorded variable V , write eV for event time and aV for availability time.
The finite project fixtures require eV ≤ aV , and a policy acting at time t can use the value
only if aV ≤ t. A derived feature becomes available no earlier than its required inputs. These
rules prevent an apparently historical feature from leaking future information into a decision.
   In the servicing fixture, an account condition occurs at day ten but becomes available
at day eleven. A rule acting on day eleven may use it; a rule acting on day ten may not.
The distinction matters even when both values later appear in the same warehouse table. A
language assistant should request the recording and availability convention, rather than infer
it from a field name or a sorted timestamp.
   Advance announcements and forecasts require different variable definitions. A forecast
observed today of next month’s condition is a current forecast variable, not a measurement of a
future realized condition with an impossible availability time. Revised historical data similarly
require a vintage or revision convention. The project’s finite validator does not implement
every revision protocol. It checks the stated recorded-value contract and leaves more complex
clocks as explicit extensions.
  Equal timestamps do not determine direction. Two columns aggregated to the same day
may hide a finer action sequence or a common cause. The assistant can propose a finer clock
and identify the evidence needed to support it. It cannot establish temporal precedence by
placing one variable first in a diagram. When the granularity is insufficient, the ambiguity
should survive into the model class.


31.5     An available covariate is not automatically an adjustment
         variable
In a sequential servicing model, A0 changes an intermediate condition L1 , which affects both
a later action A1 and the outcome Y . The same L1 is a mediator for the first action and a
common cause of the second action–outcome relation. Its appropriate use depends on the
target. Including every available column in one regression does not preserve all possible total,
direct and policy effects.
   The project declaration therefore distinguishes a policy-history purpose from an ordinary
adjustment purpose. A simple directed-path diagnostic flags a post-treatment descendant
proposed as an ordinary total-effect control. It does not declare all post-treatment conditioning
invalid. Controlled direct effects and longitudinal procedures need their own question and
formal analysis. A warning from a declaration validator is not a replacement for an adjustment
criterion or an identification algorithm.
   Observation processes can alter the target in a similar way. Suppose only successfully
linked records enter an analysis and both action and repayment affect successful linkage. The
selection indicator is part of the causal problem, and an effect among linked records may differ
from an effect in the original population. A record-link score is an observed proxy; it is not
verified ownership. The observation fixture deliberately retains a latent ownership variable, a
selection node and an unresolved population choice.
  CausalDS provides a useful literature distinction here: its conceptual SCM variables and its
separate observation model are not interchangeable. The paper’s narrated synthetic scenes
can test how an agent handles that distinction, but they do not supply authentic banking
31.6. The handoff to formal analysis                                                          299


semantic or assignment truth.Leban and Sun (2026)


31.6      The handoff to formal analysis
The assistant’s useful output is a reviewable declaration and a record of what remains unresolved.
A selected declaration contains one explicit target, its population measure, the intervention
and comparator, clocks, feasible actions, outcome and loss. An ambiguous declaration retains
candidate targets without covertly selecting one. A contradicted assumption cannot be left as
an inconsequential note while the calculation proceeds as if it held.
  The local project validator exercises these distinctions with four synthetic banking cases and
adverse contract tests. It checks declared identities, types, references and selected clock/graph
conditions. It does not authenticate an institution, certify a reviewer, determine whether a
causal assumption is true, or implement every MAG/PAG/CPDAG validity condition. A
declaration ready for formal analysis is ready for the next conditional operation, not a qualified
bank recommendation.
   This boundary also explains the limited scope of the current executable prototype. A
declaration can describe a dynamic regime while the selected operation supports only a
static binary population ATE. The correct handoff then reports unsupported target mapping.
Translating that request into a static regression would produce a result at the cost of changing
the user’s question. The appropriate remedy is to qualify a longitudinal operation or obtain
an explicit new target decision, with the original question preserved.


31.7      A complete translation example: the incentive question
Suppose a manager asks an agent to “find the incentive uplift and choose the best offer.” The
sentence leaves at least three mathematical objects open: a binary offer effect, a continuous
local slope, and a finite-dose policy value. The agent can help by presenting these alternatives
with their populations, units and action constraints. It should not select whichever object
happens to be exposed by the first available package.
   Let A be incentive intensity in a declared unit and let Y be retained net value over a fixed
horizon. The finite question is ∆(a1 , a0 ) = E{Y (a1 ) − Y (a0 )}. A local derivative, where
it exists, is µ′ (a). A covariance slope averages features of the response under an exposure
distribution and need not equal either object. The inspected grf and dose-response interfaces
make this a practical interoperability issue, not merely a linguistic distinction.grf project
(2026b); causaldrf project (2026b)
   For the stipulated curve µ(a) = 20a − 3a2 , a uniform exposure on [0, 2] gives covariance
slope 14, while moving from dose one to dose two changes the mean by 11 CNY. An agent
that labels 14 as the value of the specified change has mistranslated the problem even if it
calls its numerical tool correctly. The exact project calculation makes the error detectable
without a live model experiment.Causal banking research project (2026as)
   A useful translation record would therefore state: eligible existing customers; the information
available before the offer; current dose one and feasible dose two; a fixed retention horizon;
treatment and outcome currency units; and whether incentive expense is already included
in Y . If expense is excluded, the decision value is ∆(a1 , a0 ) − {c(a1 ) − c(a0 )}. Subtracting
it again when Y already measures net value would double-count cost. The record also needs
account closure/default definitions and a sampling unit for uncertainty.
  The agent’s role can be useful at each handoff. It can flag unspecified units, find source
300                                                            Causal analysis for a universal bank


definitions, propose alternative causal questions and generate typed requests. Formal checks
can verify that a numerical result matches the declared query. Domain owners must still
confirm the feasible intervention and measurement meanings; neither fluent prose nor a schema
establishes them.


31.8      A servicing policy is a rule with an information boundary
For sequential servicing, an action rule uses Ht , the information actually available at decision
time. A data field recorded later may describe an earlier event while remaining unavailable
to the operating policy. An agent assembling history features must preserve both event and
availability times. Otherwise the proposed policy uses information the bank would not possess
when acting.
   The causal query should distinguish evaluating a specified rule, choosing among rules and
claiming an optimal hidden-state policy. A longitudinal simulator can evaluate supplied regimes
under its assumptions. Its ability to accept a custom history function does not identify private
customer states or make an unknown logger known. The inspected pygformula class exposes
useful histories, event and regime options, but its source interface alone establishes neither
policy optimality nor uncertainty under arbitrary dependence.pygformula project (2026b)
   A concrete policy-selection hazard can be shown without an asymptotic argument. Suppose
two equally valuable policies each have independent evaluation error equal to minus one or
plus one with equal probability. The maximum of the two errors is minus one only when both
are minus one, and plus one otherwise. Its expectation is therefore 34 − 41 = 12 . Reporting the
selected policy’s same-data evaluation is optimistic. If the selected policy is evaluated with a
fresh independent error of mean zero, the evaluation error has mean zero conditional on the
selection. Exact enumeration verifies both claims.Causal banking research project (2026as)
   This example does not prove that a particular split is sufficient for a dependent servicing
panel. It explains why the selection and evaluation laws must be specified. An agent can
preserve the split, freeze candidate rules and refuse reuse of a held-out set for tuning. A
scientific argument must still justify independence or the required dependence control. Training
a policy and then narrating its favorable development score is not an independent evaluation.


31.9      Translation outputs that deserve abstention
Some business questions should produce a request for more information or a set of alternatives.
If “the customer” may mean the legal entity, the beneficial owner or a linked household,
choosing one silently changes both the population and interference structure. If the intended
action is not operationally feasible, the mathematically optimal action is irrelevant. If the loss
function and costs are unknown, the agent can compare statistical targets but cannot assert
an investment recommendation.
   Abstention should be specific. It should identify the missing definition, record the alternative
interpretations and explain which downstream operation depends on the answer. That is
different from a generic refusal to analyze. For an incentive query, the missing item may be
treatment units or whether cost is already included. For servicing it may be the information
clock or the policy class. For interference it may be network direction or the allocation policy.
These are concrete commitments that owners can resolve and numerical tools can then preserve.
31.10. A formulation workflow that preserves unresolved alternatives                          301


31.10      A formulation workflow that preserves unresolved alter-
           natives
A language model can make a business question more precise by exposing the decisions that its
wording leaves open. Its useful output is a set of explicit candidate questions, with evidence
for their variables and clocks, followed by a reasoned choice of a supported analysis. Fluency
alone does not determine which candidate the bank intended. A formal causal engine also
cannot repair a mistake that was made before the graph, intervention and target reached the
engine.
   Consider a manager who asks, “Which customers should receive a retention invitation next
month, and how much value will it create?” One interpretation is the effect of offering the
invitation to every currently eligible customer. Another is the effect among customers who
historically received it. A third is the value of a targeting rule under a fixed contact budget.
The first two are averages over different populations. The third also requires a feasible policy
class, the information available when the rule acts, a comparator policy and a cost definition.
A model that estimates historical recipients’ average effect and calls it the expected value of
the new targeting rule has changed the question.
   The formulation record should therefore contain the eligible population and exclusions,
the sampling unit, invitation and comparator, actual receipt if distinct, the decision time,
permissible information, outcome horizon, monetary units and accounting treatment of contact
cost. It should distinguish invitation from successful contact and from subsequent product use.
Those variables may be causally related, but they are different interventions. It should also
retain alternatives that remain unresolved: all eligible customers versus historical recipients, a
single action versus a sequence, and gross revenue versus net value.
  For a binary invitation A, a baseline record W available at time zero, and a fixed-horizon
outcome Y , an initial target may be

                                     ψ = Eν {Y (1) − Y (0)},

  where ν names the eligible population. The adjustment expression
                  Z
             ψ=       {m1 (w) − m0 (w)} dν(w),      ma (w) = E[Y | A = a, W = w],

   requires consistency, conditional exchangeability, positivity, suitable sampling and the
declared interference restriction. The model may help elicit and document those assumptions.
It cannot infer their truth from a plausible explanation or from a successful estimator call. In a
generated development example, the project can stipulate and inspect the complete assignment
law. In a later bank application, the assignment mechanism and measurement meanings need
accountable scientific ownership.


31.10.1     What the frontier evidence supports

The knowledge-assisted perspective of Kıcıman and colleagues motivates graph drafts, critique
and connections to formal tools. Its own memorization probes and discussion of novel scenarios
limit what benchmark success establishes. The inspected original distinguishes knowledge-
based graph generation from conventional discovery from observations. For this proposal, a
directional suggestion is a hypothesis with source provenance, not a discovered bank fact. A
model can suggest that financial distress confounds retention contact and subsequent deposits;
302                                                           Causal analysis for a universal bank


the analysis still needs to determine what was measured, when staff observed it and how it
affected assignment. (Kıcıman et al., 2023)
   The medical co-pilot proposal develops a causal roadmap from a scientific question through
study design and interpretation. Its examples of prevalent versus incident users are directly
relevant to the distinction between existing account holders and newly eligible customers. That
transfer is a project design proposal, not evidence that a medical demonstration validates
banking workflows. The paper’s evaluation discussion also makes clear that medical question-
answering ability and causal study-design quality are different evaluation targets. Carefully
cued illustrative responses do not establish reliable autonomous formulation. (Alaa et al.,
2024)
  CLadder provides formally generated causal questions and explicitly separates levels of
causal reasoning. Its results and limitations support using a formal reference to evaluate
whether verbalized information was translated into the right query. Binary answer accuracy
on its selected query families does not measure effect calibration, correct bank populations or
decision loss. The paper also identifies the language-to-formal-tool interface as a remaining
problem. The proposed baseline therefore checks the structured query before it scores a
numerical answer. (Jin et al., 2023)
   The 2026 CausalDS paper adds narrated synthetic structural models, data files, an observa-
tion layer and separate private scoring information. It distinguishes the conceptual variables
used for identification from their noisy observed proxies. Its reported results separate symbolic
reasoning, estimation, interval quality, abstention and tool cost. This is useful evidence for a
multidimensional evaluation: correctly extracting a story’s graph does not guarantee that the
observed data identify or precisely estimate the stated effect. The paper’s historical model
results are author-reported; they have not been reproduced in this project. (Leban and Sun,
2026)
   The 2026 observational causal-inference agent paper provides a concrete principal, actor and
critic workflow built around deterministic analysis tools and reproducible notebooks. It reports
favorable comparisons under its evaluated settings, while its disguised observational-study
examples retain important overlap-related refusals. This supports investigating constrained
analytical workflows with explicit diagnostics. It does not establish unmeasured-confounding
control, longitudinal-policy identification or valid conditional coverage after the critic selects
which estimates to report. Its point-in-time scope must survive transfer to the banking proposal.
(Chou et al., 2026)
   Two additional primary studies sharpen the boundary between an effective workflow and
causal truth. Sng and colleagues study inconsistencies in causal-edge ratings and compare
retrieval augmentation with a debate-and-arbiter design. Their retrieval experiment supplies a
mocked true causal graph. The authors explicitly state that reduced inconsistency does not
imply accurate causal prediction and call for true-graph validation. The title’s language about
eliminating hallucinations should therefore not become a guarantee in this product proposal.
Consistent agents can agree on an incorrect edge, and a retrieval corpus can encode the same
incorrect premise. (Grace Sng, Yanming Zhang and Klaus Mueller, 2024)
   CausalPulse describes query planning, semantic descriptions, process constraints, agent cards
and MCP/A2A coordination for manufacturing diagnostics. Its reported operational success is
a useful architecture comparison. The paper separately reports root-cause attribution, with a
PSE Hits@1 of 0.44 and F1 of 0.39, using annotations of variables that changed at the anomaly
time. Such annotations and tool-invocation success are different from interventional causal
truth. The paper’s local timing setup and manufacturing deployment discussion likewise do
not establish banking runtime or treatment-effect performance. We can adapt its separation
of semantic services, deterministic tools and workflow state as a design pattern while retaining
31.10. A formulation workflow that preserves unresolved alternatives                          303


those scientific limits. (Chathurangi Shyalika, Utkarshani Jaimini, Cory Henson and Amit
Sheth, 2026)
   These studies suggest complementary roles: retrieve definitions, draft alternatives, check
logical consistency, construct typed calls, retain execution artifacts and explain formal results.
The adverse findings point to the same missing link: a linguistic interpretation must be checked
against the intended population, intervention, measurement model and information clock.
An additional critic can help find mistakes, but agreement between related models is not
independent validation of an assumption.


31.10.2     A worked failure: an overlap remedy changes the population

Suppose the bank initially asks for the average invitation effect among all eligible customers.
A diagnostic finds weak overlap for one customer stratum. An agent proposes trimming that
stratum and continues to report the result as if it answered the original question. Even with
perfect estimation, that continuation can be wrong.
   To isolate the target issue, stipulate a three-stratum population with known masses, propen-
sities and conditional effects. These are generated numerical assumptions; the units of the
conditional effect are thousands of currency units per customer.

               Population mass p(w), invitation propensity

0              0.5, 0.05                                         0
1              0.3, 0.50                                         2
2              0.2, 0.80                                         8


   The full-population ATE is 0.5(0) + 0.3(2) + 0.2(8) = 2.2. Trimming to true propensities in
[0.1, 0.9] retains half the population and gives 2.2/0.5 = 4.4. The conventional overlap-weighted
target instead uses the measure proportional to p(w)e(w){1 − e(w)}:

                           w p(w)e(w){1 − e(w)}τ (w)

   The effect among treated customers is different again: ψATT = 316/67 ≃ 4.7164. Exact
