or a live language model. Their disagreement arises entirely from the population measure.
(Causal banking research project, 2026h)
   This distinction is visible in a real proposed reuse path. The inspected oci-agent notebook
applies a propensity-based keep mask and averages AIPW pseudo-outcomes over that subset
while labeling the output “ATO.” The accompanying paper describes the trimming remedy in
the same terminology. A hard-trimmed average and an e(W ){1−e(W )}-weighted overlap effect
are not generally equal. The integration must either label the result as a trimmed-population
ATE, with its actual eligibility rule, or implement and validate the intended weighting operation.
It must also retain the original all-eligible request and the excluded population. Estimated
propensities add randomness to selection; the simple known-law calculation above does not
validate that further inference step. (oci-agent contributors, 2026; Chou et al., 2026)
   The correct translation response is therefore a revised analysis proposal: the original target
is unresolved under the current information or diagnostics; a specified restricted-population
target may be feasible; and the bank must assess whether that restricted target still informs its
decision. In a public or generated prototype, this branch can be evaluated without bank data
304                                                           Causal analysis for a universal bank


by stipulating both populations and checking that the system preserves their difference. It is
not necessary to obtain expensive authentic evidence merely to detect a target substitution.


31.10.3    Concrete package choices and the formal baseline

The inspected pywhy-llm path is a candidate for eliciting hypotheses and candidate variables. Its
IdentificationSuggester.suggest_backdoor delegates to a language-model confounder sug-
gester. That class’s front-door method is a stub, whereas SimpleIdentificationSuggester
has a front-door method that generates text suggestions. Neither fact establishes a formal
identification algorithm. The proposal should reuse the suggestion pattern selectively and
send the resulting explicit graph and query to a separately admitted causal engine. It should
preserve cited source passages and unresolved alternatives instead of interpreting a generated
factor list as an approved adjustment set. (pywhy-llm contributors, 2026)
   For oci-agent, the useful candidate is the separation of a specification, a deterministic
analysis notebook and a critic report. The selected source has a general notebook runner and
a target-label issue requiring correction. A bounded banking interface should expose fixed
reviewed operations with resource limits and typed outputs. The proposal does not adopt a
general notebook executor as the causal MCP surface. Dependency resolution, failure handling
and executable parity remain separate implementation tasks; the source’s research status is
not a reason to infer a deployed bank service. (oci-agent contributors, 2026)
   CausalDS is a candidate for generated scene and task design, but its grader needs a semantic
review before direct adoption. The inspected identification/scoring helpers distinguish several
genuine states, yet some missing metadata defaults and finite-interval checks require attention.
Unknown identification due to a missing backend is not scientific nonidentification. A malformed
answer is not a justified abstention. A capped score can conceal severe tail losses unless the
uncapped losses and coverage are also reported. The proposal therefore takes the task separation
and private-reference design while requiring explicit metadata and failure validation. (causalds
contributors, 2026)
   The deterministic formulation baseline has three layers. A schema check verifies that
population, unit, intervention, comparator, horizon, clock and scale are present. A semantic
check compares these fields with the supplied brief and dictionary: a post-contact duration
cannot become a pre-contact covariate, an invitation cannot silently become actual uptake, and
a requested all-eligible effect cannot become a recipients-only effect. A formal check evaluates
identification under the explicitly supplied candidate graph and returns an expression, model-
relative nonidentification, unsupported scope or an unresolved input. These checks validate
different things. A well-formed schema does not prove the story is true, and a correctly
evaluated graph does not prove its edges.
   For a generated benchmark, the reference can enumerate a finite set of admissible formu-
lations Q(b) for brief b. An explicitly resolved brief may have one acceptable target. An
ambiguous brief may have several and require the system to request or retain the missing
distinction. A baseline can return those alternatives directly from the supplied reference
fields and use exact calculations such as the example above. This establishes a transparent
lower-cost comparator and exposes what a language model is expected to add: interpretation
of unstructured language, evidence retrieval and useful clarification, rather than numerical
work already handled by a deterministic engine.
31.10. A formulation workflow that preserves unresolved alternatives                           305


31.10.4     Evaluation before a costly bank study

The initial evaluation can use public data dictionaries and openly documented financial
examples alongside generated causal mechanisms. Public data support questions about
available variables and clocks; they usually do not supply intervention truth. Generated
mechanisms can supply that truth for the declared model. A reference author should create
matched examples that vary one decisive feature: invitation versus uptake, all eligible versus
treated population, pre-decision versus post-decision measurement, complete variables versus
noisy proxies, or a single action versus repeated treatment. The target-change example supplies
one exact reference family. This is a proposed evaluation design; it is not a reported live-agent
comparison.
   Train/development and final evaluation should be split by the underlying scenario or
structural model, not merely by paraphrases of the same question. Otherwise a system can
learn the reference target from exposed near-duplicates. All requests should remain in the
evaluation denominator, including ambiguous requests, timeouts, unsupported estimands,
malformed answers and justified nonidentification. Report target and clock fidelity, unjustified
resolution of ambiguity, false causal answers, valid abstention, numerical error where a target
is actually identified, interval availability and coverage where ground truth permits them, and
total resource use. A high completion rate alone rewards an agent for confidently answering
questions that should remain unresolved.
   Retrieval, structured prompting and an actor/critic loop should be compared against the
same deterministic baseline and fixed task families. A retrieval ablation tests whether source
passages improve interpretation. A critic ablation tests whether additional review catches errors,
while reporting the added calls, time and newly introduced mistakes. A graph-perturbation
comparison tests whether a system notices that an assumption changed. Repeated runs
reveal stability. These studies need their actual model, tool, prompt, data and stopping-rule
identities frozen before final evaluation. Agreement across repeated runs is useful evidence
about stability; it is not evidence that the agreed answer is causally correct.
   Several gaps remain scientific. A general method for recovering stakeholder intent from
incomplete language is not established. The immediate remedy is to preserve admissible
alternatives and make the missing decision explicit. A general guarantee that retrieval or
debate validates causal edges is also absent; the current studies justify investigating those tools
with factual and graph-specific references, not treating consensus as truth. Identification from
noisy proxies, dependent observations or repeated interventions requires the corresponding
statistical model and method. Finally, whether an assisted workflow saves bank analyst time
or changes an investment decision requires a later workflow study after a bounded prototype
shows merit. Those gaps narrow the claims and motivate specific experiments; they do not
prevent writing or testing the proposal’s public/generated formulation contract.


31.10.5     Text measurement must preserve the causal question

A servicing analyst may ask an assistant to extract financial distress from call notes and then
adjust for the extracted score when comparing repayment plans. This can be useful work.
It also combines three different claims: that the score measures distress, that the note was
available before the plan decision, and that conditioning on the score removes the relevant
confounding. An accurate summary of the note establishes none of the latter two claims. A
later note may describe a reaction to the plan; a note written only after a complaint may select
on both treatment and outcome. The proposed formulation interface must attach a time and a
measurement interpretation to each extracted variable before adding it to an adjustment set.
306                                                           Causal analysis for a universal bank


   Keith, Jensen and O’Connor review text used to measure otherwise unobserved confounders.
Their discussion explicitly distinguishes confounders, colliders and mediators and asks whether
one document can encode several of these at once. It also identifies error in measured con-
founders as an unresolved problem. A richer language representation can improve measurement,
but the review provides no guarantee that a representation eliminates confounding. The appro-
priate comparison therefore includes simple dictionaries, supervised extractors, human-coded
measurements and a language model, with the same permitted document dates and the same
effect target. Katherine A. Keith, David Jensen and Brendan O’Connor (2020)


A reproducible example of residual confounding

Consider the following project-generated population model. The intervention intensity A and
later loss Y are standardized continuous quantities; these are illustrative units, not calibrated
bank measurements. True predecision distress is U , while W is an imperfect score extracted
from a predecision note:

                   A = U + εA ,       W = U + εW ,       Y = τ A + U + εY .

   All four disturbances are mutually independent and centered Gaussian. The variances
of U, εA , εY are one, while Var(εW ) = s ≥ 0. The true effect of increasing A by one is τ .
Conditional on W , the residual variance of U is v = s/(1 + s). Residualizing both A and Y on
W therefore gives the population regression coefficient

                                             v         s
                               βA|W = τ +       =τ+        .
                                            1+v     1 + 2s
   The second term persists with an infinite sample. It is not estimation noise that a larger
language model, an accurate propensity fit to W , or a narrower regression interval automatically
removes. With the stipulated τ = −1/5, exact covariance calculations give the following values.

          Text-score noise variance s True effect Adjusted population coefficient
          0                             −1/5         −1/5
          1/4                           −1/5         −1/30
          1                             −1/5         2/15
          4                             −1/5         11/45


   The score with s = 1 leaves enough confounding to reverse the sign. This example is
independently reproduced by solving the population covariance normal equations and by
residual variance decomposition. It demonstrates a specific failure mechanism under a stated
law, not a claim that all text adjustment fails. A successful extraction study must measure the
relevant error and evaluate how it affects the causal target. If a proxy-correction method is
proposed, its additional measurement assumptions and available validation information must
be stated rather than inferred from predictive accuracy.


Freeze the measurement rule before evaluating its effects

Egami and colleagues make the measurement rule itself explicit. Let g map a document into a
category or vector. For a textual outcome, E[g(Y (1)) − g(Y (0))] is a target defined by that
particular rule. Searching over rules using the same treatment assignments and documents later
used for effect estimation can induce dependence and select apparent effects. Their proposed
31.10. A formulation workflow that preserves unresolved alternatives                           307


separation of codebook discovery from effect estimation addresses that problem, while their
text-as-treatment discussion imposes a further sufficiency restriction on the representation.
Naoki Egami, Christian J. Fong, Justin Grimmer, Margaret E. Roberts and Brandon M.
Stewart (2018)
   For a language-based measurement pipeline, the rule includes the model version, prompt,
retrieval corpus, preprocessing, extraction schema and response aggregation. Freezing only a
classifier filename while changing the prompt after reading the effect estimates does not freeze
g. The prototype should develop the rule on a designated development set, record its identity,
and evaluate it on held-out units. If several calls concern one customer or conversation, those
calls should remain together in the split. This is a proposed implementation of the separation
principle, not a claim that sample splitting alone ensures valid inference for dependent histories.
   The held-out review asks whether the labels retain their intended meaning, whether extrac-
tion errors differ by treatment and outcome, and whether missing documents have a defensible
observation model. It must preserve negative findings. Rewriting the measurement rule to
rescue a disappointing effect requires a new evaluation set or an explicitly exploratory analysis.
Neither a fixed rule nor a held-out set supplies unmeasured assignment information or repairs
a post-treatment adjustment error.


Formulate competing explanations before selecting a diagram

Geraldo Bastías proposes building diagrams from the assumptions actually used in a study,
preserving several models where the assumptions do not determine one. His workflow checks
identification within each model, derives observable implications, and distinguishes missing
relationships from missing variables. This is a methodological contribution to diagram review,
not an implemented LLM discovery algorithm. It supports an assistant that makes assumptions
inspectable rather than treating a familiar design label as sufficient. Pablo Geraldo Bastías
(2024)
   For the servicing example, a short initial brief can leave open whether distress caused
the plan assignment, whether a later complaint caused a note to be recorded, and whether
the proposed outcome is arrears, loss or customer welfare. The assistant should construct
separate compatible diagrams and show how each changes adjustment or identification. It
can check timing contradictions and derive conditional-independence implications. Passing
those checks does not establish that an omitted common cause is absent. Where the diagrams
imply different effects, the useful output is the unresolved choice and the evidence that could
distinguish it.
   These requirements permit immediate public and generated evaluation. A public document
corpus can supply realistic language, while a declared generator supplies assignment, document
timing, measurement error and outcome truth. Simple extraction and fixed numerical workflows
provide baselines. The evaluation must vary mechanisms that are difficult for the chosen
extractor, including selective note availability and notes written after treatment. Keith and
colleagues specifically caution that authors can choose semi-synthetic confounders their own
method can easily recover. Freezing adverse mechanisms and separating their construction
from final method selection addresses that concern more directly than adding familiar domain
vocabulary to a favorable simulation. Katherine A. Keith, David Jensen and Brendan O’Connor
(2020)

Variables, diagrams and justified
disagreement

32.1     From vocabulary to measured variables
A useful causal diagram begins with variables whose meanings can survive contact with data.
A business glossary may contain “risk,” “relationship” and “engagement,” while a dataset
contains a risk-score vintage, a set of linked accounts and an observed click. Those are related
concepts, but they are not interchangeable causal variables. An assistant can propose mappings,
detect inconsistent names and assemble definitions. Each proposed mapping still needs an
operational meaning, a unit and an information clock.
   OntoLearner offers relevant modular ideas for ontology loading, typing, taxonomy and
relation-learning tasks. The inspected paper reports domain-dependent errors and retrieval
failures. Its relation-learning capability is not a guarantee that a relation is causal, or that a
concept has a valid measured proxy in the bank. Ontology alignment should therefore precede
and inform graph construction without being silently promoted into causal identification.Giglou
et al. (2026)
   For example, “customer owns account” may describe a legal relation, “records share an
identifier” an administrative relation, and “records have a high linkage score” a model output.
If ownership affects both offer eligibility and repayment behavior, substituting the linkage score
for ownership leaves a measurement problem. Adding an arrow from the score to repayment
does not resolve it. The diagram should distinguish latent ownership, observed records, the
linkage procedure and sample selection.
   Likewise, an ordinal description such as “high influence” cannot be used as an effect size
without a scale. An assistant’s rating of a proposed edge may express a preference among
textual explanations. It is not automatically a probability that the edge is present, a posterior
over graphs, or a confidence level. A typed diagram can retain such a rating as explicitly
uncalibrated metadata while refusing to use it as scientific evidence.


32.2     What an edge asserts
An edge proposal should state more than two variable names. The endpoint marks identify the
proposed graphical object. A source and inspected anchor state what supports the proposal.
A scope describes the population, period and intervention to which that evidence applies. A
counterevidence record states whether contrary evidence was found, absent in the inspected


                                               308
32.3. Graph classes and collections of candidate models                                     309


material, or not successfully searched. A review disposition records acceptance as a premise,
rejection, or unresolved status.
   These fields serve different purposes. A source can be authentic but inapplicable to the
current banking action. A study can concern a different population or a different definition of
treatment. A plausible timing argument can constrain direction without establishing that any
causal connection exists. The assistant should make the supported proposition as narrow as
the evidence warrants and retain the reasons for disagreement.
   CausalChat supplies an example of interactive model development: the inspected paper
combines optional CPDAG discovery, model suggestions, graph editing and structural-equation
coefficient updates. Its prompts use ordinal causal-significance ratings and ask for possible
confounders and mediators. These are useful interaction ideas. The paper’s expert feedback
also raises missing citations and uncertainty about the quality of scientific evidence provided
by the model. A coefficient update after adding an edge cannot establish that the edge itself
is true.Zhang (2024)
   The proposed banking workflow retains the interaction but changes the scientific handoff.
An accepted premise is labeled as a premise with a responsible review, not as a truth certified
by the model. A model proposal alone cannot remove an observationally compatible graph
alternative. The tool responsible for formal identification receives the complete reviewed graph
object and its restrictions, rather than a picture whose uncertainty has disappeared in editing.


32.3      Graph classes and collections of candidate models
A CPDAG or PAG is a structured representation with its own interpretation. A list of proposed
DAGs is another object. A collection of edges marked “possible” is not automatically an
enumeration of every combination of those edges. Confusing these representations can silently
exclude models or include incompatible ones.
   The project contract preserves a CPDAG or PAG directly when that is the appropriate
object, including circle endpoints. It also permits explicitly listed candidate models. An
edge marked possible within a candidate describes the evidence status of that candidate’s
edge; it does not make all optional edge combinations an exhaustive graph class. Downstream
calculations must know which interpretation applies.
   An exact binary example shows the consequence of retaining alternatives. In model F , a
binary offer A is Bernoulli with probability one half, and response Y equals A with probability
0.9. In model R, Y is Bernoulli with probability one half, and A equals Y with probability
0.9. Both models produce
                                             Y =0 Y =1
                                    A = 0 9/20         1/20 .
                                    A = 1 1/20         9/20
In F , setting A from zero to one changes E[Y ] by 0.8. In R, intervening on the equation for A
leaves Y unchanged. The two compatible constructions therefore imply the effect candidates
{0, 0.8}. A directional suggestion favoring F does not provide new identifying information
unless its underlying premise is independently justified. These finite calculations are project
constructions, not a calibrated confidence set for a learned graph.
  More generally, for a declared graph class G, one relevant downstream object is
                                                 [
                                  Θ(P, Q, G) =         ΘG (P, Q),                        (32.1)
                                                 G∈G

where ΘG (P, Q) contains effects compatible with distribution P , question Q and the model
310                                                           Causal analysis for a universal bank


restrictions for G. A nonidentified member can make the union broad. A list of estimated
points is not automatically the whole union, and graph-selection uncertainty cannot be replaced
with ordinary coefficient uncertainty after selecting one member.
   Equation (32.1) also clarifies what a disagreement review should resolve. If two experts
differ only on an edge that leaves the target functional unchanged, that disagreement may be
immaterial for the current decision while still mattering for another target. If their graphs
imply different effect signs or feasibility, the conflict is decision-relevant. The assistant can
identify that consequence and prioritize the required evidence. It should not average expert
preferences into an unexplained graph.


32.4     Retrieval failure and scientific disagreement
An evidence assistant can fail to find a passage because the document is unavailable, parsing
failed, the query was poor, the retriever missed it, or the passage is absent from the inspected
document. These cases support different statements. “No passage was retrieved” cannot by
itself become “the authors ignored the assumption,” and neither statement establishes that
the assumption is false in the population.
   The inspected ARGUS paper makes this distinction especially useful. It audits reported
evidence concerning DiD identifying assumptions and does not claim to adjudicate causal
truth. Its synthetic flaw study exhibits a retrieval/abstention tradeoff, and its small human-
label pilot reports an in-sample calibration change that was not tested on unseen papers.
These observations motivate a banking evidence state that is separate from a scientific risk
judgment.Zhang et al. (2026)
   The proposed record contains the source bytes, the query or retrieval configuration, inspected
anchors and the resulting narrow claim. If evidence is missing, it records the missing step.
If two sources conflict, it records their populations, dates and definitions before treating the
conflict as substantive. The analyst can then determine whether the sources concern different
regimes or whether a genuine contradiction remains.
   This process does not require pretending that every edge has a published study behind it.
Some causal premises depend on institutional facts: which system sets a rate, when a policy
becomes visible, how an audit was selected, or which identifier establishes ownership. Those
facts need an accountable owner and authentic records. Literature retrieval can help formulate
the questions, but it cannot supply an institution’s missing assignment truth.


32.5     A reviewable editing sequence
The proposed interaction starts with a question and variable definitions, then records diagram
alternatives. Each edit changes a declared object: add or remove a variable, refine a clock,
replace a proxy, propose an endpoint, or accept a restriction. The edit retains its predecessor
identity and reason. A reviewer can therefore see whether an apparent improvement in fit
came from a new assumption, a different target, or an actual correction of an error.
   Formal checks can reject a directed cycle in a DAG, impossible declared time order or an
explicitly forbidden direction. They can flag mediator, collider or common-ancestor patterns
in the supported representation. Such checks help maintain a coherent declaration but do not
cover every graph class or establish that an accepted edge is causally true. In particular, a
diagram with no syntax error can still omit an important common cause or misrepresent the
observation process.
32.6. Equal observed laws can imply different intervention answers                               311


   The user should be able to retain an unresolved diagram and ask for analyses conditional on
several alternatives. A refusal to pick one graph can be the scientifically correct output. The
later discovery and identification operations then need to report what changes across those
alternatives and what remains common. This makes uncertainty operational: it directs the
next information request rather than appearing only as a disclaimer after a single confident
answer.


32.6      Equal observed laws can imply different intervention an-
          swers
A diagram assistant must recognize when available observations cannot determine the requested
direction or effect. Consider two project-constructed binary models. Let U be fair Bernoulli
and A = U . In model one Y = A; in model two Y = U . Both observed datasets contain only
(A, Y ) = (0, 0) and (1, 1) with equal probability. Under an intervention setting A = a, model
one has mean outcome a while model two has mean outcome 1/2. Their average effects are
one and zero. Exact enumeration establishes the discrepancy.Causal banking research project
(2026as)
  Estimating the observed marginal propensity as 1/2 does not solve the problem: exchange-
ability given the available information is precisely what is missing. A model that recognizes
a plausible causal story may prefer one graph, but that preference is not identification from
these data. Expert knowledge, measurements or experiments could distinguish the worlds;
those inputs need their own evidence and should remain visible in the result.
  A continuous version shows why effect sets can be unbounded. Let independent standard
Gaussian variables U and ε generate

                                 X = U,        Y = bX − bU + ε.

The factual law is X = U, Y = ε for every real b. Under do(X = x), however, the mean of Y is
bx. Therefore every real intervention slope is compatible with the same observed distribution
within this allowed model class. More observations estimate that common law more accurately;
they do not select b. A discovery tool or language model cannot remove this ambiguity without
an additional restriction.
  This is a useful evaluation case for agentic discovery. A high-quality response retains the
competing models, explains their observational equivalence and identifies the information that
could separate them. An overconfident single graph should be scored as a substantive error
even if its prose is convincing. A refusal or whole-line effect set can be the scientifically correct
output; its lack of immediate decision usefulness should be reported separately.


32.7      Prior knowledge needs a typed evidence record
The inspected DirectLiNGAM interface distinguishes a directed path, no directed path and
unspecified prior knowledge. The y0 identification dispatcher requires a supplied graph rather
than eliciting its truth. These interfaces make the translation from narrative evidence to
formal restrictions consequential. An agent saying “A is likely relevant to Y” has not supplied
a justified directed-path constraint.LiNGAM project (2026b); y0 project (2026b)
  For each proposed restriction, a useful record distinguishes a temporal order, an intervention
mechanism, a measured association, a domain assertion and a formal exclusion. It binds the
variables, their measurement/availability clocks, the source passage, the supporting scope and
312                                                           Causal analysis for a universal bank


any disagreement. A source about one population or intervention need not justify a hard
exclusion in another. The record should preserve which conclusions change if the assertion is
removed.
   Suppose a manager states that a rate change cannot be caused by next month’s withdrawal.
That supports a temporal ordering when the rate decision was fixed before the withdrawal.
It does not rule out an earlier expectation of withdrawal affecting the rate, or a common
market shock affecting both. A diagram assistant can expose the omitted expectation vari-
able and the common-cause alternative. It should not convert the temporal statement into
unconfoundedness.
   An analogous issue arises in network diagrams. MossSpider’s selected source uses a directed
influence convention that requires explicit checking, while a bank may draw arrows from
guarantor to beneficiary. A language model can produce the correct-looking graph but an
incorrectly oriented adjacency representation. A two-node semantic test with known distinct
attributes is more informative than a visual similarity score.MossSpider project (2026)


32.8     Set-valued reasoning should survive verbal reporting
If uncertainty concerns several graphs or nuisance parameters, the effect object may be a union
of intervals. A project ratio example illustrates the boundary. Let a numerator lie in [1, 2] and
an audit multiplier in [−1/2, 1/2], with the relation m = rθ. Excluding division by zero while
retaining all feasible nonzero multipliers gives
                                   Θ = (−∞, −2] ∪ [2, ∞).
The gap around zero and the unbounded tails are substantive. Replacing this object by its
hull loses the exclusion of zero; replacing it by a finite interval loses compatible effects. A
monetary transformation should be applied to each component and preserve endpoint inclusion
and infinite endpoints.
   The agent should describe why the set is disconnected, what assumptions support it and
what information would make it more useful. It should not translate “wide uncertainty” into
a invented central estimate. When both zero numerator and zero multiplier remain jointly
feasible, the effect can instead be the whole real line. The distinction depends on the joint
region, not just separate point estimates.
   This reasoning also separates model plausibility from sampling coverage. If a joint confidence
region contains the true observable and nuisance parameters, its effect image contains the true
effect on that event. The implication is elementary; constructing the valid joint region under
the bank’s actual dependence and audit law is the difficult statistical work. An agent can
propagate a supplied region faithfully. It cannot infer that its coverage is valid merely because
the downstream set arithmetic passed a test.


32.9     Comparing four ways to assist diagram construction
The useful comparison is between the operations an assistant performs and the evidence each
operation adds. An interactive editor helps an analyst see and revise a hypothesis. A language
model can propose mechanisms and missing variables from descriptions. A response-based
conditional-independence procedure can organize model judgments into a graph search. A
workflow agent can select and operate a statistical discovery method under declared assumptions.
These operations may share an interface, but they answer different scientific questions. The
proposed product should preserve that distinction when it combines them.
32.9. Comparing four ways to assist diagram construction                                     313


   CausalChat illustrates the interactive route. Its inspected preprint describes an optional
CPDAG obtained from data, GPT-4 comments on relations, visual summaries linked to
model responses, and structural-equation coefficient updates after graph changes. This is
a useful design for making an analyst’s reasoning inspectable. Its evidence for interface
benefits nevertheless needs careful interpretation. Six university students first resolved three
self-selected edges using BIC feedback, then another three using LLM text, and finally the
remaining three using CausalChat Lite. The reported error counts were 5/18, 7/18 and 1/18.
The edge sets and order changed together with the interface. Those results describe the authors’
experiment; they do not identify the effect of replacing one interface with another on matched,
randomly assigned banking tasks. Expert participants also questioned missing citations and
the quality of the scientific evidence behind model suggestions. A compact visualization may
improve comprehension while leaving the causal premise unresolved. (Zhang, 2024)
   The breadth-first method of Jiralerspong and colleagues offers a different contribution. A
query expands one variable into its proposed effects, and insertion rejects an edge that would
create a directed cycle. The authors’ linear query-count argument follows from visiting each
variable once. It does not make the total input/output token count linear: each expansion
can refer to many variables and the accumulated graph. The reported 221-node experiment
achieved an F1 score of 0.351, while some comparison configurations and the proposed variant
using observational statistics were omitted for resource reasons. That evidence motivates
an efficiency baseline with actual tokens, latency and omitted requests accounted for. It
supplies no reason to certify every retained arrow merely because the final graph is acyclic.
(Jiralerspong et al., 2024)
  chatPC places language-model judgments inside a conditional-independence search. Its
prompts include variable descriptions, context and a conditioning set; its repeated-answer test
concerns the relative probabilities of YES and NO responses. The paper reports agreement
under exchange of the two queried variables of 0.510 for GPT-3.5 and 0.870 for GPT-4, with
the latter often rejecting independence. Symmetry is a necessary property of a conditional-
independence relation. Measuring the frequency with which a model respects it is useful, but
that frequency is not the error rate of a statistical test in the bank’s observation law. The
two sources of randomness must remain separate: a model can consistently repeat a mistaken
judgment about the world. (Cohrs et al., 2024)
   The causal-learn+ system description instead places agents around formal discovery: data
inspection, assumption elicitation, method recommendation, tool coordination and interpre-
tation. It separates suggestions, user decisions, algorithm settings and graph outputs, and
emphasizes retaining CPDAG and PAG ambiguity. This is a strong architectural alternative
when the aim is access to an existing formal method. Its call for future benchmarks of diagnosis,
selection and calibrated interpretation also limits the performance conclusions available from
the description itself. Keeping a formal algorithm at the center does not establish its premises,
and user approval does not turn a disputed premise into empirical truth. Conversely, a fully
specified and evaluated hybrid method is conceivable; the architecture’s restrictive preference
is not an impossibility theorem about every use of language-model information. (Zheng, 2026)
   These comparisons support a product with several explicitly named operations. Proposing a
missing common cause should return a hypothesis and its evidence. Editing a reviewed graph
should return a new graph and the changed premises. Running a specified discovery method
should retain the method’s actual output class. Identifying a target should consume that class
through a supported formal path. A user can benefit from all four services without being led
to believe that a plausible graph proposal has already passed the last two.
