   For a proposal, publicly available dictionaries and controlled examples are sufficient to
demonstrate this failure and specify the required interface. They cannot establish the target
bank’s true measurement process. The immediate design should retain the conceptual variable,
measured proxy and measurement mechanism separately. An eventual bank study of the proxy
is justified only if the prototype and decision analysis show that the unresolved measurement
information is consequential.


32.11      What additional measurement information would buy
The proxy example also gives a concrete route beyond a generic request for better data.
Suppose a symmetric error probability e is known, and the stronger nondifferential measurement
condition

                                   P (Z | U, A, Y ) = P (Z | U )

  holds. For fixed (a, y), write oz = P (A = a, Y = y, Z = z) and qu = P (A = a, Y = y, U = u).
Then
                                       !                    !        !
                                  o0            1−e  e          q0
                                           =                       .
                                  o1             e  1−e         q1

  The determinant is 1 − 2e. For the declared range 0 ≤ e < 1/2, inversion yields

                                               (1 − e)ou − eo1−u
                                    qu =                         .
                                                     1 − 2e
   Thus known measurement information and the stated mechanism permit reconstruction of
the latent joint law in this finite example. Adjustment using that reconstructed U law recovers
1/5, exactly matching the intervention calculation. No observed customer identity or latent
label has been manufactured: the reconstruction depends explicitly on an assumed, known
error matrix. (Causal banking research project, 2026d)
  The route has a meaningful failure boundary. In the vector one-norm, the inverse matrix
has norm 1/(1 − 2e), because each column’s absolute entries sum to that value. At e = 1/5,
a worst-case perturbation in the observed joint probabilities can be amplified by 5/3 before
the further ratios needed for adjustment. As e approaches one half, measurement inversion
becomes unstable. At one half, the score supplies no information about which latent category
generated it, and this inversion is unavailable. An exact symbolic inverse alone does not make
the resulting effect precise.
   In finite samples the inverted entries can become negative. Such entries may reflect sampling
error, a misspecified measurement model or an error matrix incompatible with the observed
law. Clipping them to zero and renormalizing changes the estimator and its interpretation. A
defensible alternative is to retain a constrained uncertainty region for the observed probabilities
and measurement parameters, then project the compatible latent laws into effect values.
Whether that region has justified coverage is an additional statistical obligation; the exact
population example does not supply it.
   If e is estimated from a labeled subset, the subset’s selection and label truth matter. A
convenience sample of easily resolved customers need not identify the same error matrix for
difficult cases. If difficulty affects the error rate even after conditioning on U , the symmetric
matrix is wrong. If the score was constructed using post-offer outcomes, nondifferential
316                                                          Causal analysis for a universal bank


measurement can fail. The assistant’s useful contribution is to identify these propositions,
locate relevant documentation and propose a sensitivity analysis. Repeating a confidence
rating about the score cannot replace the missing information.
  This makes the next experiment more specific. A public or generated benchmark can
compare inversion, naive proxy adjustment and a valid refusal as the measurement error
changes. It can establish that the proposed software preserves the declared assumptions and
numerical limits. A later target-bank measurement audit would answer a different question:
whether an adequate and sufficiently representative measurement model exists there. The
expense of that audit belongs after evidence that the affected decision warrants it.


32.12        Post-action engagement can be a collider
The label “engagement” often invites adjustment, because it sounds like a useful customer
characteristic. Its clock and causal role matter more than its name. Consider another exact
example with independent fair binary variables A and U . Let A be a randomized outreach
offer, U latent willingness to repay, Y = U , and M a post-offer engagement indicator satisfying

                                                     1
                          P (M = 1 | A = a, U = u) = 10 + 25 a + 52 u.

   The graph has A → M ← U → Y . The offer has zero causal effect on repayment, and
the unadjusted observed difference is zero. All eight observed cells of (A, M, Y ) have positive
probability. Conditioning on M nevertheless makes the randomized action informative about
U.
  Among engaged customers,


                                      .9     9                                      .5
      P (Y = 1 | A = 1, M = 1) =           = 14 ,   P (Y = 1 | A = 0, M = 1) =           = 56 .
                                   .5 + .9                                       .1 + .5

   Their difference is −4/21. Among customers with M = 0, the corresponding probabilities
are 1/6 and 5/14, giving the same difference. Standardizing over M therefore reports −4/21 ≃
−.190 even though the true effect is zero. The apparently richer adjustment set has created
the discrepancy. (Causal banking research project, 2026d)
   The example separates three questions that an assistant should not merge. The total effect
concerns E{Y (1) − Y (0)}. An observed comparison among engaged customers conditions on
M = 1 after the action and can compare different latent populations across arms. A principal-
stratum question instead refers to a joint potential-response condition, such as customers who
would engage under either offer assignment. Its definition and identifying assumptions are
different again. A clearer English description does not make those targets interchangeable.
   If engagement is a mediator in another plausible graph, holding it fixed can remove part of
the pathway through which the offer works. A controlled direct effect would involve Y (a, m)
and an intervention on engagement, if that intervention has a coherent meaning. Ordinary
regression adjustment for an observed mediator does not automatically identify that effect,
especially with hidden causes of both the mediator and repayment. The assistant should
first expose the target choice and then ask which scientific conditions support the requested
calculation.
   The remedy is not a universal ban on using any variable recorded after the offer. A genuinely
baseline quantity may be entered into a database later, and retrospective measurement can be
relevant to an analysis if its measurement and selection assumptions are justified. Conversely,
32.13. Time unrolling and the difference between analysis and deployment                        317


a variable entered early may encode a forecast produced using information unavailable to the
policy at the decision time. The product needs distinct event, measurement and availability
clocks, together with an account of how the variable was constructed.


32.13      Time unrolling and the difference between analysis and
           deployment
An institution may describe a feedback loop: offers affect balances, and balances affect later
offers. A graph over two timeless variables, “offer” and “balance,” can then contain a directed
cycle. That observation does not establish that every causal model of the workflow requires a
cyclic graph. With dates made explicit, a possible structure is

                                At −→ Bt+1 −→ At+1 −→ Bt+2 .

   The arrows describe distinct variable instances. An acyclic time-unrolled model can represent
feedback across decisions while retaining a clear within-date ordering. Whether it is scientifically
adequate still depends on the sampling frequency, contemporaneous mechanisms, hidden
information and the policy that chooses each action. Deleting an inconvenient arrow from the
timeless graph would conceal these issues rather than resolve them.
   For each instance, the proposed variable record distinguishes the period described, the event
that generated its value, the time it was first available and any subsequent correction. A
customer’s end-of-month balance may be known only after settlement. A revised macroeconomic
release can describe an earlier month while containing information that was not available
when an offer was chosen. Using the revised value to reconstruct a historical policy can create
information leakage without introducing an obviously backward arrow into a diagram.
   Write Ht for the information actually available when an action is selected. A deployable
policy has the form At = πt (Ht ), perhaps with explicit randomized variation. A retrospective
adjustment variable need not belong to exactly the same information set: it might help describe
pre-action confounding after being measured later. The scientific validity of that retrospective
use and the feasibility of using it in a prospective policy are separate questions. The diagram
assistant should preserve both records rather than infer feasibility from a successful estimation
call.
   A bank also needs to distinguish a true event from the observation of that event. An offer
can affect whether a customer responds to a survey, whether a missing identifier is resolved
or whether an account enters the analysis extract. If S denotes observation, an effect among
S = 1 can concern a selected population whose composition changes with the action. Adding
an “observed” flag to a data table is not enough; its parents belong in the causal model. Public
synthetic benchmarks can vary this mechanism deliberately and reveal whether the interface
silently drops the selection node.
   These distinctions guide the assistant’s questions. A temporal contradiction should generate
a request to refine the variable instance or clock. A change in data availability should affect
the deployable policy record. An unresolved observation mechanism should remain a possible
source of selection bias. None requires the assistant to invent a hidden construct or declare a
fully specified longitudinal identification result before the required evidence exists.
318                                                             Causal analysis for a universal bank


32.14      Evidence for an arrow, a path and an exclusion
Expert statements differ in logical strength. “The offer precedes the withdrawal” can rule out
a particular backward-in-time mechanism under the declared clock. It does not establish an
arrow from offer to withdrawal, exclude an earlier common cause or prove a nonzero effect.
“The offer changes the fee, which changes withdrawal” proposes a directed path through a
mediator; it does not necessarily propose a direct arrow after that mediator is included. “The
offer was randomized” concerns an assignment mechanism and its scope. The assistant should
preserve these differences before converting prose into software constraints.
   The same caution applies to exclusions. Absence of an association in one study can reflect
imprecision, cancellation, measurement error or a different population. Absence of a retrieved
passage can reflect search failure. Neither observation automatically justifies a forbidden causal
path. A hard exclusion removes models from the admitted class; it is therefore a scientific
restriction with consequences for every downstream identified set.
   Let M be the currently admitted set of causal models and K a proposed restriction. The
restricted class is

                               MK = {m ∈ M : m satisfies K}.

   For a fixed observed law and target, its compatible effect set is contained in the corresponding
unrestricted set. Narrowing follows from set inclusion, not from new empirical accuracy. If the
true model is excluded by K, the narrower result can be more decisive and less defensible at
the same time. If the restriction leaves no compatible model, the output should identify the
contradiction rather than substitute an empty effect with the meaning “no effect.”
   A useful evidence record therefore includes the exact proposition, variable instances, popu-
lation and period, primary source passage, whether the assertion is observed or assumed, and
counterevidence. It also records the target calculations that depend on the proposition. If two
experts disagree about a common cause, the analyst should be able to see the effect bounds
and feasible actions under each branch. If they disagree about a remote edge that changes
neither the relevant functional nor the feasible decision, the next review can focus elsewhere
without declaring the remote edge resolved.
  One source can support several claims without providing several independent pieces of
evidence. A guideline, a review quoting that guideline and three generated summaries of the
review may all trace to one original study. The proposed evidence graph should retain that
common origin. It should also preserve differences between a source’s measured population and
the bank’s target population. Authenticity, applicability and inferential strength are separate
properties of the same document.


32.15      Agreement between agents does not measure causal
           certainty
Consensus can be useful for finding inconsistent explanations, but its interpretation depends
on how the answers were generated. Let V1 , . . . , Vn be binary endorsements of one proposed
edge. In a stipulated exchangeable response model, each has mean q, variance q(1 − q), and
common pairwise correlation ρ. Expanding the variance of the mean gives

                                            q(1 − q)
                               Var(V̄ ) =            {1 + (n − 1)ρ}.
                                               n
32.16. Reuse decisions for three available package paths                                       319


  The variance-equivalent count of independent responses is

                                                     n
                                       neff =                .
                                                1 + (n − 1)ρ

  For ten responses and an assumed correlation of .9, this count is 100/91, barely more than
one. This is an exact implication of the response model, not an estimated correlation or a
calibration result for any deployed agent. Shared training, retrieved passages or an initial
proposed answer can create dependence whose size must be studied rather than guessed.
(Causal banking research project, 2026d)
  Even ρ = 0 would not solve the more fundamental problem. The parameter q describes
the chance that the prompted system endorses an edge. It is not the probability that the
edge is true in the target bank. Independent repetitions can estimate a consistently wrong
endorsement probability very precisely. Assigning different role names to the same model
changes the prompts; it does not establish either statistical independence or independent
access to scientific evidence.
   The hallucination-reduction study by Sng and colleagues makes a related distinction concrete.
Its contradiction metric compares model ratings, its retrieval experiment supplies a mocked
true causal graph, and its debate setup uses opposing positions and an arbiter. The authors
explicitly distinguish reduced contradiction from accurate causal prediction and leave true-
graph validation to further work. That is useful evidence about a proposed consistency remedy,
with a narrower claim than the paper title might suggest. (Grace Sng, Yanming Zhang and
Klaus Mueller, 2024)
   The proposed product can use debate to expose an omitted assumption, ask for a coun-
terexample or compare the scope of two sources. It should retain the actual reasons and
original passages. A final arbiter’s vote should remain a workflow decision or an explicitly
uncalibrated preference. If the intended downstream operation needs probabilities over models,
those probabilities require a declared prior/likelihood construction or a separately justified
calibration target. A voting fraction cannot silently supply them.


32.16       Reuse decisions for three available package paths
The inspected pywhy-llm revision provides useful hypothesis-elicitation components. Its
identification suggester delegates a back-door suggestion to the model’s confounder suggester,
while the inspected front-door method is a TODO with a pass body and the longer estimand-
construction block is commented out. Its MIT license and declared Python/LLM dependencies
make reuse of selected interaction ideas plausible. They do not make a returned confounder list
an identified adjustment set. The proposed integration should accept suggestions as candidate
evidence records and send the resulting reviewed graph to a formal identification operation. It
should not present the front-door placeholder as an available scientific capability. (pywhy-llm
contributors, 2026)
   The pinned causal_GPT source is valuable as an experimental comparison for response-based
discovery. It aggregates model answers through voting, weighted voting and a proportion test,
then maps the selected decision to zero or one in the conditional-independence interface. Those
endpoints are software signals; they are not calibrated p-values for the bank’s joint distribution.
The source also reuses YES and NO counts from the same answer collection, which makes
their covariance relevant even to the response-level test. The analysis in Chapter 33 develops
that separate issue. The appropriate decision is to retain the method as a labeled benchmark
candidate, with its BSD three-clause obligations and actual dependencies, while declining
320                                                          Causal analysis for a universal bank


direct use as a calibrated sampling-law oracle. (causal_GPT contributors, 2024)
   CausalAgent offers an end-to-end application and MCP comparison. At the inspected
revision, its server advertises PC and OLC tools. It imports the PC analysis function, while
the OLC function called in that module is neither imported nor defined there; the surrounding
exception handler returns a JSON failure string. A separate output helper takes the text
between the first and last braces and returns an empty dictionary when decoding fails. These
static findings constrain adoption of the inspected path. They are not a claim that every
revision or every deployment behaves identically. The proposal should reuse the idea of explicit
tool handoffs, require typed invalid/unavailable outcomes, and defer the OLC path until its
concrete implementation is repaired and actually exercised. (CausalAgent contributors, 2026)
   There are three distinct reuse decisions here. Selected elicitation components can be
integrated behind a proposal-only boundary. An imperfect scientific method can remain
a useful experimental comparator. A concrete incomplete tool path can be rejected for
direct adoption while retaining other architectural lessons. Porting an entire application or
dependency stack does not resolve any of the scientific defects. A port should be considered
only after a selected path has a justified purpose and a measured constraint that the port
could address.
   Actual deployment would still require frozen package and model identities, license notices,
data-handling decisions, runtime budgets, endpoint conversion checks and independent reference
cases. The current comparison is based on saved source and primary text. No live-model
accuracy, end-to-end latency or runtime conformance is inferred from that inspection. These
limitations define the first prototype trials without blocking the present architecture and
literature argument.


32.17      Editing a graph without losing its scientific history
A graph edit should change one declared object and make its consequences inspectable. Adding
a latent node is different from adding an observed column. Resolving a circle endpoint is
different from moving a node on the screen. Accepting an expert exclusion is different from an
algorithm finding an orientation under a registered test. The interface should retain the origin
and logical status of each change even when it displays the resulting graph in one view.
   Suppose the analyst begins with a partially directed graph and a disputed assertion that
a risk score is sufficient for adjustment. A useful edit sequence first records the score as a
measured proxy, then creates a branch with the latent common cause, and finally compares
the target functional under the original and revised assumptions. The proxy example shows
why the changed value can be scientifically meaningful even when model fit remains good. The
analyst should be able to return to the earlier branch and see the exact premise responsible
for the difference.
   Constraint checking also needs a clear purpose. Rejecting cycles maintains the declared
DAG representation, but greedy rejection can depend on insertion order. Given proposed
arrows A → B, B → C and C → A, accepting the first two rejects the third; another order
rejects a different arrow. The algorithm has selected one internally consistent subset without
establishing which arrow was scientifically wrong. The remedy is to expose the conflicting set,
preserve the evidence for each member and seek a revised clock, representation or premise. A
deterministic insertion order improves reproducibility; it does not supply a causal reason for
the choice.
  The downstream dependency record should bind an identified expression to the graph, query
and assumptions that produced it. If an edit changes the outcome’s definition, the target
32.18. Which disagreement is worth resolving                                                  321


changes. If an edit changes a common-cause restriction, identification may change. If only a
displayed label changes through a valid bijection, the scientific object may remain the same.
These cases deserve different invalidation rules. Reusing an old estimate because the edited
diagram still has the same number of edges is not a defensible rule.
   Review should preserve disagreement when available evidence cannot resolve it. A graph
collection is not automatically a statistical confidence set, and a union of its effect candidates
is not automatically exhaustive over every causal model. The product must state which
alternatives were considered, why others were excluded and what additional uncertainty
remains. A well explained partial answer can still narrow the next experiment or rule out a
premature investment.


32.18      Which disagreement is worth resolving
The monetary question can organize expert review without pretending to settle causal truth.
Consider an assumed proposal scenario in which two admitted model branches imply effect
values .02 and .08 on repayment probability. Assign an assumed USD 1,000 value to an
additional successful repayment and a USD 50 offer cost. The corresponding net values per
account are

                 vL = 1000(.02) − 50 = −30,         vH = 1000(.08) − 50 = 30.

   With no justified probability over the two branches, the action is not robustly beneficial.
Relative to choosing the better action in each branch, both adopting and declining have
maximum regret USD 30 per account. The calculation locates a consequential disagreement;
it does not choose a probability because a majority of prompted agents favored one branch.
(Causal banking research project, 2026d)
   If a sponsor explicitly adopts a planning probability π for the high-value branch, the expected
net value of adoption is 60π − 30. The best current expected value is max(0, 60π − 30). Perfect
information about the branch would allow adoption only when its value is positive, yielding
expected value 30π. The expected value of perfect information is therefore

                             EVPI(π) = 30π − max(0, 60π − 30).

   At π = 1/2, it is USD 15 per account; at π = 4/5, it is USD 6. For 10,000 otherwise
comparable accounts with additive values and one shared model uncertainty, those assumed
upper bounds are USD 150,000 and USD 60,000. The higher prior confidence reduces the
incremental value of learning even though it makes immediate adoption more attractive. These
are exact planning calculations, not observed bank returns or elicited institutional beliefs.
(Causal banking research project, 2026d)
  A real experiment provides imperfect information, so its expected value of sample information
cannot exceed the perfect-information value under the same correct decision model. Delay,
implementation, review and measurement costs reduce its net value further. An experiment
costing more than this upper bound is not justified by this particular decision alone. A lower
cost is necessary but not sufficient: one must still show that the experiment can distinguish
the relevant branches and that its result can change an available action.
  A public benchmark can establish that the prototype preserves branch identities, computes
the right functional in a known mechanism and avoids the proxy/collider mistakes. It generally
cannot reveal which causal mechanism operates in a specific bank. The proposal should
therefore sequence the investment: first test the accessible computational and reasoning
322                                                         Causal analysis for a universal bank


obligations; then ask whether the remaining target-specific uncertainty is valuable enough to
investigate. Expensive authentic evidence is a conditional next investment, not a prerequisite
for writing a defensible proposal.


32.19      A benchmark for diagram assistance, with explicit failure
           credit
Evaluation should begin with a declared task object. One case might ask for a diagram
consistent with a timing description; another for possible omitted variables; a third for an
intervention answer over unresolved graph alternatives. They need different references. An
author-stipulated graph can provide controlled truth for a generated case. A public real-world
dataset may provide an observation law and metadata without a unique causal graph. Scoring
both against one arbitrarily selected edge list would confuse missing information with model
error.
   The proxy and collider cases provide exact formal baselines. The reference is the stated
structural law and its separately enumerated intervention distribution. The assistant sees the
permitted variable descriptions and observational information, with the hidden generator truth
withheld whenever the task concerns discovery. A correct output should distinguish what
follows from those observations from what depends on an additional assumption. A refusal to
declare unconfoundedness is useful when the evidence does not supply it; a refusal to do any
arithmetic in a fully specified exact model is a different failure.
   The comparison should include a deterministic dictionary-and-clock validator, an unassisted
formal method in its admitted domain, a single-model elicitation route, a retrieval-assisted
route and a reviewed human workflow where feasible. Public or generated cases permit these
designs without requiring a bank deployment. A live-model comparison additionally needs
actual model execution, recorded settings and measured resource use. An offline schema or
literature synthesis supplies neither live accuracy nor superiority.
   Perturbations should test meanings that ought to remain invariant. Permuting variable
order should not change the meaning of conditional independence. Renaming variables
through a bijection should preserve a formal answer when their descriptions remain equivalent.
Conversely, changing a variable from pre-offer state to post-offer response should change the
admissible reasoning. Removing a cited premise should weaken the claims that depended on
it. A benchmark that rewards invariance to every wording change would miss this distinction
between irrelevant phrasing and substantively changed information.
   Scores should retain unsupported, malformed and unavailable requests in the denominator.
They should distinguish valid abstention from an uninformative missing answer, graph syntax
from target identification, and a justified ambiguous effect set from an omitted calculation.
The monetary example supplies an additional loss measure: did the assistant recommend
an action that the admitted models do not justify, or identify a potentially valuable next
information request? Edge accuracy remains useful, but it is insufficient when a small number
of consequential edges determines the decision.
   Finally, reference information and retrieval material must be separated deliberately. Giving
a model the true graph can test whether it uses that information correctly, as in a controlled
consistency task. It cannot also measure discovery of that graph from evidence that did not
contain it. The proposed evaluation should report which service was actually tested, preserve
unfavorable cases, and measure the full cost of retrieving, checking and acting on an answer.
That produces a reviewable reason to build or narrow a diagram-assistance prototype while
leaving target-bank scientific truth to the later study that could establish it.
32.20. An operational ontology for four banking journeys                                      323


32.20      An operational ontology for four banking journeys
An ontology is useful when it makes different interpretations explicit before they enter an
estimate. The proposed causal ontology should distinguish an entity from an observation
about that entity, a concept from a measured variable, a variable definition from a particular
observation, and an intervention from the administrative event used to record it. These
distinctions are not cosmetic. They determine which quantities can be assigned, which can be
conditioned on, which share measurement errors and which belong to the same population.
   For the funding journey, consider “interest rate.” A contractual annual rate, a monthly
interest payment, a competitor’s advertised rate and a fitted marginal funding cost are different
variables. A unit conversion can relate two encodings of the same rate, but it cannot turn
a payment into an offer without account balance, accrual and timing information. Nor does
it turn an advertised offer into a received offer. The ontology should identify the product,
currency, contractual basis, decision date and exposure window. An agent can use a glossary
to suggest the mapping; the analyst must still see which distinctions the mapping retains.
   The associated entity hierarchy also matters. An account belongs to a legal customer, a
customer may belong to a household, and several records may refer to the same account. Those
relations do not themselves say that one node causally influences another. They do affect
aggregation and dependence. An offer randomized by household cannot be analyzed as though
each account were assigned independently merely because the extract has one row per account.
If a latent household membership is replaced by a record-linking prediction, that substitution
introduces the same kind of measurement question developed in the proxy example.
   For sequential servicing, “treatment” may mean eligibility, assignment, receipt, completion
or adherence. The stages can occur on different dates and have different causes. A rule that
assigns assistance after an arrears flag targets a dynamic regime; comparing customers who
eventually complete assistance targets a selected group unless further assumptions justify a
different interpretation. The ontology should retain the action that the bank can choose and
the later events that it can only influence. Otherwise an assistant may propose an infeasible
intervention on a customer’s future response while describing it as an ordinary policy choice.
  For discovery, a variable needs a measurement protocol as well as a label. A repeated risk
score can change because the customer changed, because the scoring model was updated or
because new source information became available. Treating all vintages as the same mechanism
can make an apparent causal change coincide with a measurement change. A diagram can
represent the score-generating mechanism or restrict the analysis to a stable declared regime.
The correct choice depends on the question; a vocabulary match alone cannot choose it.
   For trustworthy observations, separate an event from its record, a proposed match from a
true identity, and label correctness from the value being labeled. A classifier’s probability that
a record pair matches is an algorithm output with a calibration question. It is not an observed
identity. A hand-reviewed match can supply additional information, but its reviewer, selection
process and uncertainty remain relevant. The ontology can preserve these distinctions in a
public synthetic example long before the proposal needs an expensive bank labeling exercise.
   Across all four journeys, the proposed variable definition therefore contains a conceptual
role, unit of analysis, value domain, measurement mechanism, clocks, lineage and relation
to a feasible intervention. The system should support unresolved fields explicitly. A missing
clock should prompt a targeted evidence request; an unresolved proxy relation should produce
alternative measurement models. Automatically completing every field with plausible text
would hide the very uncertainty that a causal proposal must expose.
324                                                           Causal analysis for a universal bank


32.21      Semantic relations need typed boundaries
Common ontology relations carry different logical meanings. “A savings account is an account”
describes a taxonomy. “A household owns an account” describes a relation between entities.
“A risk score is computed from balance history” describes a derivation. “An offer changes a
future balance” proposes a causal mechanism. A general relation extractor may return all four
as triples, but a causal engine cannot assign them all the same edge semantics.
   A taxonomy helps establish which definitions apply to an instance; it does not imply that
intervening on an instance’s category has a coherent economic meaning. Ownership determines
which exposures should be combined and may enter a separate causal model, but the ownership
triple alone does not identify an intervention effect. A derived score carries deterministic or
stochastic dependence on its inputs; treating the score and every input as unrelated primitive
variables can contradict the declared derivation. Each relation needs a type before a diagram
operation acts on it.
   Duplicate encodings provide a simple formal example. Suppose a decimal rate R and its
basis-point encoding B satisfy B = 10,000R exactly. A vocabulary matcher may list them
as two numerical variables. Their observational distribution lies on a deterministic line. An
imagined intervention setting R = r and B = b independently is incompatible with the
encoding relation unless b = 10,000r, or unless the target is explicitly a system fault that
breaks that relation. Ordinary policy analysis should treat these as two coordinates of one
declared quantity, not as two independently selectable business levers.
   Alias resolution must be reversible. Two fields with the same display name can describe
different vintages; two differently named fields can be identical encodings. The system should
retain source identifiers, proposed canonical identifiers and the transformation between them.
A bijective unit conversion can be checked mechanically. A many-to-one coarsening, such as
mapping several delinquency states into “at risk,” discards information and can change the
adjustment or decision problem. It therefore needs a scientific interpretation as well as a data
transformation.
  The preferred local baseline is a deterministic dictionary and lineage validator. It can detect
an undeclared conversion, missing unit, duplicate identifier or a cycle in a purported derivation.
A language assistant adds value if it finds plausible semantic conflicts that the dictionary did
not encode and supplies reviewable evidence for resolving them. The two should be compared
on missed consequential distinctions and unnecessary review work. Merely producing more
complete metadata is not enough when some of the added metadata is wrong.
   The Selby study provides relevant adverse evidence for automatic completion. Its inspected
experiments elicited quantitative priors and imputed tabular values from language models.
Repeated prompts often produced consistent responses, yet some priors conflicted strongly with
observations and conventional nearest-neighbor or random-forest imputation often performed
better. The authors identify ambiguous units, incomplete descriptions and recognizable public
datasets as limitations. This supports careful metadata and benchmark design. It does not
establish a theorem about causal identification or license silent imputation of a bank’s missing
assignment mechanism. (Selby et al., 2024)


32.22      A treatment label can hide several interventions
Consider an assumed assistance program with two versions. Without assistance, successful
repayment has probability .4. The low-intensity version has success probability .42 and costs
USD 10; the high-intensity version has success probability .6 and costs USD 100. Suppose
32.23. A restricted OntoLearner integration                                                  325


assignment and version selection are randomized in this constructed example, and each
additional successful repayment is assigned a planning value of USD 1,000. The version
probabilities define the program being evaluated.
  If w is the probability of the high-intensity version among treated accounts, the effect of
that mixed program is

                        τ (w) = (1 − w)(.42) + w(.6) − .4 = .02 + .18w.

  Its expected cost is c(w) = 10 + 90w, so the assumed net value is

                             v(w) = 1000τ (w) − c(w) = 10 + 90w.

   At w = 1/4, the effect is .065 and the net value is USD 32.50. At w = 3/4, the effect is .155
and the net value is USD 77.50. Every calculation is exactly reproduced from the stipulated
rational probabilities. No observed banking profitability is asserted. (Causal banking research
project, 2026y)
   Both datasets could contain the same binary column named “assistance.” Nevertheless, the
programs have different meanings and different costs. An assistant should ask whether the
deployment preserves the version mix and the mechanisms under which those version-specific
outcomes were obtained. Reporting a precisely estimated effect for the earlier mix as the effect
of the later mix would answer the wrong question even if the graph’s two main node labels
were unchanged.
   The construction is deliberately simple. If version choice depends on baseline need, a
dynamic or covariate-dependent mixture w(x) is relevant. If customers select their own version
after assignment, assignment and receipt become different interventions. If staff implement
nominally identical assistance differently, the declared version may still omit consequential
variation. A useful ontology does not promise to remove all such ambiguity; it identifies which
variation is included in the intervention definition and which is left as an unresolved transport
assumption.
   This also explains why a prototype should retain version information before it is needed by
an estimator. A source package might accept one binary treatment and correctly estimate the
target supplied to it. The proposal’s common layer is responsible for making that supplied
target faithful to the actual decision. An LLM can identify the hidden-version possibility and
help locate policy documentation. The effect arithmetic then belongs to a separately specified
calculation, with the assumed assignment and valuation law visible to the reader.


32.23      A restricted OntoLearner integration
OntoLearner supplies an available component for the semantic stage. Its paper describes
ontology loading, learning tasks and learner models, including typing, taxonomy and relation
discovery. It also reports domain-dependent error patterns, retrieval limitations and calibration
differences. The inspected requirements were defined by the developers, and counts of ontologies
or requirements differ across passages. A proposal can use the architecture and reported
limitations without turning those counts into a certified inventory or treating every extracted
relation as causal. (Giglou et al., 2026)
  The inspected repository revision is 074a41ba23a85f5b72d4e28da042eab3d50bd90a, dated 3
September 2026. Its loader chooses a local source when a path is supplied and otherwise calls
a Hugging Face download. The inspected download call supplies a repository, file and dataset
326                                                          Causal analysis for a universal bank


type, but no revision. Further extraction calls download typing, taxonomy and non-taxonomic-
relation files without a revision argument as well. Pinning this Python source therefore does
not by itself pin the ontology bytes that an automatic download will return. (OntoLearner
contributors, 2026)
   There is another relevant boundary in the imported ontology closure. The base class’s
contains_imports hook returns false. When a subclass enables that hook, the loader follows
resolved imports, but it catches import-loading failures, logs them and continues; an unresolved
import also produces a warning without failing the load. A nonempty top-level graph therefore
does not establish that all intended imported definitions were loaded. If an unavailable import
contains the definition distinguishing a legal customer from a household, the resulting partial
ontology could still look operationally successful while supporting an incomplete semantic map.
This is a source-inspected failure possibility, not a report of an executed OntoLearner trial.
(SciKnowOrg; source inspection by Causal banking research project, 2026)
   The proposed integration should admit a fixed local ontology bundle with explicit revision,
byte identities and an import manifest. A wrapper should report complete, intentionally
partial or failed loading, preserving which definitions are absent. It should carry the original
relation types into a semantic proposal record and require a separate reviewed mapping before
creating causal nodes or edges. The initial useful output is a candidate variable dictionary
with evidence and conflicts, not an automatically accepted causal graph.
   The package’s MIT license permits reuse subject to its notice and disclaimer conditions. Its
inspected project file declares Python at least 3.10 and below 3.14, together with RDF, graph,
dataframe, validation and model-related dependencies; several version specifications are broad.
Reusing a small local loading/extraction path should still be assessed against a locked actual
environment and its transitive dependencies. A source inspection provides no build, memory
or compatibility measurement. The design decision is to integrate a restricted, reproducible
semantic path and defer automatic model-backed ontology expansion until its task, data rights,
resource use and evidence handling have been evaluated. (OntoLearner contributors, 2026)
   Porting the whole library would preserve neither ontology identity nor causal meaning
automatically. A port could be justified later by a measured platform constraint, but it would
require equivalent parsing, import handling and relation semantics. Direct adoption of a
mutable remote default would make a reproduction depend on an unspecified ontology version.
Rejecting the entire library would discard useful semantic infrastructure. The restricted path
retains its useful operations while making their scientific handoff explicit.


32.24      Evidence extraction as a separate experiment
A claim about an edge has at least three evidential questions. Was the relevant source obtained
and correctly parsed? Does an inspected passage actually support the narrow proposition
attributed to it? Is that proposition applicable and adequate for the intended banking model?
A citation attached to a graph is useful only if the workflow can answer these questions
separately. Text extraction accuracy cannot establish causal validity, and a valid causal result
from another population does not automatically establish transport.
   The ARGUS study provides a concrete adjacent comparison. It audits reported evidence for
identifying assumptions in difference-in-differences studies and explicitly does not adjudicate
causal truth. Its flaw-injection experiments supply controlled local references, while its small
human-label pilot diagnoses failures in real-paper auditing. The gated pipeline’s omissions
include cases in which retrieval found no relevant passage and the system abstained. In the
pilot, human reviewers often found evidence for cells where the system had abstained; the
32.25. Reviewing conflicts without counting votes as evidence                               327


paper’s subsequent calibration changes were evaluated on the same papers. These details
matter more to our design than a single aggregate agreement number. (Zhang et al., 2026)
   For a diagram assistant, a suitable first experiment can be public and inexpensive. Assemble
passages whose scope is explicit, paired with propositions that they support, contradict or
leave unresolved. Include genuine parse failures, omitted context, differing populations and
statements that concern association rather than intervention. An independent reference should
record the exact passage and the reason for its label. Generated alterations can expose specific
failure mechanisms, but their artificial nature should remain visible and should not be counted
as representative bank documents.
   The baseline should include direct passage lookup and a deterministic field/rule check before
introducing a model. A model-based system should report the retrieved material and the
proposition it inferred from it. If the reference passage was never retrieved, the retrieval
component failed. If it was retrieved but misread, the interpretation failed. If it was read
accurately but promoted beyond its population or assumptions, the scientific mapping failed.
Different remedies follow: improve acquisition/search, improve task interpretation, or tighten
the rules for accepting a causal premise.
   An observed negative result also needs precise wording. “No relevant evidence was found
in this bounded search” records an acquisition outcome. “The inspected document does not
state how assignment occurred” records a document-level absence under the inspected scope.
“Assignment was confounded” is a claim about the underlying process. The first two do not
prove the third. Conversely, a polished statement that assignment was “as if random” does
not establish the required condition merely because the text contains the expected vocabulary.
   This experiment can support a decision about building a literature and documentation
assistant before paying for a bank audit. It cannot show that the bank’s declared assignment
process is true. The eventual external input is a process-specific record or experiment, sought
only if the prototype and the investment calculation establish its value. The staged evidence
argument therefore has a concrete boundary: public documents test extraction and reasoning
obligations; target-specific evidence tests propositions about the target institution.


32.25      Reviewing conflicts without counting votes as evidence
Consider three separately proposed restrictions: an offer changes engagement, engagement
changes a later score, and the score determines the earlier offer. They cannot all be direct
temporal assertions about the same variable instances in an acyclic model. A syntax checker
can identify the contradiction. It cannot determine whether the score was actually measured
earlier, whether “changes” meant association, whether a date was omitted, or whether a cyclic
equilibrium model was intended. The review should return these alternatives to the analyst
with their evidence.
  One useful formal object is the set of admitted models after each restriction. If K1 , K2 , K3
are proposed predicates, the combined class is

                             {m ∈ M : K1 (m) ∧ K2 (m) ∧ K3 (m)}.

   If it is empty, the system can search for a smallest subset of the predicates that is already
inconsistent within the declared model class. Reporting that subset localizes the conflict.
It does not rank the predicates by truth or show that the smallest deletion is scientifically
appropriate. Several minimal conflicting subsets may exist; suppressing all but the first can
leave the analyst unaware of another contradiction.
328                                                            Causal analysis for a universal bank


   Priority should follow the evidence and the decision. A verified timestamp can refute a
purported same-instance temporal order. An expert’s general mechanism description may
instead need to be instantiated at a different date. A model suggestion with no supporting
source may remain a hypothesis. If withdrawing one disputed restriction changes a robustly
positive value into a set containing a substantial loss, that restriction merits attention before a
remote relation whose alternatives leave the decision unchanged. This is a proposed review
policy, not a claim that the system can mechanically rank every kind of scientific evidence.
   Conflicts between sources also need not be contradictions. Two studies can investigate
different treatment versions, observation regimes or populations. The ontology and intervention-
version records make those differences explicit. A source that supports an association at branch
level may have little to say about an account-level intervention. A diagram can preserve both
claims at their proper levels rather than force one to win a debate about an underspecified
phrase.
   The proposal’s deliverable is thus a reviewable sequence from language to typed variables,
explicit premises, compatible models, target calculations and decision consequences. Each
transition has examples that can pass, fail or remain unresolved. That sequence gives an agent
useful work throughout the causal analysis while preserving the mathematical and evidential
limits of each contribution.


32.26      Why an accurate clock need not identify the answer
It is useful to follow one restriction through an entire finite model comparison. Return to an
offer A and a later repayment outcome Y , both binary. Consider three explicitly listed models,
using mutually independent primitive variables in each model. In model F , A is fair Bernoulli
and Y = A ⊕ E, where E is Bernoulli with probability 1/10 and ⊕ denotes exclusive OR. In
model R, Y is fair Bernoulli and A = Y ⊕ E. In model C, a pre-offer latent variable U is fair
Bernoulli, A = U ⊕ E and Y = U . Each error variable has the same probability 1/10. These
are alternative constructions, not simultaneous equations for one population.
  Every model produces the observed table


                                           9                                                  1
 P (A = 0, Y = 0) = P (A = 1, Y = 1) =        ,     P (A = 0, Y = 1) = P (A = 1, Y = 0) =        .
                                           20                                                 20

   All four observed cells are positive. In model C, even conditioning on the latent variable
leaves both offer assignments possible: P (A = 1 | U = 0) = 1/10 and P (A = 1 | U = 1) = 9/10.
Thus the comparison does not rely on an empty observed treatment stratum or deterministic
assignment given the confounder. Deterministic repayment given U is part of this constructed
example, and is not a banking empirical claim.
   Replacing the action equation gives mean outcomes 1/10 and 9/10 in model F , hence
effect 4/5. In R, replacing the action equation leaves the fair outcome unchanged; in C, it
leaves the fair latent variable and Y = U unchanged. Both have effect zero. A separate
exact enumeration verifies the common observed table, positive assignment probabilities and
intervention contrasts. (Causal banking research project, 2026e)
   Now introduce a verified restriction: this particular offer was chosen before this particular
repayment outcome was generated, with no backward-time causal mechanism in the admitted
class. Model R’s direct arrow from this outcome to the earlier offer is incompatible with that
restriction. Models F and C both respect it. The candidate graph list shrinks from three
models to two, but the candidate effect set stays
32.27. Minimal conflicts locate a question; they do not settle it                           329



                                              {0, 4/5}.

   Correctly resolving an orientation has not reduced the decision-relevant ambiguity in this
example. An edge score that rewards removal of R can therefore improve while an effect-set
or decision measure remains unchanged. Both statements are useful; they measure different
progress. The set above belongs only to the three-model comparison. It is not asserted to
exhaust every effect compatible with the observed law under an unrestricted hidden-variable
model.
   There are several possible next restrictions, with different evidential costs. If the offer
equation is known to use independent random assignment, the stipulated mechanism of C
is excluded too; among these candidates only F remains. If U becomes correctly observed,
adjustment can identify the zero effect within C’s declared mechanism. If a noisy measurement
of U becomes available, the earlier proxy example shows why adjustment needs further
justification. These routes should not be compressed into one label such as “expert-validated
diagram.” They add distinct information and impose distinct assumptions.
  An offer timestamp alone supplies none of the exogeneity information. A policy document
describing randomization might support it, but the analyst must establish that the document
applies to the relevant assignment, population and period. A random seed recorded after
an officer overrode assignment does not establish the same mechanism. A public controlled
experiment can test whether software applies the restriction correctly; it cannot verify an
unobserved institution’s compliance with its policy. That is the later, targeted evidence
question.
  The assistant should show a consequence table after each accepted premise: which models
were removed, which target values were removed, and which claims now depend on that premise.
A useful diagnostic temporarily withdraws the premise and recomputes those consequences.
Here withdrawing the time order restores R without changing the two effect values, while
withdrawing the additional exogeneity restriction restores a zero-effect alternative. This
sensitivity report makes the pivotal premise explicit and can guide the next experiment
without assigning invented probabilities to the models.


32.27       Minimal conflicts locate a question; they do not settle it
The earlier offer–engagement–score example can also be made exact. Let three restrictions
require the direct arrows A → M , M → S and S → A between the same three variable
instances in a DAG. All three together create a directed cycle. Removing any one leaves
an acyclic directed path. The triple is therefore an inclusion-minimal inconsistent set of
these restrictions within the DAG class. A small exhaustive closure calculation verifies this
combinatorial statement. (Causal banking research project, 2026e)
   Here “inclusion-minimal” means that deleting any member removes this conflict. In a
larger restriction system it need not mean the smallest possible cardinality; different minimal
conflicting subsets can coexist. Nor does minimality select a scientifically preferred repair.
Deleting the arrow with the lowest language-model confidence can yield a syntactically valid
graph while deleting the only premise supported by a reliable process record.
  One legitimate repair might refine the score into St and St+1 . The earlier score affects At ,
which changes engagement and a later score; that time-unrolled construction can respect all the
underlying mechanism descriptions. Another repair might find that the phrase “engagement
changes score” described a deterministic calculation rather than the primitive intervention
330                                                           Causal analysis for a universal bank


contemplated by the analyst. A third might withdraw an unsupported causal assertion. These
are alternatives to investigate, not guaranteed equivalent versions of one graph.
  The scientific review should therefore report the conflicting predicates together with their
variable identities, clocks and evidence. It should distinguish a change to the model class,
a refinement of a variable, and a rejection of a premise. Keeping that distinction makes
both favorable and adverse prototype results interpretable: a detector can correctly find the
contradiction even if it cannot resolve its scientific cause. Its useful contribution is a precise
next question whose answer would change the admissible analysis.
Chapter 33

Language assistance, causal
discovery and uncertainty

33.1      The scientific object behind a graph proposal
A banking analyst may begin with a list of columns and a request to explain why balances move
after a change in deposit pricing. A language model can recognize the vocabulary, propose
a market-rate variable, distinguish a customer offer from a realized rate, and suggest that
customer characteristics affect both assignment and retention. These suggestions are useful
because a statistical algorithm does not recover the meaning of a column from its numerical
values. The scientific question nevertheless remains open. The proposed relation may describe
a mechanism in another population, a historical association, a direct effect, an indirect path, or
simply a familiar phrase. The role given to the suggestion determines the claim the resulting
graph can support.
   The inspected literature offers several roles rather than one method called “LLM causal
discovery.” Pairwise language judgments, breadth-first graph construction, retrieval-assisted
discovery, response-based independence queries, statistical prompting, soft graph priors, multi-
agent debate and numerical experiment design alter different parts of an analysis Kıcıman et al.
(2023); Jiralerspong et al. (2024); Zhang et al. (2024); Cohrs et al. (2024); Takayama et al.
(2024); Darvariu et al. (2024); Le et al. (2024); Murphy (2026). They should be compared by
what information they consume, what object they change, and what uncertainty survives that
change.
   Let D denote numerical observations, T the retrieved or supplied technical text, and
M the language-model mechanism, including its version, prompts and decoding policy. A
proposal is then a function or random output of (D, T, M ). It is not an additional independent
sample from the banking process. If the model proposes a graph G, the relevant questions
are whether the variables have the intended meaning, whether the graph restrictions are
scientifically warranted, whether the data support the inference procedure, and whether the
target effect is identified under those restrictions. These questions remain distinct even when
one conversational interface presents all of them together.
   The following analysis uses inspected primary methods and evaluations. Reported benchmark
gains are the authors’ results; no external discovery package or language-model endpoint is
executed here. The finite examples and probability calculations below are project constructions.
Their role is to test the logic of proposed interfaces and interpretations, not to claim bank
validation.



                                               331
332                                                          Causal analysis for a universal bank


33.2     What language-only discovery measures
The broad proof of concept of Kıcıman and colleagues motivates language support for several
causal tasks, including the elicitation of background knowledge and reasoning about causal
relationships Kıcıman et al. (2023). A model can answer a question such as whether an increase
in a borrowing rate affects demand without receiving a numerical sample. Such an answer
may encode useful inherited knowledge. It cannot reveal which of several observationally
compatible assignment mechanisms generated a particular bank’s records unless the prompt
or the model’s knowledge provides additional applicable information.
   Feng and colleagues investigate relation occurrences in accessible OLMo and BLOOM
pretraining corpora and report that relation frequency is associated with prediction success
Feng (2024). Their controlled additions of synthetic relations and the effects of reversed or
negated statements help separate recall from a claim of general discovery. The scope matters:
their pretraining investigation concerns accessible models and predominantly commonsense
relationships. It is evidence for a contamination concern and a test design, not proof that
every model operates only by memorization.
   A sensible banking evaluation therefore crosses two kinds of novelty. One can change the
variable names while holding the mechanism fixed, or change the mechanism while retaining
familiar labels. The first tests reliance on surface vocabulary. The second asks whether
a familiar story prevents the system from responding to contrary evidence. Neither test
should declare a new label intrinsically uninformative: operational definitions often carry
real information about intervention feasibility and time order. Removing all meaning from a
variable name changes the task as well as its contamination risk.
   Context must also be handled carefully. In the inspected reliability study, positive and
negative contexts alter affirmative response rates, with contexts generated by a model and
assessed by human annotators Feng (2024). Some contextual changes legitimately change a
causal claim. A policy that affects demand in one regulatory regime may have no effect in
another. A robustness test should either hold the target world fixed or declare the changed
world and its new truth. Scoring every changed answer as instability would conflate semantic
responsiveness with error.
   Jiralerspong and colleagues use breadth-first organization to reduce graph construction calls
Jiralerspong et al. (2024). This offers an engineering alternative to asking about every pair
separately. Call complexity is not total resource cost. A call that lists many nodes may have
a growing prompt and response, require retries, or depend on a long context. A complete
comparison must record input and output tokens, wall time, cache policy, model cost, failure
frequency and the review time needed to adjudicate proposals. Rejecting a cycle is useful
structural validation, but does not make the remaining acyclic graph true.


33.3     Response tests are not sampling-law independence tests
Cohrs and colleagues investigate language-model judgments in a constraint-based discovery
workflow Cohrs et al. (2024). This is a different mechanism from applying a conditional-
independence test to observed bank records. For example, the statement X ⊥⊥ Y | Z is a claim
about a distribution. A model’s frequency of saying “YES” to that statement is a property
of a prompted response process. Even a correctly estimated response probability does not
establish the distributional statement.
  Static inspection of the pinned causal_GPT source shows a further issue that can be examined
without making any model calls. Its response aggregation counts YES and NO within the
33.4. Retrieval, constraints and soft priors                                                  333


same response collection. The inspected test forms proportions pbN = NN /n and pbY = NY /n,
pools them as pb = (NN + NY )/(2n), and uses the denominator
                                                   s
                                                       2pb(1 − pb)
                                         sbind =                   .                       (33.1)
                                                            n

The formula resembles an independent two-proportion standard error. Its interpretation needs
the actual sampling relationship between the counts.
  Consider the deliberately simple project response model in which independent draws take
values NO, YES or OTHER, with probabilities pN , pY , pO . Let IN and IY be indicators for
the first two categories in one draw. The categories are mutually exclusive, so

                                       Cov(IN , IY ) = −pN pY .

Consequently the exact variance of the difference of the sample proportions is

                                                   pN + pY − (pN − pY )2

This elementary calculation is a project derivation under the stated independent categorical
law. It is not a claim that actual model calls are independent or stationary.
   Under the binary symmetric response null pN = pY = 1/2, the true variance is 1/n, √   whereas
the square of Equation (33.1) is 1/(2n). The denominator is too small by a factor 2. For
n = 100 and a nominal one-sided level of 0.01, summing the exact binomial probabilities
over the inspected formula’s rejection region gives approximately 0.044313. The calculation
enumerates all counts with their rational binomial probabilities; it does not simulate responses
or execute the downloaded implementation.
   Correcting this variance would address one response-model issue. It would not convert
language judgments into a bank conditional-independence test. Real calls may share context,
cached outputs, decoding artifacts or a changing backend. The source also converts the
response decision to a numerical zero or one at the independence-test interface. Those values
need a type that exposes their meaning. Passing them through an API named “pvalue” cannot
confer sampling-law calibration.
   In a funding example, repeated model agreement that customer risk is unrelated to pricing
conditional on branch does not validate the bank’s assignment law. The remedy is to separate
a language-evidence object from a numerical test object. The former can carry source anchors,
answer frequencies and unresolved scientific questions. The latter must identify its observations,
null, sampling assumptions and calibration. Neither object should silently replace the other.


33.4      Retrieval, constraints and soft priors
Retrieval changes the information available to a model. It may supply an operational definition
or an expert restriction that the numerical data cannot identify. It can also supply irrelevant
or contradictory evidence. Zhang and colleagues’ retrieval-assisted method reports mixed
results: in the inspected ASIA setting, documents reduce skeleton F1 from 1 to 0.73, while
other settings benefit Zhang et al. (2024). The result argues for keeping retrieval conditions
visible in a comparison, rather than labeling retrieval as a uniform improvement.
   The reported orientation accuracy in that work is evaluated on recovered true-positive edges.
Its denominator excludes missing or false edges. For a reader deciding whether a graph is
useful for intervention, skeleton error and orientation error both matter. A system must report
334                                                          Causal analysis for a universal bank


the metric and its denominator before drawing a conclusion about the full graph. Downstream
effect behavior remains a separate outcome.
  A retrieved statement may concern an ancestral path rather than direct adjacency. Ban
and colleagues elicit ancestral constraints and use soft penalties alongside numerical scores
Ban et al. (2023). In a chain A → M → Y , A is an ancestor of Y even when no direct A → Y
edge exists. If an adapter turns “can affect” into “directly causes,” it changes the scientific
input. Path, adjacency, temporal-order and exclusion constraints therefore need different
representations and conversion tests.
   Hard constraints delete graphs. If a wrong constraint removes the true graph, increasing the
numerical sample does not restore it within the constrained search. Darvariu and colleagues
investigate soft language-derived priors that retain support for possible graphs Darvariu et al.
(2024). In schematic form, one can write a search objective as
                           b λ ∈ arg max{S(D, G) + λL(T, M, G)},
                           G                                                              (33.3)
                                      G

where S is a numerical score, L a language-derived preference and λ a declared strength. This
notation is a common project comparison device; the actual score and statistical assumptions
must be taken from the chosen method.
   Positive prior support prevents one particular failure: a graph is not logically excluded
solely because a model dislikes it. A large wrong preference can still dominate weak numerical
evidence. Subsequent pruning can again remove the relevant graph. The inspected experiments
include selected combined gains and cases where standalone priors harm performance. A useful
evaluation fixes the prior rule, compares λ = 0, varies evidence quality and preserves every
failed setting. Tuning λ after viewing the final test graphs invalidates a simple interpretation
of the reported comparison.
   Takayama and colleagues instead feed statistical discovery information into language prompts,
then convert response probabilities into forced, forbidden or unknown constraints for particular
algorithms Takayama et al. (2024). The conversion differs across PC, exact search and
DirectLiNGAM. Their inspected examples contain both gains and failures and caution against
treating the procedure as an opaque automatic solution. A bootstrap frequency, a response
frequency and a posterior model probability are three different objects. A user interface should
not place them under one unqualified confidence label.
   Statistical prompting also raises a data-reuse issue. If D determines the initial graph
summary and that summary shapes the language restriction, the restriction is a function of D.
A later fit cannot casually treat it as independent external evidence. This does not make every
such procedure invalid; it changes the procedure that must be justified or evaluated. Tracking
data hashes and the full adaptive rule makes the reuse visible. Sample splitting may help a
particular construction, but it neither proves the restriction true nor automatically supplies
valid downstream uncertainty.


33.5     Debate, disagreement and scientific evidence
The multi-agent discovery approach of Le and colleagues assigns different roles to language
agents and uses their interaction to construct a graph Le et al. (2024). This can organize
critique and expose alternative stories. Its inspected assumptions exclude hidden confounding
and cycles, and the reported canonical benchmark scale is limited. Those conditions should
remain attached to a banking interpretation.
  Several agents need not provide several independent pieces of evidence. They may use the
same model family, encounter overlapping training material, or retrieve the same article. A
33.6. Graph ambiguity and the target effect                                                      335


majority can therefore amplify a common error. Disagreement is useful as a review signal,
but agreement cannot be converted to a causal confidence interval without a model of the
information and dependence involved.
   For servicing, one agent may propose that a contact causes distress, another that distress
causes contact, and a critic may resolve the conflict by choosing the more plausible story.
A more defensible workflow keeps both candidates, asks which timestamp and assignment
evidence would distinguish them, and identifies the effects under each. A later scientific owner
may supply an applicable restriction. The agent’s role is to formulate the unresolved question
and retrieve the evidence, not to manufacture the answer.
   Candidate remedies include comparing one-agent and multi-agent conditions, using the same
numerical evidence and total budget, and clustering evaluation results by shared mechanism
rather than counting paraphrased prompts as independent cases. These are proposed tests.
No multi-agent trial has been executed here, and diversity of models alone does not verify
assumptions.


33.6      Graph ambiguity and the target effect
A graph matters because it changes the interpretation of an intervention. Suppose an observed
distribution P is compatible with a class G. For a target Q, let ΘG (P, Q) contain the effects
allowed by the distribution and assumptions under G. The scientifically relevant target set is
                                                   [
                                    ΘG (P, Q) =          ΘG (P, Q).                           (33.4)
                                                   G∈G

This is a definition, not a claim that the set has been computed or that a learned class covers
the truth. An unrestricted member can make the union unrestricted. A point estimate from
the most fluent graph narrative would answer a different, more strongly conditioned question.
  The project’s two-variable example makes this concrete. Under model F, A ∼ Bernoulli(1/2)
and Y = A with probability 0.9, with an independent flip otherwise. Under model R the roles
are reversed: Y ∼ Bernoulli(1/2) and A = Y with probability 0.9. Both models yield

                     P (0, 0) = P (1, 1) = 0.45,       P (0, 1) = P (1, 0) = 0.05.

Replacing A’s equation by an intervention gives an average effect of 0.8 under F and zero under
R. In this deliberately finite class the target set is {0, 0.8}. Neither acyclicity nor observational
fit selects the effect. A sufficiently informative scientific time order or intervention could
remove an alternative, but the example intentionally assumes only a coarse shared recording
time.
  The distinction between set identification and confidence in a learned set is equally important.
Let G⋆ be the true graph, Gb a random retained class, and CG a random set for the target

under G. Define C = G∈Gb CG . If the actual joint procedure satisfies

                           Pr(G⋆ ∈

The second premise must refer to the actual procedure; it cannot simply be borrowed from a
fixed-model interval after unaccounted model selection. No independence between the two
336                                                           Causal analysis for a universal bank


events is needed for the bound. Neither premise has been established for arbitrary language-
assisted temporal discovery here. The formula exposes what would have to be supplied, rather
than supplying it.
   CPDAG and PAG representations encode ambiguity that should survive serialization and
explanation. Circle marks, bidirected relations and unoriented edges cannot be replaced with
arrows merely to produce a cleaner diagram. A PAG is not an assertion that every latent
variable has been named. Similarly a finite list of proposed DAGs is not automatically a
complete equivalence class. The declaration validator preserves the marks and the declared
alternatives while delegating full class recognition and identification to a formal engine.


33.7     Temporal discovery is not longitudinal policy inference
The word “sequential” refers to several distinct problems. Verma and colleagues process
successive batches of contemporaneous observations while querying a language model as a
noisy expert and retaining PAG information Verma et al. (2025). The query budget and
answer histograms concern the information supplied to a discovery procedure. They do not
identify the value of a sequence of treatment decisions. Semantic entropy of model answers
does not by itself establish simultaneous graph coverage.
   RealTCD combines language-derived initialization with numerical optimization over temporal
graphs and intervention targets Li (2024). Its setup assumes causal sufficiency, a known
observational regime and an unrolled finite-lag DAG. The inspected theorem conditions its
population optimization result on model capacity, intervention faithfulness, positivity and
finite entropy. A stochastic optimizer with a thresholded adjacency matrix requires additional
analysis before it can inherit any finite-sample guarantee.
   The real cooling-system study does not have a complete ground-truth DAG. It uses selected
expert physical-location rules to assess edges. That is useful domain evidence but a different
evaluation from full known-truth graph recovery. The method also models abnormal windows
as intervention regimes. In a bank, a sudden spread movement could reflect a common market
shock, a changed selection mechanism or measurement failure. Treating it as an exogenous
intervention requires substantive evidence, not a threshold crossing.
  Kougioulis and colleagues’ Large Causal Model is an adjacent numerical transformer rather
than a language-model wrapper Kougioulis et al. (2026). Its inspected scope includes additive-
noise, stationary, causally sufficient, lagged-only systems. These conditions can be useful for a
declared class; they exclude several concerns in private banking states and common shocks.
The external pretrained weights have not been audited or executed locally. A language interface
should not rename this restricted temporal predictor as a general latent-graph solution.
   For longitudinal servicing, the analyst instead needs a sequence of decisions, available
histories, treatment-confounder feedback, censoring and a value target. A graph of temporal
dependence is only one ingredient. The intermediate account state can be affected by an earlier
action while confounding a later action’s effect. The correct question and inferential law must
be specified before an agent chooses an estimator. None of the inspected temporal discovery
results closes the project’s general latent temporal effect-set problem.
33.8. New interventions, mechanism proposals and information value                             337


33.8     New interventions, mechanism proposals and information
         value
Lampinen and colleagues show how passive learning from expert demonstrations can support
active causal strategies Lampinen (2023). Their constructive argument first acquires causal
information through experiments, then exploits it. The evaluated learner can intervene in
its test environment. This is a valuable qualification: passive training is compatible with
active information acquisition, but the new interventions supply information that an analyst
restricted to historical bank records may lack.
  The inspected empirical settings use small finite acyclic systems and constrained observations
and actions. A banking translation must specify which interventions are feasible, who can
