authorize them, their costs and their effect on future information. Merely asking a model
another question is not an intervention on the customer or the funding market. The two
actions have different likelihoods, costs and ethical or operational constraints.
   Murphy’s Model Discovery Agent proposes executable mechanisms with an LLM and fits
and compares them numerically Murphy (2026). The inspected studies include algebraic
mechanisms, latent ODEs and stochastic latent dynamics. The LLM expands the candidate
library; BIC or SMC approximations provide model evidence, and a model-disagreement
surrogate approximates expected information gain for experiment selection.
   This architecture gives each component a clearer role than requesting a final effect directly
from the model. It also exposes new obligations. An adaptive library may omit the true
mechanism. Pruning can discard a mechanism that would become useful later. BIC weights
within a retained pool are conditional model weights, not uniform graph-confidence statements.
Residual checks can reveal some misspecification but cannot certify that no policy-relevant
mechanism is absent.
   The paper explicitly states that its finite held-out prediction tests do not establish causal
identification. The experiments use open-loop policies, and the reported comparisons focus
on sample efficiency rather than matched total compute. The chemistry comparison retains
matched evaluable cells from a larger attempted collection. Those denominators must ac-
company the gains. For a bank, the value of information is the expected improvement in an
actual decision after paying acquisition and implementation costs. Information gain within a
model pool can be a design surrogate, but it is not that monetary quantity without an explicit
connection to the bank’s loss.


33.9      An auditable discovery interface
Zheng and colleagues describe causal-learn+ with agents assisting data inspection, assumption
elicitation, tool choice and interpretation around a formal discovery core Zheng (2026). They
emphasize separate objects for suggestions, user decisions, algorithm settings and graph outputs.
The design is a useful default for a banking library because it makes changes to scientific input
visible. It is not a universal impossibility result for hybrid discovery; a hybrid can be evaluated
as its own fully specified method.
  CausalAgent supplies another conversational architecture, including MCP tool interfaces
Zhu et al. (2026). Static source review finds that an inspected OLC tool calls a function
not imported or defined in that module, and a parser can return an empty dictionary after
malformed JSON. These are integration findings about pinned source, not measurements of a
running service. They show why transport success, parse success and scientific success need
separate dispositions. A successful model message is not a valid graph.
338                                                           Causal analysis for a universal bank


  For each request, an auditable interface should retain the business target, variable definitions
and clocks, numerical-data identity, retrieved-source identity, model and prompt version,
proposal, applied restrictions, selected algorithm and returned graph class. A reviewer should
be able to distinguish an expert’s asserted exclusion from an algorithmic orientation and from
a model’s suggestion. Changed restrictions create a new analysis identity; they should not
overwrite the prior result invisibly.
   Failure recovery must preserve scientific meaning as well as computation. If a job stops
after producing a partial graph, replay must not publish it as a complete answer. If a source
or data hash changes, an earlier identification claim cannot simply be reused. A report should
expose a refused or unknown effect when that is the formal outcome. The completed local
operation contract provides a bounded implementation surface; new discovery adapters still
need their own source, semantic and execution qualification.


33.10      What would establish useful progress
A meaningful comparison begins with a fixed question and information set. The numerical
baseline, language-only baseline, retrieval condition, hybrid and agent-assisted workflow should
receive explicitly matched information or have their information advantage declared. Accuracy
on familiar graphs is only one outcome. The study also needs identification correctness,
retention of compatible alternatives, valid abstention, effect-set coverage where a guarantee is
claimed, interval or set width, decision loss and full cost.
   Every request belongs in the denominator. Failed parsing, unavailable models, timeouts,
nonidentification and legitimate refusals have different meanings and should be recorded
separately. A graph metric conditional on successful requests can be informative, but it must
accompany the success probability and the selection rule. A narrow accurate set emitted only
in easy cases is not the same product as one that delivers useful valid output reliably.
  The proposed remedies are correspondingly bounded. Novel labels test one shortcut;
counterevidence tests retrieval dependence; correctly typed constraints prevent a specific
semantic conversion; fixed prompts and budgets make an experiment reproducible; and
preserved graph classes prevent one form of overstatement. None of these repairs creates
missing bank assignment truth, resolves observational equivalence by itself, or proves arbitrary
dependent-sample calibration.
   The immediate adoption position is therefore to use language assistance for explicit proposals
and reviewable workflow support, while qualifying each hybrid method separately. The original
unresolved temporal graph and useful precision results remain unresolved. New scientific
information, stronger assumptions justified in a declared regime, or additional experiments
may change those conclusions. More fluent explanations alone cannot.


33.10.1     Temporal predictions and interventions on conversations

A time series can support a useful prediction without identifying a useful intervention. The
distinction remains necessary when a language model produces a graph and an accompanying
explanation. Augur offers a concrete example: a teacher model proposes relations between
covariates, a student learns from selected explanations, and the downstream task predicts a
future trend. The inspected preprint evaluates air, power, traffic and finance settings, using
classification F1 and AUROC for prediction. These are relevant forecasting outcomes; they do
not estimate the value of a deposit rate change or a sequence of servicing actions. Zhiqing Cui,
Binwu Wang, Qingxiang Liu, Yeqiang Wang, Zhengyang Zhou, Yuxuan Liang and Yang Wang
33.10. What would establish useful progress                                                    339


(2025)


What a temporal graph proposal establishes

Augur first retains highly correlated pairs using Spearman ranks, asks a language model to
choose among directed, confounded and spurious relationships, and repairs graph cycles. Its
stability score measures agreement across candidate graphs. Its groundedness score checks
that a summary agrees with the graph from which it was generated. Each component has a
clear engineering purpose, but the latter two can be high when all candidates share the same
wrong causal premise. Acyclicity is a structural property; agreement with one’s own graph is
an internal consistency property. Zhiqing Cui, Binwu Wang, Qingxiang Liu, Yeqiang Wang,
Zhengyang Zhou, Yuxuan Liang and Yang Wang (2025)
   The authors explicitly acknowledge causal sufficiency and the possibility that correlation
pruning misses nonlinear or lagged dependence. Asking the model to output “confounded’ ’
does not independently demonstrate hidden-state identification. Nor does a chronological
train/test split create exchangeability of a proposed action. In a deposit application, funding
cost and deposit outflow may respond to an unobserved liquidity shock. A predictor can
exploit that relationship while remaining unable to answer what outflow would have been
under a different offered rate.
   The proposal should retain this architecture as a forecasting and hypothesis generation
comparator. A causal evaluation needs a separate target and separate truth: for example,
generated lagged mechanisms with known interventions, omitted common causes and nonlinear
dependence deliberately missed by marginal screening. Report predictive performance and
intervention performance separately. A failure of intervention recovery can coexist with a
useful forecast and should lead to a restricted product role, rather than erasing the forecast
result or relabeling it as policy evidence.


A directly relevant longitudinal method

Zhang, Wang and Dhillon study sequences of human edits and model replies. Their Causal-
Collab method proposes an Incremental Stylistic Effect (ISE), uses a conditional variational
autoencoder to represent editing styles, and combines a fitted outcome model with Monte
Carlo evaluation of a longitudinal functional. Their identification theorem explicitly assumes
sequential exchangeability and positivity for the style interventions. Thus there is a concrete
literature route for studying longitudinal human–LM collaboration; its existence should not be
obscured by a search that returns mostly generic causal-inference papers. Bohan Zhang, Yixin
Wang and Paramveer S. Dhillon (2024)
  For clarity, let Lt denote information presented before editing step t, At the human edit, and
Ht = (L̄t , Āt−1 ) the recorded history. A potential terminal outcome is Y (āT ). Exchangeability
requires the recorded history to remove the common causes of the edit and its downstream
outcome. An analyst’s private customer knowledge, skill or intention can violate this require-
ment even when every message has been logged. The low dimensionality of a style score also
does not establish overlap: legally required text may allow little variation in some histories,
and certain kinds of edit may never occur for distressed customers.
   The source defines the outcome associated with a style functional through a conditional
mixture over text versions having that style. This matters for implementation. A learned
coordinate and an instruction such as “make this more reassuring’ ’ need not describe the same
intervention. A model can make a response more reassuring by changing tone, by promising
compensation, or by omitting a warning. Those changes can have different effects and costs.
340                                                             Causal analysis for a universal bank


Before adopting the estimand, the proposal must specify which distribution of complete edits
implements the change and which content must be held fixed.
   Consider a second project-generated reference example. Two proposed messages receive
the same “polite’ ’ label. Their stipulated response probabilities are 1/5 and 4/5, while the
reference message has response probability 1/10. Suppose an editing policy selects the second
message with probability q. Its effect against the reference is

                                       1   4  1    1  3
                                (1 − q) + q −   =    + q.
                                       5   5 10   10 5
   The effects are 1/10, 2/5, 7/10 at q = 0, 1/2, 1, respectively, despite an identical style label.
These are exact values under an invented law, not observed customer effects. They show
why the mixture is part of the intervention definition. A randomized choice among fixed text
variants is a substantive alternative to inferring a latent stylistic effect. It has a narrower
target but makes treatment versions directly inspectable.


What the available evidence leaves open

CausalCollab constructs counterfactual edits with ChatGPT, uses model-assigned outcome
labels, and changes the association between a confounding signal and the outcome in its
evaluation data. Its three sources include human–model collaborative writing, model self-chat,
and a hybrid dialogue setting. They should not all be described as independently observed
human intervention outcomes. Performance under this constructed design is useful evidence
about that design, but is not a direct measurement of how real users would have responded to
unchosen edits. Bohan Zhang, Yixin Wang and Paramveer S. Dhillon (2024)
   This supports an affordable proposal-stage evaluation. Begin with public or generated
interaction histories, fix a small set of content-preserving edit policies, and expose the evaluator
to known latent intentions and missing history in deliberately adverse cases. Compare a
fixed editing policy, an observed-association rule, a correctly specified numerical longitudinal
method, and the proposed representation-based method. Keep the true generator inaccessible
to the method. Assess policy-value error, support, refusal and total review effort, in addition
to language quality. Generated labels should be identified as such and their sensitivity to a
second label rule should be reported.
   A live human or bank experiment becomes valuable when this work identifies a consequential
uncertainty that the generated law cannot answer. It is not a prerequisite for specifying the
architecture or exposing its failure mechanisms. Conversely, neither the inspected theorem
nor a generated experiment entitles the proposal to claim identification under unrecorded
human intentions. Direct replication still requires review of the exact representation training,
integration scheme, outcome labels and source-code versions.
Chapter 34

Choosing the next experiment:
information, decisions and agent
limits

An agent that proposes a plausible causal diagram has not yet answered the bank’s next
question: which additional observation could change a worthwhile decision? A diagram may
contain a dozen unresolved arrows, although only one uncertainty affects whether a particular
retention offer should be deployed. Conversely, an apparently stable effect estimate can conceal
a decisive measurement or selection problem. Experiment selection therefore connects problem
formulation, causal discovery and investment analysis. Its purpose is to spend a limited
information budget on distinctions that matter, while preserving the possibility that none of
the proposed experiments is useful.
   The proposed role of a language model is to formulate competing mechanisms, translate
a question into an admissible design menu, locate observations that could distinguish the
mechanisms, and explain the resulting numerical comparison. A statistical component must
evaluate the observation laws and decision losses. A language model’s confidence, the number
of agreeing agents, and the novelty of an experiment description are inadequate substitutes for
those calculations. This chapter develops that separation using inspected primary literature,
concrete public software interfaces, and an exact banking planning example. The example
establishes a property of its stipulated law; it does not measure language-model ability or the
value of a bank experiment.


34.1     Three different meanings of an experimental action
A real intervention changes an admissible treatment or environment and obtains an outcome
under that change. A simulator experiment changes an input in a specified mathematical world.
A model or expert query obtains an answer from a fallible information source. All three can be
sequential actions, but their observation laws have different meanings. A simulator can reveal
its own response to an offer without establishing the response of depositors. An expert can
state that a variable precedes another without supplying a randomized treatment assignment.
Neither operation becomes a bank intervention because an agent calls it an experiment.
   Let θ index a candidate mechanism, D the information available before design selection,
d ∈ D(D) an admissible acquisition, and Od its returned observation. A Bayesian design
calculation requires p(Od | θ, d, D) and a distribution π(θ | D). For a physical experiment, the
former must represent assignment, adherence, measurement, missingness and the outcome

                                              341
342                                                           Causal analysis for a universal bank


clock. For a simulated experiment, it is the generator’s observation law. For an expert query,
it is an answer error model, potentially conditional on wording, context and common source
material. Estimating a histogram of repeated answers measures a query distribution; without
additional calibration it does not identify the probability that an asserted causal arrow is
correct.
   Consider a bank deciding whether to offer a fee waiver to a defined group of depositors. The
target is incremental 90-day stable-balance value, net of the waiver, contact and funding costs,
relative to the existing policy. Define the population before contact, use only its pre-contact
information for eligibility, and distinguish the offer from acceptance of the offer. A proposed
prospective study would need an assignment rule and a way to observe both withdrawals and
account closure. A historical query about customers who accepted cannot silently take the
place of that study. Selection, interference across accounts and changes in market rates could
each invalidate the proposed observation law.
   The information clock is as consequential as the treatment clock. A design chosen today
may produce a 90-day outcome before a later cohort’s deployment decision; it cannot inform
today’s irreversible decision before that outcome exists. Transport from the study cohort to
the deployment cohort is then an additional assumption. Delay and the value of waiting belong
in the cost calculation. Public or generated data can test whether an agent respects these
distinctions now, even when conducting the prospective bank experiment would be premature.


34.2     What the primary literature supports

34.2.1    Learning a strategy does not remove its information requirements

Lampinen and colleagues study whether agents can acquire active causal strategies from passive
demonstrations. The positive finding concerns learning how to investigate from examples
of competent investigation. At evaluation, the learner can act and obtain the consequences
needed by the task. Passive training is therefore compatible with active information acquisition;
it is not evidence that an observationally unidentified effect becomes identified without new
assumptions or observations. The paper’s finite graphs and constrained action and observation
spaces also limit transfer to a bank with latent customer states, delayed outcomes and restricted
actions Lampinen (2023).
   This distinction suggests a useful proposal component. Demonstration traces can teach
an agent to ask for the outcome horizon, request a missing assignment variable, or select a
discriminating synthetic intervention. Their training value should be evaluated separately
from the information supplied by the eventual environment. A comparison should hold that
environment and its acquisition budget fixed, and include a numerical or rule-based design
policy that receives the same history. Otherwise a more informative interface can be mistaken
for a better reasoner.
   Verma and colleagues provide a different example: sequential causal discovery with a
language model treated as a noisy expert. Their method combines batches of observational
data with background information obtained through a fixed budget of model queries, using
partial ancestral graphs to retain relevant latent-confounding ambiguity. The inspected
evaluation compares query allocation with random edge selection and reports improvements
in graph metrics. This is evidence about the tested graph-learning setup, not a physical
intervention or a measured gain from a lending decision. Sequential arrival of data batches also
does not by itself supply the treatment-history assumptions required by longitudinal causal
inference Verma et al. (2025).
34.2. What the primary literature supports                                                  343


   The paper identifies open questions that directly affect deployment: the uncertainty over
candidate graphs, calibration of language-model answers, more complex latent confounding,
the incorporation of interventions and sequential theoretical analysis. These limits argue for
retaining ambiguous graphs and for pricing questions according to their possible effect on the
decision. Repeated model answers may share training information and reasoning errors. An
empirical answer frequency is useful operational evidence, but the product should not multiply
it into independent scientific confirmation.


34.2.2    Model discovery and numerical design: gains with important excep-
          tions

The inspected version of Model Discovery Agent combines model proposals with numerical
model comparison and experimental design. Candidate mechanistic models are fit to observa-
tions, and a design component seeks experiments whose predictions distinguish the current
candidates. The paper discusses Bayesian model evidence, approximations including BIC,
sequential Monte Carlo, and disagreement-based surrogates for expected information gain.
Depending on the design space, its implementation uses numerical optimization or evaluates a
finite menu. This combination offers a concrete reason to use a language model: it can propose
representations and mechanisms that a fixed estimator does not enumerate, while numerical
components fit and compare the proposals Murphy (2026).
  The favorable evidence needs its stated denominator and comparison budget. The paper
reports experiments in chemistry, glucose dynamics and neuronal systems; its chemistry
aggregate uses 115 matched evaluable world–seed cells from 171 attempted cells over 54 worlds.
This is a conditional comparison over evaluable cells, not a claim that all attempts succeeded.
The paper also explicitly distinguishes sample efficiency from a compute-matched comparison.
Extra model proposals, optimization, fitting and retries may consume substantial resources
even when fewer environment queries are used. A bank investment argument must record
both kinds of expenditure.
  Adverse findings sharpen the design recommendation. In the paper’s source-location
experiment, a greedy joint-variance heuristic performs worse than random selection, and the
model-information criterion does not show an advantage over random design in that domain.
A numerical-looking acquisition score is therefore not a guarantee of improved information
gathering. The observation model, candidate pool, approximation error and accessible design
menu all affect whether the score is useful. Random and fixed designs remain substantive
baselines; they are not merely weak comparators to be discarded once an agent is available.
  A further limitation is support. Normalized weights over the proposed models sum to one
even when every model omits the mechanism that generated the data. Pruning can make
apparent confidence increase while removing a useful alternative. For the bank, candidate
mechanisms should include policy selection, timing error, measurement changes and null effects
where relevant. An agent should be able to propose a new mechanism after a failed predictive
check. Such revision needs an evaluation rule that prevents unlimited post hoc repairs from
making every hypothesis unfalsifiable.


34.2.3    Scientific judgment, research state and the missing validation step

DISCERN tests a complementary problem: whether agents carry evidence limitations through
scientific reasoning. Its 203 canonical life-science tasks comprise 79 data-integrity tasks, 102
analysis-verification tasks and 22 hypothesis-generation dossiers, across eight tracks and eight
evaluated models. The three levels are independently instantiated and scored. Their outputs
344                                                             Causal analysis for a universal bank


are not passed through an evaluated end-to-end research pipeline. For a counterfactual dossier,
eligibility depends on eliciting a model prior that conflicts with the supplied evidence Huang
et al. (2026).
   The reported perfect-score rates are 60.8%, 34.2% and 0.6% at the three levels under
their respective rubrics. These are rubric-specific evaluation percentages, not probabilities of
discovering a true mechanism or choosing a profitable experiment. The grading uses human-
designed criteria, deterministic checks with language-model verification and adjudication for
the first two levels, and rubric-based judgment for hypotheses. Three draws of a judging
procedure do not amount to three independent institutions validating an experimental result.
The authors identify task dependence, possible familiarity with public data and residual
grading uncertainty, and do not establish whether the proposed hypotheses lead to useful
follow-up experiments.
   For banking, the relevant failure mechanism is precise. An agent can correctly say that
offer acceptance is selected, yet subsequently recommend deploying the offer as though the
observed acceptance–balance association were a causal effect. Merely counting whether the
word “confounding” appears in a report misses that failure. A useful evaluation checks whether
the limitation changes the next action, narrows the claim, or produces abstention. It also needs
clean controls: an agent that rejects every dataset can appear cautious while destroying valid
opportunities. The proposed experiment-selection evaluation should score both unwarranted
deployment and unnecessary rejection.
   Discovery Foundation Models proposes an explicit, revisable research state, with representa-
tions, hypotheses, evidence, experiment choices and transferable research skills as objects that
can change. Its Zetema description separates proposed expectations from external outcomes
and calls for attributing a failure before promoting a lesson to reusable memory. This is a
useful architectural principle: an invalid measurement should revise the observation model,
whereas a failed mechanistic prediction may require a new hypothesis Yang et al. (2026).
   The report’s GALILEO discussion describes a structured therapeutic-discovery case and
explicitly locates specialized human-executed assays inside the coupled system. It does not
establish a general-purpose discovery system or broad transfer across domains. The underlying
biomedical original is outside the inspected evidence used here, so the account informs the
proposed architecture without independently validating its biological results. Adopting a
revisable state representation is consequently a design choice; claiming that the proposed bank
agent improves scientific discovery would require a separate controlled evaluation.


34.3      A decision criterion with an explicit option to stop
Let a ∈ A denote a deployment decision and u(a, θ) its incremental value, expressed in a
common unit and at a specified horizon. The value of acting with existing information is

                                   V (D) = max E[u(a, θ) | D].
                                              a∈A

If acquisition d costs c(d, D), its one-step net value is
                                                           
               G(d | D) = EOd |d,D max E[u(a, θ) | D, Od , d] − V (D) − c(d, D).             (34.1)
                                        a∈A

Acquisition is worthwhile under this model only if its best admissible net value is positive.
Costs can include the experiment itself, failed attempts, waiting, analyst effort and computa-
tion. Combining per-customer value with a whole-study cost requires an explicit deployment
population or amortization; otherwise the comparison has inconsistent units.
34.3. A decision criterion with an explicit option to stop                                 345


  Expected information gain asks a different question. For a finite mechanism set, write
H(π) = − θ πθ log2 πθ . Then
         P


                      I(d | D) = H{π(· | D)} − EOd |d,D H{π(· | D, Od , d)}.

This criterion can be appropriate when learning the mechanism is itself the objective. It need
not prioritize uncertainty that changes a particular decision. The target of information gain
matters: information about a nuisance parameter, an effect sign and a full dynamic model
need not have the same economic value. A remedy is to use a decision-relevant target or
evaluate Equation (34.1) directly, while examining the sensitivity of both to their assumed
likelihoods and losses.


34.3.1     An exact fee-waiver planning construction

Suppose two binary variables H and Z index four equally likely planning worlds. H represents
whether the fee-waiver policy is valuable; Z is an independent nuisance feature of the envi-
ronment. Relative to abstention, deploying has value USD 100 when H = 1 and USD −120
when H = 0. Abstention has value zero in either world. These are stipulated, already net
deployment values per normalized deployment decision, not measured customer effects. Each
information acquisition costs USD 5 in the same normalized units. The calculation assumes
that its observation is available before the deployment decision and that the world remains
relevant to that decision Causal banking proposal project (2026a).
   With prior probability p = Pr(H = 1) = 1/2, expected deployment value is 100p − 120(1 −
p) = 220p − 120 = −10. The optimal initial action is abstention. The threshold for deployment
is p > 6/11. Perfect information about H would have gross value USD 50, since deployment
would occur only in the good half of the worlds. That USD 50 is an upper bound under the
stipulated model, not a forecast of a feasible experiment’s return.
   Consider two permitted abstract acquisitions. Design dZ reveals Z perfectly. Design dH
returns a signal S ∈ {0, 1} satisfying
                                                           4
                                    Pr(S = H | H, Z, dH ) = .
                                                           5
The signal has conditional error probability 1/5, independent of Z. This accuracy is an assumed
experiment likelihood. It is not a measured accuracy of an LLM, a hypothetical expert panel
or an actual bank trial. Equal acquisition budgets make the comparison transparent: both
designs use one acquisition costing USD 5.
   The first design learns one bit about the full world but leaves the posterior probability
of H at 1/2. The bank still abstains, so net information value is USD −5. For the second
design, each signal has probability 1/2. A positive signal gives posterior 4/5 and expected
deployment value 220(4/5) − 120 = 56. A negative signal gives posterior 1/5 and expected
deployment value −76, so the bank abstains. Expected terminal value is (1/2)56 = 28 and
net value is USD 23. Full-world information gain is only 1 − h2 (1/5) ≃ 0.278 bits, where
h2 (p) = −p log2 p − (1 − p) log2 (1 − p).


       One-acquisition policy                    Information (bits) Gross USD Net USD
       Maximize information about (H, Z)                     1.000              0    −5
       Maximize deployment value                             0.278             28    23
       Uniform random choice of the two                      0.639             14     9
       Do not acquire                                            0              0     0
346                                                          Causal analysis for a universal bank


  The random policy chooses between the two designs with equal probability, so its expected
net value is (−5 + 23)/2 = 9. Its expected information gain also averages the two design gains,
conditional on knowing the selected design. An information criterion targeted specifically at
H would select the useful signal in this example. The construction therefore demonstrates
a mismatch between the full-world learning objective and this deployment objective, rather
than a general failure of information-based design. The values follow from exact finite sums,
independently checked by evaluating the realized payoff of the signal-dependent deployment
policy.


34.3.2    Unavailable observations and correlated answers

Now suppose dH returns no observation with probability 1/4, independently of the world, and
every attempt still costs USD 5. On failure the posterior remains the prior and the bank
abstains. Gross expected value becomes (3/4)28 = 21, and all-attempt net value is USD 16.
Restricting the comparison to successful acquisitions would instead report USD 23. Both
calculations can be arithmetically correct, but they answer different questions. A purchase
or investment decision needs the attempted-work denominator. If failure depends on H, the
failure event itself has a likelihood and must enter the posterior; treating it as independent
missingness would be another model error.
   Repeated agreement introduces a separate problem. Suppose five expert answers are perfectly
correlated because they all copy one underlying noisy answer whose accuracy is 4/5. After five
positive answers, the correct posterior remains 4/5. Incorrectly multiplying five independent
likelihoods would produce
                                        (4/5)5        1024
                                         5       5
                                                   =       .
                                   (4/5) + (1/5)      1025
Different prompts or agent identities do not establish independent error channels. The remedy
is to model the shared source, collect evidence from a different measurement or intervention
when feasible, and compare conclusions under plausible dependence structures. A majority
vote cannot create the missing assignment evidence.


34.3.3    A finite stopping rule and the danger of a narrow model pool

Suppose at most two useful signals are available and their errors are conditionally independent
given H. Always purchasing both gives expected terminal value 148/5 = 29.6 and costs
USD 10, leaving net value 98/5 = 19.6. This is below the one-query value of USD 23. A
conditional calculation verifies the stopping decision. After a positive first signal, the best
possible gross increment from a second useful query is 16/5 = 3.2; after a negative signal it is
zero. Both are below its USD 5 cost. A query about Z adds no deployment value at either
history. Thus, for this menu and horizon of at most two, the optimal policy purchases one
useful query and stops. This result does not establish that a myopic stopping rule is optimal
for arbitrary longer horizons or complementary experiments.
   Finally, suppose a proposed model pool contains only H = 1. Its normalized posterior
assigns probability one to good outcomes and predicts USD 100 from deployment. If the
omitted bad world is true, deployment instead yields USD −120. No entropy calculation
confined to the single-model pool detects the omission. The bank therefore needs sensitivity
to model support as well as uncertainty within the pool. Challenging a favorable mechanism
with a null, adverse or selection-based alternative can be more consequential than refining its
parameters. A formal robust recommendation would specify the larger set of admissible laws
and the associated loss criterion; it cannot be inferred merely from an agent having considered
34.4. Public software: what can be reused and what remains a design                          347


several verbal stories.


34.4      Public software: what can be reused and what remains a
          design

34.4.1    GlucoseBench: a useful acquisition and evaluation boundary

The inspected GlucoseBench source is a small adaptation of simglucose for patient-specific
intervention forecasting. Its documented target is the same simulated patient under new
interventions, not generalization to unseen patients or clinical treatment. The maintained
interface supplies two passive training episodes, a menu of available interventions, an observe
operation with a six-episode total budget, and freeze before held-out evaluation. The
inspected evaluator reports failed query cells explicitly; the summary returns no mean score if
any cell in its group failed murphyk (2026a).
   These are useful design patterns for the proposed bank library. A separate evaluator should
retain the generator truth, give the learner only the permitted history and action menu, and
prevent held-out outcomes from steering acquisition. Freezing the acquisition history before
scoring makes an otherwise subtle form of information leakage visible. The in-process object
boundary is explicitly not protection against deliberate introspection; an agent capable of
arbitrary code execution needs a separate process with limited inputs for an adversarial leakage
test.
   The root MIT notice and the vendored simglucose notice are present, and the project
provides attribution and upstream/vendored file hashes. Those records make a future audit
feasible; the inspected manifest is not an independent verification of every upstream byte or a
complete dependency and data-rights review. The physiological mechanism has no claimed
validity for depositors. The immediate recommendation is to adopt the acquisition/evaluation
contract in the bank proposal, and evaluate any actual package reuse separately with its
pinned source, numerical environment and observation semantics.


34.4.2    NeuronBench: explicit experiments with hidden operational fallbacks

NeuronBench exposes deterministic and stochastic neuronal worlds, a protocol menu and
held-out intervention forecasts. Its documented distinction between observed traces and
hidden mechanism truth illustrates how an environment can support active discovery without
showing its answers to the learner. The inspected source also includes a reference LLM
baseline with an injected client. That baseline is explicitly not Bayesian inference or numerical
value-of-information optimization murphyk (2026b).
   A source-level detail affects any comparison that reuses the baseline. If an experiment
response cannot be parsed, the implementation chooses the first remaining protocol. If a
forecast cannot be parsed, it returns the mean observed count, or zero without observations.
These behaviors keep the procedure running but change the meaning of its output. A reported
“LLM-selected” design may actually be a deterministic fallback. The proposed adapter must
therefore expose the attempted query, parse outcome, substituted action, retry cost and
downstream result. A useful ablation compares this fallback-only policy with the model-
assisted policy under equal environment budgets. Errors should count in the assigned workload,
while any successful-only estimate receives its own explicit denominator.
   The pinned project declares version 0.1.0, a Python requirement and an MIT license. Its
reference interface is a candidate for an optional public simulator study; no package was
348                                                           Causal analysis for a universal bank


installed or executed for this source comparison. Porting its neurophysiological equations into
the bank library would add an unrelated model. Reusing an isolated environment interface, or
implementing the same interface for a transparent generated bank law, is the more relevant
proposal choice. Neither route establishes that the full Model Discovery Agent has been
integrated.


34.4.3    DFM-Plans and unresolved implementation identities

The inspected DFM-Plans repository describes itself as an overview, research map and
navigation point. Its README calls Zetema a research design and states that individual
implementations are released in separate repositories. The pinned, nontruncated tree contains
documentation and assets. Consequently, this repository is unsuitable as a directly executable
Zetema causal agent. Its Apache-2.0 notice applies to the inspected repository; it does not
confer the rights or capabilities of separately linked projects Gen-Verse (2026).
   ScienceBuddy, ScienceIDE and JEPA-Anything are implementation leads from that overview,
not inspected capability evidence in this comparison. Likewise, the benchmark repositories do
not establish a complete public implementation of the model-discovery method, and dataset
links from the noisy-prior paper do not establish its full agent package. A separately identified
DISCERN task and grading harness would also require source and dataset-rights review. These
distinctions prevent a literature survey from promising integration with software that has not
yet been identified at the required level.
   The source map remains bounded by the stated literature cutoff and explicit omissions.
Relevant originals on psychological hypothesis generation and the scientific method were not
obtained as PDFs from the inspected official routes. Additional chemistry, hidden-structure
and interactive-causality candidates remain uninspected. No technical claim here relies on
their discovery metadata, and no absence or complete-frontier claim follows from those gaps.
The acquired originals and pinned sources support the developed comparisons above while
leaving those further comparisons open Causal banking proposal project (2026b).


34.5     A justified next experiment before an expensive bank
         trial
The immediate empirical question is whether agent assistance improves the translation from a
decision brief to a valid acquisition plan. That can be tested with generated worlds and public
documentation. Begin with a brief that specifies the decision, clock, admissible actions and
loss, but withholds the generator’s mechanism. Compare a fixed design, a uniformly random
design, a numerical information criterion, a numerical decision-value criterion and an optional
agent-assisted proposal policy. The numerical policies need the same candidate mechanisms
and observations as the policy being compared; an oracle with the true mechanism belongs in
a separately labeled reference.
   Vary the challenge along interpretable axes: irrelevant but highly informative measurements,
delayed outcomes, unavailable acquisitions, correlated expert errors, observationally indistin-
guishable models, misspecified model pools and malformed tool responses. Include clean cases
that reward accepting valid information. Evaluate the final decision loss, calibration of stated
probabilities where a probability target exists, the frequency of unsupported causal claims, and
whether constraints actually change the chosen action. Graph accuracy alone cannot establish
investment value.
  Before final sampled runs, freeze the generated laws, held-out families, permitted information,
34.5. A justified next experiment before an expensive bank trial                           349


cost accounting, query and compute budgets, comparators, failure handling and stopping rule.
Report every assigned case and attempted acquisition. If exploratory runs are used to select
prompts or mechanisms, keep them separate from the final comparison. A live model arm
requires its actual version, calls, prices and errors; an offline formulation exercise supports
claims about the design and reference logic only. The exact construction above is already
reproducible without live calls, random draws or an expensive bank intervention.
   A subsequent bank experiment becomes worth considering when the bounded prototype
identifies a consequential uncertainty that public and generated evidence cannot settle. Its
proposal should state which deployment decision could change, the feasible observation law, the
expected reduction in loss, and the complete cost of obtaining that information. If candidate
models remain observationally equivalent under every permitted acquisition, the appropriate
result may be a restricted recommendation or abstention. An agent adds value by recognizing
that limit and specifying the missing measurement or intervention, rather than by presenting
another confident causal narrative.
Chapter 35

Agents across the causal decision
workflow

35.1     A decision contract before an agent architecture
A banking assistant becomes useful when it helps an analyst preserve the meaning of a decision
across several transformations. A treasury question becomes a population and an intervention;
account records become measurements of that population; a diagram becomes an identification
problem; an identified functional becomes a numerical request; and the result becomes a
monetary comparison. Each transformation can change the question without producing a
software error. Fluent explanations are particularly dangerous when they make these changes
hard to notice. The appropriate object of automation is therefore a sequence of accountable
transformations, with explicit unresolved states.
   Consider a request to “reduce the funding cost of the customers likely to leave.” An analyst
must establish whether the intervention is a deposit-rate offer, a service action, or a portfolio
allocation; whether the unit is an account, customer, household, or business group; whether
likely departure is a baseline score or a future outcome; and whether cost includes the offer paid
to customers who would have stayed anyway. An assistant can list these alternatives and attach
relevant contract passages. It cannot establish which alternative the bank intends merely by
selecting the most plausible sentence. A structured interview, conducted without an LLM, is
the comparison baseline. The relevant quality measure is the accuracy and completeness of
the resulting target under expert review, together with analyst time and unresolved-question
rates.
  We represent the decision contract schematically as

                               Q = (P, U, A, g0 , g1 , Y, τ, ν, H, A),

where P is the population, U the unit, A the feasible action, g0 , g1 the comparison regimes, Y
the outcome, τ the horizon, ν the target measure, H the available histories and A the declared
assumptions. An ordinary population mean and a propensity-overlap mean have different ν.
A policy responding at day 11 and one acting at day 10 may have different H, even when they
reference the same event. This tuple is a project specification, not a theorem that every target
is identified. Its purpose is to make semantic changes observable.
   The literature supplies several useful components but no generally qualified substitute for
this contract. Causal discovery assistants can separate user decisions from formal algorithm
outputs; retrieval systems can attach passages; benchmark environments can require structured
identification and estimation answers. These roles have different failure modes and should

                                                350
35.2. Evidence retrieval and the construction of observations                              351


not receive a single undifferentiated “agent accuracy” score Zheng (2026); Zhang et al. (2024);
causalds contributors (2026).


35.2      Evidence retrieval and the construction of observations
Retrieval has two distinct products: a discovered source and a supported claim. A search
result supplies the first. The second requires reading primary text, checking its version and
population, and showing why its assumptions apply to the present query. A banking process
manual may establish when a contact occurs without establishing why customers receive it. A
statistical paper may justify an estimator conditional on exchangeability without establishing
that exchangeability holds in the bank. A source-to-claim relation must therefore record both
the supported statement and the applicability judgment.
   The retrieval baseline is a curated collection reviewed by an analyst. A useful assistant
can broaden candidate discovery, locate conflicting passages and produce an evidence table
for review. Evaluation should include relevant, irrelevant and misleading documents, missing
sources, obsolete versions and sources that contradict each other. Retrieval failure must
remain distinguishable from evidence that a proposed relation is false. The LACR results
discussed in the preceding chapter are a concrete reason not to assume that more retrieved
text monotonically improves discovery Zhang et al. (2024).
   Observation construction is equally substantive. A field called owner_id may identify an
operational account holder rather than the economic owner relevant to exposure aggregation. A
link score is a measurement about a proposed relation, not the relation itself. The observation
journey must retain candidate mappings, inclusion rules, missed records, joint dependence
and the origin of adjudicated labels. Ontology tools can help align terminology, but class
membership and linguistic relations do not identify causal arrows. The inspected OntoLearner
download path also illustrates a reproducibility problem: the code revision alone does not pin
ontology bytes when its hub download does not specify a revision OntoLearner contributors
(2026). The design uses explicit local ontology identities and keeps conceptual variables
separate from their proxies. A real ownership audit remains additional information.
   For time-dependent decisions, every relevant measurement has an event time te and an
availability time ta . An event observed on day 10 but delivered on day 11 cannot be used by a
day-10 operational policy. Retrospective analysis may nevertheless use it under a correctly
stated design; that is a different claim from saying a deployed policy could have acted on it.
Corrections and revisions need their own availability records. A validator checks the declared
ordering. Only a process audit can establish whether those declarations reflect the actual
information system.


35.3      Diagrams, discovery and identification as separate hand-
          offs
Diagram elicitation should preserve competing scientific accounts. A proposal must distinguish
a direct edge from an ancestral path, a latent common cause from a measured covariate, and
a circle endpoint from an arrowhead. Revision history should show which source, reviewer
or new experiment changed a claim. Automatic cycle removal is at most a representation
repair: deleting a scientifically important edge to obtain a DAG does not justify the repaired
mechanism. The ordinary baseline is expert elicitation with a deterministic graph editor and
explicit uncertainty.
352                                                          Causal analysis for a universal bank


   Discovery then asks a statistical question under a specified sampling law. An assistant may
suggest a method, summarize its assumptions, or propose a soft constraint. The numerical
procedure remains responsible for its own output semantics. A response histogram from a
language model is not a conditional independence test under a bank sampling law. A temporal
initialization does not establish that observed anomalies were randomized interventions. A
retained equivalence class should reach the effect-query stage intact. The previous chapter
explains why language-assisted graph methods require separate tests of proposal quality, graph
retention and downstream effect uncertainty.
   Identification maps a target and assumptions to a functional or set. It can also establish
nonidentification in a declared model class. A missing backend, unsupported graph type or
failed calculation instead means that the implementation did not answer the question. These
outcomes are not interchangeable. The inspected CausalDS helper preserves an unknown
state and does not count an IV estimand as nonparametric population-ATE identification; its
evaluator still requires care with missing metadata and invalid intervals causalds contributors
(2026). A prototype should preserve that distinction even when a downstream report would
be easier to write as a single yes/no answer.
   PyWhy-LLM is a candidate elicitation component, but the inspected front-door routine is
unfinished and back-door suggestions delegate to a language model pywhy-llm contributors
(2026). Such output can propose variables for review; it does not supply a verified adjustment
proof. Similarly, the inspected CLadder IV template requires generator-level scrutiny before
its population-ATE labels can become benchmark truth cladder contributors (2024). The
project example with half compliers and half never-takers has Wald ratio one and population
ATE two under randomization, exclusion and monotonicity. Correct algebra for the ratio does
not fix an incorrectly named target.


35.4     Estimation, diagnostics and the temptation to change the
         target
Once identification has supplied a functional, the assistant can prepare a fixed estimator
request, summarize diagnostics and explain the output. It should not choose a more convenient
target after inspecting poor overlap. If trimming changes the population, that change belongs
in a new target or an explicitly reported sensitivity analysis. An estimated propensity score,
nuisance learner, sample split and covariance rule must be versioned together with the result.
Prediction accuracy does not by itself qualify the resulting effect interval, especially with
dependent observations or adaptively selected specifications.
   The inspected OCI example makes the target issue concrete. It averages an AIPW quantity
uniformly over a trimmed sample while using an ATO label oci-agent contributors (2026).
Under the corresponding assumptions this construction targets the retained population’s
average effect, not the usual overlap-weighted population. In the project’s two equally frequent
strata, propensities are 0.2 and 0.5 and effects are 0 and 10. Retaining both strata gives mean
effect 5. Weighting by e(X){1 − e(X)} gives
                             0.16 · 0 + 0.25 · 10   250
                                                  =     ≃ 6.09756.
                                0.16 + 0.25         41
These are exact arithmetic consequences of different target measures, not a performance
comparison of fitted estimators. They give a small independent oracle for a semantic validator.
  Diagnostics need similarly explicit interpretations. A negative control can falsify an impli-
cation of a causal account; passing it does not prove all unmeasured confounding absent. A
35.5. Longitudinal policies require a causal history                                              353


critic can identify a missing source or an inconsistent formula; agreement between two models
exposed to the same text is not independent scientific confirmation. Uncertainty reporting
should preserve identification uncertainty, sampling uncertainty, sensitivity to assumptions
and numerical approximation separately. A disconnected effect set cannot be replaced by its
midpoint, and a whole-line set cannot be described as a precise zero effect. Reporting all
requested cases, including failures and refusals, prevents success-conditioned accuracy from
masquerading as general availability.


35.5      Longitudinal policies require a causal history
Servicing decisions expose the limits of a generic planner particularly clearly. Let L0 be
baseline information, A0 an initial contact, L1 the subsequent account state, A1 a second
action and Y a later net value. The state L1 can be affected by A0 while confounding the
relation between A1 and Y . Ordinary regression adjustment for L1 can block part of the
earlier treatment effect or induce selection bias. Omitting it can confound the later action.
Hernán and Robins develop the corresponding g-methods and the assumptions under which
they identify longitudinal intervention means Hernán and Robins (2020).
  For a discrete two-decision example, write g0 (l0 ) for the first action and g1 (l0 , a0 , l1 ) for
the second. Under consistency, appropriate sequential exchangeability and positivity for the
policy’s supported histories, a specialization of the g-formula is
                                     X
                           V (g) =            m{l0 , g0 (l0 ), l1 , g1 (l0 , g0 (l0 ), l1 )}
                                     l0 ,l1

                                                  × p{l1 | l0 , A0 = g0 (l0 )}p(l0 ),          (35.1)

where m(l0 , a0 , l1 , a1 ) = E[Y | L0 = l0 , A0 = a0 , L1 = l1 , A1 = a1 ]. The sum is over supported
covariate values; an integral is required for continuous components. The first treatment changes
the distribution over which the later outcome regression is averaged. That dependence is why
simply conditioning on a fixed observed distribution of L1 can answer a different question. A
recursive regression representation integrates the final outcome backward, while IP weighting
reweights observed histories toward the regime. Their identification relationship does not
imply equal finite-sample behavior.
   An assistant can help check whether the proposed regime uses available information and
whether the analyst has stated assumptions at each decision. It can propose an evidence
request for treatment assignment, censoring or action feasibility. It cannot infer sequential
exchangeability from the fact that all database columns have timestamps. Causally relevant
history is not simply every past variable; some past variables can induce selection bias, as
the source’s discussion of history emphasizes Hernán and Robins (2020). A policy might also
lack support in distressed segments where staff always take the same action. More generated
explanations do not create that support.
   The availability rule is operationally separate from the identification rule. If the second
decision occurs on day 11, a state available on day 11 may enter g1 under a specified within-day
ordering. If the action occurs on day 10, it may not. A missing within-day ordering must
remain unresolved. Censoring and interference require additional modeling; neither appears
automatically in equation (35.1). The assistant’s proposed handoff therefore includes the
policy, available history, assignment/retention assumptions, support diagnostics and explicit
limits. This is a design for review, not a claim that the current orchestration frameworks
implement qualified longitudinal causal inference.
354                                                            Causal analysis for a universal bank


35.6     What the available packages can contribute
The pinned package comparison separates reusable ideas from ready adoption. PyWhy-LLM
offers candidate elicitation interfaces. CausalAgent illustrates a causal MCP wrapper, but its
inspected OLC function is called without being imported or defined in that module; malformed
JSON may become an empty dictionary in its helper CausalAgent contributors (2026). That
path requires repair and independent qualification before direct use. The response-based test
in causal_GPT is not accepted as a bank CI engine, for the reasons derived in the preceding
chapter causal_GPT contributors (2024).
   OCI’s separation of specifications and reporting is worth evaluating, but its unbounded
notebook-execution route is inappropriate for the proposed fixed-tool surface. CausalDS is a
stronger candidate for a bounded benchmark environment after scorer and metadata handling
are repaired. CLadder remains a useful formal-question lead with problematic IV cells excluded
until reviewed. OntoLearner may assist semantic mapping with explicit local bytes. The
adjacent numerical LCM is neither a language assistant nor a presently qualified temporal
backend: weight identities, component terms and its sufficient lagged model class need separate
treatment LCM contributors (2026).
   The Java/Python research bundle LLM-CD and the LLM-SCD notebooks also illustrate
why publication and code adoption need different decisions. Inspected component licenses
do not establish a license for a repository as a whole; missing root terms and code–paper
version alignment remain unresolved LLM-CD contributors (2025); LLM-and-SCD contributors
(2024). Their scholarly arguments can be discussed from genuine papers while code adoption is
deferred. No package in this comparison is credited with a successful local bank or live-model
trial.


35.7     Orchestration is an implementation choice
Three generic frameworks were inspected at revisions no later than the client cutoff. LangGraph
supplies state-graph compilation, checkpoint and interrupt interfaces. Its interrupt documen-
tation explicitly says that resumption starts the node again, re-executing its preceding logic
langgraph contributors (2026). A node that publishes a result before interrupting therefore
needs idempotent publication. A checkpoint is useful state, not proof that an arbitrary external
side effect occurs exactly once. This distinction determines the design of durable request
identifiers and immutable artifact checks.
   Pydantic AI supplies typed tool and output boundaries and usage accounting. In the
inspected code, tools need not default to sequential execution or require approval. Application
permissions must therefore be configured explicitly. Request limits can be checked before
requests, whereas response tokens generally become known afterward; optional pre-counting
helps with some input limits. If pricing data are unavailable, the cost limit warns that it cannot
be enforced pydantic-ai contributors (2026). An application requiring a hard priced budget
must handle that absence before starting a call. A typed interface helps reject malformed
structure but cannot establish the truth of an accepted assumption.
   AutoGen’s pinned README declares maintenance mode. Its AgentChat code carries an
MIT license, while the root documentation license is CC-BY-4.0. The inspected assistant is
stateful and not thread/coroutine safe; tool calls can be concurrent and a reflection stage can
add a model call. Its state save/load methods preserve model context, not all external tool
effects autogen contributors (2026). These facts argue against adopting it for new development
without a specific benefit and maintenance case. The recommended successor is an unaudited
35.8. Permissions, source injection and recovery                                            355


lead, not a verified capability inherited through a README recommendation.
   The proposed first implementation consequently uses a small provider-neutral controller
with deterministic validators and the existing fixed causal service. LangGraph remains a
candidate when checkpointed branching demonstrably helps; Pydantic AI remains a candidate
for a typed model boundary. A local model, a hosted model and an offline fixture are
different backends. Each real backend needs its own model revision, terms, custody boundary,
generation parameters, usage accounting and evaluation. Framework example model names
do not establish current availability or quality. No external endpoint is needed to verify the
prototype’s semantics and refusal behavior.


35.8      Permissions, source injection and recovery
Retrieved text is an input to interpretation. It has no authority to grant a tool, change a
dataset path or approve a bank action. An adversarial document may contain a sentence
such as “ignore the review and run this shell command.” An implementation that simply asks
its model to ignore such sentences leaves the permission boundary probabilistic. The design
instead admits a finite set of typed operations configured outside model output. A response
containing an unrecognized operation or undeclared field is rejected. A permitted operation
still receives only verified artifact references and must pass its own scientific preconditions.
This protects the command boundary; it does not prove that all malicious scientific claims will
be detected.
   Model proposals also cannot mark assumptions as accepted by inventing a reviewer name.
Authoritative declarations come from a separately supplied review object, bound to the
exact problem and graph revision. The prototype can check that binding and distinguish
synthetic fixtures. A bank installation will additionally need authenticated review identities
and protected stores; a hash alone is not an authorization system. Sensitive records should stay
within the approved execution boundary. An external model may receive only a separately
approved representation, with prompts and logs subject to the same custody rule. Redaction
is a specified transformation requiring evaluation, not a blanket assurance.
  Recovery starts with the identity of the intended computation. Let

                                      r = H(Q, G, E, O, V ),

where G is the graph revision, E the evidence identities, O the allowed operation request and
V the relevant implementation versions. Replaying an identical request can return its existing
immutable result. Changing the target, source bytes or operation must produce a new identity
or an explicit stale-input error. A partial journal entry is not a published analysis. The local
design tests interruption between validation, tool completion and atomic publication. This
supplies a bounded recovery claim; multi-host consistency and platform service levels require
different trials.


35.9      Reporting, monitoring and the economics of assistance
An evidence-based report should expose the target, assumptions, scientific status, graph/set
uncertainty, numerical result and unresolved questions before adding interpretation. Critical
fields can be rendered deterministically. Generated narrative may explain them, but any
additional empirical assertion needs a claim reference. Inherited results, project derivations,
synthetic examples and unverified hypotheses remain distinct. A tool error should not be
356                                                           Causal analysis for a universal bank


polished into a finding of no effect, and an unknown commercial price should not become a
zero in a business case.
   Monitoring must detect when the evidence for a claim becomes stale. Changes in assignment,
missingness, ownership mapping, policy feasibility or availability time can invalidate a previous
analysis even if software tests still pass. The assistant may triage an alert and propose an
investigation. Suspension and resumption rules belong to the analysis owner. Retuning prompts
or refitting a learner after inspecting drift creates a new procedure whose old calibration does
not transfer automatically.
   The economic comparison includes model calls, retrieval, numerical computation, review,
failures, rework and ongoing maintenance. If Cm , Cr , Cn , Ch , Cf denote these components, a
proposed net benefit is a change in held-out decision value minus Cm + Cr + Cn + Ch + Cf ,
relative to a specified ordinary workflow. This expression is an accounting design, not an ROI
estimate. The available evidence does not supply authentic bank losses, prices, review times
or accepted decision outcomes. A faster explanation can be valuable, but it must not conceal
a lower rate of scientifically usable answers. The appropriate next trial therefore measures
decision quality, all-request availability and total cost separately, while the implementation
preserves the reasons an answer was ambiguous, refused or unavailable.


35.9.1    Agent architectures must preserve scientific uncertainty

Several systems now make causal analysis a sequence of tool-supported decisions. Their
strongest contribution is often a concrete representation of the intermediate work: a dataset, a
graph, an estimand, a proof statement or a failed tool call. Comparing these systems requires
examining what each intermediate object means and which transformations are allowed. A
graph stored in agent memory can prevent a variable-name error while still carrying an
unsupported orientation into every later calculation.


Causal Agent: useful tool boundaries and unequal baselines

Han and colleagues store causal graph objects in a dictionary that agents address by name.
This connects independence tests, graph questions and effect calculations without requiring
each operation to reconstruct the graph from prose. Their CausalTQA examples combine small
generated nonlinear additive Gaussian mechanisms with medical and marketing vocabulary.
The vocabulary tests a language interface; it does not turn the generated mechanism into a
medical or marketing observation. Kairong Han, Kun Kuang, Ziyu Zhao, Junjian Ye and Fei
Wu (2026)
   The paper documents informative failures: requesting conditional rather than marginal
independence, passing the wrong variable name, using the wrong graph operation, and building
unnecessarily long tool chains. Typed variable references and explicit tool signatures are
plausible remedies. The main code-generation baseline, however, executes once, whereas
the agent uses specialized tools and iterative reasoning. Its measured advantage therefore
combines tool design, supplied knowledge and opportunities for repair. An evaluation intended
to isolate orchestration should give a deterministic workflow and a simpler agent the same
tool implementations and permitted repair budget.
   The reported average cost of 3.37 seconds, 2.51 iterations and 5,308 tokens comes from 100
sampled variable, edge and graph questions with a maximum iteration count of 15. It does
not establish the cost of the full effect workflow, rare failures or deployment under a different
model and platform. An average well below a limit is also insufficient evidence to remove that
limit. The prototype should retain explicit budgets and report tails, timeouts, failed requests
35.9. Reporting, monitoring and the economics of assistance                                     357


and review effort. The source’s effect-answer tolerance and benchmark oracle require code
inspection before its reported 157 correct answers out of 160 become a reproduction target.
Kairong Han, Kun Kuang, Ziyu Zhao, Junjian Ye and Fei Wu (2026)


ORCA: shared state without silently choosing a causal world

ORCA organizes analysis of relational databases around dataset exploration, discovery and
inference. It records table choices, joins, variable roles, candidate graphs and estimation
configurations, with opportunities for human review. Its REEF benchmark uses a specified
structural causal model inside a relational e-commerce database. This is directly relevant to
a banking proposal: a mistaken join or aggregation can change the unit of analysis before a
causal estimator is called. Joanie Hayoun Chung, Sumin Lee and Sungbin Lim (2026)
  The important limitation lies between graph discovery and inference. The paper describes a
consensus PAG that retains uncertain endpoints, followed by a separate “actionable’ ’ DAG.
Uncertain directions are resolved using the highest-ranked candidate, cycle-safe orientation,
reversal or edge removal. Acyclicity does not establish that the selected orientation is true.
An effect computed from this one DAG is conditional on choices added during that conversion,
and cannot automatically represent all models encoded by the uncertainty-preserving graph.
   For a servicing decision, suppose distress and contact intensity remain ambiguously related.
Directing the edge one way can make distress an adjustment variable; directing it the other
can make it a treatment descendant. The proposed interface should retain the original graph
object and give every added orientation an explicit assumption record. It should compare
identification across compatible models, return an effect set where appropriate, or state that a
scalar target is not identified. Ranking an orientation for display is not authorization to treat
it as scientific fact. This is a proposed restriction on reuse, not behavior shown to exist in
ORCA’s implementation.
   The reported user study also requires careful interpretation. Twelve participants used ORCA
and a baseline with tools, step gates and minimal state in counterbalanced order. Table 1 gives
rounded completion rates of 0.83 and 0.75. The abstract’s 42-percentage-point completion
gain is not consistent with that table; it should not be repeated as a verified result. Appendix
E defines completion as producing an ATE regardless of accuracy, and discovery success as
including both treatment and outcome nodes. Neither definition establishes correct discovery.
Joanie Hayoun Chung, Sumin Lee and Sungbin Lim (2026)
   The paper’s “CI coverage’ ’ description counts an estimated ATE falling within an interval
around a ground-truth effect. That wording differs from the usual repeated-sampling event in
which an estimated interval contains a fixed true effect. Its exact oracle and implementation
require clarification. Likewise, the full-data test for the ATE-error condition effect has p = .321,
whereas the analysis excluding large configuration-error outliers reports p = .020 under OLS.
Configuration failures are central outcomes for a workflow product. They should remain in
the primary comparison, with conditional numerical accuracy reported separately.


CausalPulse: operational success has a different denominator

CausalPulse supplies another concrete design: agents coordinate semantic descriptions, domain
rules and causal tools through a utility layer that includes MCP. Such interfaces can make
tools accessible and operations traceable. The inspected manufacturing study nevertheless
distinguishes successful operation from successful root-cause attribution. Its PSE example
reports Hits@1 of .44, precision .46, recall .40 and F1 .39 despite much higher operational
success. Tool availability and completion are necessary engineering outcomes, but substituting
358                                                            Causal analysis for a universal bank


them for causal correctness would misstate the evidence. Chathurangi Shyalika, Utkarshani
Jaimini, Cory Henson and Amit Sheth (2026)
  This distinction determines the proposed monitoring interface. It should record whether
the request was parsed, whether the analysis was admissible, whether the tools completed,
whether the scientific target was answered, and whether the decision was useful under the
declared loss. These events need separate denominators. A scientific refusal can be a correct
answer, while a complete report can be wrong. Banking acceptance would additionally need
appropriate target-bank evidence; the public prototype can already test these distinctions with
generated known-truth cases.


CausalSmith: a checked proof still needs a checked statement

CausalSmith combines a Lean library with proposal, formalization, proof and presentation
stages. Its paper reports 8,179 declarations and a catalog of 144 runs: 14 accepted, 59
downgraded and 71 failed. Those counts include reruns as separate entries and exclude a
legacy track. They describe one campaign with changing model versions, not independent
draws from a fixed research-task population. The authors explicitly acknowledge that research
quality ratings lack independent human validation and that the error rate of their LLM
statement-match audit is unknown. Jiyuan Tan and Vasilis Syrgkanis (2026)
   The source’s most useful distinction is between checking a proof against a formal statement
and checking whether that statement expresses the intended claim. A compiled artifact can
assume a hard step as an axiom, weaken a conclusion, strengthen an assumption or make a
predicate vacuous. The paper describes mechanical scans and dependency checks alongside
language-model statement review. These are complementary checks with different assurances.
The latter does not acquire a formal guarantee merely by sitting next to a proof checker.
   For a proposed bank-effect theorem, the statement record should expose the unit, intervention,
estimand, time ordering, conditioning information, positivity and dependence assumptions.
The proof environment should bind the toolchain, imported definitions and axioms. A separate
review should compare the English claim with that exact formal statement and test whether
its assumptions are satisfiable in the intended model. A theorem conditional on observed
confounders cannot be presented as solving unmeasured confounding in operational data.
Formal correctness, semantic fidelity and scientific relevance each need their own evidence.
   The near-term reuse choice is therefore selective. Retain typed graph memory, explicit
intermediate state, preserved failures, and formal statement/dependency records as design
candidates. Defer executable adoption of these newly inspected systems until exact code,
dependencies, licenses and relevant numerical or proof paths have been reviewed. This permits
a concrete prototype architecture now without claiming that paper descriptions have already
been integrated or independently reproduced.


35.10      Choosing an agent architecture for a servicing decision
A bank considering assisted causal analysis faces an architectural choice before it faces a model
leaderboard. It can give a language model a broad notebook environment, surround a fixed
statistical pipeline with conversational assistance, or ask several specialist agents to negotiate
an analysis. Each choice changes which mistakes are easy to detect, what must be reviewed
by a person, and how much an apparently completed answer costs. The useful comparison
is therefore between complete analytical paths with declared scientific obligations. Counting
agent roles or successful tool calls gives little guidance about whether a servicing decision has
35.10. Choosing an agent architecture for a servicing decision                                 359


been answered.
   Consider a manager asking: “Should we offer an early restructuring review to customers
entering arrears?” Let the unit be an eligible account at its first qualifying arrears date, X the
information available immediately before the offer, A ∈ {0, 1} the offer, and Y the discounted
net cash recovery over a fixed following horizon. The offer is distinct from acceptance and
from the eventual restructuring terms. For a specified eligible population P , an initial target is

                                     τP = EP {Y (1) − Y (0)}.                                (35.2)

If Y excludes the incremental cost c of making the offer, an expected-value decision compares
τP with c. If costs are already inside Y , subtracting them again is wrong. An agent should
make this definition explicit before requesting an estimator. Neither an offer-acceptance
prediction nor the effect among customers who accepted is automatically an answer to this
question.
   The information clock is equally consequential. A field can carry an event date before
the offer but be entered into the database after it. The admissible record is the version
available at the decision time, with the extraction and revision rule specified. A distress
assessment obtained during the offer call cannot silently become a pretreatment covariate.
Multiple accounts held by one customer, branch policies and shared collection teams require
an explicit sampling and interference analysis; calling each row an independent customer does
not settle these issues. The simple point-treatment example below assumes one eligible unit,
no interference and a declared independent-unit law. The longitudinal construction earlier
in this chapter is needed when subsequent contacts and evolving distress become part of the
intervention.


35.10.1     What the competing architectures actually contribute

The primary literature supports several distinct proposals. Zhu and colleagues’ CausalAgent
