routes processing, structure learning and reporting through agents and MCP tools. Its four-
page demonstration uses the Sachs dataset; quantitative effect estimation and counterfactual
modules remain among its stated future directions. Its conversational interface is evidence of
an interaction design, not a demonstrated solution to the servicing target in (35.2). Han and
colleagues’ separately authored Causal Agent instead illustrates named graph objects in tool
memory and a generated question benchmark. Keeping these two systems distinct prevents a
result from one from being attributed to the other’s implementation Zhu et al. (2026); Kairong
Han, Kun Kuang, Ziyu Zhao, Junjian Ye and Fei Wu (2026).
   The actor/critic design of oci-agent addresses a closer statistical problem: point-in-time
observational effects under supplied unconfoundedness. It exposes specifications, notebooks
and diagnostics to a human principal. This can reduce the effort of reproducing an analysis
or finding a failed overlap diagnostic. The critical question is whether a proposed revision
preserves the target. Removing unsupported parts of the population may make an estimate
more stable while answering a different banking question. That is a substantive decision which
an attractive report must not hide. The paper’s benchmark results remain reported source
findings, and are not reproduced live-model results of this proposal Chou et al. (2026).
   The causal-learn+ position takes a stricter approach. Agents assist data inspection, method
explanation and interpretation around a protected discovery core. Their proposed edges,
orientations or constraints do not automatically become scientific evidence. This reduces
one path by which language-model beliefs enter a graph, but leaves assumption elicitation,
variable construction and statistical method choice as important tasks. Its call for future
360                                                          Causal analysis for a universal bank


benchmarks is consistent with treating the architecture as a candidate for evaluation rather
than an established performance advantage Zheng (2026).
   ORCA emphasizes shared relational state: joins, variable roles, graphs and estimation
configurations. This is especially relevant when banking data are spread over account, customer,
contact and transaction tables. However, the paper’s conversion of a consensus PAG into an
actionable DAG introduces orientation, reversal or deletion decisions. An analysis conducted
on that DAG inherits these extra choices. The architecture should expose them as additions
to the assumptions, and preserve the original uncertain graph. The numerical comparison
is also narrower than its headline suggests: the inspected table reports completion rates of
.83 and .75, whereas the abstract claims a 42-percentage-point gain. Completion is defined
as producing an ATE regardless of its accuracy. These are reasons to preserve the source
discrepancy and to design a better denominator, not to invent a corrected experiment Joanie
Hayoun Chung, Sumin Lee and Sungbin Lim (2026).
   Two further architectures broaden the comparison. CausalSmith makes a formal statement,
proof dependencies and compiler results explicit; its own limitations separate proof checking
from unvalidated model judgments about statement faithfulness and research quality. Model
Discovery Agent proposes executable mechanisms, then uses numerical fitting and experiment
design to compare them. The latter’s model-disagreement criterion approximates information
gain within a changing candidate set. Its reported predictive tests do not establish causal
identification, and its illustrated experiments use open-loop policies. Neither formal proof
search nor mechanism proposal alone replaces the observational assumptions needed for the
servicing target Jiyuan Tan and Vasilis Syrgkanis (2026); Murphy (2026).

35.10.2     A target can drift while every tool succeeds

Suppose consistency, conditional exchangeability (Y (0), Y (1)) ⊥ A | X, positivity and the
stated sampling law hold. Write e(x) = P (A = 1 | X = x) and ma (x) = E(Y | A = a, X = x).
The familiar augmented inverse-probability score is
                                                        A{Y − m1 (X)}
                        ϕ(O; m, e) = m1 (X) − m0 (X) +

At the true nuisance functions, conditioning on X removes both residual terms, leaving
E{ϕ | X} = E{Y (1) − Y (0) | X}. Consequently, averaging over P gives τP . Estimated
nuisance functions, cross-fitting, dependence and uncertainty require the additional arguments
developed elsewhere in this monograph. Calling this score does not establish exchangeability
or those rate conditions Hernán and Robins (2020).
  Now let an overlap diagnostic cause the workflow to keep only K = {x : .1 ≤ e(x) ≤ .9}. A
uniform average of the score among retained units targets
                                      E[1K (X){m1 (X) − m0 (X)}]

By contrast, define the overlap-weighted target explicitly as
                                  E[e(X){1 − e(X)}{m1 (X) − m0 (X)}]

                                          E[e(X){1 − e(X)}]

Equations (35.4) and (35.5) integrate against different measures. They coincide only under
additional restrictions, such as a constant conditional effect; their labels cannot make them
equal. If K is estimated from the same data, uncertainty about the selection rule is another
issue. The present calculation uses known propensities and a fixed rule so that this additional
difficulty does not obscure the target distinction.
   In the inspected oci-agent notebook, the branch labeled ATO calls a propensity trimming
function and then applies a uniform AIPW summary to the retained pseudo-outcomes. The
serialization retains this label and exports retained indices separately. This source path supports
a trimmed-population interpretation under the relevant assumptions; it does not implement
the weighting in (35.5). The appropriate adaptation therefore reads the implemented weights
and retained population, not just the display name oci-agent contributors (2026).

  An exact generated example makes the financial consequence visible. Take three strata
with masses (1/4, 1/2, 1/4), offer probabilities (.05, .5, .8) and conditional net-recovery effects
(−200, 100, 500) dollars. Direct summation gives
                          700                         48200
      τP = 125,    τK =       ≃ 233.33,       τov =         ≃ 170.32 USD per account.           (35.6)
                           3                           283
Trimming retains three quarters of the original population. If the offer cost is 180 dollars per
eligible account and lies outside the recovery outcome, the full-population expected net gain
is −55 dollars. Substituting the trimmed effect into that full-population calculation would
reverse the sign. A policy confined to the retained stratum is a different decision and needs its
own eligibility rule. The numbers are authored potential outcomes, not observations about
any bank. A separate 400-unit finite-population calculation with exact nuisances reproduces
all three weighted averages Causal banking proposal project (2026c).
   The same problem occurs in graph handoffs. Under one declared DAG, a baseline distress
measure can be a common cause of offer and recovery and belong in an adjustment set. Under
a different timing definition it can be a descendant of the offer, so conditioning on it can remove
part of the total effect. An architecture should attach the variable definition, information
time and graph assumption to the adjustment result. Caching by column names alone cannot
preserve that meaning.


35.10.3      What repeated critics can and cannot repair

A critic is useful when it brings a distinct check: reconstructing weights, reading a source
passage, evaluating a graph criterion or reproducing a numerical baseline. Merely repeating the
same prompt with the same evidence does not create independent scientific information. To
quantify this distinction, suppose each of three critics misses an error with marginal probability
q = .1. If their errors are independent, majority failure has probability

                                     q 3 + 3q 2 (1 − q) = .028.                                 (35.7)

Perfectly shared errors instead leave the failure probability at .1. Consider an intermediate
stipulated law: with probability γ = .05, all three fail from a common cause; otherwise they
fail independently with probability r = 1/19. Each still has marginal error γ + (1 − γ)r = .1,
but majority failure becomes

                             γ + (1 − γ){r3 + 3r2 (1 − r)} ≃ .05762.                            (35.8)

Thus the same individual error rate can accompany quite different benefits from voting. Exact
enumeration over all eight independent-error patterns checks the calculation. None of these
probabilities is an empirical estimate of a language model or a deployed critic Causal banking
proposal project (2026c).
  There is also an information limit. Consider two linear Gaussian worlds with mutually
independent standard normal noises in each world:
                                                            q
                             W1 : X = U,       Y = 12 X +     3/4 V,
                                                             q
                             W2 : Y = V ′ ,     X = 21 Y +        3/4 U ′ .                     (35.9)

Both observed pairs have zero mean, unit marginal variances and covariance 1/2, hence the
same joint distribution. The effect of increasing X by one is 1/2 in W1 and zero in W2 .
Suppose an adaptive agent system receives only samples from that common law, identical
35.10. Choosing an agent architecture for a servicing decision                                  363


documents in both worlds and randomness independent of the world. The first transcript step
then has the same law in both worlds. If this holds through step t, the next tool or agent
applies the same conditional transition to an identically distributed history, so it holds at t + 1.
Induction gives the same distribution for the final answer. An additional critic operating on
that transcript cannot distinguish these worlds.
   This argument concerns the stated information set. Genuine temporal knowledge, an
intervention or a justified scientific restriction can break its premise. Retrieval is valuable
when it supplies such information with an inspectable provenance; fluent agreement alone
cannot do so. The appropriate output before the added information is available can be an
identified set, a conditional answer or a request to clarify the decision model. It need not be
an arbitrary scalar produced to make the workflow look complete.
   Repeated repair also changes evaluation. In a deliberately simple experiment, suppose a
scientifically invalid candidate independently has probability .05 of passing a fallible screen
on each try. Allowing twenty tries and retaining the first apparent pass gives probability
1 − .9520 ≃ .6415 of at least one false pass. Without independence, the union bound is only
min(1, 20 × .05) = 1. This example describes independent screening attempts, not deterministic
replay of the same input, and does not assign a statistical significance level to real agent review.
It explains why the proposed evaluation must retain all attempts, give comparators the same
repair budget and separate development feedback from held-out evaluation Causal banking
proposal project (2026c).


35.10.4     Typed handoffs and the scope of recovery

For the servicing prototype, a useful analysis state contains the decision contract, data identity
and clock, graph or graph class, assumptions with their source and status, target measure,
method applicability, numerical artifacts, uncertainty statement and request history. These
objects should refer to one another by immutable identity. A revised target or graph invalidates
dependent results even when the data bytes are unchanged. A successful statistical call must
not make an unresolved assumption disappear.
   The controller can enforce local invariants. An estimation request must name a target and
population; every variable must exist in the supplied schema; a numerical interval must have
finite, ordered endpoints unless the result type explicitly supports an unbounded set; and
a result must bind the method and input versions that produced it. A graph-identification
operation can check a formal condition relative to a supplied graph. These checks support
meaningful handoffs, but none proves that the graph or observation law describes the bank.
Scientific assumption status should therefore remain visible alongside mechanical validity.
   This distinction leads to several result types with different continuation actions. Malformed
input calls for correction of the request. A missing backend calls for an implementation or
environment remedy. A mathematical nonidentification result calls for different information or
a different target. An unsupported method calls for a scoped alternative. A valid set-valued
answer can proceed to a decision calculation that respects the set. Collapsing all of these into
either an empty successful object or a single generic failure would discard the reason that
determines the next useful action.
   The inspected CausalAgent server illustrates a concrete boundary to repair before reuse.
Its OLC handler refers to a function not imported or defined in that module and catches
the resulting exception into a JSON error string. Separately, its output helper extracts text
between braces and returns an empty dictionary on a decoding failure. These are static source
findings, not a claim that this proposal executed the upstream server. A wrapper must validate
the scientific result and propagate an explicit failure before downstream analysis; successful
364                                                           Causal analysis for a universal bank


transport of an error string is not a learned graph CausalAgent contributors (2026).
   Recovery has a related distinction. A graph checkpoint preserves enough state to resume an
operation; it does not automatically make external effects occur exactly once. The inspected
LangGraph interrupt restarts its node from the beginning. An application should therefore
give an expensive computation a stable request identity, record its durable outcome and check
that identity on replay. For a remote provider call interrupted before a receipt is saved, the
outcome can remain unknown unless the provider supports lookup or idempotency. Blind
resubmission cannot be advertised as exact-once execution langgraph contributors (2026).
   Pydantic AI supplies typed tool boundaries and usage controls, but the inspected price
check cannot enforce a monetary limit when price is unavailable. Some usage becomes known
only after a response. A prototype requiring a hard budget needs a known pricing contract,
conservative reservation and explicit behavior for unknown cost. AutoGen’s inspected save/load
methods preserve model context; they do not constitute a journal of arbitrary external side
effects. Its maintenance declaration and separate code/documentation licenses also enter
the adoption decision. These observations favor a plain controller baseline before adding a
framework whose incremental benefit has not yet been measured pydantic-ai contributors
(2026); autogen contributors (2026).
   The existing local prototype provides narrower positive evidence. Six authored offline cases
preserve blocked, unsupported, ambiguous and completed outcomes, including directed-revision
recovery and a weak moment set. The saved replay reproduces those outcomes using real local
tools with no live model calls. This supports selected semantics and recovery behavior. It does
not test whether a language model elicits the right servicing graph, reduces human effort or
behaves correctly on an external platform. The library, CLI and MCP contracts should carry
this same distinction when transporting the result Causal banking proposal project (2026d).

35.10.5     Selecting the next experiment by useful output and total cost

The minimal comparison has a deterministic analyst template, a single assisted controller
and, if justified, a controller with a critic. All receive the same documents, permitted tool
implementations and task budget. Generated cases should include correctly identified effects,
ambiguity requiring a set or refusal, misleading variable clocks, a target change after trimming
and a tool failure. A held-out task split separates adaptation of prompts and templates from
evaluation. Numerical truth comes from the declared generator, while semantic scoring needs
an independently specified reference and ambiguity rubric. A correct refusal is a successful
answer to a nonidentified task; unnecessary refusal on an identified task is a separate error.
   Let N count all eligible assigned requests and Ui indicate that request i produced an
admissible, correct and decision-appropriate answer under the rubric. A useful workflow
summary is                          PN
                                         (C tools + wTireview + Ciother )
                         Cusable = i=1 i
                         b                        PN                      .              (35.10)
                                                    i=1 Ui
It is undefined when there is no usable output. Costs for failed requests stay in the numerator.
The statistic should accompany the usable fraction, error categories, refusal behavior, latency
distribution and conditional numerical accuracy. Reporting only accuracy among completed
estimates can reward a system that abandons difficult requests or hides configuration errors.
   For planning, suppose manual review costs 15 minutes per request at 120 dollars per hour
and yields a usable fraction .9. Its ratio is 30/.9 = 33.33 dollars. An assisted workflow costing
3 dollars in tools plus 6 review minutes, with usable fraction .8, gives 15/.8 = 18.75 dollars. At
20 review minutes the same tool and quality assumptions give 43/.8 = 53.75 dollars. Equating
the assisted ratio to the manual ratio yields a review-time threshold of 71/6 ≃ 11.83 minutes.
35.10. Choosing an agent architecture for a servicing decision                              365


These stipulated scenarios omit fixed build costs; they show which quantities to measure, not
that assistance saves money Causal banking proposal project (2026c).
   The next justified experiment is consequently a bounded public/generated task study
measuring semantic failures and total review effort, with matched tools and frozen denominators.
A live-model performance claim requires a recorded backend revision, actual calls and measured
usage. A literature and architecture proposal can proceed without that claim. Authentic
bank experiments become worth considering when the prototype isolates an uncertainty whose
resolution could change the build or investment decision. The unresolved questions are specific:
how often assumptions are elicited correctly, whether criticism adds independent information,
how much adjudication is needed and whether the resulting gain survives a change in task
population. None is answered by adding agent roles to a diagram.
Chapter 36

An auditable proposal-to-tool
prototype

36.1     The implemented boundary
The prototype implements a local handoff from a structured business proposal to fixed causal
operations. It accepts an authored fixture or a recorded model output in a provider-neutral
envelope. It does not contact a model endpoint. The envelope contains the question and its
alternative targets, candidate diagrams, proposed operation names and a provenance record.
That record names the provider, model, revision and generation parameters, retains the exact
prompt, and checks the prompt’s SHA-256 identity. The complete proposal receives its own
content identity. A recorded label is provenance supplied by the caller; it is not independent
proof that a particular model generated the bytes.
   This boundary is deliberately useful before a provider is selected. It permits the same
semantic checks to be applied to different proposed backends without making a framework’s
response format the definition of a causal question. It also separates two evaluations. One
asks whether the controller preserves a given declaration and result. The other asks whether a
model produces good declarations from unfamiliar business questions. The executed examples
answer the first. They supply no empirical answer to the second.
   A proposal can request graph review, graphical identification, discovery or a moment-based
effect calculation. These names do not imply that every operation is implemented for every
input. The fixed service implements syntax review, a supplied-DAG back-door attempt, and
a declared Gaussian moment-inversion calculation. Discovery remains unsupported in the
present service. An unsupported operation returns that status; it does not invent an empty
graph or an effect of zero. There is no operation for sending a customer communication,
altering an account or approving a bank action.


36.2     The three identities of a proposed analysis
Three identities control the handoff. The proposal identity describes the complete proposed
content and model record. The declaration identity covers the problem and diagram together,
including every target alternative, evidence reference, assumption, clock and graph revision.
Finally, the execution identity covers prepared requests, the caller’s grant, source code, schemas
and numerical environment. Changing a population while keeping the same diagram changes
the declaration. Changing an implementation while keeping the same question changes the


                                               366
36.3. A narrow projection with explicit refusals                                              367


execution. Neither change can silently reuse an old result as if nothing had changed.
   The declaration validator checks structure and selected semantic constraints. These include
whether referenced evidence exists in the declaration, whether graph endpoints refer to declared
variables, whether a DAG has a directed cycle, whether a proposed history includes a future
decision, and whether a policy uses information before its declared availability. It also flags
unresolved targets, contradicted assumptions, post-treatment adjustment for a proposed total
effect and conditioning a population on treatment descendants. It does not prove that an
asserted DAG is true or fully recognize every MAG, PAG or CPDAG. A successful declaration
review means that a stated problem can proceed to an appropriately scoped formal analysis.
    Evidence identities receive an additional byte check. Source records reference bounded local
files under the documentation tree; symlink escapes and paths outside that boundary are
refused. The actual bytes must match the declared hash. This catches a changed source or
stale citation record. It does not check whether a source’s scientific assertion is true. The full
source record, declaration and proposal are retained as immutable artifacts so that a result
can be traced back to both the claim and the bytes that supported its review.
   The external grant is a trusted local caller object bound to the declaration identity. It
lists permitted operations, names the reviewer and supplies the sampling declaration and any
numerical inputs. Putting a reviewer’s name into the model response does not create this object.
Requesting a new operation does not extend its permissions. The grant is an application
boundary, not a digital signature or a bank identity service. Institutional authentication and
approval stores remain requirements for a later deployment.


36.3      A narrow projection with explicit refusals
The implemented translator supports an unconditional population ATE for one static binary
action, with intervention one and comparator zero. Its horizon starts at the declared origin.
It retains all variables and requires the graph to account for them. Outcome and target-loss
units must agree. It does not silently convert a dynamic regime, an overlap target, a selected
population or a utility transformation into this static ATE.
   For a supported target, the translator builds the fixed operation’s scientific context and
places the complete original declaration in its source evidence. The smaller operation schema
carries the treatment, outcome, population, units, horizon, assumptions and graph. The
retained declaration carries the detailed measurement lineage and numeric decision/availability
clocks. Thus a consumer can reconstruct the original problem even where the narrow operation
schema has no field for every detail. No synthetic or analyst assertion is upgraded to externally
verified truth during this projection.
   Candidate graphs are processed individually. For the synthetic offer question, the input
includes an undirected CPDAG and its two directed alternatives. The controller preserves
all three candidate identities. Syntax review returns the CPDAG’s tail endpoints intact. A
supported directed graph can receive a conditional back-door result. Another candidate may
be outside the implemented identification method. The overall record stays ambiguous, and
every candidate’s response remains visible. It does not average graph outputs or select the
most convenient result. These alternatives describe possible worlds; the prototype does not
assert their simultaneous truth or estimate probabilities for them.
   The distinction between nonidentification and an unsuccessful implementation attempt is
essential here. Failure of the supplied back-door procedure does not prove that no other valid
identification argument exists. Likewise, refusal to translate the servicing policy does not
prove that its value is unknowable. It records that this controller has no qualified mapping
368                                                           Causal analysis for a universal bank


from that richer target into its fixed service. The full policy, clocks and assumptions remain
available for a future longitudinal adapter.


36.4     Representative executed paths
Six synthetic local paths were executed and exported with their artifact descriptors and
checkpoint records. The ambiguous funding question is blocked before invoking a tool because
its economic target has not been resolved. The observation example is also blocked: ownership
and selection questions remain substantive. The servicing declaration passes its own chronology
checks but is unsupported by the narrow static translator. These outcomes are useful behavior;
returning a number would answer an unstated substitute question.
   The discovery example reaches actual graph-review and identification tools for each candidate
and preserves ambiguity. A separate directed fixture exercises ordinary conditional execution,
interruption and exact replay. It is an explicit fixture choice of a supplied graph, not a
discovered resolution of the original ambiguous problem. Finally, a weak moment example
reaches the effect service and retains a two-component unbounded set. The mean vector
supplied is (1, 0), the covariance matrix is diagonal with entries 0.01 and 1, and the declared
sample size is 100. The resulting set has two unbounded tails separated by a finite excluded
region. The controller preserves both tails and the service’s joint-confidence label together
with its Gaussian-approximation limitation. It neither replaces the union by a finite interval
nor interprets the zero denominator estimate as a finite causal effect.
   The numerical example checks propagation of a declared mathematical result. It does not
estimate moments from bank observations or prove that the supplied covariance is valid under
dependence. The original scientific gaps concerning persistent maps, latent temporal graphs
and dependent learners therefore remain open. A semantic adapter cannot repair a failed
inferential law by attaching a more complete provenance record.


36.5     Recovery and adverse inputs
The local journal stores each completed tool response under a hash of the full execution identity.
Publication is atomic. On resumption, the controller checks that saved results form a prefix of
the planned operations, that their content hash is unchanged, that each response belongs to
the correct request, and that referenced artifacts still match their bytes. Source verification
also runs before a completed replay. A changed source is therefore rejected even when a result
already exists in the journal.
   In the interruption fixture, the controller stops after saving the graph-review response and
before the identification step. Resumption keeps the saved review and executes only the
remaining identification operation. A later complete replay returns the same record without
reinvoking tools. This is a tested single-host property of the local fixed operations and journal.
It does not establish distributed exactly-once execution, authenticated tamper resistance
against the local operator, or recovery for arbitrary external side effects. Those stronger claims
would require different implementations and trials.
  The adverse tests exercise both content and authority boundaries. They reject unknown
operations, injected command or permission fields, nonfinite model parameters, changed
prompt bytes and a live-mode declaration. A retrieved text fixture tells the system to ignore
checks and execute a shell command; the controller keeps it as source data and performs only
the granted graph review. This verifies the deterministic command boundary. It is not a
measurement of a live model’s susceptibility to scientifically misleading text.
36.6. What the next evaluation must establish                                                  369


   Other tests change source bytes, corrupt a checkpoint, alter a target after the grant, introduce
a contradicted assumption, or move the servicing decision before L1 is available. Missing
numerical evidence returns a failed calculation without an estimate. The recorded output
retains the cause of failure. Together with the inherited problem and operation contract cases,
80 checks pass. This is local conformance evidence, not an accuracy percentage for unseen
banking questions.
   The first integration runs also exposed ordinary engineering limits. Some frozen operation
schemas accepted fewer optional fields than the general context schema. Retaining detailed
clocks in the bound declaration supplied a compatible mapping without dropping them. A
256 MiB address-space allowance was insufficient for imported numerical dependencies; the
executed configuration uses the existing runtime’s tested 1 GiB allowance. Both failed runs are
retained in the evidence. Memory ceilings constrain execution; they do not imply measured
peak memory or comparative efficiency.


36.6      What the next evaluation must establish
The prototype creates a stable place to evaluate actual assistance. A model can eventually
propose a target and diagram, but its output must pass the same declaration and permission
boundaries. An evaluation must compare those proposals with an ordinary structured workflow
and with independent reference judgments. It must score target meaning, evidence applicability,
unresolved ambiguity, graph classes and downstream effect conclusions. Faster or more fluent
reports are secondary when the intervention, population or clock has changed.
   The present records contain zero live model calls. Model tokens and prices remain unavailable,
rather than being reported as measured zeros. All examples are synthetic, all graph resolutions
are explicit fixture assumptions, and no customer action is authorized. A real comparison still
needs exact backend versions, approved data custody, original benchmark identities, experts for
business and diagram judgments, and a frozen analysis of every requested case. The controller
supplies traceable inputs and outputs for that work; the missing scientific and institutional
evidence cannot be inferred from its successful execution.
Chapter 37

Evaluating causal assistance without
changing the question

37.1     The benchmark unit is a causal problem
An agent can produce a plausible report, execute valid code and still answer the wrong causal
question. Evaluation must follow the entire chain from business meaning through assumptions
and identification to uncertainty, availability and decision loss. A benchmark of text fluency,
graph edit distance or successful tool calls measures only part of that chain.
   CLadder demonstrates the value of formal questions with varied verbalizations, including
commonsense and deliberately unfamiliar or conflicting stories. The inspected paper also
identifies language-to-formal-tool formulation as a continuing challenge. Its historical binary-
answer accuracy is evidence about those tasks and models; it is not a measurement of effect
coverage, decision loss or banking readiness.Jin et al. (2023)
  CausalDS expands the evaluation object to narrated synthetic mechanisms, data and a
separate observation model. Its inspected results show why symbolic success, uncertainty
quality, abstention and cost should be reported separately. Its author-reported exam and
repeated runs are useful design evidence, not model evaluations conducted in this project. A
generated world with known truth also remains different from authentic bank data whose
semantic and assignment mechanisms must be established externally. Leban and Sun (2026)
  The proposed experimental unit is therefore an independently generated or independently
adjudicated causal mechanism and question. Several phrasings, label conditions or stochastic
model calls can be nested within that unit. They do not create new independent worlds.
Repeating one problem fifty times can measure response variation for that problem; it does
not provide fifty independent demonstrations of general causal competence.


37.2     Matched information and meaningful alternatives
The prospective design compares a fixed numerical workflow, a language-only workflow, retrieval
assistance, a hybrid of numerical tools and typed model proposals, and structured expert
workflows with and without assistance. Each arm needs a declared information budget. If one
receives the true causal graph and another must discover it, their effect-estimation scores do
not isolate the value of language assistance. If retrieval adds a valid institutional fact, that
information gain should be distinguished from a better inference algorithm.
  Eight strata are proposed: independent sufficient DAGs; latent-variable graph classes;

                                              370
37.3. A target error can survive perfect arithmetic                                           371


temporal data with known clocks; treatment-confounder feedback; panel or quasi-experimental
assignment; proxies, linkage and selection; weak or nonidentifying effects; and ambiguous
business targets or monetary loss. Label and evidence conditions cross ordinary descriptions,
unfamiliar labels, misleading or irrelevant material, and conflict between numerical evidence
and text. These strata test different failure mechanisms rather than treating all causal questions
as interchangeable.
   The current planning allocation is 400 mechanisms, with 50 per stratum and three stochastic
repetitions nested within each mechanism. This is an allocation for developing the design,
not a frozen final sample size or a power calculation. For orientation, the worst-case normal
approximation
    p           for one Bernoulli proportion at 400 independent observations has half-width
1.96 0.25/400, approximately 0.049. Paired differences, stratified outcomes and rare severe
errors require their own precision design. A development pilot would inform that design and
must be excluded from the final test.
  Both natural-workflow and matched-budget comparisons can be useful. The first asks what
an analyst can achieve with a realistic workflow, including review. The second asks what
changes when information or computation is controlled. Neither should hide extra expert time,
repeated retrieval or retry costs. The comparison must state which question it answers.


37.3      A target error can survive perfect arithmetic
An exact project IV construction illustrates a benchmark-label hazard. Let a randomized
binary instrument Z affect treatment for half the population, the compliers; the other half
never receives treatment. Set Y (0) = 0 for everyone, Y (1) = 1 for compliers and Y (1) = 3 for
never-takers. Treatment equals Z for compliers and zero otherwise. Randomization, exclusion
and monotonicity hold in this construction.
   The observed outcome difference across instrument values is 0.5 and the treatment-probability
difference is 0.5, so the Wald ratio is one. The population ATE is two. Changing the never-
takers’ unobserved treated outcome changes the population ATE without changing the observed
law. A scorer that calls the unrestricted Wald ratio the population ATE would reward a target
substitution. This is a finite counterexample supporting review of generator assumptions, not
a claim that every IV question in a named benchmark uses this construction.
   The same concern applies to trimming, overlap weighting and selected populations. A
language answer can reproduce the right formula for a different target. Evaluation should
therefore compare the population, measure, action, comparator, horizon and units before
comparing the numeric answer. Critical semantic errors deserve their own count, even when a
numeric discrepancy happens to be small in the test mechanism.


37.4      Graphs, sets and refusals need separate scores
Graph evaluation should compare adjacency and endpoint statements against the appropriate
identifiable class. A justified circle or undirected edge should not be penalized merely because
a simulator internally selected one fully directed graph. Orientation informativeness can
be reported alongside validity. This makes a method that preserves genuine ambiguity
distinguishable from one that returns little information and from one that confidently overorients
the graph.
  Identification outcomes also need separate labels. Scientific nonidentification, unsupported
implementation, malformed output, explicit abstention, timeout and missing input are not the
372                                                            Causal analysis for a universal bank


same event. A well-designed agent can correctly identify a missing premise without successfully
computing an effect. A backend can be unable to implement a valid functional. Combining
these into one “incorrect” or “no answer” category would obscure the remedy.
   For identified scalar targets, bias and error can be meaningful. For reported sets, evaluate
coverage, topology, finite availability and size. Whole-line answers can have high coverage and
little decision value. A method that returns short intervals on a selected easy subset needs an
all-request availability denominator. Unbounded and disconnected sets must remain in the
evaluation rather than being replaced by finite plotting limits.
  For an eligible finite interval [l, u], one prospective score at nominal level 1 − α is
                                   2                  2
                       (u − l) +     (l − θ)1{θ < l} + (θ − u)1{θ > u}.
                                   α                  α
The formula balances length with penalties for missing the target. It is not an instruction to
compress a union of intervals into one interval. For unions, coverage and total Lebesgue length
can be reported while retaining infinite lengths. Raw losses should not be capped simply to
make a plot or ranking convenient. The eligible target type must be stated before the score is
selected.


37.5     Contamination, adaptation and selective reporting
An exposed demonstration cannot become a held-out evaluation merely because its variables
are renamed. The local problem fixtures and replay examples have already been used to
develop and debug the prototype. They can continue to test conformance, but they cannot
provide independent estimates of a language model’s causal accuracy.
   The final design needs a frozen development/test split, mechanism identities, prompts,
model/provider revisions, retrieval corpus and ranking rules, numerical baselines, stopping
rules and analysis code. Mechanism families should be separated where family reuse would
reveal the answer. Label novelty and mechanism novelty should be varied independently. An
unfamiliar name attached to a memorized mechanism is not the same test as an unfamiliar
mechanism.
   Test outcomes cannot be used to tune prompt templates, choose the best retriever, strengthen
selected priors or discard difficult cells while retaining a final-test interpretation. A changed
method requires a new reviewed evaluation revision. Failed and unavailable requests remain in
the record. Reporting only the critic-approved subset would confound answer quality with
selection by the critic.
   The inspected OCI paper provides a useful refusal example: its critic declines many
replications when overlap is poor. That can be preferable to an unsupported estimate, but it
makes the denominator essential. The reported successful answers, refused requests, review
effort and remaining target population must all be visible. The external results are author
reports, not a validation of this project’s critic. Chou et al. (2026)


37.6     Decision value and cost
The ultimate question is whether assistance improves feasible decisions at an acceptable total
cost. In a known synthetic mechanism, a policy’s expected loss can be calculated under the
mechanism and compared with the chosen baseline. In a bank, the feasible policy, valuation
model, risk limits, operating costs and outcome truth need authentic inputs. Synthetic decision
loss does not establish institutional return on investment.
37.7. The probability of passing a coverage screen                                             373


  The prospective cost record includes model calls, input/output/cache tokens, retrieval,
numerical CPU time, wall time, memory, retries and human review and rework. Actual dated
prices are needed to turn these quantities into a currency total. Unknown prices remain
missing; zero live calls in an offline prototype do not imply a free live workflow. A fast answer
that requires substantial correction can have a worse total cost than a slower transparent
analysis.
   No final experiment has been registered or run here. Five prerequisite classes remain: an
exact live backend and custody terms; actual prices and a bounded budget; independent
held-out mechanisms and original benchmark bytes; named business/diagram adjudicators and
a rubric; and qualified numerical baselines. These are missing program inputs. No credentials
were read and no provider endpoint was probed to infer that a service is unavailable. The
design provides a route to evaluation once those inputs are supplied; it provides no current
empirical model-performance claim.


37.7      The probability of passing a coverage screen
Evaluating an agent that recommends inferential procedures requires a clear distinction between
nominal coverage, an argument for coverage and an empirical qualification rule. Suppose a
fixed procedure is tested in n independently generated replications of a declared mechanism.
Let K count requests whose reported sets cover the truth; unavailable or failed requests remain
in the declared denominator. If the per-request coverage is p, then under these simulation
assumptions K has a binomial law.
  For a simultaneous family of m cells and total error budget α, consider the one-sided exact
lower bound
                 L(K, n) = BetaQuantile(α/m; K, n − K + 1),         K > 0,
with L(0, n) = 0. A rule requiring L ≥ 0.95 certifies a minimum in this specific finite experiment.
At true p = 0.95, its probability of passing one cell is at most α/m. This is how a lower-bound
certification test behaves at its boundary, not evidence that the procedure’s true coverage is
zero.
  Before qualification, a designer can compute the smallest integer k∗ that passes and the
operating characteristic
                                  Pr(pass) = Pr(K ≥ k∗ ).
                                      p              p

The project calculation evaluates this exactly for several replication counts, family sizes and
values of p, and independently checks the equivalent binomial-tail threshold. It draws no
random data and does not test a causal estimator. Its purpose is to make the qualification
design interpretable. Causal banking research project (2026as)
   Increasing replications can distinguish a genuine coverage margin above 95more sharply.
It cannot make a level-controlled test have high power at the exact boundary. This does
not justify lowering the required minimum after seeing results. The analyst must state what
guarantee is theoretically justified, what empirical screen is being applied and what its power
is. A method may have a plausible asymptotic argument while failing this finite screen; that
should be reported as a qualification shortfall rather than silently recoded as success.
   An agent could otherwise exploit this distinction in two bad ways. It might declare a method
invalid merely because a low-powered boundary screen failed, or widen intervals until they
pass while ignoring decision usefulness. The evaluation should penalize both. Coverage, finite
availability and useful width are separate dimensions. A whole-line interval covers every finite
374                                                           Causal analysis for a universal bank


truth but may support no action. Bank width and loss thresholds require actual decision
owners; synthetic thresholds should remain labeled as such.


37.8      A live comparison needs independent mechanisms and
          complete costs
An offline controller can demonstrate request validation, abstention, tool dispatch and preser-
vation of graph/set semantics. It cannot measure how a live model translates a new banking
problem, how often retrieval changes its graph, or what the workflow costs. Zero model calls
means those empirical quantities are unmeasured; it does not mean accuracy is zero or costs
are free.
  A credible live comparison binds the exact backend/revision and inference settings, data-
custody arrangement, actual prices and approved budget, independent held-out mechanisms
or benchmark bytes, adjudicators and rubric, and qualified numerical baselines. The final
prompts, retrieval corpus, tools, retry rules, token/time limits and numerical tolerances should
be frozen before the first final request. Development cases already exposed to the agent cannot
become held-out by receiving different filenames.
  Compare data-only, model-only, retrieval-assisted, hybrid and expert-assisted workflows
under matched information and budgets. A hybrid receives additional information when it
uses a valid domain exclusion; its improvement should not be attributed solely to reasoning.
Conversely, a data-only baseline should not be asked to identify an effect that the observed law
cannot identify. The equal-law counterexamples in Section 32.6 make this boundary testable.
   Metrics should include whether the translated intervention/population is valid, whether
graph output respects equivalence and latent ambiguity, whether the downstream effect is
scientifically supported, and whether abstention occurs for the right reason. Repeated-run
disagreement is relevant even when the average score is favorable. Fluent explanations and
exact string matches to one graph are inadequate substitutes for these criteria.
  Complete costs include unsuccessful calls, retries, retrieval, tool computation, human
review and operating overhead. If an agent frequently produces a request that needs manual
correction, its low token bill can conceal high workflow cost. Decision value should be evaluated
on feasible actions and held-out outcomes or an explicitly justified reference, with uncertainty.
A stipulated arithmetic example explains the accounting but cannot establish provider pricing,
model calibration or bank ROI.


37.9      Testing semantic failures before the expensive study
Several low-cost deterministic cases can be exercised before live qualification. A y0 nonidentifi-
cation response must not become a zero effect. A continuous density must not be interpreted as
a binary probability. A grouped allocation contrast must not become an individual direct effect.
A statsmodels internal covariance option must not be reported as final clustered uncertainty
when the inspected implementation supplies HC0.y0 project (2026b); CausalGPS project
(2026b); inferference project (2026); statsmodels project (2026b)
   These cases test the proposed interface and evaluation rubric. They are useful development
evidence, and their exposure should be recorded. Fresh independent mechanisms are still
necessary to evaluate generalization. Keeping those roles separate allows an agentic workflow
to improve through development while retaining a meaningful final assessment.
37.9. Testing semantic failures before the expensive study                                  375

Relation extraction is a serious baseline, with a narrower claim

Susanti and Holsmoelle compare prompting with fine-tuned models on four relation datasets.
On DDI, Table 1 reports F1 of 67.4 for Single-Prompt C and 87.9 for PubMedBERT: a
20.5-point difference. The paper reports five-fold averages and explicitly limits its evaluation
to binary pairwise causality assessment. It neither demonstrates joint graph verification nor
establishes a universal advantage for fine-tuning under equal annotation costs. The comparison
does establish that a supervised smaller model deserves consideration when the proposed task
is extraction from a stable document domain. Yuni Susanti and Nina Holsmoelle (2025)
   For banking notes, evaluate the extraction role on held-out documents with independently
specified labels and timestamps. Track abstention and the treatment of ambiguous or contra-
dictory passages. Then separately evaluate whether extracted statements are admissible graph
evidence. A sentence that says “the waiver caused repayment’ ’ is evidence of what the author
claimed; it is not, by itself, evidence that assignment was unconfounded. A useful agent should
retain the quotation, its source and the alternative causal interpretations.
   Sng and colleagues illustrate why agreement is a separate target. Their retrieval experiment
supplies a mocked true causal graph, and their conclusion explicitly says that reducing
inconsistent ratings does not imply accurate causal prediction. A comparison in which one arm
receives such a graph evaluates its use of supplied information. It does not measure whether
retrieval can discover the graph in a bank setting. Registering both correct and misleading
376                                                           Causal analysis for a universal bank


retrieved evidence is necessary to expose that distinction. Grace Sng, Yanming Zhang and
Klaus Mueller (2024)

Task-specific gains should remain task-specific

In CausalEval’s Table 3, GPT-4o scores 69 on CLADDER with ordinary chain-of-thought
and 76 with FunctionCall, but its e-CARE scores are 90 and 73, respectively. These are
author-reported pass@1 results for the named versions and samples. The gains and losses
should remain visible rather than being replaced by the claim that tools always improve causal
reasoning. The table is also preferable to silently repeating inconsistent numerical values in
the paper’s surrounding discussion. Longxuan Yu, Delin Chen, Siheng Xiong, Qingyang Wu,
Qingzhen Liu, Dawei Li, Zhikai Chen, Xiaoze Liu and Liangming Pan (2025)
   The study repeats each question five times with greedy decoding. Repeated calls can reveal
response variation, but five calls to the same question are not five independent causal problems.
For illustration, suppose there are N independent mechanisms, m calls per mechanism, equal
marginal score variance σ 2 , and common within-mechanism correlation ρ. Then

                                            σ2
                                Var(S̄) =      {1 + (m − 1)ρ}.
                                            Nm
  At N = 100, m = 5, ρ = 1, the effective independent count is 100, not 500. This is a
project-derived sampling illustration, not an estimate of the paper’s unreported correlation.
The appropriate prototype analysis clusters calls and paraphrases by underlying mechanism,
reports the number of distinct mechanisms, and uses paired comparisons when methods see
the same cases.
   CausalEval also evaluates some expensive models on 100 cases rather than the usual 500.
Its human row combines scores from original benchmark papers with a study of three graduate
students on 100 questions for remaining datasets. A combined human/model gap therefore is
not one uniform matched experiment. Any investment argument should state the comparison
actually performed, the cost and failure accounting, and the uncertainty that remains.

An affordable, falsifiable evaluation sequence

The proposed sequence starts with fixed causal mechanisms, explicit public document prove-
nance and deterministic numerical answers. It then tests formulation, variable timing, graph
uncertainty, identification, execution and reporting separately, followed by their composition.
Baselines receive the same data, permitted documentation and tools. Model-only reasoning,
retrieval, a typed numerical workflow, and a supervised extractor answer different engineering
questions and should be included where relevant.
   The primary denominator includes every attempted case, with scientific refusals distinguished
from crashes and wrong answers. Numerical accuracy conditional on successful execution is a
secondary outcome. Cost includes failed calls, retrieval, annotation, retries and human review.
Deliberately adverse cases include an accurate quotation supporting a false causal claim, a
timestamp that makes a proposed control post-treatment, alternative graphs with different
effects, a misleading retrieved graph, and an unsupported edit policy.
   Public and generated data can establish that these failure cases are handled as specified and
can compare methods under a known law. They do not establish the frequency of those failures
in a target bank or the value of changing its real decisions. The next expensive experiment
should address a remaining uncertainty that could change the build or adoption decision. Until
such evidence exists, the proposal can recommend a bounded prototype and a testable research
37.9. Testing semantic failures before the expensive study                                     377


direction while preserving uncertainty about live-model performance, source completeness and
bank transport.


37.9.2    A prospective experiment for causal assistance

The first live comparison should determine whether language assistance improves a specified
causal workflow enough to justify its complete cost. A fluent explanation, a correctly guessed
graph and a correctly identified effect are different outcomes. The design therefore evaluates
formulation, information timing, graph ambiguity, identification, numerical execution and
reporting as separate tasks, followed by their composition. Public documents and generated
mechanisms can support this experiment before a bank funds access to proprietary records.
Model revisions, final sample sizes, acceptance thresholds and prices remain to be selected
from actual inputs; the calculations below are planning examples, not a registered trial or
evidence of live-model performance.
  CausalEval’s inspected experiment repeats each question five times and averages the results
within question. Such repeats can expose output variation, but cannot create additional inde-
pendent causal problems (Longxuan Yu, Delin Chen, Siheng Xiong, Qingyang Wu, Qingzhen
Liu, Dawei Li, Zhikai Chen, Xiaoze Liu and Liangming Pan, 2025). The same issue arises in the
proposal’s authored tasks. Its development collection contains 24 variants in twelve template
groups; its reserved collection contains 48 variants in twenty-four groups, with two variants in
every group. These assets support interface and rubric development. Their authorship and
generation history do not establish independent, identically distributed final mechanisms or
independently adjudicated causal truth (Causal proposal project, 2026a).


Mechanisms, information and the reference answer

A final task should begin with a declared scientific information state. For a generated structural
model, the evaluator can retain the full graph, assignment mechanism and intervention outcomes
while the analysis sees only its permitted observations and metadata. The reference must
answer two questions: what is true in the generating world, and what is identified from the
information supplied to the method? They need not have the same answer. An agent that
guesses the hidden true effect in a nonidentifying problem has not correctly solved identification.
   The task portfolio retains six functional families: business formulation; clocks and selection;
graph construction and discovery; identification and estimator choice; evidence tracing; and tool
composition. Across them, stress conditions include hidden confounding, temporal dependence,
treatment– confounder feedback, panel assignment, imperfect linkage and ambiguous monetary
objectives. A selected first experiment need not claim every condition at once. Its included
cells, excluded capabilities and substantive alternatives should be fixed before evaluation rather
than chosen from successful outputs.
   The split should occur at mechanism and template-family level before paraphrases, renamed
variables or translations are created. A new name for a familiar graph does not make its
mechanism unseen. Public benchmarks require their own provenance and label review; public
availability does not establish absence from a model’s training data. A generated final collection
must have its generator, information restrictions and scoring rules checked before the final
draw. Prompts and retrieval settings are chosen on a separate development collection. Any
inspected final case is recorded as exposed, and subsequent method changes require a new
evaluation revision.
  Author-reviewed algebraic references can support a bounded proposal demonstration. Am-
biguous business language, source applicability and multilingual meaning may also require
378                                                          Causal analysis for a universal bank


human judgment. Such judgments should use a frozen rubric, method-blinded presentation
and retained disagreements. Until independent adjudicators actually participate, the result
must remain an author-reviewed study. Neither a generated label nor agreement between two
model responses substitutes for authentic bank assignment evidence.
   The adverse conditions should change both language and information. Useful paired variants
include an unfamiliar variable vocabulary, a unit change, a delayed feature timestamp, a quoted
but scientifically unsupported causal claim, a misleading retrieved graph, and conflict between
text and observed data. Additional languages require a checked translation that preserves
the population, intervention, clock and uncertainty. Language versions and stochastic repeats
stay nested within the original mechanism. At least one primary variant must be chosen
prospectively for the binary comparison derived below; sensitivity results on the other variants
remain visible.


What each comparator is allowed to know

The comparison should hold a backend fixed while changing its information and tool access.
This separates the value of retrieval and numerical composition from a change in the underlying
model. Comparing backends can be a later, explicitly costed dimension. Four proposed live
arms are a frozen prompt alone; the same model with audited retrieval; the same model
with typed numerical tools; and a hybrid with both. A critique step can be ablated within
the hybrid when it fits the same declared total resource budget. It is not free additional
computation.
  The model-only arm receives the same declared task and permitted summaries, but no
hidden graph or numerical-tool result. Retrieval arms use an immutable corpus and a fixed
query/ranking policy, and save the returned passages. Tool arms share pinned algorithms and
the same observations. Constraint proposals must state their evidence and can be refused
by the numerical operation. A proposed restriction cannot silently change the population,
sampling law or model class to make an inconvenient query identifiable.
   Non-model comparators remain essential. A deterministic form/schema workflow tests
whether structured elicitation is sufficient. A data-only estimator tests the numerical stage
on admissible structured inputs. A retrieval-only system tests whether locating a primary
passage suffices. These comparators have different roles: a data-only estimator given a correct
structured estimand is not simultaneously solving free-text business translation. Report stage-
specific results and end-to-end results with the information differences exposed. Human and
human-plus-model workflows are optional additional arms whose time, expertise and reference
independence must be measured rather than inferred from a model benchmark.
   Equal budgets should cover total tokens, model calls, tool calls, elapsed time and retries
per assigned task. If one arm consumes less than its cap, retain that advantage in the cost
account. If an agent uses more calls, compare its benefit against the additional actual cost. A
transport retry and a deliberate internal critique are different events; both belong in the call
ledger. Timeouts, parse failures and exhausted budgets remain assigned outcomes.


Useful abstention and unjustified certainty

Let Ui indicate a useful, scientifically correct resolution of an assigned task, Ei a critical
scientific error, and Ai availability of a usable response. The rubric requires Ui ≤ Ai and
Ui Ei = 0. A useful resolution can be a justified effect set or a specific request for missing
information. It cannot be an unsupported point estimate or a generic refusal unrelated to the
task.

   Graph scoring compares the returned object with the admitted equivalence class. Unsup-

scalar target; set results retain disconnected components, empty sets and unbounded regions.
Coverage and length are separate outcomes, and infinite length stays infinite. Monetary policy

measurement of bank ROI.

Consider an illustrative critical-error indicator for independent, identically distributed mecha-

Cost, freezing and the next decision

For each model call, retain input, output and cache-token counts, model revision, chargeable
tool actions and the actual dated price schedule. Add retrieval, numerical computation, storage,

human review and rework. Unknown prices remain missing; public tasks do not imply free

                  X

where token rates and token counts use matching units and cache distinctions are retained

   For illustration, 100 independent mechanisms in each of six disjoint task families, two
variants per mechanism and four live arms give 4,800 assigned arm-variant cases. Three
attempts and up to three internal model calls per attempt yield a conservative envelope of

   Before any final model calls, the design must bind exact backend revisions, generation
settings, permitted endpoints, prompts, retrieval corpus, numerical algorithms, final mechanism
distribution and draw, reference adjudication, primary contrasts, multiplicity allocation,
numerical thresholds and a priced resource ceiling. A fixed stopping rule retains all assigned
tasks. A global outage or exhausted budget is recorded as an interruption with unexecuted
cases visible, not repaired by silently replacing difficult cases. A materially changed model or
prompt requires a new evaluation identity.
   The recommendation is therefore to fund a bounded prototype comparison only when its
development evidence identifies a consequential uncertainty and its expected information can
change the next investment choice. The proposal can already specify the experiment, expose its
likely precision and resource trade-offs, and reject unsupported universal performance claims.
Authentic bank experiments become worthwhile when the resulting prototype leaves a specific
transport, assignment or operating question that public and generated evidence cannot answer.
