the value of assistance

38.1      Value belongs to a decision and an information set
The value of an agent is the change it makes to a feasible decision after including its information,
review and operating costs. Producing a longer report, drawing more edges or executing a
notebook faster can help that decision, but none is the economic target itself. The banking
application must specify the action, baseline workflow, affected population, financial horizon
and loss before comparing systems.
   Let a range over feasible actions and let V (a, θ) be their monetary value under a causal
state θ. An information set I might contain observed data, authenticated design records and
unresolved alternatives. If a justified probability law for θ is available, an expected-value
decision solves
                               a∗ (I) ∈ arg max E{V (a, θ) | I}.
                                               a

This expression is a decision rule conditional on a probability model. A language model’s
self-reported certainty, the frequency of repeated answers, or a fraction of retrieved documents
is not automatically that probability. The distinction matters most when a small change in
the assumed probability changes a lending, servicing or funding action.
   If the evidence instead supports a set Θ(I) without probabilities, the bank needs an explicit
ambiguity policy. For example, a robust rule can maximize inf θ∈Θ(I) V (a, θ). Expected value
and this robust criterion answer different decision questions. The software must preserve the
information needed for either and require the policy to be named. It must not manufacture
a distribution by assigning equal weight to whichever graphs an algorithm happened to
enumerate.


38.2      An exact example of useful and costly information
Consider a stipulated one-customer intervention whose incremental gross return is either
CNY 0 or CNY 400, with intervention cost CNY 300. Suppose the two states have equal prior
probability. These are project assumptions for an arithmetic example, not bank estimates,
elicited probabilities or measured model performance. Acting has expected net return 200 −
300 = −100, so the unassisted expected-value decision is to do nothing, with value zero.
  Perfect information would permit action only in the CNY 400 state. Its expected gross


                                                382
38.3. Refusal can preserve value, but it also consumes resources                                383


value relative to doing nothing is therefore
                         1                   1
                         2 max(0, 0 − 300) + 2 max(0, 400 − 300) = 50.

For this action set and loss, no information service can justify an expected payment above
CNY 50 per decision solely through improved action selection. The bound would change if the
service had other validated benefits or changed the feasible actions; neither is assumed here.
   Now stipulate a binary signal that reports “positive” with probability 0.9 in the high-return
state and 0.1 in the low-return state. Each signal outcome has marginal probability 0.5. Bayes’
rule gives posterior high-state probabilities 0.9 after a positive signal and 0.1 after a negative
signal. The conditional net returns from acting are respectively

                        0.9(400) − 300 = 60,            0.1(400) − 300 = −260.

The optimal rule acts only after a positive signal. Its gross expected value is 0.5(60) = 30. An
independent calculation keeps the loss from false positives visible:

                               0.5(0.9)(100) − 0.5(0.1)(300) = 30.
                               |      {z       }    |       {z       }
                               true-positive gain   false-positive loss

The information value is below the perfect-information bound, as it should be.
   Suppose obtaining and checking the signal costs CNY 2 in computation and CNY 8 in
review for every request, including negative ones. The incremental net value is then CNY 20.
Under the additional simplifying assumptions of identical expected value, linear costs and no
discounting, a CNY 50,000 fixed development cost breaks even at 50,000/20 = 2,500 decisions.
These figures are reproduced with exact rational arithmetic. They are a transparent planning
construction, not a price quotation or an ROI estimate for the implemented prototype.
   The threshold for acting is a high-state probability above 300/400 = 0.75. An assistant
that says “90% confident” can cross that threshold without having a calibrated probability.
Review must establish the meaning and reliability of the signal. A syntactically valid report, a
correct posterior formula and an accurate multiplication cannot compensate for an invented
likelihood.


38.3      Refusal can preserve value, but it also consumes resources
If all that is defensible is the set Θ = {0, 400}, robust net value from acting is −300, while doing
nothing guarantees zero incremental value. The robust rule therefore declines the intervention.
This conclusion differs from a claim that the true effect is zero. It expresses how the bank
chooses under unresolved uncertainty and the stated loss.
  A service that exposes the ambiguity can be valuable if the incumbent workflow would act
on a falsely precise estimate. The evaluation must include that incumbent behavior explicitly.
Against an already cautious baseline, the same refusal may add little decision value while still
costing analyst time. A refusal is neither automatically a failure nor automatically a benefit.
  The inspected observational workflow illustrates this problem through critic declines under
poor overlap.Chou et al. (2026) The denominator must include the declined requests, their
review cost and what happened next. Did a reviewer obtain a better design, narrow the
population with explicit authorization, commission an experiment, or simply lose time? Each
path has a different economic implication. Changing to a selected population must also change
the target rather than make the original request appear successful.
384                                                               Causal analysis for a universal bank


38.4     Four banking journeys require different evidence
For a funding decision, assistance can assemble the rate action, balance units, margin horizon
and policy constraints. It can also flag a mismatch between calendar covariance and an
assumed independent sampling unit. Value arises only if these corrections improve a decision
or avert an error relative to the baseline. A conservative interval wider than the bank’s action
threshold may be scientifically defensible and economically inconclusive.
   For sequential servicing, the central object is a policy adapted to information available at
each decision. The total bill includes state measurement, assignment logging, intervention
delivery and customer outcomes, as well as model calls. An agent can help describe a dynamic
regime, but a static ATE translator cannot evaluate it by substituting a single treatment
indicator. The economic study must compare genuinely feasible policies under common
information and count unsuccessful or unavailable evaluations.
   For discovery followed by intervention, a visually simpler graph can conceal alternative
effects. The useful information is whether additional evidence changes the set of financially
acceptable actions. More accurate recovery of irrelevant edges may have little value for the
selected decision. Conversely, one mistaken orientation near the treatment or outcome can
reverse a policy recommendation. Graph accuracy and decision loss should both be reported,
with neither used as a proxy for the other.
   For trustworthy observations, a language system can reconcile field names and suggest
ownership or inclusion questions. The bank must still establish actual linkage, label and audit
truth. Reviewing a source dictionary may prevent a semantic error; it does not supply sampled
identity labels or independent calendars. The cost of obtaining those scientific inputs belongs
in the information budget, and their absence remains a legitimate stop condition for an effect
calculation.


38.5     A complete cost model
For request i, a prospective accounting identity is

           Ci = Ci,model + Ci,retrieval + Ci,numeric + Ci,review + Ci,data + Ci,operation .

The terms represent distinct resource uses, not independently measured values in the current
project. Model cost includes all calls and retries. Retrieval includes acquisition and any
permitted indexing. Numerical cost includes the complete fit, uncertainty calculation and
serialization. Review includes time spent on wrong, refused and unsupported answers. Data
cost includes audits and additional information. Operations include storage, recovery and
support.
   A natural-workflow comparison measures the quality and cost of complete workflows. A
matched-budget comparison holds selected resources fixed to study one contribution. The
two can produce different rankings without contradiction. An agent that improves answers by
using more expert review may be valuable, but the result is about the combined workflow. It
does not isolate autonomous reasoning quality.
   The experimental unit must also match the cost and outcome calculation. Repeated prompts
about one mechanism are correlated observations within that mechanism. Counting them
as independent bank decisions understates uncertainty and can exaggerate the amount of
evidence. Error bars for incremental value should use the prespecified mechanism or decision
clusters and retain the paired comparison wherever both workflows face the same problem.
38.6. What can be concluded before a live evaluation                                      385


38.6     What can be concluded before a live evaluation
The local controller demonstrates preservation of declarations, alternatives, refusals and
numerical set topology in selected authored examples. It makes zero live model calls. Its
measured interface behavior cannot reveal a provider’s accuracy, token use, price or review
burden on unfamiliar questions. Those fields remain unavailable rather than being filled with
zeros.
   Published benchmarks support the design of a prospective evaluation. They cannot be
combined across different model revisions, task distributions and information budgets into
a bank ROI estimate. CausalDS in particular reports divergence between symbolic success,
interval quality, abstention and cost, which supports measuring them separately.Leban and
Sun (2026)
   The next empirical step requires a specified backend and custody arrangement, actual prices
and budget, independent held-out mechanisms, adjudicators and qualified numerical baselines.
For bank adoption it additionally requires feasible actions, authentic records and accepted
loss thresholds. Until those inputs exist, exact decision examples can check the accounting
and expose threshold errors. They cannot establish that assistance crosses an institutional
investment threshold.
Chapter 39

Deriving a common causal-analysis
product

The bank’s recurring difficulty is that an analysis crosses several scientific representations. A
commercial question names a feasible action and a financial consequence. Its data are event
records with changing identities and reporting delays. An economist supplies restrictions
on assignment or shocks; a learner estimates conditional distributions; a validator needs a
sampling argument; a decision maker needs the value of a feasible policy. A shared product is
useful when it preserves the meaning of the question across those transformations.
   The proposed product is a library and a standalone analytical workspace built around the
same scientific objects. Its first release should expose a bounded collection of well-defined
operations. More general discovery, inverse problems and latent control remain important
research capabilities, but their outputs must retain the assumptions and unresolved alternatives
developed in the preceding chapters. The construction below derives this boundary; it is a
specification, not a claim that the entire product already exists.


39.1     The scientific request is larger than an estimator call
Write a request as
                                   Q = (M, K, g, ν, θ, E, F),                              (39.1)
where M is a class of causal models, K the observation operator, g the intervention, ν the target
population, θ the requested functional, E the sampling experiment and F the information
available to the decision rule. For a model M ∈ M, the observed law is P = K(M ) and the
causal answer is θ(M ; g, ν). The observation operator includes selection, measurement, clocks,
aggregation and record linkage when relevant. The sampling experiment specifies independent
households, randomized branches, a dependent calendar series, or another explicit design.
   For deposit retention, the request might ask for the difference in six-month discounted net
funding contribution under two invitation rules for households eligible on a specified date.
It must distinguish invitation from receipt, and baseline eligible households from eventual
activators. If the action is instead an increase in offered interest, both customer balances and
the price paid on existing balances change. These are different interventions and financial
functionals even when the same table is used.
  The target needs a measurable definition before computation. For example, with monthly




                                              386
39.2. Identification returns a mathematical object or an explicit limit                                  387


contribution Rt in a declared currency and discount factor dt , use
                                                 "T −1             #           "T −1             #
                                                         dt Rtg1                       dt Rtg0
                                                  X                             X
                      θ(M ; g1 , g0 , ν) = EνM                         − EνM                         .
                                                  t=0                           t=0

Here Rt includes the agreed funding, servicing, incentive and expected loss components without
counting the same balance benefit twice. An average balance effect is an input to this account,
not already its answer. Currency conversion, discounting, exposure weights and eligibility are
part of the target rather than invisible formatting options.
   Several request fields can be inferred syntactically from data, but the scientific restrictions
cannot. Software can detect a duplicate decision or a covariate first recorded after action. It
cannot infer that a pricing instrument has no direct effect or that all private underwriting
information has been measured. The workspace should let an analyst draw and explain
the model, compare plausible alternatives, and attach empirical diagnostics to particular
restrictions. A single numerical validity score would erase the distinction between those
obligations.


39.2      Identification returns a mathematical object or an explicit
          limit
Define the identified set

                          ΘQ (P ) = {θ(M ; g, ν) : M ∈ M, K(M ) = P }.

An identification routine receives the model and observation declarations; it does not receive
permission to add whichever assumptions make a preferred estimator available. A singleton
set can be represented by an observed-law functional Ψ(P ). A non-singleton set may admit
bounds, a union of functionals, or only a nonidentification witness. The useful result types are
therefore distinct.
Identified expression.
An expression for Ψ together with the assumptions and transformations that derive it. Numer-
ical evaluation may still be unsupported.
Identified set or outer bound.
A set with its model class, support, restrictions and sharpness status. A conservative outer
bound is useful, but must not be labelled sharp without a compatible-model construction.
Nonidentification witness.
Two allowed models with the same observed law and different targets, or a valid source-specific
failure certificate such as a hedge in the applicable ID model.
Unsupported query.
The registered algorithm does not handle the graph class, intervention, observation process or
requested target. This makes no claim that the target is unidentified.
Incompatible specification.
The declarations are logically inconsistent or violate a deterministic support/schema require-
ment. A statistical model-check rejection should separately carry its test and error level.
   These types follow from Chapter 1 and the ID/IDC construction of Shpitser and Pearl
(2006). Failure to find a back-door set is not a nonidentification certificate. Nor is failure
of an optimizer. For example, the front-door expression is identified under its restrictions,
but a backend implementing only covariate adjustment should return an identified expression
with no available estimator. Conversely, the two invitation models of Section 2.3 agree on
388                                                           Causal analysis for a universal bank


all observed records and disagree on the population ATE. Increasing an estimator’s iteration
budget cannot supply that missing information.
   For an initial implementation, observed-law expressions can use a small typed language:
conditional probability kernels, products, integrals or finite sums, substitutions, and ratios on
declared positive support. A kernel records its random arguments, conditioning arguments,
units, dominating measure and observation regime. The type of p(y | a, x) differs from pg (y | x);
a density in currency units differs from a probability mass. Marginalization removes a random
argument; it must not accidentally integrate a fixed intervention value.
   Each allowed transformation should produce a trace. In ordinary adjustment, that trace
names the adjustedR
                     variables, explains why their predecision status and separation condition
apply, and yields p(y | a, x)p(x) dx. In recursive ID, it records ancestors, districts, extracted
kernels and support restrictions. The trace certifies the consequence of the supplied assumptions.
It cannot certify that the graph supplied by a bank economist is the true graph.


39.3     Adapters must preserve targets and statistical experi-
         ments
The target-preservation identity Ψ(P ) = ΨB (T# P ) in Section 17.1 is necessary for converting
data through T to backend B. It also constrains uncertainty. Suppose, for this paragraph, that
observations Oi are independent and identically distributed, T is fixed and applied separately
to each unit, and Z = T (O). Let Pε be a regular submodel with score S(O). Differentiating
the pushforward density gives the reduced score

                                     SZ (Z) = E[S(O) | Z].

If ϕB (Z) is a gradient for the reduced functional, then
                                d
                                   Ψ(Pε ) = E[ϕB (Z)SZ (Z)]
                                dε       0
                                           = E[ϕB (T (O))S(O)].                            (39.2)

Thus the pulled-back score is a gradient for the original target. In an unrestricted original
model it is the canonical gradient when the stated differentiability conditions hold; in a
restricted model projection onto the model’s tangent space may improve efficiency. This is
a project consequence of the pathwise argument in Chapter 3, not a theorem for arbitrary
preprocessing.
   The qualifications explain common failures. A learned encoder is random and may need
independent training and a remainder analysis. Demeaning over a panel is not a fixed
transformation of each independently sampled row. Expanding one household into transactions
changes the sampling units. Discarding a component of history may destroy target preservation.
An adapter must therefore declare both its mathematical transformation and its mapping of
sampling units, weights and information sets.
   A backend estimator should return sufficient information for the specified inference route.
For a regular scalar moment this includes unit-level scores, the Jacobian, target normalization,
fold assignments and nuisance estimates or their immutable references. For an identified set
it includes bound objectives and constraint certificates. For a weak-IV inversion it includes
the accepted set, including disconnected or unbounded components. For a likelihood model it
includes the exact factorization, numerical approximation and parameter restrictions. Forcing
all of these outputs into an estimate/standard-error pair would discard information that
changes the bank decision.
39.4. A bounded mathematical language and a concrete lowering rule                             389


   The companion scientific protocol gives this separation a concrete design form. A request
binds the model, observation, target and sampling specifications by content hash. A result
separately records computational completion, identification and inferential availability. A scalar
confidence set is an ordered union of intervals, including empty, disconnected and unbounded
sets; posterior credible sets have a different type. Derivations, bounds and failure witnesses
have distinct artifact roles. The supplied schema fixtures check these representation invariants.
They do not execute an identification algorithm or establish coverage. The following versioned
extension supplies explicit vector, curve and graph-set types for the bounded constructions
developed in this monograph. A general graph probability distribution remains a different
object.


39.4      A bounded mathematical language and a concrete lower-
          ing rule
The specification must be stronger than a collection of file hashes. A variable declaration
contains its name, support, physical unit, causal role and clock. A population declaration
identifies the economic unit and the role of its weights. An observation declaration identifies the
immutable view, revision relation, availability convention and sampling frequency. The model
specifies a structural class and an assumption set. A target specifies the action, outcomes, fixed
horizons or policies, normalization and population. These declarations together determine a
statistical experiment; no single field can substitute for the others.
  For finite mechanisms an executable expression grammar is particularly transparent. A
mass kernel has ordered parent variables U , ordered child variables V , declared finite supports
and an array of shape |XU | × |XV |. Every parent slice must be nonnegative and sum to one
over the child axes. A generative product j Kj (xj | xpa(j) ) requires one mechanism per child
                                          Q

and a topological order. Marginalization sums named random axes; substitution fixes an axis
without summing it. Replacing an action mechanism by g(a | h) requires that its information
variables precede the action. This operation evaluates the supplied causal factorization; it
does not establish that an arbitrary observed kernel can be intervened upon.
   The local finite-mass interpreter implements product, marginalization and mechanism
replacement, checking support, normalization and information order. For a binary confounded
example it recovers the interventional mean 0.5 and rejects a policy using a future outcome. A
general expression language would additionally need density measures, positive-denominator
restrictions and numerical integration error. The initial lowering rules do not pretend that
this finite interpreter implements continuous ID or general latent identification. Instead they
recognize the complete constructions already derived and reject mismatched target/sampling
combinations.

   These are conditional method choices, not six interchangeable backends. The standalone
reference runner checks the request and data identities, dispatches these bounded numerical
recipes and validates their typed result. Its two servicing families retain their stated reward,
state and policy semantics; a new family requires a new mathematical and numerical qualifica-

with declared learner settings. General controlled continuous states, unrestricted temporal
discovery and policy optimization remain separate extension requests.


39.4.1    Results that can carry the actual uncertainty

Protocol version 0.4 supplements the historical scalar protocol. A scalar is a one-coordinate
result; vectors and response curves have named ordered axes and one physical unit per flattened
coordinate. A response curve orders outcome before horizon. Its covariance has that same
coordinate order and already includes the sample-size divisor. A confidence object carries its
method, level, coverage target and an interval union for each coordinate. For a simultaneous
rectangular set, the Cartesian product of these unions is the confidence region. Empty,
disconnected and unbounded coordinate sets remain representable; an unbounded endpoint is
a typed null, not a JSON infinity or a large arbitrary number. Pointwise coverage cannot be
relabeled simultaneous by an adapter.
   A graph result retains ordered nodes and its graph class. A DAG set stores directed binary
adjacency matrices. CPDAG/PAG endpoint matrices use zero for absence, one for a tail, two
for an arrowhead and three for a circle; the latter is permitted only for a PAG. Basic endpoint
validation is not a complete PAG-recognition algorithm. The temporal reference instead stores
lower and upper coefficient matrices with edge marks “present” or “zero or nonzero”. Its graph
class is not a posterior distribution over graphs. The effect union is explicitly an outer set,
and uncertainty about the causal-sufficiency assumption is not encoded as its confidence level.
   Computational completion, conditional identification and inference have separate status
fields. Numerical error bounds, when available, use the same output units. A null numerical
bound means no certified bound was provided; it must not be interpreted as zero error. Solver
diagnostics and all requested failed repetitions remain attached evidence. Hashes bind those
arrays and declarations to a computation, while scientific validation determines whether their
asserted premises are plausible.
39.5. Concrete sibling boundaries and the standalone study                                        391


39.4.2    Allowed conversions and explicit rejection cases

For a fixed known diagonal scale matrix S, the converted effect and covariance are S θb and S Vb S ′ .
Interval endpoints reverse when a scale is negative; the order of disconnected components
also reverses. A rate denominator changing from percentage points to basis points divides a
normalized response by 100. A fixed currency multiplier can be applied in the same way. A
time-varying exchange rate generally changes the reward functional and requires rebuilding it;
a monthly stock cannot be converted into daily flows by relabeling an axis.
   Population weights, inverse behavior probabilities, inverse observation probabilities and
bootstrap frequencies have different mathematical roles. The request validator rejects their
substitution. It also rejects an iid row experiment for the dependent response route, a split
inside a purportedly independent trajectory, inclusive availability when the request requires
strict predecision information, and a learned policy supplied to fixed-policy inference. A
valid clock conversion can preserve timestamp/sequence order exactly; changing that order
requires a new observation analysis. These checks enforce declared meaning, not the truth of
exchangeability or instrument exclusion.


39.5      Concrete sibling boundaries and the standalone study
Read-only inspection of the actual sibling APIs changes the integration design. FinMarketing’s
CausalData.from_record requires pretreatment features, mature outcomes, binary actions
and independent groups. Its FeatureSnapshot orders availability, cutoff and decision by
timestamp/sequence pairs. The local mapping preserves those pairs, horizon and dependence
unit. It does not coerce a dynamic curve into FinMarketing’s scalar Estimate; that requires a
richer result consumer. A causal response to a macro shock also cannot inherit its independent-
group standard error merely because the source rows are account records.
   dataml’s LineageGraph.append accepts run, dataset, partition and metadata, while its cor-
rection schema requires a resolvable assumption and a numerical confidence field. Observation
candidates therefore map to lineage metadata with their assumptions and alternatives. An
uncalibrated hint score does not populate correction confidence, and ambiguous candidates do
not generate an automatic correction. This preserves dataml’s distinction between an original
source and an assumed overlay.
   BayesFilter’s SSMStaticShape, SSMDataSignature and BayesianSSMProblem can record
dimensions, data/mask identities and parameter coordinates. For the binary controlled family,
the local mapping adds action identity, randomized-logger semantics, reward, finite state
support and the full observation order to its model manifest. A generic Bayesian SSM
descriptor alone does not supply those causal meanings or a controlled categorical filter
implementation. Its numerical target and derivative still need to refer to the same likelihood,
as required by Chapter 7.
   MacroFinance’s DirectedPairMeasurement and ObservationContract distinguish
directed quote pairs, maturity, observed rows and derived diagnostics. Its convention is
xm = −χ; reversing a pair reverses the quoted wedge sign. The local mapping preserves these
identities and requires a separate causal role for the measured variable. A triangle diagnostic
is not automatically an identified structural cycle intervention. The inspected MacroFinance
BayesFilter facade also references a different import root from the workspace checkout, so
inspection alone cannot establish runtime compatibility between them.
  The same scientific request/result files support an independent study: choose the economic
target and observation plan, inspect the identifying assumptions, select a supported regime,
392                                                         Causal analysis for a universal bank


execute its estimator and mandatory comparison, and publish the result with its uncertainty
and source trace. Local examples exercise the mappings and numerical operations here. Sibling
checkouts remain unchanged; accepted adoption, shared release management and institutional
data access remain separate implementation work.

   For adjusted and longitudinal means, the product can initially support the scores derived in
Chapters 3 and 5, with finite categorical actions and fixed horizons. This is a useful construction
boundary: it permits both simple randomized comparisons and repeated collections policies
while keeping the intervention density explicit. A continuous deterministic intervention under
a continuous observed action law is not automatically absolutely continuous; density ratios for
point masses require a different identification/estimation route. Modified policies and smooth
stochastic shifts can supply one, under the assumptions in Chapter 6.
  Panel support should begin with specified cohort estimands and strong linear-moment
baselines, not an unrestricted auto-panel operation. The equal-weight branch target, household
target and balance-weighted target require different aggregations. Temporal shock support
should likewise identify a normalized response under the stated instrument exclusions, with
the fixed-horizon inference of Section 9.5. Structural breaks and weak impact normalizations
should produce an explicit alternative analysis.
   Controlled latent support can be valuable before a general latent causal identification engine
exists. The same workspace can compare a randomized logging model, a private-logging model
and an observed-history policy value, displaying which conclusions require which assumptions.
The known-emission inversion in Section 7.2 supplies a finite validation case; it is not a general
theorem for learned emissions. Proxy-value routes should be registered with their bridge and
rank conditions rather than offered through a generic hidden-state option.


39.7      Estimation and uncertainty form one qualified composi-
          tion
An inference contract has five parts: the target and its differentiability class; an estimator
expansion; the statistical sampling units; the covariance or test construction; and the conditions
controlling nuisance and numerical error. For a regular vector target one common form is
                                     1X                          √
                    θb − θ = −Jb−1       ψi (θ, η0 ) + Rn ,          nRn = op (1),
                                     n i

where the meaning of n and the scaling must match the experiment. Independent trajectories,
independent clusters with variable sizes, crossed arrays and a long time series imply different
normalizations and limit arguments. A covariance option alone cannot establish them.
   For one-way independent clusters, reduction of all score contributions within each cluster
precedes forming outer products. For crossed entity/date dependence, inclusion–exclusion of
cluster covariance components requires the appropriate crossed-array assumptions; a large
entity count does not compensate for a fixed handful of macro dates. Multiway cross-fitting
must prevent training/evaluation overlap in the relevant coordinates (Chiang et al., 2021). A
simple entity split is not automatically a multiway construction.
   For a time series, keep the time order, outcome window, separation gap and score bandwidth
as distinct fields. Overlapping outcomes can extend dependence past disjoint origin blocks.
394                                                                           Causal analysis for a universal bank


When a stationary mixing argument is invoked, its mixing and moment restrictions must be
named. A user selecting a HAC option has specified an estimator family, not proved that a
structural-break or unit-root score obeys the required CLT. Simultaneous bands require a joint
horizon construction.
   Uncertainty for weakly identified parameters, nonsmooth bounds and selected policies needs
separate operations. Ratios with weak denominators should use a qualified test inversion;
graph ambiguity requires a union or other defensible set operation. Learned-policy evaluation
must distinguish a frozen policy on an independent evaluation sample from a data-adaptive
optimal-value target. Bayesian posterior intervals require their likelihood, prior and numerical
diagnostics; they cannot inherit frequentist coverage merely because they are called credible.
   The result should consequently carry several evidence dimensions: identification conditional
on stated restrictions, numerical convergence, sampling inference, sensitivity to disputed
restrictions and decision adequacy. A converged point estimate can coexist with unsupported
uncertainty. A wide but valid confidence set can be adequate for a decision if every contained
model favors the same affordable action.


39.8      Policy evaluation has a separate information boundary
A controlled-state adapter must expose the observational and interventional laws separately.
In the finite model, a pre-action belief is bt (s) = P (St = s | Ht ). Under a private logger, after
seeing the historical action it becomes proportional to bt (s)qη (At | s, Ht ) before the transition,
reward and next signal update. Under an intervention using only the recorded history, the
action density gt (At | Ht ) is constant across hidden states and cancels in normalized filtering.
Replacing the logger changes the law, not simply one input tensor.
   The planner receives a distribution over the information it is allowed to use. A smoothed
posterior P (St | HT ), T > t, includes future evidence and is not an online policy state. A
retrospective smoother is useful for fitting and diagnosis, while prospective evaluation must
reconstruct the predecision filter. The adapter must also specify whether reward is observed
before the next signal and whether reward carries additional information about the state.
  For a supplied causal model the finite-horizon value recursion is
                                                     Z                                            
                                                                          ′            ′
              Vt (b) = max            rt (b, a) + γ       Vt+1 (τt (b, a, o , r)) pt (do , dr | b, a) .
                       a∈At (b)

The belief update τt and predictive observation/reward law must use the same factorization.
This is the information-state construction of Kaelbling et al. (1998) specialized to the declared
timing. For this display all decision-relevant recorded context is assumed to be included in the
belief state or its explicit arguments. Action constraints can depend on recorded eligibility,
customer consent and a specified budget. An estimate of a hidden risk state does not authorize
using unavailable information in those constraints.
  Model ambiguity creates another decision problem. If MP contains several observationally
compatible causal models, a robust policy may maximize inf M ∈MP VM (π). In general the
same M must govern the whole trajectory. A stagewise minimization that freely chooses a
new adverse model at each date solves a larger, rectangular uncertainty problem. Its result
can be conservative and need not be the sharp value bound for persistent hidden types. The
dynamic-bound analysis of Section 16.7 shows why the uncertainty-set type must accompany
the planning algorithm.
  For a two-date fixed policy with no discount, suppose the allowed reward vectors are (0, 1)
and (1, 0), with one model applying at both dates. Worst-case total value is one. Independently
39.9. Discovery should improve a decision-relevant model class                               395


choosing the worse component at each date instead gives zero, a vector absent from the original
model class. This exact example isolates the extra freedom introduced by rectangularization;
it is not a claim that a bank’s ambiguity set contains those two models.
   Finally, solver error needs its own budget. The Bellman residual bound in Section 7.5
controls numerical error for the specified contraction. Parameter uncertainty, model ambiguity,
reward accounting and policy support remain separate. A planner can report a precise solution
to a scientifically weak model; the user needs enough information to recognize that situation.


39.9      Discovery should improve a decision-relevant model class
The discovery workspace begins with mechanisms and timing. It proposes variables and
lags from the available data, records business restrictions, and returns a DAG, CPDAG,
PAG or named functional-model object with its endpoint semantics intact. Metadata lineage
is displayed separately from causal ancestry. An upstream database dependency does not
establish an economic intervention edge.
  The next operation asks a specific causal query across compatible models. For the chain
example of Section 10.9, the observed Gaussian covariance and CPDAG imply effects {0, 1/4}
within the declared linear causally sufficient class. The product should expose both values,
explain the orientations that produce them, and show which credible timing information
or intervention would distinguish them. Returning the effect of one arbitrarily oriented
representative would turn an unresolved scientific question into a spurious estimate.
   General PAG completion is expensive and may still leave latent nonidentification within
each completion. The first bounded route should therefore use verified generalized-adjustment
criteria on supported graph classes (Perković et al., 2018), small enumerated classes for exact
examples, and unresolved results beyond those capabilities. Search limits, CI test assumptions,
variable screening and lag windows must be retained. A timeout is computationally unresolved,
not a certificate that no adjustment set exists.
   A useful experiment recommendation should name the ambiguity it resolves. For deposit
pricing, a randomized encouragement may distinguish a price response from latent liquidity
selection. For collections, a new predecision signal may improve a bridge’s measurement rank.
For treasury, a higher-frequency observation may remove an aliasing ambiguity. Their cost and
decision value can be compared; edge-count improvement alone is not the economic objective.


39.10      Acceptance is a collection of scientific obligations
Each registered operation needs a reviewable construction dossier. It contains the exact target
and restrictions, an identification derivation or witness, an estimator/inference derivation, the
qualified backend version and transformation, and reproducible positive and negative examples.
Exact finite laws should be used when they expose semantic errors that a large benchmark
can conceal.
  For adjustment, compare the estimator’s population expression with explicit intervention
enumeration, and include a confounded pair of models that observation cannot distinguish. For
IV, hold the observed law fixed while changing the unobserved outcomes of never-takers; ensure
that the requested ATE remains unresolved although LATE is returned. For longitudinal
analysis, verify the recursive score under feedback, then change the policy’s dependence on the
propensity and require the corresponding gradient change.
  For controlled states, enumerate hidden paths to check the likelihood, filter and sufficient
396                                                                 Causal analysis for a universal bank


counts with and without the logger; compare interventional value against independent dynamic
programming. For discovery, round-trip all endpoint marks and propagate every supported
completion into its effect set. For data organization, delay and revise events across the decision
boundary and verify exactly which history the policy receives. For distributed inference,
repartition the same scores across workers and preserve folds, cluster sums and accepted
uncertainty sets.
   Repeated-sample experiments then assess bias, coverage or policy regret under named laws,
including failures of support, rank, stationarity and model specification. Their purpose is to
test the implemented construction and characterize its operating range. They do not prove
that the bank’s unobserved confounding assumption holds. Bank data validation subsequently
evaluates the actual information, process and financial account.
   This division makes a staged product possible without shrinking its scientific ambition. A
bank can use rigorous observed-history analyses while researchers develop controlled latent and
discovery-to-effect routes in the same representations. Promotion of a method then requires its
missing mathematical and empirical obligations to be discharged, rather than a new wrapper
around an attractive estimator name.

           tions
The common layer should earn its cost by preserving meaning across reused operations. A
small implemented composition begins with an AdjustmentQuery: action, outcome, controls,
population unit, outcome units and sampling law. A supplied acyclic graph is checked using
the sufficient back-door criterion: reject action descendants among controls, remove outgoing
action arrows, take the ancestral moral graph and test separation after removing the controls.
A passing trace determines the functional

  Whole-unit folds produce out-of-fold predictions. A separate score operation forms

39.11.1     A substantive package adapter with a matched reference

DoubleML 0.11.4 provides an installed IRM ATE operation (Bach et al., 2022; doubleml
contributors, 2026). The adapter supplies the exact same folds and nuisance predictions as the
independent score calculation, uses unnormalized inverse weights and propensity truncation at
.01, and checks the resulting estimate and standard error. Across the six public learner/split
runs and the second bank-contact example, coefficient discrepancy is zero and standard-error
discrepancy is at most 4.55 × 10−13 . This is a meaningful test of target, weight and covariance
semantics under matched inputs. Comparing independently fitted learners would conflate
those semantics with nuisance variation; the public study reports that second comparison
separately.
   The software choice is to reuse DoubleML for the qualified static semiparametric oper-
ation and Tigramite for qualified temporal search. Build the observation/clock contracts,
identification traces, result-state preservation and cross-library comparison layer. Keep the
explicit references for controlled likelihoods, dependence-sensitive moments and generated
observation plans, because these operations carry assumptions that no generic estimator
interface supplies. Defer unrestricted PAG identification, general neural POMDP inference
and distributed execution until their scientific and operational contracts are qualified.
   The installed-source records supplement the 44-project document survey; they do not
retroactively turn that whole survey into runtime qualification. DoubleML’s archived distri-
bution declares BSD licensing. Tigramite’s installed metadata declares GPLv3 or later, so
the packaging/distribution decision must preserve those obligations; a mathematical adapter
test is not distribution clearance. The standalone design exposes these operations through
explicit requests and preserved artifacts. Sibling integrations map existing domain fields to
those requests, with adapters tested here; accepted execution inside the sibling repositories
remains separate work.


39.12      One dynamic scientific brief, two product consumers
The treasury brief asks for a one-month ten-basis-point price shift’s seven-month funding
contribution for a fixed portfolio. Source records contain candidate entity assignments and
delayed balance revisions. The information plan specifies an independent nuisance pilot,
independently audited pair matches, fixed calendar origins, the conditional price-innovation
restriction, and the common-calendar covariance rule. A causal result requires all of these inputs;
a regression formula alone cannot substitute for the observation and sampling experiment.
398                                                            Causal analysis for a universal bank


   The local construction first materializes the two candidate outcome histories. Predecision
features must be available by the decision date. Realized outcomes may arrive later, but
only revisions available by the fixed retrospective extraction cutoff enter the evaluation view.
These are different clocks: a realized four-month outcome cannot be required to exist before
its treatment. The raw fixture includes later revisions whose balances depend on the action.
They are excluded by their arrival time; business dates alone would leak them into the
view. Missing horizons, duplicated origin features and unavailable predecision information
are rejected. Conflicting source semantics remain unresolved before fitting. The selected
materializer accepts the account unit and received-day availability only. Even a uniquely
supplied business-day interpretation is rejected as unsupported by this operation. Source-owner
assertions are simulated provenance inputs here; real authentication and semantic review are
not established by the fixture’s trusted flag.
   The same observation object feeds the nuisance fit, stratum-specific response moments,
inverse-linkage correction, calendar plus calibration covariance and funding account derived
in Sections 9.12 and 11.11. Source and audit identities are preserved alongside hashes of the
actual pilot, evaluation and audit arrays. Target units, horizon, financial weights, linkage law,
sampling law and bandwidth and nuisance-selection candidates also enter the analysis identity.
The supplied source assertions and retrospective extraction cutoff are bound as well, even
when a changed assertion leaves numeric arrays unchanged. Changing bytes while retaining
an old source name invalidates reuse, just as changing the sampling law does.
  The treasury consumer displays total funding contribution, its interval and the response
curve. An application builder consumes the same result and divides by an externally fixed
480,000-account exposure. In the 720-origin reference, the estimate is 132,418 currency units,
with interval [−149,326, 414,162]. The second consumer reports .276 per account and interval
[−.311, .863], carrying exactly the same scientific identity. This rescaling is valid because its
denominator is fixed. Estimating or selecting the account population from outcomes would
need an additional influence term and target definition.
  Changing the externally supplied funding margin from .002 to .0015 is supported: the re-
sponse estimate is reused scientifically, while the financial linear combination and its covariance
are recomputed under a new identity. An attempted balance-stock-to-cash-flow reinterpre-
tation is rejected because the price cost and balance retention account no longer apply. An
independent-branch sampling request is rejected by the calendar backend. Submitting an old
cached identity after any of these economic or data changes is rejected before its interval can
be displayed. These are executed interface outcomes, not only proposed validation messages.
   The reusable layer therefore owns observation and intervention semantics, uncertainty com-
position and economic result transformations. Numerical regression, array algebra and mature
graph search remain delegated to qualified library operations. The direct statsmodels compari-
son uses the same residuals and covariance convention (statsmodels contributors, 2026); the
independent linked-response reference checks the complete correction and financial covariance.
The prototype deliberately has no generic compiler for arbitrary identification formulas. New
score/likelihood families need an explicit implementation with its own assumptions.
   This is a local common library and two reference consumers. FinMarketing, dataml and
MacroFinance can adapt their observation and result interfaces to these objects, but no sibling
adoption is asserted. A bank workbench would add data access, review interaction, entitlement
and lifecycle features around these scientifically qualified operations. The build choice is to own
the common scientific contract, reuse numerical libraries and defer unsupported nonlinear/PAG
procedures. The observed small-workload cost does not justify a distributed platform merely
to run these examples.
39.13. Three experiments, shared meaning and deliberate refusal                              399


39.12.1     A financial set is a different public result

The same public operation accepts the projection procedure in Section 11.12. Its result carries
a finite list of interval components, confidence level and the separate audit/response coverage
conditions. A missing lower or upper endpoint explicitly means an infinite endpoint; it never
means a missing estimate to be filled by zero. The treasury view shows the monetary set,
while the application view divides each component by the fixed positive account count. A
disconnected set remains disconnected after this transformation. There is no invented point
estimate or symmetric standard error when the information only supports a set.
   The regular and projection procedures are selected explicitly, and the procedure, confidence
level, fixed error allocation and sum/difference coordinates enter the scientific identity. A
caller cannot choose the narrower interval after inspecting both and inherit either procedure’s
coverage claim. Displaying them as sensitivity comparisons is different from a prespecified
inferential choice. The candidate-coordinate projection is retained as a mathematical challenger,
not an automatic width selector.
   The input domain is part of the calculation. The public operation checks finite observations
and economic quantities, complete response dimensions, the declared driver/stratum basis,
full pilot-training rank, both evaluation strata, residual price variation, binary calibration
records and an integer bandwidth below the calendar length. Conflicting copies of the same
outcome revision and nonfinite extraction clocks are rejected. Regular inverse-map inference
also needs audit records in both strata. Projection can instead use [0, 1] for an unaudited
stratum, often producing an uninformative set. An unsupported variance or nonfinite financial
result cannot carry a successful computed status. These checks verify numerical and structural
compatibility; they do not establish the source owner’s truth, pilot independence, the causal
innovation restriction or audit representativeness.
   An executed adversarial case removes all audits from one stratum. The regular operation
rejects the missing calibration, while projection returns the appropriate set under its larger
probability region. Other retained cases change the inference procedure and confidence level,
remove an evaluation stratum, introduce nonbinary audit labels, break the pilot basis, and
supply conflicting revisions. Their failures identify the particular information or procedure
that must change before a result can be requested again.


39.13      Three experiments, shared meaning and deliberate re-
           fusal
The preceding constructions support reuse because they expose compatible scientific meanings,
not because every problem is converted into the same regression. A request declares its
population, intervention normalization, unit, information clock, sampling law, inference method
and fixed monetary scale. The persistent-funding request invokes the independent-pair audited
moment. The servicing request invokes the identified nonlinear model and a policy fixed
independently of evaluation. The discovery request retains its latent class or its separately
justified encouragement restriction.
   Each result distinguishes a numeric calculation from its uncertainty claim. The inference
description contains the method, nominal level, finite-sample or asymptotic interpretation,
assumptions, numerical status and adverse empirical evidence. Both a treasury account and a
customer-facing application retain that description. The latter may divide a set by a fixed
external account count, preserving disconnected components and unbounded endpoints. An
estimated exposure denominator instead requires a joint influence argument.
400                                                          Causal analysis for a universal bank


   This requirement repairs a practical defect in the earlier regular funding path: its public
consumers dropped the scope field even though the underlying calculation carried it. The
revised request makes the inference method explicit before fitting. The retained regular method
discloses its adverse calibration; neither it nor the projection is selected after comparing
favorable widths. Legacy callers preserve their original procedure while receiving the fuller
description. The change preserves the original numeric results and changes what their recipients
are told.
   The local examples execute two eligible requests within each family and send each result
to both consumers. The second funding request changes horizon and sample size; the second
servicing request changes the fixed observable policy; the second discovery request supplies
valid encouragement information. These are new scientific inputs and receive new identities.
The identity binds the request, data and implementation, but it does not certify the truth of a
supplied assumption.
   Incompatible requests fail at meaningful boundaries. A pair-level persistent map cannot
borrow a calendar HAC covariance. A current audited hidden state cannot become an input
to the deployed policy. An account-date cannot replace the independent customer unit. A
selected graph cannot inherit confidence from an outer structural union without carrying the
union’s information conditions. Wrong clocks, empty populations and unsupported inference
combinations are rejected. These refusals express missing scientific arguments and information,
not a generic software inconvenience.
   Direct expert composition can call the same qualified kernels and satisfy the same unit,
provenance, uncertainty and reporting obligations. The shared product is valuable only if
it helps preserve those obligations across repeated tasks. The local matched computation
compares identical public output bytes; it does not measure analyst savings or establish
acceptance by FinMarketing, BayesFilter, MacroFinance or dataml. Their inspected interfaces
remain concrete integration proposals until their owners qualify and adopt the mappings.
Chapter 40

Causal operations and mathematical
interchange contracts

40.1     The unit of exchange is an analysis with meaning
A funding service, a servicing notebook and an analyst’s agent may all request an “effect”, while
referring to different populations, actions, horizons and units. Exchanging a floating-point
number is therefore insufficient. The proposed common object contains a scientific context, an
operation, input identities, an execution disposition and a qualified result. The local reference
implementation enforces selected parts of this contract; it does not validate the truth of every
declaration.Causal banking research project (2026ao,aq)
  For a scalar intervention query, write the context schematically as

                              Q = (P, µ, a, a0 , Y, H, u, s, T , A, G),

where P is the population, µ its weighting measure, a and a0 the intervention and comparator,
Y the outcome, H the horizon, u the units, s the sign convention, T the information clocks, A
the assumptions and sampling declarations, and G the graph or graph class. This mathematical
notation expresses the required meaning; particular schema fields may encode only a supported
subset. The original declaration must be retained when a narrower operation representation is
used.
   Changing a − a0 from a ten-basis-point offer to a one-percentage-point offer changes the
question, even if the same coefficient field can store both. Replacing customer weights by
balance weights changes µ. Treating a post-decision observation as available history changes
T . A digest can detect that the declared context changed. It cannot establish that the context
describes the actual banking process.
  The implementation binds supplied moments and sensitivity artifacts to their scientific
context. Reusing their bytes with a changed sign, clock, unit or target is rejected unless a
new, appropriate artifact is supplied. This prevents a consumer from reinterpreting a cached
numerical object through an unannounced schema change. It does not replace a scientific
argument for the moments or covariance.Causal banking research project (2026aq)


40.2     Execution, science and qualification are different states
A successful invocation can return unsupported identification, an empty sensitivity set, or a
whole-line confidence set. These are not necessarily transport failures. Conversely, a timeout

                                                401
402                                                            Causal analysis for a universal bank


supplies no scientific answer even if the requested mathematical object exists. The common
response separates invocation state, scientific disposition and qualification evidence.
   This separation gives a batch operator a defensible continuation rule. A completed negative
answer can be archived and used in a report. A malformed request needs correction. An
unsupported operation needs another qualified backend or a narrower, explicitly authorized
question. A contradiction in the declared premises needs scientific review. Automatically
retrying all four events until a finite number appears would select answers according to their
convenience.
   The library’s supplied-DAG back-door operation illustrates the distinction. It can attempt
an adjustment expression in its bounded domain. Failure of that attempt does not prove
general nonidentification; a different graphical functional or additional information could be
relevant. The response must describe the actual method and its limitation. Likewise, graph
syntax review checks declared structures but does not discover their causal truth. Causal
banking research project (2026aq)


40.3     Sets must retain their topology
The local representation distinguishes unknown from empty, and permits a union of intervals
with infinite endpoints. Unknown has no asserted interval list; an empty set has an empty
list. A whole-line set has one interval unbounded in both directions. A disconnected set keeps
its components.Causal banking research project (2026ao) None should be represented by an
arbitrary plotting range.
  Consider the stipulated effect set

                                    Θ = (−∞, −2] ∪ [3, ∞)

and a known monetary map V = 100θ − 300. The image is

                                V (Θ) = (−∞, −500] ∪ [0, ∞).

Taking the convex hull would return the entire real line and discard a real exclusion. Clipping
the tails would falsely assert boundedness. Changing to a loss convention L = −V gives
(−∞, 0] ∪ [500, ∞); endpoint order must reverse when multiplying by a negative number.
   If Θ has a stated coverage guarantee for θ, applying a known deterministic map preserves
containment on the same event. It does not create a guarantee for an estimated conversion
factor or a randomly chosen target. When margins, discount rates or exposure weights are
estimated, joint uncertainty or an explicitly conditional analysis is needed. Serialization cannot
make uncertain financial inputs fixed.
   The same care applies to graph sets. Member identities, endpoint semantics and evidence
must travel with the alternatives. A CPDAG, PAG and selected DAG are not interchangeable
edge lists. The present schema retains declared classes and hashed membership; its validator
is not a complete recognizer or confidence construction for arbitrary temporal equivalence
classes.


40.4     A contract for future numerical adapters
Each adapter should state its accepted targets, graph classes, sampling laws, missingness rules,
numerical inputs and output uncertainty. A source package may use an ATT where the caller
requested an ATE, return pointwise intervals where simultaneous inference is required, or
40.5. When a conversion preserves the question                                             403


approximate a set with a hull. Those are semantic mismatches even when both sides exchange
valid JSON.
   The adapter must either preserve the requested meaning, return a disclosed qualified
approximation, or refuse the mapping. A proposed R, Python, Java or C++ bridge therefore
needs matched fixtures at ordinary and adverse boundaries, including disconnected sets, weak
identification and unsupported models. Cross-language execution, licenses, data copying and
complete workloads remain qualification obligations. The existing local dispatcher is a common
boundary for that work, not evidence that those bridges already exist.


40.5     When a conversion preserves the question
The interchange obligation can be stated as a commutation requirement. Let FQ (D) be a
scientific calculation on observations D for context Q. Let E encode the observations and
question for an engine, M denote that engine’s computation, and R decode its result. If T is a
declared change of coordinates, an exact adapter should satisfy

                                  R{M (E(D, Q))} = T {FQ (D)}.

   The right side specifies what the answer means before serialization. The left side describes
the proposed software path. This equality is an obligation on the admitted domain, not
a theorem established by two programs returning parseable JSON. It includes a negative
scientific answer or a set with several components whenever that is the defined output of FQ .
A method that changes the target while improving numerical stability has changed Q; it has
not merely implemented E.
  There are three useful levels of equivalence. Exact structural equivalence preserves a graph,
variable map or expression tree up to declared renaming. Numerical equivalence permits a
quantified error in the requested coordinates. Scientific equivalence additionally requires the
same population, intervention, sampling law and uncertainty interpretation. A fixture showing
agreement of two printed means addresses only a small part of the second level. The design
should state which level it establishes and where further evidence is required.
   An adapter also needs an explicit domain. Write DM for the queries and inputs admitted by
engine M . If (D, Q) ∈/ DM , the proper response is a typed unsupported result that preserves
the original request. Automatically dropping weights, selecting one graph, clipping an interval
or replacing a temporal sample with independent rows does not extend the domain honestly.
A proposed approximation can still be useful, but its transformed question and additional
assumptions must be disclosed as a different operation.
   This view explains why a generic language bridge is insufficient. A Python-to-R array
conversion can preserve all floating-point values while losing the fact that columns represent
treatment arms in a specific order. A Java graph object can preserve adjacency while reversing
an endpoint mark. A C++ routine can accurately optimize an objective for a different weighting
measure. The mathematical interface must bind these meanings alongside the numeric payload,
and its review must include examples for which apparently harmless changes lead to materially
different bank decisions.


40.6     Population measures and rate coordinates
Consider a bank’s effect target
404                                                             Causal analysis for a universal bank


                                       Z
                                τµ =       {m1 (x) − m0 (x)} dµ(x),

   where ma (x) is a conditional mean potential outcome under action a, and µ is the declared
distribution of customers or exposures. The same response functions can imply different targets
under different measures. In an assumed two-segment example, the customer shares are 3/4
and 1/4, the segment effects are USD 20 and USD -40 per account, and relative balances are
one and nine. The customer-average effect is

                                       3        1
                                       4 (20) + 4 (−40) = 5.

   Balance weighting gives masses 1/4 and 3/4, and hence an effect of USD -25. The sign
reverses even though no within-segment estimate changed. The example is stipulated arithmetic,
not evidence about the distribution of any bank’s customers. Its purpose is to make the
weighting measure an indispensable part of the requested estimand. (Causal banking research
project, 2026t)
  A caller may intentionally prefer the balance-weighted target for a treasury decision. That
choice should create a new target identity and explain which decision it serves. It cannot
be inferred from a column named weight, because a supplied weight might instead describe
unequal sampling probabilities, treatment assignment, transport to another population or
a numerical objective. These roles have different identification and variance implications.
Multiplying several weights without preserving their definitions can conceal that distinction.
   Treatment coordinates require similar care. Let r be a decimal interest rate, so a basis-point
change is 10−4 . If a linear response derivative is β = ∂E(Y )/∂r, then the derivative per basis
point is 10−4 β. A hypothetical estimate of USD 2 million per unit decimal rate becomes
USD 200 per basis point; an interval of USD 1–3 million becomes USD 100–300. Reporting
the original number under the new label would create a factor-of-10,000 error. The exact
calculation is reproducible. It does not assert that a constant derivative is an appropriate
response model over an arbitrary offer range. (Causal banking research project, 2026t)
   For a finite nonlinear rate change, the target is instead E{Y (r1 ) − Y (r0 )}; rescaling a
local derivative does not identify that contrast. Nor does a per-month response become an
annual causal response by changing its unit label. Timing, compounding, feedback and the
intervention path may matter. Units should therefore describe the mathematical coordinate
actually estimated, while the horizon and intervention path remain separate fields. A conversion
that requires new structural assumptions belongs in a scientific transformation, not a formatting
function.
