   For an exact arithmetic illustration, let the first coordinate be a gross revenue effect in USD
and the second an operating-cost effect in thousands of USD. Suppose the supplied covariance
is
                                            !                            !
                                40000 20                    1/1000 0
                         Σ=               ,          L=               .
                                  20  1/4                     0    −1

  The new coordinates are gross benefit and negative operating cost, both in thousands of
USD. Their covariance is
                                                               !
                                        ⊤       1/25 −1/50
                                   LΣL =                   .
                                                −1/50 1/4

   The negative cross-covariance matters when adding the two coordinates to obtain net value:
its variance is 1/4, whereas dropping that covariance gives 29/100. A column-order error or a
failure to reverse the covariance sign changes the uncertainty even if both marginal standard
errors look reasonable. The matrices here are assumed, positive definite reference objects whose
conversion is checked by exact arithmetic. They are not fitted bank uncertainty estimates.
(Causal banking research project, 2026t)
  Marginal intervals cannot substitute for a joint region. If C1 , C2 each cover their own fixed
coordinate with probability at least .95, the union bound gives only

                                   P {(θ1 , θ2 ) ∈ C1 × C2 } ≥ .90.

   Even with independent coverage events and exact marginal coverage, the joint probability is
.952 = .9025. A simultaneous 95% statement needs a construction that supports it; a transport
cannot supply that construction by changing the uncertainty label. The same issue arises if an
agent inspects several analyses and reports only the most favorable one. Coverage for each fixed
query is not automatically coverage for the selected query. Preserving the full query-selection
rule and any simultaneous or selective argument is part of the workflow’s scientific identity.
   These distinctions already appear in the local semantic validator: confidence, posterior
credibility and sensitivity have separate meanings, a joint-confidence declaration requires
construction evidence, and the declared sampling law must match the context. Those checks
constrain what can be serialized. They do not independently prove the submitted construction
or establish Bayesian calibration. (Causal banking research project, 2026u)


40.8      A confidence set is not a pair of convenient endpoints
Weak identification supplies a practical reason to retain topology. For a ratio target θ = µY /µX ,
one can invert a test of µY − θµX = 0. With supplied approximately Gaussian mean errors,
write their variances as sY Y , sXX and covariance as sXY . A residual-test set takes the form

                            (Ȳ − θX̄)2 ≤ c2 (sY Y − 2θsXY + θ2 sXX ).

  Its interpretation depends on the stated Gaussian approximation, covariance and critical
value; algebraic inversion alone is not a finite-sample theorem for an arbitrary dependent
sample. Collecting terms gives

                                         aθ2 + bθ + d ≤ 0,
406                                                              Causal analysis for a universal bank


  where

                 a = X̄ 2 − c2 sXX ,   b = −2X̄ Ȳ + 2c2 sXY ,   d = Ȳ 2 − c2 sY Y .

   When the denominator is weak, a may be negative. With two real roots the solution then
consists of exterior rays; with other coefficients it may be the whole line or another topology.
The point ratio can fail to exist while the test-inversion set still has a precise meaning. For the
stipulated values Ȳ = 2, X̄ = 0, c = 2, sY Y = sXY = 0, sXX = 1/4, the inequality is 4 ≤ θ2 ,
giving

                                        (−∞, −2] ∪ [2, ∞).

   This degenerate but positive-semidefinite reference covariance makes the algebra transparent.
It does not validate that covariance for a data-generating process. It shows why a response
object must allow a valid set without a finite point ratio. The existing local supplied-moment
operation retains these distinctions under its declared approximation. (Causal banking research
project, 2026t,u)
  Unknown, empty, whole-line and disconnected results answer different questions. Unknown
says that no set has been computed. Empty may signal incompatible restrictions in a particular
construction, and does not mean an effect of zero. Whole-line uncertainty means every real
value remains allowed by that construction. An exterior-ray set excludes a middle region
despite being unbounded. A graph-class result may instead be a set of distinct functionals
whose numerical evaluation is not yet available. None can be reduced to a nullable scalar
without losing information that could change a decision.
   Nonlinear monetary transformations make the loss visible. Take the assumed effect set
[−3, −2] ∪ [2, 3] and value map V (θ) = 100(θ2 − 1). Its image is [300, 800]. Applying the
same map to the convex hull [−3, 3] gives [−100, 800]. Both are outer possibilities for different
retained information, but the latter invents a negative-value possibility that the original set
excludes. A hull may be a disclosed conservative approximation; it must not be described as
exact interchange. The reverse mistake, returning only transformed outer endpoints without
considering interior extrema, can omit valid values and lose coverage. (Causal banking research
project, 2026t)


40.9      Combining statistical, measurement and numerical uncer-
          tainty
Suppose an effect set C contains the fixed target θ with probability at least 1 − αC , and a set
H contains a needed valuation parameter η with probability at least 1 − αH . For a declared
value function v, the projection

                                  W = {v(t, h) : t ∈ C, h ∈ H}

   contains v(θ, η) whenever both input events hold. Thus the union bound yields coverage
at least 1 − αC − αH , without independence. A valid joint region can be projected instead
and may be narrower because it retains dependence between θ and η. Independently varying
marginal ranges is generally an outer approximation to that joint region. Fixing η at an
estimate has no such unconditional guarantee without an additional argument.
   Numerical containment is a third obligation. Let W
                                                    f be an approximate computed set. If a
certificate establishes
40.10. Sampling declarations and partial scientific answers                                 407



                                        W ⊆W
                                           f ⊕ [−ε, ε],

   where ⊕ denotes addition of sets, then the enlarged computed set preserves the preceding
coverage event. If the numerical certificate itself can fail with probability δ, the resulting
guarantee is at least 1 − αC − αH − δ. Budgets of .02, .02, .01 give a 95% lower guarantee.
This arithmetic does not prove that a particular optimizer supplies the assumed certificate; its
error bound must come from the numerical method. (Causal banking research project, 2026t)
   A grid of feasible points usually supplies an inner sample, not the required outer enclosure.
Missing a disconnected component or an unbounded tail is therefore a scientific failure, even if
all sampled points satisfy the constraints. An optimizer’s small objective change also need not
certify the set boundary. For a nonlinear map, a Lipschitz constant can propagate an input
approximation error only over a region where the constant is valid; a bound obtained on a
clipped plotting window does not control unbounded tails outside it.
   The currency of the numerical error should be the currency of the decision. If a statistical
lower value is USD 30 but an admitted numerical approximation has error up to USD 40, the
certified lower value is USD -10. Reporting only the statistical endpoint can reverse a claimed
robust recommendation. Conversely, a deliberately coarse computation may be adequate when
its certified error cannot change the decision. This makes numerical precision an explicit
investment tradeoff rather than an unexamined default tolerance.


40.10       Sampling declarations and partial scientific answers
A shared data format does not create shared sampling assumptions. Consider the generated
one-date account model Yi = θ + C + Ei , where independent centered Gaussian components
have Var(C) = .09, Var(Ei ) = 1, and C is shared by every account. Then

                                       Var(Ȳ ) = .09 + 1/N.

  At N = 10,000, the correct variance is .0901. Treating the rows as independent with
their individual variance 1.09 gives .000109, understating variance by 90100/109, or about
827 times. The number of rows was preserved exactly; the scientific information was not.
This exact generated calculation illustrates why a panel or calendar declaration must survive
conversion and why an iid-only method must reject it. It makes no claim about an observed
bank covariance. (Causal banking research project, 2026t)
   The same problem occurs with persistent linkage errors, cluster treatment assignment
and policies that condition on shared history. A consumer that sees only row count and a
floating-point estimate cannot reconstruct the lost sampling unit. The local bounded back-door
reference explicitly restricts its sampling regime, while the proposed symbolic identification
adapter preserves the declaration without supplying estimation uncertainty. Those are different
services with different obligations. (Causal banking research project, 2026u,al)
   Finally, the response should identify what has actually been established. A source-inspected
method may support a proposal decision. An executed adapter may establish that particular
conversions work. A statistical region may be valid under declared scientific assumptions. A
banking action may still be undecided because its loss function or information is insufficient.
Preserving a partial answer makes the next step precise: obtain a needed assumption, improve
information, choose another method or refine numerical containment. Automatically converting
every partial answer into a confident recommendation would obscure the very gap the product
is meant to explain.
408                                                              Causal analysis for a universal bank


40.11      Preserving causal meaning in a Python identification
           adapter
A common causal interface is useful only if a question keeps its meaning when it passes into
another library. An outreach decision can become a different question if a transport drops a
condition, converts an uncertain graph into one directed graph, or treats a symbolic probability
formula as an estimated monetary return. The proposed Python path therefore begins with a
narrow service: identify an intervention distribution in one supplied causal graph, preserve the
assumptions that make the formula relevant, and report an explicit limit when that service
cannot answer the question.
   y0 is a plausible component for this service because its inspected Python API separates a
query, a mixed graph and a symbolic identification expression. The source considered here
is commit cc6644d3b470a1ab2a1eb9da4f0fdb0c843f5d3a, dated 13 April 2026; its project
metadata declares development version 0.2.12-dev. The acquisition is later than the liter-
ature cutoff, but the reviewed commit predates 7 October 2026. These identifiers describe
inspected source, not a tested deployment. The proposed decision is to integrate a restricted
identification path and verify its conversions before admitting it to a prototype. Porting an
entire identification engine would create a second implementation to maintain before the first
interface has established its scientific meaning. (y0 contributors, 2026a,g)


40.11.1     A distributional question before an estimate

Let A denote a bank action, Y an outcome and Z a collection of explicitly named conditions.
The requested object is

                                           p(y | do(a), z).

   It is distinct from an observed conditional probability, an average difference between two
actions, and a confidence interval for an estimated difference. For a finite outcome support, a
later evaluator might form
                             X
                 µ(a, z) =       y p(y | do(a), z),    τ (z) = µ(a1 , z) − µ(a0 , z).
                             y

   That calculation requires the original outcome coordinates, treatment/control order and
units. If Y is a repayment indicator, τ is a probability difference. If Y is net cash received, it
has the declared currency and horizon. Multiplying the first by a loss avoided per repayment
is an additional valuation model; it is not an operation that the identification library can infer
from a variable label.
   The first adapter is deliberately limited to one scalar outcome and treatment, optional
conditions, one causal DAG or acyclic directed mixed graph (ADMG), and declared finite
discrete domains. This makes its numerical references and interpretation concrete. It does
not establish an absence of wider functions elsewhere in y0. A graph representing selection,
transport between populations, cross-world counterfactuals, an adaptive longitudinal regime
or unresolved graph alternatives needs a separately reviewed path. An account panel can still
describe its sampling law in the request, but a symbolic formula supplies no independence
assumption, standard error or calibration for that panel.
  The scientific context should travel with the formula: target population, action values,
outcome horizon, observation and availability clocks, variable domains, units, sign convention,
40.11. Preserving causal meaning in a Python identification adapter                           409


sampling unit and assumptions. A hash of that complete context identifies the request. A
changed population, a reversed action contrast or a different availability clock produces a
different identity even when the graph picture is unchanged. The shared library, CLI and
MCP operation contracts already distinguish transport completion from scientific disposition;
the proposed adapter specializes that distinction for identification. (Causal banking research
project, 2026al)
   A condition deserves particular care. Conditioning on a pretreatment risk category and
conditioning on a response to the action are different targets. The interface should require
the caller to state which is intended, preserve the chronology, and avoid silently relabeling a
post-action variable as an adjustment covariate. Syntax can reject a missing clock declaration.
It cannot determine whether the bank’s claimed chronology or causal model is true.


40.11.2     Graph and coordinate conversion

The graph object in the inspected source contains a directed component and a component
named undirected. In the causal mixed-graph interpretation, the latter carries bidirected
latent links: the source’s causal-graph importer maps the input type bidirected into that
field, and its latent expansion creates a shared hidden parent for each such edge. It is therefore
incorrect to put an unresolved CPDAG edge into this component merely because both are
stored by an undirected graph data structure. (y0 contributors, 2026c)
   For the admitted path, a tail–arrow pair becomes a directed edge, and an arrow–arrow
pair becomes an ADMG bidirected edge. Circles, tail–tail edges and graph collections receive
an unsupported disposition that retains the original representation. A directed edge and a
bidirected edge may coexist on the same pair of variables; erasing one would change the model.
The directed component must be acyclic, with all endpoints in the declared node set. These
checks belong in the adapter: the inspected graph initializer sets metadata flags and does not
itself establish acyclicity.
   Every variable, including an isolated one, must be passed explicitly. Constructing a graph
solely from edges can lose an outcome or an independent condition that has no incident edge.
The adapter should compare the node and typed-edge sets before and after conversion and
use a deterministic valid topological ordering. The purpose is reproducibility and semantic
preservation, not the selection of a statistically preferred causal ordering.
   Names are another coordinate system. External identifiers may contain spaces, non-ASCII
text or labels that collide after informal sanitization. The proposed conversion assigns opaque
internal symbols through a bijection and keeps a sidecar containing the external identifier,
displayed label, domain order, time coordinate and units. It never guesses temporal order
from a name such as lag1, and it never converts category labels into numeric doses without a
declared mapping. A graph-set request remains a graph-set request even when unsupported.
An uncomputed effect set remains unknown; it is not represented by a convenient point
estimate or an empty region.


40.11.3     Why conditional identification needs a restricted route

The high-level API calls ID when its conditions field is empty and IDC otherwise. By default
it converts the specific Unidentifiable exception to None; with strict=True it preserves
the exception. Other exception types are not caught by that branch. The adapter should
preserve this distinction, because a malformed graph, a runtime failure and nonidentification
are different outcomes. The inspected ID recursion supplies node/district arguments when
raising Unidentifiable, but those arguments should not be presented as an independently
410                                                             Causal analysis for a universal bank


verified graphical certificate. (y0 contributors, 2026a,d)
   Two additional source findings restrict the proposed conditional route.              First,
Query.expression builds a conditioned distribution when conditions exist, using an
elif branch for interventions. When both are present, that convenience property does not
add the intervention. This is a serialization hazard, not evidence that the separate IDC
algorithm discards its treatment field: Identification retains outcomes, treatments and
conditions separately. The adapter should serialize its original query triple independently of
that convenience property. (y0 contributors, 2026k)
   Second, IDC tests whether an observation may be exchanged for an action using a separation
routine. The inspected routine takes a directed-ancestor subgraph, connects directed co-parents,
flattens the remaining edges and removes conditioning vertices. For a DAG this is a familiar
construction. The same steps do not generally implement the collider behavior of bidirected
paths. The source-level discrepancy can be demonstrated without relying on a package’s own
numerical output. (y0 contributors, 2026e,h,i,c)
  Consider the ADMG

                                         Y ↔ B ↔ Z,

   with an unrelated action X. The middle vertex B is a collider. Conditioning on it can
connect Y and Z; treating it as an ordinary undirected intermediate vertex and deleting it
instead disconnects them. In the rule-2 check for exchanging Z, removal of incoming edges
to isolated X and outgoing edges from Z does not change this path. The inspected directed
co-parent rule adds no Y –Z link because there are no directed edges. Its subsequent deletion
of B therefore predicts separation where the causal mixed graph does not.
   An exact generated law makes the consequence explicit. Let U, V be independent fair bits,
let Y = U , Z = V , and let B report whether U = V , correctly with probability .9. The
observed law of (Y, B, Z) has positive probability in all eight cells. Direct enumeration gives

                                         9                                       1
           P (Y = 1 | B = 1, Z = 1) =       ,      P (Y = 1 | B = 1, do(Z = 1)) = .
                                         10                                      2
  An intervention on Z overwrites that measurement but does not change U, V or the
mechanism generating B. Exchanging the observation for the action would therefore change
the requested probability. This is an exact reference for the scientific meaning of the graph
and a trace of the inspected source path; it is not a report of an executed y0 failure. (Causal
banking research project, 2026am)
  The initial adapter can avoid that native conditional path. It first applies ID to the joint
query p(y, z | do(a)). If it obtains an observational functional N (y, z, a), it forms

                                           N (y, z, a)
                                        P          ′
                                                            ,
                                           y ′ N (y , z, a)

   on coordinates for which the denominator is positive. This is a direct probability identity.
It neither uses the questionable separation step nor relies on the query-expression convenience
property. The route is conservative: failure to identify the joint distribution does not prove
failure to identify the conditional target. Such a failure must return “unsupported by the
admitted conditional route,” leaving the original question intact. Re-enabling native IDC
requires a corrected or otherwise justified path and an actual engine comparison against
independent collider references.
40.11. Preserving causal meaning in a Python identification adapter                        411


40.11.4     A front-door reference with a banking interpretation

A second exact example supplies a positive identification reference. Let A be assistance, M
completion of the assisted process and Y successful repayment. In the generated example an
unobserved U affects both assistance and repayment. The assumed graph has A → M → Y
and A ↔ Y , with no direct effect of assistance on repayment outside M . This is a strong
exclusion assumption. In a real service workflow an agent’s advice, fees or other treatment
channels could violate it, and observed associations alone do not establish it.
  Specify the finite law by

                                            P (U = 1) = 12 ,
                                    P (A = 1 | U = u) = 15 + 53 u,
                                    P (M = 1 | A = a) = 14 + 21 a,
                                                     1
                          P (Y = 1 | M = m, U = u) = 10 + 21 m + 15 u.

  Independent rational enumeration first constructs the observed joint table, hiding U , and
evaluates

                                                    E(Y | m, a′ )p(a′ ).
                               X               X
                                    p(m | a)
                                m              a′

  It separately evaluates the intervention law from the specified mechanisms. Both routes
produce 13/40 = .325 under a = 0 and 23/40 = .575 under a = 1, for a difference of 1/4. The
naive observed difference is 37/100. The exact calculation therefore distinguishes a successful
symbolic formula from a shortcut that merely compares observed groups. No fitted sample,
randomized qualification study or engine runtime is involved. (Causal banking research project,
2026am)
  If a proposal scenario assigns an assumed USD 1,000 benefit to each additional successful
repayment, the gross expected difference is USD 250 per account, before assistance costs and
any other consequences. That number is planning arithmetic under the declared law and value
assumption. It supplies neither observed bank ROI nor evidence that the front-door graph
describes a bank.
   The inner treatment variable a′ reveals an important serialization requirement. It is a
dummy summation coordinate, while the outer a is the requested intervention value. A global
string replacement could capture the dummy variable and change the formula. The proposed
result format uses a typed expression tree with lexical bindings for marginalized variables. It
preserves probability factors, products, sums and ratios, alpha-renames bound symbols when
needed, and maps free coordinates back to the original question. The inspected symbolic
classes expose those structures; rendered LaTeX or the library’s Python-like display string is
suitable for presentation, not as an executable interchange format. (y0 contributors, 2026b)
   An independent negative reference is equally necessary. In a graph allowing A → Y and
A ↔ Y , take a fair hidden U , let A = U , and let an independent bit E equal one with
probability .2. The mechanisms Y = A xor E and Y = U xor E give the same strictly positive
observed law of (A, Y ). Under intervention their effects are respectively .6 and zero. Both
belong to the model allowing those edges; no faithfulness restriction is imposed. A library
cannot choose between the effects from their identical observed distribution. A successful
adapter retains this nonidentification rather than translating every completed request into a
finite effect. (Causal banking research project, 2026am)

40.11.5     Responses, deployment and the next prototype decision

A symbolic identification result should contain the original query, graph and context identities,
engine revision, typed functional, support conditions and source provenance. Its numeric
estimate, standard error and confidence region remain absent. When the unconditional ID
path reports nonidentification in an admitted model, the response should identify that origin
and retain its diagnostic without exaggerating its verification. When the conditional joint
route fails, the response is unsupported. An invalid graph is rejected; a missing engine, internal
failure, timeout or cancellation is unavailable. These distinctions determine whether the next
action is to repair an input, add scientific information, select a different method or provision a
runtime.
  Library, CLI and MCP surfaces should call the same core implementation and return the
same context and result identities. The symbolic service requires graph and question artifacts,
not bank account rows. A worker can enforce wall-time, memory and output budgets while
keeping engine diagnostics separate from scientific conclusions. Cancellation must preserve
a completed result if publication has already occurred; an interrupted partial expression
cannot become an identified functional. These are proposed implementation requirements, not
performance guarantees supplied by the inspected y0 API.
   The pinned project metadata requires Python 3.11 or later and lists twelve direct runtime
dependencies, including NetworkX, SciPy, pandas, scikit-learn and statsmodels. The build
backend is uv_build in its declared version range. Its optional R extra uses rpy2; upstream
test groups include additional packages that are not all runtime requirements of the proposed
pure-Python path. The inspected tree has no root lockfile establishing resolved transitive
versions. A prototype admission therefore needs a frozen interpreter/platform and dependency
manifest, saved distribution hashes, actual build/import logs and license notices. Source
inspection alone cannot promise compatibility with whatever environment happens to be
installed. (y0 contributors, 2026g,j)
  The saved BSD three-clause license permits redistribution under its notice, disclaimer
and nonendorsement conditions. That supports a possible integration route, while leaving
dependency rights and actual deployment behavior to be checked. It supplies no scientific
warranty. A port may become justified if a later measurement shows that the Python
environment or latency is a decisive constraint; there is no such measured advantage for
porting in the present evidence. (y0 contributors, 2026f)
   The prototype’s first engine trials should compare the actual pinned runtime with the
independent front-door, bow and collider references, including retained unsupported requests.
Conversion checks should exercise isolated variables, edge-type distinctions, coordinate permu-
tations, dummy-variable binding, zero conditional support and distinct failures. A successful
trial would support the named adapter in its declared regime. It would not establish discovery
accuracy, graph truth, estimation calibration or institutional acceptance. The value of this
restricted design is that each later claim has a specific test and a specific scientific object that
must survive the interface.


40.12      An isolated condition must survive internal graph modi-
           fication
Preserving the node set at the adapter boundary is necessary but does not establish that every
internal graph operation preserves it. The inspected y0 revision’s remove_in_edges rebuilds a
graph from the intervention vertices and the endpoints of surviving edges. It does not explicitly
40.13. Numerical equivalence must survive composition                                       413


seed every original vertex. An isolated vertex outside the intervention can therefore disappear.
The ID recursion later requests ancestors of its outcome set in this modified graph. These are
source-level observations about the same pinned revision, not results from an installed package
trial (y0 contributors, 2026c,d).
   Consider the supplied DAG with A → Y and an isolated condition Z. The requested object
is p(y | do(a), z). The proposed joint route begins with p(y, z | do(a)), retaining Y, Z as its
outcomes. All three vertices are ancestors of this outcome set or members of it before graph
modification, so the initial ancestor restriction does not remove Z. In the subsequent source
path, removing incoming edges to A reconstructs vertices A, Y from the intervention and the
edge A → Y . The ancestor request for Z then concerns a vertex that is absent. An actual
installed-engine run is required to record its precise exception and response; the source trace
already establishes why checking only the initial conversion is insufficient (Causal banking
proposal project, 2026j).
   This failure mechanism is distinct from a failure of causal identification. For an exact
reference, let A, Z be independent fair binary variables and let an independent outcome
mechanism satisfy
                             P (Y = 1 | do(A = a)) = 41 + 12 a.
The eight observed cells have positive probability. Under the supplied causal DAG and its
independent mechanisms,
               p(y, z | do(a)) = p(y | a)p(z),          P (Y = 1 | do(a), z) = 14 + 12 a
on both supported values of z. The effect is 1/2 within either condition. Independent rational
enumeration reproduces this result. These are stipulated mechanisms, not inferred bank facts
or fitted package outputs (Causal banking proposal project, 2026j).
   The admission decision is consequently more specific. The proposed joint route needs tests
for isolated conditions and outcomes at every internal graph transformation, in addition to the
front-door, bow and collider references. A reviewed patch that retains all vertices would need
an actual engine comparison and regression checks before admission. An adapter may instead
implement an independently justified isolated-variable factorization for the exact supported
graph class, but must not discard a condition merely because it appears inconvenient. A
condition with an incident edge does not qualify for the isolated-variable shortcut. Until a
route passes these checks, a missing-node exception is an unavailable computation with the
original question retained. It is neither a proof of nonidentification nor a successful empty
result. The public proposal can therefore recommend the restricted integration while keeping
its unresolved implementation obligation visible.


40.13      Numerical equivalence must survive composition
Even an adapter that preserves the exact mathematical expression can fail when independently
acceptable numerical errors accumulate through a workflow. Conditional identification provides
a concrete example. Suppose a returned functional is f = N/D, with a strictly positive
denominator, and a downstream evaluator computes N   e , D.
                                                         e Assume certificates give


              |N − N
                   e | ≤ εN ,           |D − D|
                                             e ≤ εD ,        |N | ≤ B,   D ≥ d0 > εD .
  By writing the difference over a common denominator and using |D|
                                                                 e ≥ d0 − εD , one obtains


                                N
                                e       N      εN         BεD
                                    −     ≤         +               .
                                D
                                e       D   d0 − εD   d0 (d0 − εD )
414                                                            Causal analysis for a universal bank


   Thus an absolute tolerance on probability calculations has no fixed interpretation for the
conditional answer as the denominator approaches zero. The mathematical statement that
a conditional probability exists at a positive coordinate is weaker than a uniform numerical
stability claim. A service that promises a useful numeric answer needs either an adequate
support margin or a certified set that reflects the weak denominator.
  For a reproducible assumed example, let N e = .004, D
                                                      e = .010, with bounds εN = .001 and
εD = .004. Independent interval division gives

                                 N   .003 .005    3 5
                                                           
                                   ∈     ,     =   ,  ,
                                 D   .014 .006   14 6
   while the point ratio is .4. All numerator/denominator corners here obey 0 ≤ N ≤ D, so
intersecting with the probability range does not narrow the interval. A valid dependence
relation between their errors might narrow it, but it must be supplied and retained as joint
information. The broad result is produced by bounded deterministic error alone; it is not a
statistical confidence interval. (Causal banking research project, 2026s)
  If an uncertainty region includes D = 0, the service should preserve the unresolved support
condition. Clipping the denominator to a positive constant silently changes the functional
and generally supplies no error certificate. If only strictly positive but arbitrarily small
denominators are allowed, a ratio may be highly sensitive even though the target is defined at
every admitted point. The response should distinguish a model-relative identification result, a
supported numeric coordinate and a finite-precision certificate. These objects answer different
questions and may become available at different times.
   Composition also requires the correct order of nonlinear operations. Suppose two equally
weighted customer groups have success probabilities 1/5 and 1/2. Their population probability
is 7/20, with odds 7/13. Averaging their odds instead gives (1/4+1)/2 = 5/8, which transforms
back to probability 5/13. Neither number arose from a floating-point error. Averaging and
the nonlinear odds map do not commute. An interface that substitutes an average log-odds,
odds or probability because each is called a “risk” has changed the target. In a causal contrast
the error can affect both action-specific means before they are differenced. (Causal banking
research project, 2026s)
   These examples motivate a transformation graph accompanying the result. Its nodes should
identify the scientific object and coordinates, and its arrows should identify an exact map, a
conditional approximation or a certified outer enclosure. A population aggregation followed by
valuation is one path; conversion to a subgroup score followed by averaging is another. The
workflow should be able to explain why the selected path answers the declared question. A
chain of individually sensible package defaults is insufficient evidence that the composed path
does.
   Cross-language comparison can test these properties without pretending to qualify every
estimator. For an exact finite reference table, an admitted identification expression should agree
with a separately computed intervention distribution; variable renaming and category-order
changes should preserve that answer after inverse mapping. A sign reversal should reverse
an effect and reorder interval endpoints. A probability marginal should normalize on its
declared support. These are necessary checks on the concrete path, not sufficient evidence
of universal scientific correctness. The front-door and collider examples provide particularly
useful references because a superficially plausible formula can return a different probability.
  The same testing discipline should retain expected refusals. An unsupported graph class
must not become an empty graph. A normalization failure must not become an estimated
zero effect. A numerical timeout must not be cached as a scientific negative answer for an
40.14. A Java discovery boundary that retains the question                                    415


unrelated context. Matching those dispositions across library, CLI and MCP is part of semantic
equivalence. The preserved local transport trial demonstrates selected comparisons for the
existing bounded operations; the proposed y0 path still requires its own actual engine and
conversion evidence. (Causal banking research project, 2026u)
   For investment planning, the practical question is whether the information and computation
are adequate for the decision. A numerically precise conditional effect on a vanishingly small
subgroup may be irrelevant to the bank’s target population. A broad but valid effect set may
establish that a costly expansion cannot be justified yet. A slightly more expensive evaluator
may be valuable if certified containment resolves a decision that uncontrolled approximations
cannot. The proposed product should expose these consequences through the scientific result,
its restrictions and its value calculation, rather than hiding them behind a generic success flag.



40.14      A Java discovery boundary that retains the question
The Java comparison motivates a concrete first integration: a pinned Tetrad process for
a restricted PC discovery request, with a separate admission path for FGES. The initial
request concerns complete continuous observations under an explicitly assumed IID linear
Gaussian model with causal sufficiency, acyclicity, faithfulness and no unmodeled selection.
These restrictions identify a reviewable prototype. They do not imply that a table of banking
observations satisfies them. Clustered customers, repeated account histories, missing-data
correction, latent-variable discovery and background-knowledge constraints require other
profiles. The adapter is a proposal contract; no Java engine or new transport endpoint has
been implemented here. (Causal banking research project, 2026v; cmu-phil/tetrad, 2026a)
   The request retains the downstream target even though discovery does not compute it. A
funding analyst’s population, treatment contrast, outcome, time horizon, units and sampling
declarations remain attached to the graph. They prevent a later identification step from
silently changing the question. The generic operation contract already provides these fields
for effect operations. The Java discovery profile deliberately requires that context as well.
A standalone graph request without a downstream treatment and outcome needs its own
reviewed context extension; inserting arbitrary variable names would create a fictitious causal
question. (Causal banking research project, 2026v)
   The logical interface is the same across the proposed library invocation, causalbank
operation graph.discover command and causal_graph_discover MCP tool. Each trans-
ports a versioned canonical request and receives the same typed result. A complete scientific
context digest accompanies a broader request digest containing input hashes, engine revision,
algorithm settings, adapter version and resource limits. An interface that changes USD into
thousands of USD, reverses the treatment contrast, changes the sampling law or orients an
ambiguous edge has changed the scientific request, even if its JSON remains valid. The
reference serialization examples demonstrate those identity changes on local objects; they are
not executions of a server or MCP client. (Causal banking research project, 2026v,w)


40.14.1     The graph object preserves a class of possible interventions

Use opaque variable identifiers and a bijection into engine symbols. Store the original column
order and its permutation separately from the engine’s order. Every variable, including an
isolated node, travels through the conversion. Human-readable labels, availability times and
units remain metadata with their own scientific meaning; names do not supply an orientation
rule. For every pair, retain its two endpoint marks. When the serialization orders the pair
416                                                             Causal analysis for a universal bank


lexically, it swaps the marks with the nodes. Thus R → B, expressed as a tail at R and an
arrowhead at B, agrees with the reversed pair representation having an arrowhead at B and a
tail at R. Reversing only the node order changes the graph. (cmu-phil/tetrad, 2026a; Causal
banking research project, 2026w)
  A Gaussian example illustrates why an unoriented link must survive this boundary. Consider
three standardized variables X, Y, Z with covariance
                                                           
                                           1 4/5 2/5
                                     Σ = 4/5 1 1/2 .
                                                    
                                          2/5 1/2 1

For a banking interpretation, X can denote a rate concession, Y a balance response and Z a
funding outcome, all in stipulated standardized units. The covariance obeys X ⊥ Z | Y . The
undirected path X − Y − Z represents three acyclic orientations without an unshielded collider.
The orientation X → Y ← Z is excluded because it would require a different independence
pattern under faithfulness. (Causal banking research project, 2026w)
  For each retained orientation, regress a variable on its proposed parents using the same
Σ, and assign the residual variance as its independent Gaussian noise variance. In matrix
notation, if Wij is the coefficient from source i to target j, then

                                  Σ = (I − W T )−1 Ω(I − W )−1 ,

where Ω is the diagonal noise covariance. The exact reference calculation verifies this equality
for all three models. In the forward chain, the coefficients are 4/5 and 1/2; intervening on X
changes Z by 2/5 per unit. In the fork and the reverse chain, X has no directed path to Z, so
the effect is zero. The same observational covariance therefore supports the effect multiset
{2/5, 0, 0}. (Causal banking research project, 2026w)
   Returning the forward chain alone would select the positive effect by an unrecorded conven-
tion. Returning the interval [0, 2/5] would introduce values such as 1/5 that none of these
three specified linear Gaussian models produces. That interval is a hull, not the discrete effect
set, and neither object is a confidence set without a separate statistical construction. The
discovery response consequently retains the CPDAG and returns no effect estimate, effect
region or uncertainty level. A later identification operation must state how it handles the whole
class and the additional functional assumptions. (Causal banking research project, 2026v,w)
   Checking endpoint syntax is insufficient to award the CPDAG label. A graph can contain
only tails and arrows and still fail to represent a completed Markov equivalence class. The
existing reference validator does not recognize all such cases. The proposed Java boundary
therefore requires an independently reviewed graph-class check before publishing a completed
CPDAG. A circle, bidirected conflict or invalid completion in the initial route is an invalid-
engine-output failure, with the raw graph retained for diagnosis. It is not silently coerced
into a DAG. Background knowledge is initially excluded because orienting an observational
CPDAG using additional restrictions requires an appropriate constrained-graph representation
and provenance. (Causal banking research project, 2026v)


40.14.2     Admission must cover the failure path as well as the constructor

The proposed PC profile sets the conditioning depth to the inspected unbounded value, enables
the stable skeleton option, selects the separating-set collider rule, disallows bidirected conflicts,
and prevents directed cycles. It supplies empty background knowledge and a caller-declared
test level. These choices make the attempted operation explicit. A user-requested depth cap is
initially unsupported; exhausting a runtime budget returns an incomplete job, not a graph
40.14. A Java discovery boundary that retains the question                                    417


advertised as the result of the completed search. (Causal banking research project, 2026v;
Tetrad contributors, 2026)
   The numerical test profile is equally specific: complete data, no shrinkage, zero ridge and
no pseudoinverse fallback, with all settings frozen before search. The inspected Fisher-Z
source exposes these alternatives separately. Automatically activating regularization after
a singularity would change the test while keeping the same apparent method name. That
may be useful in a different profile, but it needs a separate calibration argument. The initial
profile requires at least n ≥ p + 2 complete observations for p variables so that even the largest
possible conditioning set has positive Fisher-Z degrees of freedom. This is only an arithmetic
prerequisite; it does not guarantee useful power or stable covariance inversion. (Causal banking
research project, 2026v; Tetrad contributors, 2026)
   As the Java comparison showed, the inspected checkIndependence path converts a singular-
matrix exception into a dependence result with p = 0. The proposed wrapper instead uses the
exception-preserving getResult path and derives a decision only from a valid result. Every
invocation receives a query identity and a terminal record. Before propagating an exception,
the wrapper sets a job-level failure flag. Publication then checks that every issued call has a
valid terminal record and that the flag is clear. This matters because search code may catch
interruptions internally: receiving a graph object alone does not prove that all its requested
tests completed. (cmu-phil/tetrad, 2026a; Tetrad contributors, 2026; Causal banking research
project, 2026v)
   That wrapper remains an implementation prerequisite. Its full independence-test interface,
ancillary methods and interaction with the search implementation must be inspected and com-
piled; calling one method in a design document is not sufficient. Numerical rank checks before
dispatch help detect duplicate accounting columns, but per-query records remain necessary
for failures that arise during the search. A zero test probability cannot be reinterpreted as
maximal causal confidence. If the required failure provenance cannot be obtained, the route is
unavailable in this runtime. (Causal banking research project, 2026v)
   Parallelism and deadlines also belong to admission. The stable FAS path uses a parallel
stream and requires thread-safe records. FGES’s separate worker setting does not control that
path. The inspected PC search delegates the skeleton phase to FAS without demonstrating an
end-to-end deadline guarantee from PC’s timeout setting alone. The proposed parent process
therefore enforces the whole-job deadline, memory and output budget. An engine’s cooperative
timeout is supplementary. A cancellation or a process death preserves the attempt’s failure
record and withholds its graph. (Tetrad contributors, 2026; Causal banking research project,
2026v)


40.14.3     Units, unsupported requests and the next executable comparison

The signed funding model in the Java survey provides a useful independent conversion reference.
If x′i = di xi , the source-row coefficients must transform as Wij′ = dj Wij /di . Rescaling the
rate by 100, balances by 1000 and cost by 10, then applying the correspondingly rescaled
rate intervention, must recover the original responses after converting units back. The exact
reference does so. It also verifies that an unchanged absolute coefficient threshold can select a
different graph after rescaling. This does not give coefficients to the PC adapter, whose result
is graph-only; it supplies an admission example for any later weighted route. (Causal banking
research project, 2026w,x)
  A valid request outside the initial scientific scope receives a completed unsupported response
with its context preserved and a specific alternative. Repeated account observations point
toward a separately reviewed temporal or cluster profile; latent-variable assumptions point
418                                                           Causal analysis for a universal bank


toward an appropriate PAG route; missing values require an explicit observation mechanism
and correction profile. An uninstalled or unqualified runtime receives an unavailable response.
Neither condition is called nonidentification, which would be a stronger scientific conclusion
about an effect under a model. Malformed inputs and failed computations carry structured
errors, with no effect or graph result masquerading as a completed calculation. (Causal banking
research project, 2026v)
   The first prototype should use a fixed local Java process so its dependency and runtime
identity can be measured. The process boundary does not remove the inspected GPL conditions.
The actual compiler target, runtime vendor and version, dependency artifacts, operating system
and thread configuration must be locked for the chosen route; the source’s compiler setting
and bridge README cannot substitute for that environment check. Result publication is
atomic after validation. A crashed search is restarted as a new retained attempt under the
same immutable request, with no promise of resuming an internal search state. If completion
wins a cancellation race, the immutable published result remains the observed outcome.
(cmu-phil/tetrad, 2026a; Causal banking research project, 2026v)
   The executable comparison begins with independent oracles: the three-model Gaussian
class, a collider and an isolated node, the depth-three separator, signed matrices and unit
changes, singular input, and injected failures. Only after these pass should a prospectively
specified generated-sample study estimate graph error and resource use under the declared
assumptions and their violations. It should retain every attempted request, including timeouts
and refusals, and compare a matched baseline under the same budgets. These steps test
whether the proposed boundary deserves a prototype claim. Expensive bank experiments
become relevant when that bounded evidence exposes a decision-relevant uncertainty that
public or generated data cannot settle.


40.14.4     Encoding algorithm settings without changing the shared schema

The existing discovery request schema permits only an algorithm identifier and algorithm
version in its parameter object. The proposed Java profile therefore places the detailed
settings in a separate immutable configuration artifact. The request supplies its opaque
handle, hash, media type, schema version and role, alongside the data artifact. Resolving
that artifact recovers the test level, conditioning depth, missingness policy, numerical controls
and background-knowledge choice. The full request identity includes its hash, so changing
a setting creates a different request even when the downstream scientific context remains
identical. This preserves compatibility with the shared schema while retaining the scientifically
relevant settings. (Causal banking research project, 2026v)
  The adapter’s admission check must require exactly one configuration artifact of the reviewed
version, verify its bytes and recognized fields, and check that the declared algorithm version
admits that profile. Generic schema validation alone cannot establish those conditions. The
worked wire records separately represent an unavailable runtime, an unsupported sampling
regime, a failed invocation and a graph response from an independent population reference.
Their data fixture is deterministic, and their graph is not a fitted result. These records make
the proposed response contract concrete without treating a valid message as evidence of an
executed engine.
40.15. A native forest boundary that preserves the banking question                                   419


40.15      A native forest boundary that preserves the banking
           question
A servicing analyst asks whether making a specified offer changes twelve-month net receipts
for eligible customers. The proposed treatment is the offer, coded one, against no offer, coded
zero. The outcome includes the offer’s cost and is measured in dollars per customer over the
stated horizon. A heterogeneous-effect forest can help estimate this contrast under a declared
identification model. Its C++ implementation cannot decide whether the recorded offer was
randomized, whether all confounders were measured, or whether the analyst actually wants
the mean over customers, branches, or treated customers. Those choices must precede engine
dispatch and survive it.
   The proposed first grf integration uses its maintained R interface in a pinned local process,
which in turn invokes the native C++ core. Direct native embedding is a separate alternative.
Inspection covers commit 5bee99b51471, dated 30 April 2026, whose package description
declares version 2.6.1. The snapshot therefore precedes the literature cutoff; its October
acquisition date is separately retained. The design is not an installed adapter. The executed
examples below are project-owned arithmetic references; they neither train grf nor measure its
statistical performance GRF contributors (2026d); Causal banking research project (2026l,m).


40.15.1     From an offer question to a local moment

Let X contain information available before the offer, W ∈ {0, 1} denote assignment, and Y (w)
denote the potential twelve-month net receipt. With consistency, no interference, conditional
exchangeability and positivity, the target is

                       τ (x) = E[Y (1) − Y (0) | X = x],          θ = E[τ (X)].

The outer expectation defines the customer population. An observed treated subpopulation or
an overlap-weighted population gives a different target. The initial proposed profile accepts
complete observations from independent customers, a binary treatment, one fixed outcome and
a fixed horizon. It excludes repeated decision histories, unmeasured confounding, interference,
survey weighting and latent-graph ambiguity that has not been resolved for this estimand.
These are restrictions of the proposed profile, not assertions that the package has no other
functionality.
   Write m(x) = E[Y | X = x] and e(x) = E[W | X = x]. The inspected R wrapper either
obtains nuisance predictions or uses supplied predictions, then passes Y − m(X)

that boundary. The causal binding selects the instrumental trainer and sets the instrument
coordinate to the treatment coordinate. Consequently the inspected native prediction is a
ratio of locally weighted covariances, with the treatment variance in its denominator GRF
contributors (2026c,b).

rule, not evidence that positivity holds in a bank population. The native source divides by
its local first-stage quantity; the adapter must inspect finite outputs and retain weak-support
diagnostics instead of silently replacing a failed division with zero.
   Honest tree splitting and out-of-bag prediction address particular reuse of observations.
They do not establish the causal premises or turn customer rows from a common branch shock
into independent samples. Generalized forest theory also imposes regularity, subsampling,
smooth local identification and variance conditions; a named package and a successful fit do
not verify them Athey et al. (2018). The proposed first profile retains the R nuisance path and
its out-of-bag predictions. Supplying an independently estimated nuisance vector requires a
later profile with explicit training identities, alignment and sampling-unit split rules. A known
randomized propensity may be supplied only with the corresponding assignment declaration;
it is never inferred from a convenient constant.

The average of fitted conditional effects is not interchangeable with the package’s default
augmented average-effect estimator. In the inspected binary path, write τbi for the out-of-bag

   For target weights qi , the corresponding estimator is θb = i qi Γi / i qi . Choosing qi = 1
targets a customer-weighted population; choosing inverse branch sizes gives each observed
branch equal total weight. A branch with two customer scores of ten dollars and a branch with
four scores of forty dollars produce a customer mean of thirty dollars and an equal-branch
mean of twenty-five dollars. A planning cohort of ten thousand customers turns the five-dollar
difference into fifty thousand dollars in a naive projection. That calculation exposes the target
change; it does not justify applying an equal-branch mean to an arbitrary customer portfolio.
   The R interface documents that equal cluster weighting changes both training sampling
and average-effect weights, and disallows user sample weights in that mode. Replacing the
final mean alone cannot reproduce training under that option. A native port would have to
preserve both mechanisms. The initial independent-customer profile therefore rejects cluster
and weight options; the independent-cluster extension is specified for later qualification and
must name whether customers or clusters define its target GRF contributors (2026c).

This specifies a computation. Asymptotic validity needs an appropriate independent-cluster

   For the six scores above, treating all rows as independent gives variance forty dollars squared.
Preserving two branch clusters while retaining the customer target gives 1600/9 dollars squared.
Giving the two branches equal total weight gives variance 225 dollars squared around the

it using grouped trees and a variance-debiasing calculation; the binding copies the variance
values into variance.estimates. The R average-effect operation instead returns std.err,
already square-rooted. Squaring the wrong field or taking its square root twice changes the units.
The proposed adapter keeps the raw field identity, method and units, then creates any reported
interval only under a declared inference profile. Pointwise conditional intervals cannot become
a simultaneous customer band or an interval for their average through serialization. Likewise
excess.error, a finite-forest error diagnostic, is not a substitute for sampling uncertainty
GRF contributors (2026b,c).


40.15.4     Memory ownership, coordinates and model persistence

The inspected Data class is a read-only view of a borrowed contiguous column-major buffer.
Element (r, c) is read at offset cn + r, where n is the number of rows. Constructing the view
from a temporary vector does not transfer ownership. The host must keep the allocation alive
until all training or prediction threads have finished; it must validate shape, index ranges
and multiplication overflow before the call. A three-row, two-column example has columns
(1, 2, 3) and (10, 20, 30). Correct layout reads twenty at zero-based coordinate (1, 1); passing
row-major bytes to the same index formula reads three. Neither value is a memory error, so a
mere successful call cannot detect the scientific corruption GRF contributors (2026a); Causal
banking research project (2026m).
   Role coordinates must remain separate from predictor coordinates. The native setters
mark outcome, treatment, instrument and weight columns as disallowed split variables. The
host records the ordered covariate dictionary, row identifiers, role indices and training/query
distinction. It cannot infer those roles from whichever columns happen to be numeric. Missing
values in covariates are supported by inspected package paths, but are excluded by the initial
profile so that an undocumented imputation or missingness assumption is not introduced.
Conversion to double precision must preserve identifier strings separately and refuse nonfinite
numerical values rather than silently dropping affected customers.
  Model serialization also has ownership semantics. The inspected Rcpp helper iterates by
moving the unique pointer to each native tree into its serialized representation. The header
explicitly says the original forest cannot be used after that operation. A direct embedding
that serializes and then predicts on the consumed forest is therefore invalid. Either serialize an
explicitly supported copy, or deserialize the saved representation into a new object. Retain the
engine commit, ordered feature map, original training-data identity, nuisance vectors, options
422                                                             Causal analysis for a universal bank


and format version beside the forest. The selected source does not establish a stable C++ ABI
or a portable standalone model format. These are admission questions for a native route, not
problems solved by choosing a file extension GRF contributors (2026a).


40.15.5     A concrete request and result contract

The operation is estimate.effect. Its generic parameter schema accepts an engine
identifier and estimator identifier, so the proposed profile uses grf-r-native-2.6.1 and
binary-iid-aipw-all-v1 there. Detailed settings reside in an immutable configuration
artifact, carried through the existing artifact list. That artifact binds the exact source commit,
treatment contrast, outcome/horizon, row and column roles, seed, thread count, tree options
and target. The adapter validates its own profile before dispatch; generic JSON acceptance
alone does not validate these scientific restrictions Causal banking research project (2026l).
   Library, CLI and MCP surfaces must resolve identical authorized data and configuration
identities. The context digest retains the estimand, population, units, information clock,
assumptions, sampling declaration and graph. The full request identity additionally binds
data bytes, configuration, engine environment and numerical settings. Changing the target
population or turning branch weighting on produces a different request; transport names
cannot cause reuse of a previous result. Graph endpoint marks and unresolved sets remain
intact. A forest is not a graph-identification service: if a retained model class gives different
effects and the query has no accepted identification argument, this profile cannot silently select
a graph.
   Before runtime admission, discovery of this engine returns unavailable. A recognized but
unsupported sampling regime, continuous treatment, dynamic policy request or unresolved
graph requirement returns unsupported with an actionable explanation. Nonfinite output,
failed subprocess execution or an invalid model artifact is a failure; no finite effect accompanies
it. A reviewed identification failure can return not-identified with its evidence, but the adapter’s
inability to analyze a model is not an impossibility proof. An overlap alarm produces a refusal
under the declared profile. Trimming or switching to an overlap population requires a newly
reviewed target and request.
   After engineering admission, a computed scalar estimate keeps its dollar unit, signed offer-
minus-no-offer contrast and target identifier. A diagnostic conditional-prediction artifact retains
query-row coordinates and explicitly denotes conditional means, not individual counterfactual
differences. The initial engineering result carries execution-only qualification and no confidence
claim. Conditional inference needs its own reviewed uncertainty construction and evidence.
A mathematically unbounded or disconnected result from another method must be returned
with its topology; this forest profile does not approximate it by a large finite interval.


40.15.6     Deployment choices and the next informative comparison

The package description requires R at least 3.5.0, C++17 and GNU make, links Rcpp and
RcppEigen, and imports additional packages including Matrix, DiceKriging, lmtest and
sandwich. These declarations are minimum/source requirements, not a tested environment
lock. The proposed R process must record the installed R and dependency versions, source and
binary hashes, compiler and flags, thread settings and runtime options. The inspected native
CMake file collects both source and test files into an executable; its presence does not supply a
ready production shared library or a reviewed installed ABI. Package metadata declares GPL-3
and the inspected source headers state GPL version 3 or later. Preserve file and dependency
terms and review distribution obligations before shipping; a subprocess boundary alone settles
40.15. A native forest boundary that preserves the banking question                          423


neither licensing compatibility nor distribution duties GRF contributors (2026d).
   The parent process bounds wall time, memory and output size and publishes only a
complete validated result atomically. Standard output is the protocol channel; diagnostics
have a bounded separate log. A crash or timeout leaves a typed failure and its input identities.
No mid-tree recovery is promised. Replaying an immutable request starts from its recorded
seed and environment; bitwise equality across different compilers or thread settings remains
a measured property. One worker per isolated R process is the conservative initial choice
because the inspected binding also writes global runtime context. Concurrency inside a shared
embedding requires its own review.
   The proposal recommends the R/native route first because it retains the inspected nuisance,
score and aggregation paths. Direct native embedding may later reduce interface overhead
or fit a host’s deployment constraints, but would transfer those statistical and ownership
responsibilities to the host. A full algorithm port has the greatest maintenance and conformance
burden. Reject direct embedding for the initial profile until it reproduces the R path; this is a
scoped engineering choice, not a claim that native integration is impossible.
   The next comparison should freeze one environment and the complete workload: data
conversion, nuisance estimation, forest training, average-effect scoring, serialization, output
validation and failure handling. Compare the maintained R route with a direct-native candidate
only under identical inputs, target, options and estimator formulas. Exact fixtures first check
coordinates, residualization, score aggregation and refusal behavior. A separately registered
generated-data study can then examine coverage, availability, heterogeneity recovery and
resources, retaining weak-overlap and dependent cases in its denominator. Pure arithmetic
agreement cannot replace that study, and local runtime cannot establish bank workflow savings.
The useful investment question is whether a native route improves the complete workload
enough to justify owning the additional statistical and deployment machinery.
Chapter 41

The library, command line and MCP
service

41.1     An interface must preserve a scientific question
A servicing analyst asks whether an offer would improve the next twelve months’ net value
for accounts eligible today. A notebook, a scheduled command and an agent can all transmit
this question. They should receive the same conditional answer when they submit the same
declaration, inputs and method. They should also retain the same unresolved assumptions. A
successful call which replaces the target population, changes the sign or drops an unbounded
component of an uncertainty set has failed as a scientific interface even if its JSON is valid.
The preceding chapter establishes the exchange contract; this chapter develops the actual
access paths and the client behavior needed to preserve it.
   The implemented library entry is causalbank.runtime_v12.Runtime.invoke. The
command-line adapter and local MCP server use that runtime, its artifact store and the
scientific dispatcher. This shared implementation reduces divergence among surfaces. It does
not prove their equivalence: parsing, version negotiation, error handling and asynchronous
state can still alter the result seen by a client. Consequently an interface comparison must
examine complete canonical responses, including negative findings, rather than compare only
the estimated coefficient. The inspected source and recorded local trials support this narrow
architecture claim (Causal banking research project, 2026aq,n).
   The runtime advertises nine operations. Capability inspection reports the implemented
subset. Graph review checks a supplied declaration’s syntax. Identification attempts a supplied-
DAG back-door expression for independent units and a binary contrast. Estimation inverts
a Gaussian residual test using supplied moments and covariance. Sensitivity solves supplied
quadratic inequalities. Observation auditing checks declared timestamps. Report building,
job status and job cancellation provide the remaining three operations. Automatic problem
formulation, data-driven graph discovery and design comparison have no engine in this runtime.
They belong to the proposed architecture, and are absent from the advertised MCP tool list.
   These distinctions matter when an agent chooses a tool called estimate.effect. The
name identifies an operation family; the supported engine and estimator identifiers determine
what can actually run. An agent cannot turn the supplied-moment engine into a fitted causal
forest by changing its description. Nor does the graph syntax operation establish that a graph
represents the bank’s assignment mechanism. Capabilities should be inspected at the start
of a client session and retained with its results, because a proposed method and an installed
method are different inputs to a decision.


                                              424
41.2. A complete request for an offer decision                                               425


  Write a canonical request as Q = (o, C, A, p, B, k), where o is the operation, C the scientific
context, A the artifact references, p the operation parameters, B the resource budget and
k an optional replay key. The separate request identifier correlates a reply with a call. For
deterministic synchronous examples, the desired transport property is

                               Rlibrary (Q) = RCLI (Q) = RMCP (Q),

after decoding each transport’s wrapper. This is a scoped design property, tested on selected
cases. For jobs, compare stable handles and the same observed terminal state; two polls at
different times need not report the same intermediate state. Neither equality proves that C is
causally correct.


41.2      A complete request for an offer decision
Let A denote a binary offer, Y twelve-month net value in USD and X a pre-decision risk
score. The generated example declares the arrows X → A, X → Y and A → Y . Its target is
the offer-minus-no-offer average effect for eligible accounts. These are example declarations,
without bank observations or independently verified graph truth. An explicit unverified
assumption is more useful than silently treating the graph as known.
   The following Python file creates a complete request. Save it as offer_request.py and run
it with Python; its only output file is request.json. The example uses a loop to retain the
same evidence and review fields on each edge. There is no hidden inference step in that loop.
import json
