   Trials should also examine composite failure. A correct feature clock does not rescue an
incorrect population map; a correct graph representation does not repair missing selection
information. The acceptance object is the entire declared workflow. Nevertheless, a failure
should be localized: an unavailable Java dependency should not prevent a reviewed Python file
exchange, and an unsupported longitudinal estimator should not block the exact funding-value
transformation. The common contract allows each consumer to see which part is available,
which scientific claim remains conditional and which next input could change the answer.
   For deterministic conversions, exact arithmetic or a stated floating-point tolerance is
appropriate. For a stochastic method, compare targets and matched distributional behavior
under a registered design, not a single numerically similar run. Calibration, failure frequency,
useful precision, runtime and memory are distinct measurements. A faster adapter does
not repair undercoverage; a conservative whole-line set does not satisfy a decision precision
requirement simply because its coverage is high. The operating chapter develops these resource
and failure distinctions further.


42.13       Choosing the first connection and the next experiment
For this proposal, a reviewed manual artifact exchange is the baseline for each selected consumer.
It forces the target, units, clock and provenance to be written down before automation hides
them. The first automated connection should address a frequent, stable exchange whose
scientific interpretation is already defensible. FinMarketing’s source and target declarations
and dataml’s artifact-oriented CLI provide plausible observation interfaces; MacroFinance with
the selected BayesFilter authority provides a plausible funding route. Their priority follows
from the banking questions, not from an assertion that the mappings are complete.
  A planning comparison can make the choice explicit. If a manual process costs cm per
admitted request, an automated route costs ca , and design, verification and maintenance have
present cost F , then the cost advantage over n otherwise equivalent requests is

                                        n(cm − ca ) − F.

The expression requires equivalent output quality, exception handling and retention; it is not
a measured return on investment. If cm ≤ ca , volume alone does not pay for the automation.
If an adapter reduces meaningful translation errors, their expected loss can be added only
with an explicit error model, baseline and uncertainty. Runtime for one arithmetic call omits
human specification, source review, data transfer, failures and revision cost.
   The immediate informative experiment is therefore a small matched workflow trial on public
or clearly generated requests. Measure the manual and automated routes against the same
independently declared targets, preserve every refusal and failed request, and include the
adverse cases in Table 42.2. Record where the actual consumer changes or drops a field.
This can justify building a broader adapter without the cost of an authentic bank study. A
450                                                          Causal analysis for a universal bank


later bank experiment is warranted when the unresolved question concerns representative
assignment, ownership, precision, operating fit or value that the public trial cannot establish.
   The reusable contribution is the target-preserving workflow, including its failure states.
The exact examples are reproducible with tools/workspace_examples_20261013.py, using
a fresh output path; they require only the Python standard library and execute no sibling
code (Causal banking research project, 2026q). They demonstrate why the proposed interfaces
need the information specified here. Actual adapter conformance, consumer acceptance and
bank applicability require their own evidence, attached to the selected implementation and
the claim being made.
Chapter 43

Operating the local causal service
and qualifying its limits

43.1     An execution identity is larger than a request name
A durable analysis must bind the canonical request, scientific context, input bytes, code,
schema, numerical environment, seed and budget. A repeated job name alone cannot establish
that a result is still valid. The implemented runtime records these identities and rejects
idempotency collisions involving changed requests or execution identities.Causal banking
research project (2026aq)
   Artifacts use canonical JSON, content and descriptor hashes, opaque identities and bounded
local reads. Regular-file and nonsymlink checks reduce accidental path redirection. A content
hash establishes byte identity under the relevant assumption about the hash function; it is
not an authenticated endorsement of the input’s scientific accuracy. A local operator can still
supply a false declaration whose bytes remain perfectly stable.
   The scientific request contains no arbitrary shell command, Python import or network
endpoint. Fixed worker entry points execute the supported operations. This makes the scope
of the local tool explicit and allows a review grant to refer to actual operations. The current
controller’s trusted caller object is not a substitute for an institutional identity and approval
service.


43.2     Budgets, durable jobs and cancellation
Scientific workers have wall-time and address-space limits. The memory bound applies to the
worker, not to all memory used by the resident SDK and coordinator. A complete operating
measurement must include both. Small control or error envelopes may exceed an extremely
small requested output limit to explain why the request cannot be fulfilled. These are disclosed
boundaries of the present implementation.Causal banking research project (2026aq)
   Report jobs retain a hashed prefix of completed work identities. The local retry rule is
bounded to three attempts under the original deadline. Publication is atomic, and replay
checks request, artifact and checkpoint identities before continuation. The recorded restart
fixture kills a report worker after its first checkpoint and completes all one hundred distinct
work identities once. This is evidence for that local workflow, not a distributed exactly-once
guarantee for arbitrary external side effects.
  Cancelling an in-flight protocol request and cancelling a durable application job are different

                                              451
452                                                           Causal analysis for a universal bank


operations. The inspected specification also recognizes cancellation/completion races.Model
Context Protocol contributors (2026b) If publication has already completed, a cancellation
response must report that terminal state. It must not imply that a displayed result or an
external action was undone. The present service has no operation that changes a bank account
or sends a customer communication.


43.3     Fault evidence and what remains unmeasured
Nine recorded fault cases cover replay with conflicting budgets, wall timeout, output limits,
worker memory, kill/restart with checkpoint, cooperative cancellation, changed artifact bytes,
changed scientific context and changed checkpoints.Causal banking research project (2026aq)
The tests distinguish preserving a result from merely restarting a process. An interrupted
computation that silently uses new inputs is a different analysis even if it eventually finishes.
  These fixtures do not measure institution-scale availability, multi-host recovery, adversarial
tenant isolation or a service-level commitment. They also do not show that streaming always
improves elapsed time. The earlier complete local workload comparisons retain small or absent
gains; engineering choices must be justified by the intended workload rather than by the
existence of a streaming interface.
   Operational qualification should measure the complete request: artifact import, scientific
work, uncertainty, serialization, reporting and recovery. A benchmark of one reducer omits
fitting and coordination costs. The comparison needs matched inputs, numerical tolerance
and an explicit accounting of unsuccessful requests, just as a scientific comparison needs a
common target.


43.4     Compatibility is a maintained scientific obligation
A new backend release can change defaults, graph encodings, estimator targets, uncertainty or
failure behavior. A compatible JSON schema alone does not prove scientific compatibility. The
proposed adapter register should bind a version, accepted inputs, method identity, preserved
result types and matched adverse fixtures. A material semantic change requires a reviewed
successor rather than relabeling an old qualification.
   Transport migration likewise needs real client/server tests. The current legacy MCP choice
is useful for its tested environment. Supporting a modern protocol or both eras requires a new
compatibility argument, discovery behavior and failure tests. It should not be advertised by
extending a version string while keeping the old handshake.
   Ownership must also remain explicit. The causal library owns its result contract and
adapters. Numerical providers own their implementations and scientific domains. Consumers
own their target interpretation and displayed decision. The bank owns actual data authority,
assignment records, operational constraints and acceptance. A report can connect those
responsibilities; it cannot replace their evidence.


43.5     What a recovery identity must preserve
Consider a daily deposit report that aggregates customer-level evidence into a 90-day funding
decision. A restarted process must answer the same question using the same admitted
observations. Replacing a data extract with a later vintage, changing a sign convention, or
upgrading a numerical routine can alter the scientific result even when the file name and
43.6. Checkpoint invariants and the scope of idempotence                                       453


command remain unchanged. This is why recovery needs an analysis identity rather than only
a process identifier.
  Write the intended identity as

                                    J = Hash(Q, A, S, E, ρ, B),

where Q is the scientific request, A the input identities, S the schema and method semantics,
E the relevant execution environment, ρ the randomization state where applicable, and B the
declared budget. This is a proposed completeness condition. The inspected runtime fingerprints
a selected list of source files and schemas, Python, and four named package versions. Its
request digest omits the display request identifier and idempotency key while retaining the
other request fields. It rejects reuse of a key with a changed request or selected execution
identity Causal banking proposal project (2026n).
  The selected fingerprint is useful but does not describe every numerical or platform depen-
dency. It does not, for example, independently record the complete transitive dependency
graph, numerical-library build, operating system and hardware state. A future numerical
adapter must identify which of those properties can affect its result, then bind and test them.
Extending the fingerprint is an engineering obligation; it does not establish that the underlying
causal assumptions are true. Conversely, irrelevant display metadata need not invalidate a
deterministic result if the scientific and execution identities remain unchanged.
   Three compatibility questions follow. Byte replay asks whether the same admitted compu-
tation returns the same canonical bytes. Numerical compatibility allows a declared tolerance
or stochastic comparison under an unchanged mathematical target. Scientific compatibility
asks whether the population, treatment, horizon, units, assumptions and inferential meaning
remain the same. A backend upgrade can satisfy a numerical tolerance while changing which
observations are dropped or which population is weighted. Such an upgrade needs a semantic
review even if its output schema is unchanged.
   For the funding report, sensible adverse fixtures include a changed date cutoff, a currency-unit
conversion, a negative monetary map, a missing assignment field, an unbounded uncertainty
set and a default that drops customers without complete histories. The comparison must
preserve valid refusals and ambiguous results. Substituting a point estimate for an unbounded
set is not a compatibility repair.


43.6      Checkpoint invariants and the scope of idempotence
Suppose a report combines deterministic contributions si for a frozen ordered list of work
identities (a1 , . . . , am ). A useful checkpoint is

                             Ck = (J, (a1 , . . . , ak ), (s1 , . . . , sk ), hk ),

where hk binds the preceding contents. The required invariant is that the completed identifiers
form a prefix of the frozen request, each identifier has one committed contribution, and the
public result is a function of those committed contributions. Recomputing an uncommitted
contribution after a crash may waste work; committing it twice changes the answer.
   An exact project construction makes the distinction visible. Three intended contributions
are 100, −40, 70, so the total is 130. A crash and retry can produce the calculation trace
100, −40, −40, 70. Naively appending every returned value gives 90. A map from work identity
to its immutable contribution still gives 130, provided a repeated identity cannot carry changed
contents. These are finite arithmetic results, not measurements of a distributed serviceCausal
banking proposal project (2026l).
454                                                              Causal analysis for a universal bank


   The inspected local report worker verifies its completed prefix and digest, skips already
committed identities, and updates summaries and completed identities together in the job
state. Its preserved restart trial completed 100 distinct work identities, with 100 unique entries,
after two worker starts. The more recent preserved fault replay also reports the nine declared
cases passing; that replay was not a fresh MCP client/server trial Causal banking proposal
project (2026n,m). This evidence supports the named local report path. It does not establish
recovery for arbitrary estimators, multi-host execution or transactions at a bank.
   The atomicity boundary is also specific. The artifact store publishes its content and
metadata as individually atomic files, checks any already present bytes, and can complete a
repeated deterministic publication. The report’s result reference and terminal job state are
then published in the job record. These are several transitions, not one transaction spanning
arbitrary external systems. A crash can leave an unreferenced artifact even when no incorrect
public result is exposed. Retention and garbage collection therefore need a separate rule that
preserves artifacts referenced by admitted jobs and evidence. Hash verification alone cannot
establish that cleanup is safe.
   A customer communication illustrates the stronger problem. If an external system sends an
offer and the acknowledgement is lost, a retrying client may not know whether the offer was sent.
Recording the local calculation once does not resolve that ambiguity. An eventual external-
action adapter would need a cooperating transaction or deduplication contract, reconciliation
and a named owner for unresolved outcomes. The present service performs no such bank
action. Its proposal should retain report generation as a distinct, read-oriented capability
rather than infer action safety from a successful restart.


43.7      Retries purchase attempts, not independent chances of
          success
Let K be a maximum number of attempts and q the probability of a transient failure on each
attempt. If failures are independent and identically distributed, the probability of obtaining a
result is 1 − q K and the expected number of attempts is
                                                 K−1
                                                 X
                                         ENK =          qj .
                                                  j=0

For the stipulated values q = 1/5 and K = 3, these are 124/125 = 0.992 and 31/25 = 1.24.
The numbers express an assumed failure law. Nine passing fault fixtures do not estimate q,
and a retry cap alone cannot establish the 99.2% success probabilityCausal banking proposal
project (2026l).
   Persistent failures change the calculation. Suppose one tenth of requests cannot succeed
under the supplied environment, while the remaining nine tenths have independent per-attempt
failure probability one tenth. Three attempts then succeed with probability
                                    9     1
                                                
                                       1− 3          = 0.8991,
                                    10   10
and require 0.1(3) + 0.9(1 + 0.1 + 0.01) = 1.299 attempts on average. The marginal first-
attempt failure probability is 0.19. Treating that marginal value as independent across
retries would predict 1 − 0.193 = 0.993141, substantially overstating success. The retry
has not changed an unavailable dependency, an unsupported method or contradictory input
declarations. Operational classification should distinguish those persistent causes from a
recoverable interruption.
43.8. Resource budgets and cancellation at the right boundary                                 455


   A bounded retry policy also retains its original time account. In the inspected report path,
remaining time is computed from the job creation timestamp and original wall budget, and
the worker-start count is capped at three. Restarting does not intentionally grant three new
full deadlines. The implementation uses local wall-clock timestamps and operating-system
timers; this is not a distributed clock or a hard real-time guarantee. Launch overhead, host
suspension, clock adjustment and recovery of a failed machine require a target-environment
study before making a service-level claimCausal banking proposal project (2026n).
  Statistical retries need an additional distinction. Replaying an interrupted calculation with
preserved random state is different from drawing new randomness until a desired conclusion
appears. If three independent valid null p-values are generated and the smallest is selected,
the probability of at least one value below 0.05 is

                                  1 − (1 − 0.05)3 = 0.142625.

This exact counterexample assumes independent uniform null p-values; it does not allege
that the runtime performs such selection. It shows why the proposed adapter must separate
mechanical recovery from a new statistical replicate and preserve all requested analyses. The
same issue arises when timeouts depend on difficult data and only easy completed fits enter a
coverage reportCausal banking proposal project (2026l).


43.8      Resource budgets and cancellation at the right boundary
The local worker sets an address-space limit and a wall-time timer. The coordinator starts a
fixed worker entry point, collects its output and validates the canonical response against the
requested output size. This supports a bounded set of local operations. It does not impose
one aggregate memory bound on the worker, coordinator, SDK and all clients, and the output
check is applied after collection rather than as an incremental bound on an arbitrary producer’s
streamCausal banking proposal project (2026n).
   For a proposed third-party numerical adapter, admission should therefore include peak
resident memory of the whole workflow, temporary disk use, serialization and parent-process
buffers. A limit that is safe for a short report may be inappropriate for an estimator returning
a large covariance matrix. If a result exceeds the public response size, the design can publish
a separately bounded artifact with explicit custody and expose a small reference. It must
retain the scientific object’s meaning and cannot silently truncate interval components or omit
unsuccessful fits to meet a size limit.
  Cancellation is a race between a request and the computation’s next state transition. For
pure report generation, a useful rule is that an accepted cancellation recorded before the
publication transition prevents a new public result; cancellation after publication returns
the actual completed state. The inspected implementation checks a cancellation flag around
report work and before publication. That cooperative behavior does not guarantee that every
numerical kernel can be interrupted at an arbitrary instruction. A later adapter may need
worker termination and a rule for discarding uncommitted artifacts.
  A timeout should be recorded as an execution outcome. A scientifically unidentified effect
can instead be a completed result with an explicit scientific limitation. Converting both into
one generic failure statistic obscures the remedy: the first may need resource or implementation
work, while the second may need a different target, new information or abstention. A successful
process exit likewise says nothing by itself about whether the effect is precise enough to support
a decision.
456                                                           Causal analysis for a universal bank


43.9     Ownership and a reversible adoption path
Operational ownership follows the claim being made. A method maintainer owns the supported
algorithm and numerical domain. The common-library owner owns the request/result contract,
method-version binding and admitted conversions. The consumer owns the displayed target,
units and business action. A later bank study additionally needs a data owner for the actual
observation and assignment processes and a decision owner for losses and feasible actions.
These are proposed responsibilities, not names or approvals that have already been supplied.
   For example, a deposit report may use a valid backend estimate while a consumer interprets
the coefficient as currency rather than thousands of currency units. The remedy belongs partly
in the shared unit contract and partly in the consuming application’s acceptance examples. A
central numerical team cannot certify a silently altered presentation. Conversely, an application
owner cannot declare a confidence procedure valid merely because the resulting interval is
displayed correctly.
   The proposal should make an adoption decision reversible at its natural boundaries. Retain
the incumbent expert workflow and its artifacts while a new adapter is evaluated on matched
public/generated requests. Publish both methods’ complete outputs with their own identities;
compare discrepancies before replacing the default. A schema migration should have a declared
mapping and refusal cases for information it cannot preserve. Where a new method changes
the estimand, the migration is a new scientific analysis, not a formatting conversion. A rollback
retains access to the previously admitted version and evidence without rewriting its result as
if produced by the new version.
   The same approach applies to workspace consumers. Read-only inspection of a repository
can reveal candidate objects and interfaces. It cannot establish that its owner accepts the
proposed contract, that its launch environment is compatible, or that an integration saves
work. A local mock consumer can test the proposed request and response boundary now.
Actual consumer execution, deployment ownership and institutional operation remain distinct
later claims, with their own narrowly defined studies.


43.10      The economic denominator is every attempted request
Let R denote whether a request returns a usable result and D its incremental decision value
relative to the incumbent workflow, including the specified fallback when R = 0. Let C include
all request-specific compute, review, retry and recovery costs. The per-request economic target
is
                                            E[D − C],
plus a consistent allocation of fixed construction and shared operating costs. Reporting
E[D | R = 1] with a nominal successful-run cost answers a different question. Reliability
and economic comparisons require both the success probability and what happens on the
unsuccessful branch.
   In an exact stipulated example, 70% of requests are easy, complete and add USD 10 of
gross value. Another 15% complete but add USD −30. The remaining 15% fail and revert to
the baseline action, adding zero gross value but requiring USD 20 of recovery work. Every
attempt costs USD 2 in tools and computation. The completed-only calculation reports

                            0.70(10) + 0.15(−30)     16
                                                 −2=    ≃ 0.941
                                     0.85            17
43.11. The next complete qualification                                                           457


USD per completed request. The all-attempt account instead gives

                          0.70(10) + 0.15(−30) − 2 − 0.15(20) = −2.5

USD per attempted request. The apparent gain changes sign when the unsuccessful work and
correct denominator enter the account. These numbers are generated planning assumptions,
not workflow prices or measured bank returnsCausal banking proposal project (2026l).
   Measurement should therefore retain attempted task identity, terminal execution state,
scientific disposition, usable-result status, fallback action and disjoint cost categories. Repeated
attempts are costs within a request, not new independent banking opportunities. Correlated
requests from one institution, calendar or scientific task family also cannot be treated as
independent evidence merely because their request identifiers differ. The analysis unit should
follow the source of independent information.
   A prototype can measure machine resources and trace whether required fields survive
recovery. It cannot price saved analyst time without observing a matched workflow, nor infer
business value from seconds saved. The next inexpensive operational study should compare
complete local workflows under declared faults and budgets, preserve adverse results, and
report source and environment identities. Only a subsequent justified platform or bank study
can supply institution-specific availability, ownership, labor, and decision-value evidence. Their
absence limits those claims while leaving the public/generated proposal work executable.


43.11       The next complete qualification
The remaining engineering route is concrete: choose source-audited packages and permitted
integration forms, implement representative bridges, and run matched consumer workflows
across all three surfaces. The trial must include unsupported methods, late observations, graph
ambiguity, weak or disconnected effect sets, interruption and changed-input rejection. Passing
results should name the actual supported environments and domains.
   This work will close an engineering gap only in those domains. Negative persistent-map,
latent-graph and dependent-learner studies remain scientific obligations. Independent review,
authentic bank validation and measured economics remain additional gates. A coherent runtime
makes their required inputs and outputs reviewable; it does not turn missing information into
an accepted causal answer.


43.12       A discovery journey that preserves refusal and uncer-
            tainty
A bank’s request to discover why an offer changes twelve-month customer value contains
several operations. The information must precede the offer, the candidate graph must retain its
unresolved orientations, the requested effect must be identified under a declared model, and the
financial interpretation must preserve the resulting uncertainty. A common command-line or
library interface is useful only if its callers can tell which of these operations actually occurred.
   The local reference service supports graph syntax review and a particular supplied-DAG back-
door calculation. Its graph.discover request remains unsupported. A syntax response can
preserve a CPDAG or PAG and its endpoint marks without establishing that the graph is true
or recognizing every valid member of the represented class. The supplied-DAG identification
method does not thereby become a method for arbitrary graph classes, latent confounding,
temporal discovery or dependent sampling.
458                                                            Causal analysis for a universal bank


   The extended local exercise froze 24 authored cases and 98 invocation slots before executing
them (Causal banking research project, 2026f). Each case was called through the library
and CLI, initially and after restart or re-instantiation. Two additional requests retained a
completed request’s key while changing its target horizon. The elementary references were
graph paths, factored inequalities, exact timestamp order and explicit changes to request
identity. They support a deterministic behavior comparison, not a statistical discovery accuracy
or causal-coverage estimate.


43.12.1     Identification and refusal in a concrete offer graph

For the supplied graph A → Y , an empty adjustment set satisfies the selected back-door
criterion. Add a pre-offer risk variable R with A ← R → Y . If R is observed and included
in the adjustment request, the method returns the corresponding conditional identification
expression. Omitting R leaves the path open. Declaring it latent does not make an observed
adjustment possible. Conversely, requesting adjustment for the mediator in A → R → Y fails
this particular criterion for the total effect. Such failures must remain failures of the attempted
method; they are not proofs that every identification strategy is impossible.
   The cases also require refusal when a declared premise is contradicted, unsupported disposi-
tions for CPDAG/PAG identification and dependent-month sampling, and an invalid-request
response for a directed cycle. Correctly recognizing these boundaries is useful behavior. It
does not supply the causal effect that the bank originally wanted.


43.12.2     Numerical sets, information clocks and immutable context

Four deterministic sensitivity calculations check set serialization: 1 − x2 ≤ 0 gives two rays,
1 + x2 ≤ 0 gives the empty set, −1 − x2 ≤ 0 gives the whole line, and (x − 1)2 ≤ 0 gives
a singleton. The service retains those different topologies. The examples have no sampling
coverage probability; numerical edge cases outside these selected polynomials still need an
independent error analysis.
  The observation audit admits the timestamp row satisfying event ≤ available < decision.
Availability exactly at the decision, a missing timestamp, and an availability time preceding
the event are retained as failures. These declarations alone cannot establish that a real source
system recorded the correct timestamps.
   Two artifact cases test a different failure mechanism. Changing the sign of the target
after importing a moment artifact must prevent its reuse under the new scientific context.
Corrupting the stored bytes must fail their identity check. Keeping an idempotency key while
changing the horizon must yield a conflict. A client that receives such a failure has no new
computed effect to display. Its request correlation ID can change across a replay, while the
scientific content must remain equal.


43.12.3     Observed behavior and the cost of this local exercise

All 98 slots matched their frozen expectations, and all 24 case comparisons retained the same
scientific responses across the four route/restart calls. There were 44 computed responses,
36 unsupported responses, four refusals, four invalid requests and ten unavailable responses,
including the two target conflicts. The computed group includes capabilities, syntax, conditional
expressions, sensitivity sets and an audit; it is not a count of 44 estimated causal effects. All
groups remain in the denominator.
43.13. From a funding response to a defensible treasury decision                              459


  The run resumed after 40 and 80 recorded invocations, preserving both completed prefixes
exactly. The 98 invocations took approximately 41.99 seconds in this local run, including
worker/process launch, failed requests and replay. This measurement excludes author effort,
process startup before the runner’s timer, and pauses between runner segments. Separate active-
runner time includes artifact imports and journaling. Reported resident-memory readings are
maxima for individual parent/child processes, not concurrent process-tree memory. These
measurements neither establish bank throughput nor estimate bank ROI.
  Restarting these calls is a narrower exercise than killing a multi-host service mid-operation.
A crash between a completed call and its journal write can repeat that call with the same key;
the exercise does not establish exactly-once execution. It also runs no actual sibling consumer,
MCP transport, live language model or installed discovery engine. Those distinctions preserve
the meaning of both positive checks and remaining work.


43.12.4     How the proposed consumer uses the result

A consumer first reads capabilities and checks its clock, target, sampling law, graph type
and requested method. A syntax pass allows a graph to be displayed with its marks intact.
A conditional identification expression permits the next estimation design to be considered.
An unsupported or refused result routes the question to another justified method or requests
missing information. It must not trigger an automatic point estimate from a language model.
   A contract double can demonstrate these client decisions using typed local responses.
Acceptance of an actual workspace integration additionally needs the owner’s request and
unit map, source clock, execution trace, failure and restart results, and an explicit disposition.
This is later evidence about that integration. For the present proposal, the local exercise
already makes the required behavior concrete and reproducible while preserving the missing
discovery-to-effect capabilities.


43.13       From a funding response to a defensible treasury decision
A treasury team considering a deposit-rate change needs more than a response coefficient. It
needs to know which balance the response concerns, whose accounts constitute the target
population, which information was available when the quote was chosen, and whether the
uncertainty survives the journey from estimated scores to a financial recommendation. This
section develops that journey through exact project examples and a bounded local interface
exercise. The examples are generated constructions dated 13 October 2026; they are not
observations of a bank or later additions to the literature search cutoff (Causal banking research
project, 2026i,j).
   Let β denote the response of the next twelve months’ average retained deposit balance,
measured in USD millions, to a one-percentage-point increase in the quoted deposit rate.
A response of the balance at month twelve is a different quantity: earning a spread on a
closing balance does not describe the interest income earned over the preceding year. A
quarter-percentage-point action has response 0.25β only under an additional local-linearity
and intervention-stability premise. A normalized proxy response does not by itself establish
that a feasible deposit-rate decision implements the corresponding structural intervention.
   These distinctions belong in the proposed product’s scientific context. The target, horizon,
units, sign, intervention and sampling law must travel with the estimate. A consumer also
needs evidence for the population map, inclusion mechanism, score construction and covariance.
It should be possible to compute a conditional mathematical object while withholding a funding
460                                                                     Causal analysis for a universal bank


recommendation whose premises remain unresolved. The existing service implements the
former operation on supplied summaries; the broader decision layer remains proposed (Causal
banking research project, 2026k).


43.13.1     Information clocks and the population behind the balance

A feature available to a quote decision must satisfy

                                    tevent ≤ tavailable < tdecision .

The first time that a value could actually be used is the relevant availability time. Substituting
a subsequently revised figure into a past feature record can violate this requirement even if
the revision carries the same economic reference date. The rule concerns decision information.
Future outcomes are necessarily observed later and instead require an explicit follow-up and
censoring rule. An audit that rejected every post-decision outcome would be auditing the
wrong object.
   Correct timestamp order cannot establish that two records belong to the same household.
To see why this matters, consider four generated households with truth-known contributions
(0, 2, 4, 6). Their household mean is 3. Repeating the first household’s zero contribution in
four records gives seven records,

                              (0, 0, 0, 0, 2, 4, 6),    y record = 12/7.

The true household mean remains 3 when the four zero records have a common identity. If
they represent four distinct households, 12/7 is instead the mean of that seven-household
population. Identical values and valid clocks cannot distinguish these two interpretations. An
artifact hash establishes which bytes were used; it does not recover the missing unit map.
   Inclusion creates a separate problem even with known identities. Suppose the four households
are independently included with probabilities (1, 1, 1/2, 1/2). The first two are always present;
the last two generate four equally probable selection states. The observed unweighted means
are
                           1, 2, 8/3, 3,          E[y observed ] = 13/6.
For known target size N = 4 and known positive probabilities πi , the population-total estimator
divided by N is
                                      4
                                   1X   Si yi
                             µHT =
                             b                ,    E[µ
                                                     bHT ] = 3.
                                   4 i=1 πi
Its four possible values are 1/2, 5/2, 7/2, 11/2. The equality follows by enumeration or by
E[Si /πi ] = 1; it does not follow from observing only the selected records. Unknown inclusion
probabilities, an unknown target population or a stratum with zero inclusion require additional
information or a restricted target. The contributions in this construction are generated
truth. The calculation does not make both potential outcomes observable in a real funding
study (Causal banking research project, 2026i).
   For the proposed workflow, unit and inclusion evidence therefore precede claims about a
target-bank response. A useful public-panel prototype can exercise institution identifiers, dates
and observed balance aggregation. It should not label public institution identifiers as a verified
household map, nor claim assignment truth from a panel that does not record it. Generated
studies remain useful because the hidden truth can be deliberately corrupted and kept out of
the estimation inputs.

43.13.2     The covariance must include what the workflow estimated

Write a normalized response as β = µY /µD , where µY is a numerator moment and µD is the
normalization moment. The estimator may first fit a conditional mean, propensity, proxy,
linkage model or other nuisance quantity. If a justified expansion has leading score

                                            ψt = ψ0,t + Aϕη,t ,

then, when the corresponding stationary long-run covariance exists, it is

Here A maps the nuisance influence into the moment coordinates. This is an algebraic
consequence of a supplied expansion, not a proof that an arbitrary learner has one. Overlapping
twelve-month outcomes can introduce dependence across monthly origins. Cross-outcome and
denominator covariance must also survive aggregation. A label saying “dependent monthly
origins” does not establish that the supplied matrix includes these contributions.
  An exact Gaussian example makes the possible omission concrete. Let

                      Xi = θ − 2η0 + Ui ,          ηb = η0 + V ,     θb = X + 2ηb,

stipulated Gaussian law, the variance-nine interval has exact coverage 2Φ(2) − 1 ≈ 0.95450.
The variance-one interval’s coverage is instead 2Φ(2/3) − 1 ≈ 0.49501. These are analytic
probabilities under a known law, not estimates of empirical performance. The example is
intentionally nonorthogonal and independent; it does not settle the dependent or arbitrary-
learner problem (Causal banking research project, 2026i).
   Orthogonal scores, suitable sample splitting or an explicit joint influence-function construc-
tion are substantive alternatives. Each needs its own assumptions and remainder control. With
dependence, a nominal split of adjacent months may retain information leakage and correlation.
A proposal should specify which learner, split rule, dependence class and variance construction
a minimal prototype will actually support. It should then compare that restricted path with a
matched simpler baseline and retain the regimes in which the argument or precision fails.

be read with that construction and its supplied-covariance qualification.


43.13.4      Useful precision is a property of the decision

Consider an explicitly assumed annual funding scenario. A baseline average balance of USD
2.6 million is repriced by 0.25 percentage points, costing USD 6,500. Incremental retained
funds earn a 1.5% annual spread net of their own offered deposit interest. The incremental
average balance is 0.25β million USD. With an illustrative workflow allowance of USD 500,
net profit is

        Π(β) = 106 (0.25β)(0.015) − 2.6 · 106 (0.0025) − 500 = 3750β − 7000 USD.              (43.2)

The average-balance convention is necessary for this annual spread calculation. A different
repricing base, within-year balance path, liquidity cost or net spread changes the function and
should be represented explicitly.
  The scenario allowance assigns USD 120 to data and identity preparation, 150 to integration
amortization, 100 to scientific review, 30 to computation and 100 to monitoring and recovery.
43.13. From a funding response to a defensible treasury decision                                  463


These are planning assumptions. Actual human adjudication, optional model calls, platform
review, implementation, security, deployment and continuing operations may exceed them.
Failed requests and retries belong in the workflow denominator. The allowance cannot be
presented as an observed bank price.
   The break-even response is β = 28/15. A point estimate β = 2 gives profit USD 500.
Mapping the two intervals from the fitted-nuisance example through the increasing function in
(43.2) gives

               Π([1.9, 2.1]) = [125, 875],      Π([1.7, 2.3]) = [−625, 1625]   USD.

The first interval excludes a loss under the stated cost scenario; the second does not. This is
the practical importance of the missing variance component. It neither demonstrates bank
profit nor makes every interval decision-ready. The identification, unit map and covariance
premises must also be justified. Uncertainty about costs can be propagated by taking the
financial image over their declared scenario set as well.
  For the weak-denominator rays, a finite favorable point estimate is especially misleading.
Under the same monotone profit map their image is

                                  (−∞, −10750] ∪ [−3250, ∞).

Neither a finite lower bound nor a narrow range is available. Increasing the number of
observations need not resolve a structurally weak or invalid normalization. Possible responses
include changing the target, seeking a better justified design or reporting sensitivity. Choosing
a favorable representative point does not resolve the information problem.


43.13.5     What the local library and CLI actually demonstrated

The bounded exercise specified 29 authored cases, each invoked through the library and CLI
initially and after re-instantiation or process restart. Two further calls changed the horizon
under a previously used key. The resulting 118 service slots all matched their fixed expectations
after two disclosed harness repairs. The original harness first omitted a standard library import
and later referred to a nonexistent copied fixture identifier. The first failure preceded any
service call; the second occurred after 116 completed slots. Both failures and the unchanged
116-result prefix were preserved, and the corrections were recorded before the affected calls.
This is evidence from an amended execution, not evidence that the original executable ran
without repair (Causal banking research project, 2026j).
   Of the 118 responses, 48 were computed outputs, 40 were failed or unavailable input results,
eight refused contradicted premises, twenty reported unsupported operations and two rejected
changed-horizon reuse. The computed outputs include diagnostics, deterministic sensitivity,
unbounded and empty sets. They must not be counted as 48 useful causal estimates. All
29 library/CLI/restart comparisons agreed on complete semantic responses, excluding only
the request identifier. Independent decimal root calculations and 451 direct rational-grid
membership checks agreed with the retained sets. This finite screen does not estimate statistical
coverage or a population failure probability.
   The feature-clock case retained four failures: availability at the decision, a missing availability
field, availability before the event, and timestamps without time zones. The valid row passed.
Changing units or the availability field after binding a moment artifact caused a context
failure, and corrupting the artifact bytes caused an access failure. Continuous-treatment
and dependent-unit back-door requests, identity/inclusion audits, nuisance fitting and design
evaluation remained unsupported in the selected paths.
464                                                            Causal analysis for a universal bank


   Most consequentially, summaries with explicitly unresolved household identity or unknown
inclusion still returned conditional intervals. Contradicted premises caused refusal, but an
unverified premise was not automatically treated as a contradiction. The service also retained a
declared dependent sampling label without verifying an upstream long-run covariance estimator.
These observed boundaries mean the proposed consumer needs an explicit prerequisite review
before presenting a financial recommendation. Passing schema validation, a hash check or a
clock audit is insufficient.
   The measured sum of invocation times was approximately 56.46 seconds, including failed,
replayed and rejected service requests and their worker or CLI startup. This is a local
measurement of the stated exercise. The initial failed harness startup was not timed, and
the measure excludes authoring, repairs, review, manuscript work and idle intervals. Process
high-water memory is not simultaneous memory for an entire process tree. These measurements
therefore cannot establish complete bank workflow cost or production throughput. No new MCP
transport qualification, foreign-language adapter, live model or actual workspace consumer
was exercised.


43.13.6     A minimal next prototype with an informative stopping rule

The next prototype should first restrict the scientific claim. One useful design jointly generates
dependent monthly funding histories, known households, observed and missing follow-up, and
a specified nuisance estimator. It can compare covariance methods under the same generated
law, keeping the household truth and future outcomes outside the analysis inputs. Useful
outputs are all-attempt coverage where justified, set topology, availability, width relative to the
financial threshold, erroneous action rates and complete resource categories. A matched simple
estimator supplies a baseline; a flexible learner must justify its extra cost and assumptions.
   This experiment needs a reviewed derivation and prospectively fixed regimes, replications,
criteria and stopping rule. The present finite conformance screen cannot supply those perfor-
mance results. Public funding panels can inform plausible scales, release delays and institutional
continuity. Generated truth supplies controlled interventions and unit maps that the public
observations may lack. Neither source should be credited with information that it does not
contain.
   A contract double for a treasury consumer can separately test whether absent identity,
inclusion, covariance or decision-cost evidence causes the intended hold disposition. Such a
double demonstrates a proposed consumer boundary; it is not an accepted sibling-repository
workflow. An owner-run bank study becomes informative after a bounded prototype identifies
a consequential remaining uncertainty, an attainable precision target and plausible value from
resolving it. This preserves a practical path from proposal to evidence while retaining the
distinction between a computed response set and a defensible funding decision.
Chapter 44

Data organization, execution and
reusable interfaces

The mathematical operations of Chapter 39 share infrastructure, but not every fitted model or
sampling argument. Their common construction starts with reproducible decision histories,
then separates the scientific plan from its physical execution. A standalone application and an
embedded library should submit the same request and receive the same result. Otherwise an
analysis can change meaning when moved from a research notebook into a bank workflow.


44.1      Constructing a history from economic and information
          time
Represent an event revision by e = (k, j, v, te , ta , x, u, z): stable event key k, entity j, revision
v, economic time te , availability time ta , value x, unit u and void marker z. A decision has a
stable key and time τ . Under an explicitly chosen inclusive availability convention, its known
revision of event k is
                                 v ∗ (k, τ ) = max{v : ta (k, v) ≤ τ }.
If the source has a different revision order, that order must replace the numerical maximum.
For a lookback ℓ, a monetary feature is
                                     X
                   Xj (τ ) =                       xk,v∗ 1{τ − ℓ < te,k,v∗ ≤ τ, zk,v∗ = 0}.     (44.1)
                               k:entity(k)=j
                               v ∗ (k,τ ) exists

Revision selection precedes economic-window filtering. If a later correction moves an event
beyond τ , filtering time first would resurrect an obsolete revision. Likewise a late-arriving past
event belongs to a retrospective accounting view but may be absent from the history available
to the historical policy.
   The feature computation needs a source-completeness declaration. Zero observed transac-
tions can mean a complete feed with no activity, an unconnected account or a failed batch.
Only the first supports a zero activity value under the stated feed contract. Missingness
indicators, known outages and event-count denominators should survive construction. Treating
each absent row as zero would silently replace the observation operator in Chapter 11.
   A bank may have several decision clocks: quote, approval, acceptance, settlement and
account posting. Features available at approval need not have been available at quotation. A
timestamp equality may also conceal unknown within-batch ordering. The initial convention


                                                          465
466                                                           Causal analysis for a universal bank


can reject such ambiguity or use a documented cutoff; it should not invent millisecond order.
Period-end stocks, period sums and period averages need separate aggregation definitions, as
the aliasing calculations demonstrated.
   Entity linkage introduces another layer. Legal customer, household, account, facility, branch
and corporate group are distinct units. A household action can affect several accounts; a branch
rollout induces shared assignment. Crosswalks need effective and availability dates. When
entity membership is uncertain, the product should preserve the linkage hypothesis or weighted
alternatives needed by the declared analysis. A hard merge changes both potential outcomes
and the independent sampling units. The total-variance decomposition in Section 11.5 shows
why exporting one identifier without its uncertainty can understate error.


44.2     What automatic organization can and cannot infer
Automatic profiling can propose event keys, candidate clocks, repeated decisions, missingness
patterns, currencies, ownership crosswalks and aggregation rules. It can compare the proposal
with physical data, report violations and display the rows that justify a mapping. An analyst
then supplies the economic semantics: which field is the action, when the bank knew a
value, what the outcome means, and which changes were possible. This produces a reusable
observation specification rather than an unexplained cleaned table.
  The proposal process should use competing hypotheses when evidence is ambiguous. For
example, a table with several rows per customer-month may contain revisions, different
products, or repeated actions. Deduplicating it under the first hypothesis can delete genuine
decisions under the third. The system can rank the hypotheses by key consistency and source
metadata, but causal conclusions require the selected interpretation. A useful user view shows
the consequences: population size, affected histories, assignment timing and target units under
each mapping.
   Schema tools, columnar engines, feature stores and catalogs provide parts of this workflow
(duckdb contributors, 2026b; pola-rs contributors, 2026; unionai-oss contributors, 2026; feast-
dev contributors, 2026; datahub-project contributors, 2026; open-metadata contributors, 2026;
moj-analytical-services contributors, 2026). Their source-specific limitations were established
in Section 17.7. The common product should preserve the bank’s existing asset identifiers and
attach the causal observation semantics. It should avoid maintaining a competing catalog or
treating catalog lineage as a discovered economic graph.
   The output is a versioned trajectory or panel view with an explicit loss-of-information
declaration. For example, a monthly snapshot may discard within-month action order. That
view is suitable for a model assuming one monthly decision, but cannot support a finer
sequential intervention merely by adding a lag column. The original event references must
remain recoverable so an alternative clock can be reconstructed.


44.3     A scientific plan and a physical plan
The scientific plan fixes the target, model restrictions, observation view, identification expres-
sion, estimator, inference construction, statistical split and numerical tolerances. The physical
plan chooses data partitions, workers, memory limits, caching and reduction order. Changes to
the latter are permitted only when they preserve the former. This is the execution counterpart
of Equation (39.2).
  Each materialized object should identify its inputs and semantic version. A result refers to
44.4. The algebra that can be distributed                                                     467


the frozen scientific plan, data snapshot, qualified backend revision, random seeds, numerical
diagnostics and source lineage. An input correction creates a new result lineage; it does not
rewrite the earlier answer. Deterministic content hashes are useful identities, but they do not
establish that two differently serialized scientific models are equivalent. Canonicalization rules
need their own specification.
   For cross-fitting, a fold is a function of the permitted sampling unit, assigned before
scheduling. A household remains in the same fold when its account rows move between
workers. Multiway or blocked-time designs need their own split objects. Hyperparameter
selection, feature screening and representation learning must follow the same training/evaluation
boundary as the nuisance model. Storing only a model checkpoint while losing its training
population makes later leakage review impossible.
   Retries need contribution identities. A task can be retried without adding its score twice if
the reducer commits at most one completed artifact for each tuple of analysis, fold, partition
and attempt lineage. This is an engineering idempotency requirement; a mathematical sum
alone does not supply it. Partial failure should leave a resumable plan and an incomplete
result, not a silently smaller study.


44.4      The algebra that can be distributed
For precomputed vector scores ψi ∈ Rd , a partition can return counts, sums and derivative
sums:                                  X              X

Their sums reconstruct the global moment and Jacobian. For a cluster covariance, it must

yields Uc = i∈c ψi . Outer products Uc Uc′ are formed after that regrouping. Their order is
              P

essential, as the counterexample in Section 17.8 shows.
   When the contribution is an uncentered influence-value candidate Di for a mean ψ, retain
Sc = i∈c Di and nc . The centered cluster sum is Sc − nc ψ,
      P                                                     b with ψb = P Sc / P nc . Centering
                                                                          c      c
each partition by its own mean destroys this identity. For entity/date clustering, retain sums
for entities, dates and observed intersections. The inclusion–exclusion covariance can be
indefinite in a finite sample; silently projecting it to a positive matrix changes the reported
estimator. A qualified remedy requires an explicit rule and justification.
   Different estimators require different reductions. Linear IV/GMM can accumulate moment
cross-products, but nonlinear GMM may require repeated passes and candidate-specific
moments. A weak-IV inversion evaluates a test over parameter values; replacing it by one
inverse Hessian changes the inference method. An empirical quantile, a survival curve and a
regularized inverse problem do not generally reduce to the same score mean. The operation
catalogue must advertise its actual sufficient computational outputs.
  For C observed clusters and score dimension d, keyed sum storage is O(Cd) before matrix
construction, and outer products cost O(Cd2 ). Dense storage for E entities by D dates uses
O(EDd) even when few intersections occur. A sparse implementation can reduce storage to
the observed intersections, but its hash/sort costs and data skew must be measured. Streaming
over rows is not a guarantee of bounded memory as the number of statistical groups grows.
468                                                           Causal analysis for a universal bank


44.5     State-space and discovery workloads scale differently
For N independent trajectories, horizon T and K hidden states, dense forward/backward
evaluation costs O(N T K 2 ) per likelihood pass. An EM iteration can distribute trajectories
and combine expected transition/emission counts under a common parameter vector. Mixing
counts from different parameter iterations breaks the EM objective and its ascent argument.
Online or asynchronous updates are different algorithms and need their own convergence
conditions.
   Within a single trajectory, messages have a chronological dependency. Unnormalized
transition/emission matrices can be composed associatively, so a parallel prefix construction
is possible, but dense matrix products cost O(K 3 ) instead of the O(K 2 ) vector update and
require careful scaling. It is a performance tradeoff, not free parallelism. Smoothing requires
corresponding backward information. For continuous states, particle count, state dimension,
degeneracy and resampling communication can dominate costs; likelihood error must be
assessed in the downstream parameter or policy units.
   A learned structural model also has repeated optimizer, posterior or regularization loops.
Reporting only the speed of one filter pass omits much of its cost. The relevant workload
includes initialization, multiple starts, rank diagnostics, parameter uncertainty and policy
evaluation. The approximation should be named: sparse transition, low-rank factor, variational
family, particle distribution or finite state truncation. Each may change a scientific model or
numerical error.
  For p observed series and maximum lag L, even storing candidate lagged pairs requires
order p2 L objects. Conditional-independence searches add conditioning-set complexity; dense
matrix-exponential acyclicity constraints have another scaling profile. Screening or hierarchical
grouping can make the workload feasible, but may remove an adjustment path or a weak
confounder. Any screening restriction therefore belongs in the discovery model or its recovery
argument. Changing to monthly frequency is an observation change, not merely a compute
optimization.
   The initial deployment should support local columnar execution for bounded workloads,
then qualified distribution where the algebra allows it. Ray is a potential scheduling component
(ray-project contributors, 2026); it does not provide the cluster or mixing assumptions. GPU
acceleration is most plausible for dense numerical kernels and learned nuisance models. Sorting
temporal revisions, irregular groups and small exact identification problems can have different
bottlenecks. A hardware choice should follow a measured workload and error tolerance.


44.6     One core library and three standalone workspaces
The standalone product should offer three initial workspaces sharing the same request and
evidence objects.
   The intervention study workspace starts with a population and a proposed or historical
decision. It constructs an encouragement, adjusted effect or rollout analysis; shows overlap,
timing and comparison groups; and produces effects in outcome and financial units. A reviewer
can inspect which assumptions distinguish receipt from invitation and which aggregation
defines the reported business effect.
   The sequential decision workspace reconstructs customer histories, compares observed-
history policies and controlled-state explanations, and displays feasible actions, support and
value uncertainty. It includes policy alternatives and the cost account. An attractive latent
policy cannot bypass its logger and identification review.
44.7. Interfaces for neighboring financial applications                                       469


  The dynamic systems workspace combines panel and macro time series, observation-frequency
analysis, structural-shock alternatives and discovery. It compares graph/model classes and
their implied response sets. A user can see why finer data, a new instrument or an experiment
would change the conclusion.
   In each workspace the primary view should answer the user’s decision: what action is
compared, for whom, over which horizon, at what expected value and with which unresolved
assumptions. Technical traces, scores and solver logs remain available to researchers and
validators without becoming mandatory steps for every business reader. An embedded client
uses the same operations through a library or job service and can render its own application-
specific view.

44.8      Construction sequence and measurable acceptance
The first construction stage implements immutable observation views, scientific requests,
identification traces and bounded result types. It needs exact positive and negative fixtures
before a general interface is advertised. Stage two qualifies adjusted/encouragement/cohort
methods and finite-horizon observed-history values against independent numerical references,
including their cluster and policy-specific scores.
   Stage three connects controlled-state fitting and discovery to the same scientific objects. It
starts with finite models, supported graph classes and explicit unresolved outputs. Latent
causal identification, proxy stability, uncertainty propagation and structural choice remain
visible subtasks. They belong in the initial research architecture, even where their numerical
qualification takes longer than ordinary adjustment.
   Stage four measures the complete workflow and tests reuse in the three workspaces. For
a fixed scientific request, measure data reconstruction, nuisance/latent fitting, inference,
sensitivity, review and report production separately. Record wall time, peak memory, pro-
cessor/accelerator use, retries, spill volume and numerical disagreement against the qualified
reference. Throughput without the required diagnostics is a different output and an invalid
economic comparison.
   Acceptance should require successful replay, deliberate failure behavior, target-preserving
adapter tests and appropriate repeated-sample checks. Performance targets must be attached
to a workload: number of entities, decisions, variables, lags, clusters and latent states, rather
than a single bank-wide row count. Availability, access control, locality and operational
recovery are deployment requirements to be specified with a particular bank; the proposed
scientific core does not establish their implementation.
   This sequence permits a useful independent product and shared library without assuming
that all host applications use the same causal model. Its central reusable asset is the preserved
scientific meaning of an analysis, supported by qualified computation and a traceable financial
decision.


44.9      Computational scale follows the statistical construction
Ten million precomputed scores say little about the cost of fitting a latent decision model. A
scientific workload must retain the dimensions that make its inference difficult. For responses
these include dates, horizons and covariance coordinates; for controlled states, the number
of states, trajectory length, validation sample and complete refits; for discovery, variables,
44.9. Computational scale follows the statistical construction                               471


lag window and conditioning-set search. The expanded measurements therefore execute the
operations developed in the preceding chapters.

44.9.2    Deriving the execution choices

For N independent trajectories, H decisions and K finite states, one forward/backward pass
with dense transitions costs O(N HK 2 ). With A actions and M signal categories, the parameter
count is
                 p = (K − 1) + K(M − 1) + K(A − 1) + AK(K − 1) + AK.
The current reference retains adjacent-state posterior arrays, requiring O(N HK 2 ) memory
as well as forward/backward arrays. Batching whole trajectories can reduce that memory
because their likelihoods and scores add at a common parameter. It cannot replace the shared
parameter by independently optimized shard parameters. Finite-differencing an analytic score
for information adds 2p score evaluations and an O(p3 ) dense factorization. Extra starts and
B full refits multiply the fitting cost; the elapsed-time table includes only its stated B = 3
cost experiment.
   Independent trajectories and independent bootstrap fits are natural parallel units. For a
fixed parameter, deterministic reductions can combine batch log likelihoods, gradients and
information, with roundoff checked against the serial reference. Distributed optimization
additionally needs synchronized parameters and a stopping rule on the global score. Emission
validation terms must enter exactly once, with their original sample weight; duplicating them
on every worker changes the likelihood and understates calibration uncertainty. A trajectory
cannot be cut into independent fragments without transferring the correct filtering distribution
and its parameter sensitivities across the boundary.
   For a response vector with d coordinates, direct dense Bartlett covariance cost is O(nLd2 )
and storage includes the n × d scores. Prefiltering adds a d-variable regression and recolouring
solves. A date partition needs the original lagged observations, future outcome horizons
and score-lag cross-products that straddle its boundaries. Halo records supply context; only
owned origins contribute to the target sum. Center with the global mean and retain the
cross-boundary terms. Dropping them for faster reduction changes the covariance. Customer
shards under common shocks must combine their scores by calendar date before a time-series
covariance is formed.
   Conditional-independence search has a different obstacle. With v variables and lag window
L, each node can have    order vL candidate parents. Testing all conditioning sets of size s
involves up to vL
                   
                 s   sets per candidate relation before pruning; a dense partial-regression
calculation also depends on sample size and s. Actual parent selection can remove much
of this work, explaining why two samples with the same dimensions need different time. A
search cap is an algorithmic restriction that can remove oracle completeness, not a purely
physical optimization. Parallel tests must preserve stage dependencies and orientation rules.
Distributed throughput cannot be inferred by multiplying the one-thread table by the host’s
256 logical CPUs.
   The resulting architecture uses whole-customer batches for history and controlled fits,
date-aware reductions for common-shock responses, and explicit stage scheduling for discovery.
Every physical plan must reproduce the declared serial target and numerical tolerance before
claiming a speed benefit. The measured references identify dominant costs and feasible parallel
units. Large distributed storage, fault recovery, accelerator qualification and institutional
workload service levels remain concrete construction tasks rather than conclusions of these
local measurements.
44.10. Partition the experiment without changing its information                              473


44.10      Partition the experiment without changing its informa-
           tion
A serial reference is especially useful when calibration, nuisance fitting and dependent inference
interact. In the dynamic funding construction, workers first accumulate independent audit
successes and counts by stratum. The pilot fitting pass accumulates X ′ X, X ′ Y , response sums
and squared sums on the same fixed training half. Validation losses use the same candidate
penalties and pilot holdout. After choosing the penalty, a second pilot pass forms the full
normal equations. The evaluation pass accumulates the candidate score numerators and
denominators by stratum. No evaluation outcome chooses the learner or covariance bandwidth.
  Let ψ̂t be the stacked candidate-response influence, and let ψ̄ be its global mean. For lag k,
partition the later index t:

                           Γ̂k = T −1                  (ψ̂t − ψ̄)(ψ̂t−k − ψ̄)′ .
                                        X    X

                                        b t∈Ib , t>k

Each partition receives a left halo of at most L dates, so cross-boundary products occur once.
Computing a covariance inside each partition and then averaging would omit those products
and could center different experiments. The resulting Bartlett matrix, inverse-linkage Jacobian,
audit covariance and financial weights are applied in the same order as the serial derivation.
Partition counts are not independent-cluster counts.
   Eighteen fresh-process runs compare one, two and four workers at 720, 5,760 and 23,040
evaluation origins, with four times as many pilot origins, 48 branches, seven horizons, two
candidate portfolios and two audit strata. Each worker’s numerical libraries are limited to one
observed thread. The measured workflow includes synthetic source generation, revision-aware
materialization, calibration, pilot selection/fitting, response fitting, covariance and financial
result construction. The direct reference comparison, consumer formatting, semantic checks
and receipt serialization are excluded from the reported workflow time. All serial/partitioned
financial and covariance outputs agree with the separate reference to below 5 × 10−10 in the
recorded absolute comparisons. Floating-point reduction order can change last bits; it cannot
change the data splits or the number of independent dates.
   Mean times over two fresh processes are about .195/.282/.367 seconds at 720 origins and
4.818/5.038/5.024 seconds at 23,040 origins, in one/two/four-worker order. The largest parent
process peaks around 474 MiB; this whole-process peak also includes the untimed reference
comparisons and semantic checks, rather than isolating the timed workflow’s memory. Child
peak-RSS counters are also retained, but are process-accounting maxima, not a measured
simultaneous sum across hosts or workers. Parallel execution is slower here: process and
transfer overhead dominate this small fixed basis. The evidence supports serial execution as
the default for these dimensions. It does not support a claim of distributed speedup.
   The partition construction nevertheless qualifies a harder boundary than reducing precom-
puted independent scores: audit uncertainty, pilot model selection, complete nuisance fits and
chronological covariance remain in one experiment. It is still a single-host, in-memory reference.
At scale, the source materialization and sufficient-statistic passes can be streamed, but network
transfer, object storage, fault recovery and concurrent study load remain unmeasured. Longer
POMDP histories and graph search have different dominant costs and cannot inherit this
timing result. Capacity planning must combine these measured dimensions with the earlier
latent and discovery workload profiles.
