44.11      Streamed reconstruction and restartable score account-
           ing
A physical execution plan must preserve the statistical experiment after interruption. The
selected calendar source is a sorted retrospective feed: predecision controls arrive by their
decision date, outcomes correspond to the declared horizon, and realized outcomes arrive by a
fixed extraction cutoff. Streaming materialization validates these clocks and exactly one record
per origin, writes numeric columns to a temporary memory-mapped array, checks the complete
source identity, then commits the completed array. Incomplete output is not advertised as a
valid observation view. The dense reference parses the same feed and must produce identical
columns.
   The nuisance learner may still copy those columns into its fitting matrices. Streaming the
source is therefore not a claim of a general out-of-core Lasso. Where the estimator admits
sufficient-statistic passes, the score computation can stream without changing inference. For
scalar scores st , first obtain the global mean s̄. A second pass accumulates
                      X                                  X
               P0 =       (st − s̄)2 ,   Pk =                            (st − s̄)(st−k − s̄),
                      t                         t: t,t−k in same block
                                                             PL
                                            b = P0 + 2          k=1 (1 − k/(L + 1))Pk
                                            Ω                                                .
                                                                          n
Each partition carries its immutable bytes, fold, chronological offset and contribution identity.
A halo of at most L prior scores supplies boundary lag products within the same block. It
resets between blocks, so no artificial lag pair bridges a deleted temporal gap.
   The checkpoint binds data and procedure identities, completed contribution prefixes, count,
global sum, lag products and halo. Atomic rename commits a coherent state; a content
checksum detects corruption of that state. Retrying a committed contribution verifies its
source and skips its numerical update. A changed source, changed bandwidth, overlapping
contribution or reordered manifest is rejected. The design is an exactly-once contribution
calculation on one host, not a claim about a distributed transactional service.
  Failure injection covers interruptions after committed moment and lag passes, interruptions
before rename, duplicate retry attempts, corrupted checkpoints, changed inputs and changed
procedures. Recovered results agree with a separately computed dense Bartlett reference to
10−12 . Source fixtures reject late features, wrong horizons, duplicate origins and outcomes
beyond the cutoff. These checks substantiate the local recovery mechanism. Network partitions,
concurrent writers and remote object-store semantics require their own platform experiment.
   The complete local comparison includes reading, fitting, uncertainty, both consumers and
serialization in fresh processes. It matches direct expert composition to the shared operations
under the same unit, provenance and inference obligations, asserting identical public output
bytes. Separate workloads vary pair counts, learner dates, audited nonlinear trajectories and
finite Gaussian episodes; peak memory and source/output/checkpoint bytes are recorded
alongside elapsed time. First JIT compilation is included in the nonlinear interval, while
imports and generation of the synthetic source are outside it. These boundaries matter more
than a favorable isolated kernel time.
   Local wrappers show computational parity for the shared scientific kernels; restartable
score persistence adds work and does not establish a speedup. The recommendation is a
serial local reference with optional checkpointing when recoverability matters. A real multi-
host comparison must retain identical samples, outputs and numerical tolerances, introduce
storage/network faults, and measure concurrent complete requests. Analyst time, adoption
and business value require repeated matched tasks by independent users, rather than an
44.11. Streamed reconstruction and restartable score accounting   475


extrapolation from this author’s implementation effort.
Chapter 45

Banking studies as tests of the
scientific construction

The preceding design becomes concrete when the same analysis is followed from its intervention
to its financial account. This chapter uses published banking designs to explain which
information is useful, and reproducible synthetic studies to test selected estimators and
interfaces. The simulated populations and cash schedules are deliberately specified. None is
data from JPMorgan Chase, Bank of America, HSBC or another institution.


45.1     What banking evidence can transfer
Published estimates arrive with an institutional design and population. In Drechsler et al.
(2017, printed pp.2–4), the deposits-channel argument uses within-bank branch comparisons
across local market concentrations. Bank-specific lending opportunities are controlled through
the comparison; the interpretation relies on a bank being able to transfer funding across its
branches. The subsequent lending analysis compares banks within a county and uses their
deposit-market exposure. Those are different aggregation levels and identifying comparisons.
The design supports a mechanism linking market power, deposit pricing and transmission, not
an effect for any new household retention offer.
   Relationship banking adds endogenous selection. The mover design in Basten and Juelsrud
(2026, Section 4.2.1, equations (6)–(8)) instruments an existing deposit relationship with the
bank’s market share in the household’s former municipality, while controlling current share
in the new location. It investigates stickiness and persistent preferences. The exclusion that
prior market availability affects later borrowing through the relationship remains substantive;
the mover population also limits transfer. This is a useful banking connection to Chapter 2,
not a universally valid instrument recipe.
   For credit supply, the preserved 2006 version of Mian and Khwaja (2006, Section III.B,
equation (5)) compares lenders to the same firm after differencing. Firm effects remove
common borrower-demand shocks. The paper explicitly discusses the multiple-bank population,
anticipated adjustments and bank-specific demand components that might remain correlated
with funding shocks. A same-borrower comparison is therefore much stronger than a pooled
lending regression, while still requiring a defensible residual supply variation.
   The HARP design of Agarwal et al. (2020, printed pp.2–3) compares program exposure
for similar agency and non-agency high-LTV mortgages. It distinguishes selected refinancing
outcomes from program-level differences including take-up. The product lesson is to retain
eligibility, assignment, application, acceptance and closing separately, and evaluate the original

                                               476
45.2. A deposit rollout with a complete contribution account                                  477


eligible population. A borrower cash-flow gain is not automatically a gain to the bank that
owns or services the old mortgage.
   Finally, Beraja et al. (2019, printed pp.112–113) explains why regional refinancing differences
do not identify common aggregate responses: those responses were differenced out. Its model
adds collateral and lender-income channels. Benetton (2021, pp.5–6) combines discrete-
continuous mortgage demand with multiproduct lender pricing, using capital requirements
as cost shifters under additional exclusions. These sources motivate a structural extension
interface when the bank asks about competitor responses or market-wide regulation. A local
causal estimate may discipline that model but does not determine its entire equilibrium
counterfactual.

The collections model has three observed states: current, moderate arrears and severe arrears.
An assistance action is unavailable in the current state. For no assistance and assistance,

The initial state distribution is (.6, .3, .1), and historical assistance probabilities are (0, .35, .60).

independent trajectories. The estimator uses half-count smoothing on supported transition
cells. The policies give no extra assistance, assist only severe arrears, or assist every eligible
state. Backward dynamic programming computes the reference values from the generating
kernels, which are unavailable to fitting.

they occurred, would remain in the denominator.

   Strong instruments have innovation loading one; the weak case has loading .06. The reference
system has spectral radius .81; the near-unit case uses .985. Persistent instrument noise has

   Several method decisions follow. Joint covariance matters because a pointwise interval is
not a curve guarantee. Yet a consistent HAC estimator can still underestimate finite-sample
uncertainty: the Gaussian-maximum band covers only .886 and .876 in the two persistent strong-
instrument experiments, and .724 near the unit boundary. Bonferroni is more conservative,
but its .818 near-unit coverage also fails the preset adequacy threshold. These failures prohibit
482                                                          Causal analysis for a universal bank


presenting the default bandwidth as automatically calibrated for persistent bank series. The
statistical result remains asymptotic under a fixed stability margin, not uniform near a unit
root.
   The proxy VAR has much smaller mean squared error in the correctly specified finite-order
generating law. That advantage is a consequence of its propagation restriction. It does not
establish that an economist should replace direct moments when finite-order dynamics are
misspecified. Weak normalization makes the direct and proxy mean squared errors about
752 and 13.5; 96.4% of runs yield an unbounded residual-test set in at least one coordinate.
A narrow decision recommendation would conceal the information deficiency. Instrument
invalidity defeats both routes, including zero proxy-VAR coverage in this example.
   A separately specified follow-up, with a new random seed, compares bandwidth L = ⌊n1/4 ⌋
and 4L at 5,000 origins. Their whole-curve coverages are .948 and .968, with mean widths
.312 and .338. This new experiment does not replace the original .926 finding or establish
that 4L is universally preferable. The selected workflow reports sensitivity to the lag window,
compares the structural challenger when justified and withholds a calibrated finite-sample
claim in regimes that fail the stated qualification. Picking the more favorable seed or interval
after observing the answer would be a different, unqualified procedure.
   The integrated experiment has one common random-walk trend and two stationary spreads.
Mapping stationary-change IV estimates to cumulative level responses gives whole-curve
coverage .966 and mean squared error .0479. Treating the levels as stationary gives .586
coverage and error 55.66. Cointegration is substantive here: it defines which components are
stationary and which intervention response is being summed. The comparison does not certify
unknown rank selection or arbitrary local-to-unit triangular arrays.
   With 4,000 dates and 80 bounded controls, separated-block sparse IV gives .942 coverage of
the scalar effect 1.2, compared with .950 for oracle nuisances. A three-factor reduction and an
unadjusted estimator both have zero coverage, with mean squared errors about .058 versus
.00102 for sparse adjustment. The causal confounder is sparse in this generator and need not
align with its leading covariance components. Factor compression requires an information-
preservation argument, not only a prediction score. The fixed penalty multiplier in this
experiment establishes feasibility; the required population nuisance rates remain assumptions
to justify in each application.
   For a fixed 96-bank panel, the additional mean-score experiment separates common and
bank-specific Gaussian AR components. At 800 dates, row-iid intervals cover in .116 of runs;
date-aggregate HAC covers in .856; an oracle using the exact finite-sample Gaussian variance
covers in .938. At 2,000 dates the corresponding values are .104, .890 and .946. Correctly
recognizing the date as the information unit removes a gross variance error, but the short
Bartlett lag window still underestimates persistent uncertainty. More customer rows do not
repair either problem.

   For the response workload, bank deviations are centered across banks so that the fixed
weighted aggregate equals the common structural series. Raw data contain an initial publication,
an eligible correction and a future revision. The SQL operation restricts availability before
selecting the highest eligible version, then aggregates to dates. It is checked against the
separately retained generating series, and the fitted curve against its direct numerical reference.
Maximum discrepancies are below 10−9 at every scale. The largest case reconstructs 3,849,216
versioned records for 256 banks and 5,012 dates, then fits direct and proxy responses, joint
covariance, residual-test sets and a bandwidth comparison. It is one common-shock analysis;
the record count does not create millions of independent macroeconomic shocks.
   The learned-control workload reconstructs a wide versioned table and fits both separated-
block sparse adjustment and the factor challenger, retaining their errors and covariance. The
large case has 12,000 dates and 200 controls. The temporal graph workload fits 12 variables
at 4,000 dates and propagates the joint coefficient box through 13 horizons. Its timing does
not establish uniform high-dimensional graph coverage; the inferential reference remains the
declared fixed-dimensional structural class. Exponential DAG enumeration and the 25-DAG
Gaussian reference are different workloads.
   The latent workload reconstructs complete customer trajectories, fits the unknown-emission
model with multiple starts, computes observed-information value uncertainty and refits every
bootstrap sample. The larger case has 3,200 customers and 12 decisions. Its model fit and
information calculation cost only a small fraction of the 19-refit workflow. Nineteen bootstrap
draws are suitable for demonstrating cost scaling, not precise 95% interval endpoints. The
separate 79-refit fixed-policy example and repeated-sampling study address different inferential
questions. All caps, boundary and optimizer diagnostics remain in the receipts, including
intermediate EM caps followed by likelihood refinement.
   These results change the engineering priority. For short response curves, data reconstruc-
tion and process overhead can dominate the numerical moment calculation. For controlled
likelihoods, repeated fitting dominates. Caching immutable views helps the first workload;
efficient likelihood scores, warm initial proposals checked against independent starts and
parallel independent bootstrap fits can help the second. Each proposed acceleration must
retain the same target and numerical tolerance. No bank-level labor saving follows from these
CPU timings: the expert composition comparator can use the same engines and estimators.

45.8      The implemented data and score components
Two small local components implement selected parts of Chapter 44. The temporal component
constructs Equation (44.1) under its declared inclusive availability convention. In an adversarial
fixture, the correct early and later amounts are 160 and 90. Using the latest retrospective
values gives 90 at the early decision; filtering economic time before choosing the revision
gives 110 at the later decision. Delayed data, voids and a moved economic date explain the
differences.
   The component rejects duplicate event revisions, incompatible currencies, unqualified feed
completeness and naive timestamps. Reconstruction review also added explicit rejection of
empty or non-string event/decision identities. Without it, a missing decision entity could
return a misleading zero. This is a per-decision semantic reference, not a bank-scale temporal
query engine.
   The score reducer retains raw sums/counts for entities, dates and their intersections, centers
globally and computes the stated crossed covariance. Independent batch calculations agree to
numerical precision for both unique and repeated entity/date cells. Partition merges preserve
the result. Invalid multidimensional cluster keys now fail before changing accumulator state.
The caller still owns the target weighting, Jacobian, training split and dependence argument;
duplicate-task protection remains part of the proposed execution layer.

is not ten million fitted causal analyses or evidence of distributed end-to-end bank performance.
   The combined evidence establishes several useful construction tests: incorrect cash accounts
can reverse a business conclusion, current-only weights can answer the wrong dynamic question,
omitted private logging can reverse a policy estimate, and row counts can conceal shared shocks.
The additional constructions above qualify local study recipes and selected package operations.
Complete product workspaces, institutional validation and accepted sibling adoption remain
distinct engineering and review tasks.


45.9      A public household-finance analysis with unknown causal
          truth
Public data expose choices that a known-truth simulation cannot. The archived 401(k)
application extract contains 9,915 observations from the SIPP 1991 design used in the DML
literature (Chernozhukov et al., 2018; DMLonGitHub application-data repository, 2026, Section
6.2). The outcome is net financial assets; eligibility and participation are separate binary
variables. The declared controls are age, income, education, family size, marriage, two-earner
status, defined-benefit pension status, IRA participation and home ownership. All required
45.10. Public monetary histories and the boundary of an empirical claim                           485


fields are observed in the retrieved extract, so no row is removed by the declared missingness
rule. The dollar values are those in the archive, without an inflation conversion.
   The first question is the average effect of eligibility on assets under conditional exchangeability
given these controls. This is an identifying assumption about employer/program selection
and saving behavior, not a consequence of fitting a flexible model. The second question is
participation’s complier effect with eligibility as an instrument. It adds exclusion, instrument
independence and monotonicity. The ratio of the adjusted eligibility effect on assets to
its adjusted effect on participation yields that target under those restrictions. Ordinary
participation regression would answer neither question without a different selection argument.
The graph and observation choices must also establish which controls are appropriate pre-
exposure covariates; the cross-sectional extract alone cannot verify their timing or rule out
unmeasured saving preference.
   Two nuisance families are compared: standardized quadratic features with ridge outcome
regression and logistic propensity regression, and histogram gradient boosting for both roles.
Three folds and seeds 7101–7103 are fixed in advance. The original paper’s 100-split aggregation
and learner collection are not replicated numerically; this reproduces the design and score with
declared alternative learners. The matched DoubleML check isolates score agreement from
those learner differences.

                 Nuisance family        Seed Eligibility ATE Participation LATE
                 Quadratic ridge/logit 7101              8,223               11,905
                                       7102              8,391               12,089
                                       7103              8,932               12,935
                 Histogram boosting    7101              7,968               11,398
                                       7102              8,502               12,261
                                       7103              8,299               11,879

These estimates use archived dollars, with the LATE interpreted per complier under its
additional assumptions. For the first quadratic run, the eligibility 95% interval is approximately
[5, 737, 10, 710]; for the first boosting run it is [5, 683, 10, 253]. First-stage estimates range
from .691 to .699. The three quadratic fits each clip one propensity; the boosting fits clip
none. The largest realized inverse-action weight ranges from about 32 to 47. Small clipping
counts do not prove adequate population overlap. The raw eligibility mean difference is about
19,559, substantially larger than the adjusted estimates, but that comparison does not reveal
the unknown causal truth.
   The reported covariance uses an iid household working law. The extract does not supply
survey weights, strata or primary sampling units. Consequently these intervals are a repro-
ducible working analysis, not a design-valid survey inference claim. Alternative control timing,
employer selection, survey design and weak support require sensitivity or additional data. The
result does not transfer automatically to a bank offer, a different country or current wealth.
The useful product behavior is to preserve the eligibility/participation target distinction,
identical matched-reference inputs, overlap diagnostics, empirical uncertainty and unverified
design assumptions through the final result.


45.10       Public monetary histories and the boundary of an em-
            pirical claim
The archived statsmodels macroeconomic extract contains 203 quarterly observations from
1959Q1 through 2009Q3, assembled from FRED and labor statistics with source access dated
486                                                            Causal analysis for a universal bank


15 December 2009 (statsmodels dataset contributors, 2026). It includes an end-quarter M1
stock, a quarterly average of monthly three-month Treasury-bill rates, output and inflation. Its
data, source notes and exact numerical implementation are preserved. This is a real dynamic
financial-data analysis with a known historical snapshot; it is not a current bank deposit-offer
dataset.
   The fixed projection response is 100(log M 1t+h − log M 1t−1 ) per percentage-point change in
the quarterly-average bill rate. Two lags each of the rate change, money growth, output growth
and inflation enter every regression. Four specifications are fixed before fitting: these lagged
controls; adding current output growth and inflation; a pre-1984 origin window; and a post-1984
origin window. Horizons zero through four use common origins within each specification.
Bartlett lag four covariance is computed from the complete OLS influence, including controls.
An independent statsmodels OLS/HAC call agrees in coefficient and covariance to below
3 × 10−14 .
   At horizon four, the full-sample lag-control estimate is −2.102 percentage points of cumulative
money growth, standard error .452. Adding current output/inflation gives −2.163 (.453). The
pre-1984 estimate is −.997 (.262), while the later window gives −4.329 (.685). There are 196
common full-sample origins and 97/99 in the two windows. The different windows define
different projection populations; selecting one after observing its significance would add a
selection problem. Their contrast is a registered sensitivity analysis, not proof of a known
break date or a homogeneous policy effect.
   These numbers do not identify a bank’s price intervention. A quarterly average rate and
end-quarter stock do not supply a within-quarter decision clock; central-bank information
and money demand can confound the innovation; M1 is not one bank’s retained deposits;
structural and measurement regimes can change over fifty years. Current output controls may
be post-policy variables under one causal ordering and predecision information under another.
The data alone cannot settle that ordering. The inference reported is conditional projection
uncertainty, not uncertainty over all these causal interpretations.
   The public-data investigation also inspects the Federal Reserve H.8 description (Board of
Governors of the Federal Reserve System, 2026). Its aggregate bank balance-sheet statistics are
useful for surveillance, but do not reveal customer offers, the private assignment information,
first-available entity-linked histories and representative audited matches required by the
treasury brief. Neither that feed nor the archived macro series identifies the stipulated bank
experiment. Obtaining a current bank-specific price/offer history and its assignment evidence
is therefore a genuine empirical requirement, rather than an excuse to call any public time
series causal.
   The central known-truth evidence uses the realistic but explicitly synthetic funding mech-
anism, common shocks and revision/linkage construction. At 360 and 1,440 dates, 400
repetitions give financial interval coverage .945 and .9375; pretending the branches supply
independent calendar information gives .230 and .2175. The corresponding joint Bonfer-
roni response coverage is .9425 and .965. Binomial Monte Carlo error is approximately one
percentage point for coverage near .95 at 400 repetitions; these differences do not certify
exact nominal calibration. The pair-linkage and audited-servicing experiments add separate
observation and information failures. Taken together, the public analysis challenges economic
interpretation, while the synthetic analysis checks statistical behavior when its assumptions
are known. Neither estimates a named banking group’s causal benefit.
Chapter 46

Reliability when identities, calendars
and models are uncertain

A deposit intervention can affect many customers on the same date, while one customer’s
uncertain identity persists across dates. These are two different sources of repeated information.
Auditing the same identity every month does not produce independent identity evidence, and
adding customers on one calendar does not remove uncertainty about a common funding shock.
The scientific question is therefore not simply whether a database has enough rows. It is which
independent dimensions inform the intervention target, what information the audits buy, and
whether the resulting interval is precise enough to support the decision. This chapter develops
selected extensions with those distinctions intact. Its new arguments are project derivations;
its known-truth examples are synthetic. They do not establish a generally validated bank
product.


46.1     Persistent identity audits on a shared calendar
Consider N independently sampled persistent customer pairs observed on T common dates.
Let Ait ∈ {−1, 1} be a randomized signed action, with two candidate outcomes Yi0t , Yi1t .
Randomization, the outcome model and the fixed outcome units identify a response moment
Uit = Ait Yi,focal,t . This identification premise is separate from the identity-audit calculation.
For example, if Y = (θi + Ct )A + e with E[Ae] = 0, the moment averages the customer response
and common shock; multiplying it by a declared monetary scale gives currency per signed
action. An observational bank action cannot inherit this interpretation merely by satisfying
the input shape.
   Write Vikt = Ait Yikt and Hit = (Vi0t + Vi1t )/2. A persistent audit Ri has known conditional
inclusion probability qi , bounded below by a positive constant. The accurate binary identity
Mi = 1 selects candidate zero. If Uit is revealed by the audit, the augmented moment is

46.1.1    A selected joint limit, rather than an arbitrary cluster rule

Let the corrected score have the representation Zit = h(Wi , Ct , Eit ). The persistent attributes

bounds sufficient for the calendar central limit and the residual covariance sums below; for
instance k αC (k)δ/(2+δ) < ∞ with a suitable uniform envelope. Define θ = EZit and the

substituting for a sampling theorem.

consistency here also needs the new score’s joint sampling conditions. Sufficient selected
rates include L → ∞ and L2 / min(N, T ) → 0, with summable covariance tails and moment
bounds. Pair and calendar estimates can both contain interaction noise. Its population order is
1/(N T ), so retaining both is compatible with the leading limit; it is not an exact finite-sample
conservative confidence guarantee. Truncated serial covariance and other finite-sample errors
can still cause undercoverage.

Let M independently sampled gold labels estimate ϵ by the observed error fraction ϵ̂. Gold
truth must be accurately adjudicated and representative of the same symmetric flip law.

With ϵ bounded away from one half, and M comparable to N, T , a Taylor expansion adds

result. This is neither a bound for arbitrary label contamination nor semantic proof that the
recorded customer is the economic unit of interest.


46.2      What audit spending can and cannot buy
Suppose a complete pair supplies an audit correction difference D. Conditional on the
complete history, the audit-randomization variance is (q −1 − 1)D2 . For strata with population
proportions πs , per-audit relative costs cs > 0 and second moments ds = E[D2 | s], minimizing
                                        P
this contribution at expected budget s πs cs qs = B gives the Lagrangian first-order condition
                                                                       q
                  −ds /qs2 + λcs = 0,         qs = min{1, max{qmin , κ ds /cs }}.

The objective is convex for positive qs , so the clipped rule with a budget multiplier solves the
stated finite-stratum objective. An independent fully audited pilot estimates ds and freezes
the allocation before evaluation. It does not certify the unknown population optimum, and it
must not use the final coverage outcomes to choose the design.
   In the synthetic two-stratum example, costs are 1 and 3 relative units, proportions are one
half and budget is .6 per pair. The independent pilot has 4,000 fully audited pairs, costing
7,936 relative audit units under its realized strata. Conditioning on the supplied symmetric
error probability .15, it produces inclusions .2282 and .3239, against uniform inclusion .3 at
the same expected budget. Final evaluation uses new histories and independent gold labels.
The gold sample has 1,200 labels per request; its adjudication price and the history-acquisition
cost are additional, unmeasured economic inputs. They are not assigned a zero price.
   The realized mean audit costs are 144.50 and 144.76 per 240-pair evaluation for uniform and
pilot allocation, respectively. Their expected costs are matched by design, not forced to match
every random audit count. Mean joint standard errors are 204.9 and 203.8 currency units, a
small change which does not by itself justify the pilot’s expense. The optimization theorem
concerns an audit variance component; it does not guarantee an attractive whole-program
return.

   A common-calendar floor survives even perfect identity information. Under the declared
AR calendar with marginal standard deviation .8 and persistence .65, the asymptotic calendar
variance is .82 (1 + .65)/((1 − .65)T ). At T = 180 and monetary scale 1, 000, its nominal 95%
halfwidth is about 253.75. Halfwidth targets of 100 or 200 therefore cannot be attained by
purchasing more pair audits alone. A target of 400 clears this calendar floor, but still has pair
and validation uncertainty. Changing the calendar, the target or a scientifically justified model
is a different experiment; the audit optimizer cannot make this limitation vanish.


46.3      Calibrating the dynamic funding inverse
The earlier deposit construction transforms two candidate responses in each stratum into
sum/difference primitives m and covariance Vb . With correctness probabilities p0 , p1 , the
financial response before direct price cost is c(p)⊤ m, where
                                                                         ⊤
                                                 1               1
                                     
                                         1               1
                            c(p) =       2 , 2(2p − 1) , 2 , 2(2p − 1)        .
                                                 0               1

The primitives are half-sums and half-differences of the horizon-weighted candidate responses.
This factor matters for both currency units and variance. Independent binomial audits
contribute the delta variance through js = −m2s+1 /(2ps − 1)2 and ps (1 − ps )/ns . More audits
stabilize this inverse when its rank is separated from zero; they do not repair a truncated
calendar covariance estimate or a wrong outcome model. The weak-rank confidence-set
alternatives remain available separately.
   Fresh original-design replications retain 720 dates, 2,880 independent pilot dates, 200 audits
per stratum and correctness probabilities .95, .8. Two larger designs have 1,200 or 4,800 dates, a
1,600-date pilot, 1,600 audits per stratum and probabilities .9, .85. These changes alter several
information dimensions, so a favorable larger-design result is not a unique diagnosis of the
historical undercoverage. Within each design, prespecified Bartlett windows with multipliers
2, 5, 10 are compared on the same fresh samples.
   Known-audit arms remove calibration uncertainty only for diagnosis. A separate 1,000-draw
synthetic training sample estimates the primitive response covariance for each design, including
independently retrained nuisance fits. Its estimated covariance is frozen before final evaluation.
A Student multiplier acknowledges finite reference training but is not an exact theorem
for these non-Gaussian estimated responses. These arms can expose a variance-estimation
contribution; they are not deployable oracle procedures and do not retroactively qualify the
earlier intervals. Finite coverage, bias, precision and the remaining inverse assumptions must
be assessed together.
   The fresh original-design interval covers 468/500 = .936; the 1,200-date design covers
474/500 = .948, whereas the 4,800-date design covers only 459/500 = .918. Its pilot remains
at 1,600 dates. Larger windows do not consistently improve these arms. The independently
trained covariance raises the corresponding frequencies to .954, .968, .930, but still leaves
the largest design short of nominal coverage. Its empirical response standard deviation is
about 71, 401 currency units, versus mean default standard error 64, 424, with positive mean
error about 11, 718. Known-audit comparisons likewise retain a shortfall. Thus audit-count
uncertainty is not the sole observed limitation. Finite-pilot and calendar-variance contributions
need separate further investigation; these comparisons do not uniquely identify their causes or
supply a generally calibrated replacement.
46.4. Sharper confidence in a finite latent information class                                     491


46.4      Sharper confidence in a finite latent information class
Suppose independent Gaussian episodes have ordered variables (Z, A, Y ). The information
class is supplied scientifically. Under observed sufficiency, the coefficient of A in E[Y | Z, A] is
the causal target throughout the declared finite class. Gaussian linear regression with intercept
gives an exact conditional tn−3 interval when the design has rank three. This uses causal
invariance across the class, rather than selecting a graph and then ignoring its uncertainty. A
broad latent observational class still supports every real effect through the earlier same-law
witness. More precise computation cannot remove that lack of information.
  Under valid randomized encouragement and exclusion, the true null effect θ makes Y − θA
have zero Z regression slope. Its Gaussian reduced-form error is independent of Z even when
the treatment residual is confounded with outcome error. The exact null-test approach is the
Gaussian specialization of the weak-IV principle discussed by Staiger and Stock (1994); no
lower bound on the first-stage coefficient is needed.
  Center all three variables and write k = Z ⊤ Z, a = Z ⊤ A/k, y = Z ⊤ Y /k. Let eA = A − aZ,
eY = Y − yZ and Suv = e⊤  u ev . Inverting the two-sided null test gives


                                  2
                                      t2n−2,1−α/2
                         (y − θa) ≤                 (SY Y − 2θSAY + θ2 SAA ).                   (46.5)
                                       (n − 2)k

To verify the pivot, regress Y − θA on (1, Z): its slope is y − θa, residual sum of squares is the
expression in parentheses, and residual degrees of freedom are n − 2. At the true null, normal
slope and independent scaled residual variance give the Student distribution. Membership of
the true effect therefore has probability 1 − α, including at zero first-stage rank. The confidence
set can nevertheless be practically uninformative.
   Equation (46.5) is a quadratic sublevel set. A positive leading coefficient gives the interval
between real roots; a negative one can give two rays; absent roots give the empty or whole-
line answer according to sign. Linear and constant cases must also survive. Stable root
formulas, extended-precision discriminants and outward endpoint rounding reduce numerical
error without providing a complete floating-point certificate. These are new prespecified
confidence procedures, not intersections with the earlier 95% covariance rectangle. Intersecting
independent-looking 95% answers would require its own simultaneous confidence argument.
   In 2,000 fresh strong-encouragement episodes, the new set is bounded throughout, with
median width .2079 in outcome units per action and coverage .9525. Weak encouragement
often yields whole-line or disconnected sets, while exact zero first stage does not invalidate
true-null coverage. Supplied sufficiency has coverage .954 in its valid law. False exclusion has
zero encouragement-set coverage, and falsely supplied sufficiency under hidden confounding
likewise fails. An exact statistical pivot cannot make an incorrect causal restriction true.
General PAG confidence and dependent histories remain distinct problems.

The extension supplies an explicitly identified model capability, not an empirically proven
superiority. Adding an omitted nonlinear transition term causes all 120 fits in each arm to
become unqualified. Retaining unavailable outcomes is more informative than computing
coverage only among favorable fits. General nonlinear state models, uniform boundaries and
global policy optimization remain open.


46.6      A richer dependent learner that fits in chunks
The partial-linear IV score retains the Robinson form of Chernozhukov et al. (2018), with
nuisance conditional means (ℓ, r, m):

                      ψt (θ) = (Zt − m(Xt )){Yt − ℓ(Xt ) − θ(Dt − r(Xt ))}.

The source’s iid inference theorem is not a theorem for an arbitrary temporal learner. Here the
dictionary is fixed as (1, X, X0 X1 ), observations are bounded and geometrically mixing, the
population Gram and IV slope are separated from singularity, and all three nuisance means
lie in the dictionary. Fixed-dimensional OLS then has root-sample error under these selected
46.7. What the comparisons establish for a bank                                              493


conditions. Orthogonality leaves a product error of order n−1 ; a growing temporal gap makes
training and evaluation coupling negligible, and a slowly growing Bartlett window with the
corresponding score-error rate supplies the covariance argument.
   Two held-out blocks are separated by gap 100. Each trains on the other; windows and
feature availability are checked before fitting. The whole declared origin is the sampling unit.
Inference globally centers retained scores and computes lag products within each evaluation
block. Concatenating separated blocks and forming lags across their missing calendar gap
would create nonexistent adjacent observations. The declared population mixing rate is
supplied, not estimated from a successful fit.
   For chunked fitting, form each block of the augmented matrix [Xdict , Y, D, Z] and take
its QR factor. Stack the small retained R with the next augmented block and repeat QR.
Orthogonal transformations preserve the least-squares objective; the final leading RXX and
target columns solve the same three nuisance problems as dense least squares. Predictions
use the identical fixed dictionary, folds and envelope clipping. Rank loss is refused. This
construction avoids the full expanded fitting matrix; it still retains input storage and O(n)
residuals/scores. It does not make arbitrary adaptive dictionaries or learners safe to fit out of
core.
   Fresh synthetic laws add the previously omitted interaction to outcome and instrument
conditional means. The old linear dictionary has zero coverage in 300 draws. The richer QR
and independent dense SVD routes agree to floating-point tolerance and remove that large
bias, yet their original-window coverage is only 271/300 = .9033. A separately registered larger
16,000-date design reaches 282/300 = .94 with both the original and a longer window; its Monte
Carlo interval is [.9068, .9641]. Equal coverage counts do not show that the longer window is
unnecessary in general. A further omitted quadratic term gives zero richer- dictionary coverage.
Representation, numerical algebra and calibrated uncertainty are separate achievements.

46.8     Evidence required before institutional use
Independent scientific review must reconstruct the target, assumptions, identification, un-
certainty and limitations, including negative comparisons. Authentic bank validation then
needs assignment and source-clock owners, representative independent audit truth, known
selection probabilities, a frozen question and held-out evidence. An unknown-truth bank study
cannot simply reproduce synthetic truth-coverage counts. It needs assignment diagnostics,
placebos, audit sensitivity and financial reconciliation appropriate to its design, together with
a decision-relevant precision requirement.
  Application acceptance requires consumer maintainers to preserve qualifications, unbound-
ed/disconnected sets and refusals under their actual interfaces. Workflow economics require
matched complete analyst tasks and quality, active labor, rework, audits and infrastructure
46.8. Evidence required before institutional use                                          495


costs. Multi-host qualification requires the target platform and declared fault/recovery and
service objectives. Local serialization, mapped-input fitting and restart checks do not supply
these external observations. The investment argument therefore continues with bounded
scientific capabilities and explicit dependencies, rather than an assumption that completing
the author program has completed adoption.

A distinct practical procedure estimates the prespecified fixed regression jointly on the eval-

equation. Its argument does not authorize selecting an adaptive dictionary from evaluation
outcomes and then treating that dictionary as fixed.

47.4     What the fresh comparisons support
The first fresh comparison uses 600 requests in each of seven laws. Its joint-regression horizon
interval covers 550/600 at 720 dates, with Monte Carlo interval [.8916, .9375]. This is a retained
calibration failure. At 1200 and 4800 dates coverage is .935 and .94; the persistent ρ = .96
case gives .9467. Changing the covariance does not remove all finite-regression error. In the

is about .953, but all-request coverage is .202. Reporting only the conditional fraction would
hide the information shortfall. Omitting the quadratic action-mean term gives .2633 coverage;
correlating the action innovation with the structural disturbance gives zero. These are false
scientific declarations that a numerical API cannot detect.
   The exact pilot calculation suggests another route: retain an independent pilot but let
M = 4T . This satisfies the selected sufficient rate and avoids claiming that the small joint-
regression failure has been repaired. A separately frozen fresh study compares the inherited
pilot, a fourfold pilot with Bartlett covariance and a fourfold pilot with horizon covariance.
For the latter, the fitted score converges in mean square to the true-nuisance score, so each of
its fixed-H lag moments converges to the moment in (47.4). The vanishing pilot remainder
supplies the required centering at the desired target. An imperfect pilot held fixed need not
have zero score covariance beyond H; the growing-pilot argument is asymptotic. The last
procedure has coverage .9600, .9417 and .9333 across the three designs in Table 47.3. Each
Monte Carlo interval includes .95, but the largest point estimate remains below nominal. Its
mean SE is 64,431 compared with empirical SD 65,867. Relative to the same-draw inherited
baseline, the coverage changes are 4/600, 0/600 and 1/600; descriptive paired Monte Carlo
intervals include zero. Clear superiority is not established.
   At 720 dates the old pilot was already fourfold; only covariance differs. The 1200/4800
designs require three/twelve times the inherited pilot history. Mean fit-and-inference time for
the horizon route is about 1.35/1.57 times the baseline in those two cases, excluding acquisition.
Thus a justified information rate has a real requirement even where nominal calibration is
statistically compatible. The independent pilot must also represent the same economic law. A
long history drawn from a different assignment regime does not satisfy that requirement.

47.6      From a qualified request to an institutional decision
The public request names the procedure, financial target, covariance rule, audit counts and
scientific declarations. Its identity binds evaluation and pilot bytes as well as those choices.
Two local consumer examples preserve the status, qualifications, monetary units and interval
through serialization. Unavailable results withhold monetary estimates and intervals rather
than becoming a confident zero. Interrupted unfinished fits can be retried from immutable
inputs; no partial-fit checkpoint or distributed recovery is implied.
   Independent review must reconstruct the nuisance-bias and filtration arguments and chal-
lenge the retained small-sample failure. Bank validation requires authentic assignment, source-
clock and audit evidence, an independently invariant pilot when that route is used, and a
decision-relevant precision target. Consumer maintainers must accept the real interface; plat-
form operators must measure complete workloads under intended storage and faults. Workflow
evaluation must price pilot/audit acquisition, active labor and rework at matched output
quality. These are additional observations, not consequences of an author having obtained a
passing calculation or a useful local memory ratio.
Chapter 48

Pilot information, calibration
precision and complete streaming
inference

The funding desk’s question remains the value of a one-month price intervention over a
fixed balance-response horizon. Chapter 47 shows why a fixed imperfect pilot can move the
target of a residual regression. Increasing pilot information and reducing working memory
address different obstacles. More independent history can reduce nuisance error, but does not
create identity truth or remove finite-sample covariance error. Streaming makes a specified
calculation feasible with less working storage, but leaves its statistical assumptions intact.
This chapter gives an equivalent streaming construction and compares fixed procedures with
enough repetitions to resolve larger calibration shortfalls. The banking consequences include
the extra history required, the financial width retained, and the cases in which inference
remains unavailable.


48.1      Preserving the pilot’s learning objective
Let a pilot independent of evaluation supply M dates, the six-column design X of the
preceding chapter and the K = 1 + 2(H + 1) targets Z: the action followed by the two
candidate response curves. The design contains the intercept, driver, centered driver square
and their stratum interactions. Divide the dates chronologically into m1 = ⌊M/2⌋ training
dates and m2 = M − m1 validation dates. For each prespecified penalty λ the original pilot

Orthogonality yields, for every coefficient matrix B,

Rows removed in a thin factorization contribute zero because all columns of [Xb Zb ] lie in its

standardized loss without storing all predictions. Stacking the two factors gives the full-pilot
refit. These are exact real-arithmetic identities, independent of the stochastic dependence
within a pilot half.
   Training variances are accumulated from centered block moments. If two blocks have sizes

componentwise. This avoids cancellation from subtracting two large raw second moments.

   Floating-point equivalence additionally requires a stable problem. If each computed valida-
tion loss is within ϵ of its exact value, a unique minimum separated by more than 2ϵ has the
same selected penalty. This implication is an algebraic diagnostic, not a global error certificate
for every input. The reference exposes all validation losses and their gap; identical repeated
penalties retain the first occurrence. Near ties, ill conditioning and arbitrary high-dimensional
learners require further numerical or statistical qualification. In the selected independent dense
comparisons, coefficients, loss ordering, financial results and both covariance choices agree
within the reported numerical tolerance, including chunks of one row and boundaries shorter
than the response horizon.

information cannot be obtained merely by repartitioning the same shorter history.

48.4      Information and adoption boundaries
The extra pilot must be independent of evaluation under an invariant relevant law. A bank
cannot replace that condition with arbitrary historical volume; regime changes or overlapping
histories require a different separation and influence argument. Likewise, more nuisance history
cannot create representative identity truth. Near-singular audit information can still require
refusal, and false scientific declarations can yield precise but invalid financial answers. Earlier
omitted-feature and endogenous-map counterexamples remain relevant.
   The selected implementation supplies a bounded scientific operation. It does not identify a
general nonlinear private-state model, retain the true class in arbitrary latent-graph discovery,
or establish rates for an arbitrary learner. Independent review, authentic bank assignment and
source clocks, audit truth, target storage and concurrency, adopted interfaces and measured
analyst costs remain distinct inputs to product qualification. These distinctions determine
which evidence the funding desk can act on and which claims still need testing.
Chapter 49

Weak-audit projection for funding
value

      The V10 funding interval refuses inference when a representative identity audit cannot
      distinguish two candidate portfolio assignments. This supplement tests a different reporting
      design: simultaneous bands for the four observable candidate monetary responses, exact
      binomial audit intervals, and projection through the assignment inverse without dividing
      by a nearly zero estimated rank. In 3,000 fresh paired synthetic requests, the resulting
      set has high all-request coverage but markedly worse financial precision. At the near-rank
      design, 546 of 600 sets equal the whole real line. Exact audit inversion does not make the
      response bands finite-sample exact, verify causal exogeneity, or provide a bank decision
      threshold. The frozen V10 monograph is unchanged; this is an author-reviewed research
      supplement, not an implemented product.

   In the false-exogeneity design, regular coverage was 122/600 and projection coverage was
591/600. The latter had median width about USD 1.367 million, roughly 2.4 times the regular
width. This high selected-law coverage does not validate the false declaration. The method
has no causal guarantee there; a different violation magnitude or economic threshold can
expose the bias. No method was chosen after observing this cell, and no universal correction is
established.


49.4      Decision meaning, alternatives and remaining obligations
Projection can trade noncoverage or refusal for width. That trade is not automatically useful.
A funding decision based on the sign of V would need the entire defensible set on one side
of the bank’s specified decision threshold. A whole-line set can never meet that rule. Even
the baseline median set width exceeds the synthetic target value (about USD 375,000) by
more than a factor of three. The exercise does not provide a bank threshold, the price of
representative audit labels, or the cost and availability of independent pilot history. Width
conditional on a finite set cannot substitute for all-request coverage and finite-set availability.
   The inherited regular inverse is tighter in selected cases but can refuse near rank and
undercovers under some finite designs. A sharper transformed average/difference confidence
region or candidate-specific covariance inversion is a substantive alternative; it would need its
own simultaneous dependent-score argument and numerical qualification. More representative
audit labels can shrink Ps but cannot cure a false origin-swap or exogeneity premise. New
outcome-linked information may identify targets that counts and candidate responses cannot.
These are prospective designs, not results of this supplement.
   The next scientific D09 step is a newly derived, prespecified precision improvement with fresh
independent evaluation, retaining small-audit, near-rank, persistence and false-law challenges.
D07/D08/D10 still require named platform and bank owners, authentic histories and audit
truth, independent review, a bank precision threshold, prices, fault/service evidence and signed
acceptance. The completed local experiment does not establish a deployed service, adopted
interface or measured institutional savings.


Evidence and source scope
The registered plan, pre-execution challenge, code, fixed specification, 3,000-row journal, exact
reconstruction, independent numerical receipt, generated table and source-role audit are all in
this repository under docs/program/, docs/studies/, docs/reviews/, src/causalbank/,
and tools/. The source audit binds the exact primary PDF copies and inspected anchors for the
two inherited technical roles below. The projection formula, bounded-memory implementation
and fresh synthetic findings are project work; neither cited source is represented as proving
them. Literature cutoff for this program is 7 October 2026.

Joint candidate information and
calibration limits

      The first weak-audit supplement retained rank ambiguity but produced broad funding-value
      sets. This follow-up uses shared information in the two observed candidate responses,
      forming average and difference scores before covariance estimation. A repaired 3,600-request
      study finds narrower transformed sets in all 2,937 paired finite cases of six selected designs,
      without a general dominance theorem. Weak audit information remains the limiting factor:
      558/600 near-rank outputs are whole-line; even with eight times as many audit labels,
      105/600 are whole-line and the finite transformed median width is about USD 15.4 million.
      A pathwise observational-equivalence construction shows that false exogeneity cannot be
      solved by interval algebra alone. This is an author-reviewed research follow-up, not a
      bank-calibrated product.

   The first supplement constructed four separate bands for the candidate responses. Those

are the observable influence scores, the new scores are (ϕbs1 ± ϕbs2 )/2. Their marginal variances
therefore include the candidate cross-covariance. Four two-sided normal bands share response

the orthogonal-score/rate premise in its own iid setting, not this project’s dependent result
Chernozhukov et al. (2018). The inspected Newey–West 1986 working paper supports a

score Newey and West (1986). Exactness applies only to the binomial audit component.

variance at most (8ϵmachine )2 times its positive average-score variance. That last guard prevents

50.2      Registration, preserved failure and fresh comparison
The original set’s large widths motivated this separate plan, which was registered before the
follow-up’s final draws. Its first 3,600 requests are retained as exploratory and not qualified.
An adversarial fixture with identical candidate outcomes exposed an inadequate zero-variance
guard: the fitted difference-score variance was numerically positive, roughly 2 × 10−33 of the
average-score variance. The initial check had exercised an exactly zero accumulator but failed
to require refusal for this fitted fixture. The complete initial code, specification, check receipt,
journal and summary were archived and read back before repair. The scale-aware guard and a
strengthened refusal check were registered before a new 3,600-draw comparison with a fresh
seed. The initial results were not promoted or quietly hash-replaced.
   The qualified comparison holds each evaluation history, 4,800-date independent pilot and
audit counts fixed across two methods: the candidate-response rectangle and the transformed
average/difference rectangle. Five 1,200-date stress laws are inherited; a sixth keeps the near-
rank law but uses 12,800 instead of 1,600 representative audit labels per stratum. All have 600
fresh requests, no early stopping, the same fourfold pilot training and the same error allocation.
Numerical checks compare transformed slopes and lag covariance with an independent dense
four-coordinate calculation; its maximum scaled variance difference was 1.65 × 10−15 . Whole-
line, disconnected and empty rank-one geometry, the repaired degenerate fixture and a pathwise
causal counterexample were checked separately. A read-only journal reconstruction verifies all
3,600 request identities, both primitive bands, audit intervals, financial sets, coverage counts
and paired finite widths.

50.3      Why exogeneity is an information problem
The failure is not merely an interval formula. Let m(Wt ) = .5Wt +.2(Wt2 −1), At = m(Wt )+et ,
and let g(Wt ) be an otherwise unknown baseline balance response. Consider the structural law
                                                             p
                    Bt = ρBt−1 + βAt + g(Wt ) + σ{cet +          1 − c2 zt } + ξt ,          (50.2)

with independent centered et , zt , ξt before the displayed shared term. Define a second law with
independent structural error but
                                                                                      p
β ′ = β +σc,     g ′ (W ) = g(W )−σc m(W ),        Bt′ = ρBt−1
                                                            ′
                                                                +β ′ At +g ′ (Wt )+σ 1 − c2 zt +ξt .

Because At − m(Wt ) = et , the two observed balance recursions are identical path by path
for the same initial balance and exogenous draws. The candidate swaps, independent audit
labels and any statistic of the observed histories are therefore identical as well. Yet under a
one-month intervention on At , the first law has response βρh and the second (β + σc)ρh . At
the registered false-law values σ = 2, c = .5, their one-unit response coefficients differ by 1 and
the fixed financial target differs by about USD 387,575. A direct coupled numerical witness
reproduced identical observed paths to floating precision.
     This is an identification counterexample for a class permitting the adjusted nuisance mean
g ′ . An externally known g, randomized action variation, valid instrument or other justified
scientific restriction could separate the laws. More audit labels about candidate identity or a
narrower confidence box alone cannot. Numeric declarations of exogeneity are assertions to be
validated by assignment and source owners, not tests performed by the API.


50.4      Decision and delivery boundaries
The transformed region is a locally reproducible way to use covariance that the first box
omitted. It does not close D09’s useful-precision gap: whole-line sets and multi-million-dollar
finite widths remain under weak audit rank, even in the higher-audit cell. The observational
514                                                          Causal analysis for a universal bank


counterexample isolates a separate D04/D09 limit that requires new causal information. Any
next statistical refinement must be derived, preregistered and tested on fresh adverse laws,
reporting all-request coverage and finite decision precision.
   The bank has not supplied an acceptable value-width threshold, representative history/audit
prices, authentic assignment truth, independent reviewers, target-platform service evidence
or an adopted interface. The frozen V10 monograph and first supplement retain their own
identities. This follow-up is appended to a single reader PDF for convenience; that assembly
is not a claim of independent scientific approval or production readiness.

Linked outcome audits for a
dependent funding decision

      Correctness counts can leave an individual funding response unidentified when two can-
      didate histories mix equally. An audit that resolves the actual focal history supplies a
      different observation. We derive a sampled-outcome score for the existing continuous-action,
      common-calendar funding target, including its additional audit variance and independent
      nuisance pilot. A registered 4,800-request comparison finds finite intervals in every linked-
      outcome request. At exact identity rank one, the augmented method has median width
      about USD 527,000, while the count-based set is whole-line in all 600 requests. Its coverage
      there is 559/600, so finite availability is not general calibration. False exogeneity, incorrect
      inclusion probabilities and noisy truth labels produce severe failures. The result identifies
      useful new information to seek from a bank; its authenticity, price and acceptable decision
      precision remain external requirements.

51.6     A design calculation before buying labels
For a constant, truthful q, write K = E[c2t {w′ (Ft − Bt )}2 ] and let ΩF be the latent focal

When K > 0 and L ≥ ΩF , this gives q ≥ K/(L − ΩF + K); if L < ΩF , even complete audit
cannot meet the width target at that calendar size. If K = 0, audits add no variance in this
specific moment, but the caller still needs a valid information law. This algebra is a planning
approximation, not a finite-sample coverage certificate. Values of K and ΩF used for a new
design must come from an independent design pilot and include their estimation uncertainty.
   For the registered M = 4T pilot, expected linked-label demand is q(T + M ) = 5qT . An
economic comparison also needs history acquisition, truthful resolution, pilot fitting, complete
evaluation and review costs. Count labels and linked histories are different services; 1,500

Evidence, scope and continuation
Independent enumeration checks the audit expectation and added diagonal variance. Dense
fitting and direct lag products agree with the implementation across chunk boundaries to about
1.9 × 10−14 relative error. Complete audits reduce to observed focal histories; unsampled labels,
invalid probabilities and degenerate variance are rejected. The first 600 raw requests were
preserved as unqualified after an interval-serialization mismatch stopped summary generation.
The shared-format repair and round-trip check preceded a fresh registered seed; none of those
first requests is part of the 4,800 final comparison. The saved journal reconstructs every
summary and interval; eight fixed requests were separately regenerated. These are author
checks, not an independent scientific review.
   The local advance concerns D01/D09’s additional-information route. Exact-rank finite
availability is demonstrated in this selected funding law; bank calibration and useful decision
precision are unqualified. D04’s assignment, inclusion and label truth remain indispensable,
and D05’s arbitrary persistent identity/calendar composition is not covered by independent

   The frozen monograph and two prior supplements retain their identities. This new standalone

Information, uncertainty and
executable limits

      A causal banking service must return a decision quantity together with the information and
      uncertainty that make it defensible. This extension connects funding response, sequential
      servicing, temporal graph effects and audited observations. A funding experiment uses
      supplied action randomization and independent calendars to remove a fitted-ratio mean
      shift. A nonlinear servicing extension evaluates a fixed observable policy using truthful
      state audits and supplied action probabilities. Both meet a preregistered minimum-
      coverage screen on selected synthetic grids with conservative 99% critical values. A joint
      pair/calendar/gold-label experiment still fails finite calibration in important regimes. A
      corrected temporal graph union retains effects but can return the whole real line. A
      corrected sparse learner fails qualification at higher dimension or support. Full linked-
      outcome streaming agrees with its dense reference and survives real local process failures,
      without a consistent measured performance gain. These are author-reviewed research
      findings; independent review, bank truth, operating acceptance and economics remain
      separate gates.


52.1      One decision, several kinds of evidence
A bank deciding whether to raise a deposit rate, change a collections policy or act on a
discovered relationship needs a target with units and timing. It also needs an observation
model: a row may not identify the customer whose balance matters; a public signal may omit
the private state used by a historical decision maker; an apparent edge may permit several
intervention effects. Computation cannot supply missing identity, assignment or exclusion
information.
   The standard is a connected argument from the banking target and information clock
through causal modeling, identification or an identified set, estimation, uncertainty, sensitivity,
numerical error and monetary consequence. The FinMarketing comparison motivates that
depth; its length is not a target. The preserved 259-page reader develops the inherited
foundations. This extension adds new evidence without rewriting predecessors or treating file
checks as scientific acceptance.
  Four gates remain separate: author completion, capability qualification in a declared law,
authentic bank acceptance, and investment/adoption. A well-supported negative investigation
can complete author work. A conservative set can be statistically defensible and too wide to
support a decision.
  Every table cell has 512 fresh Monte Carlo requests. Covers uses all requests, including

refusals. MC lower is a simultaneous one-sided exact-binomial 95% lower bound, Bonferroni-
adjusted over all method/cell comparisons in the study. The minimum screen is .95. These
screens do not prove uniform coverage or validate supplied scientific assumptions. Primary
methods use frozen 99% critical values or covariance regions; some challengers use 95% critical
values. Width and coverage have a disclosed tradeoff.

52.3     Persistent maps, common dates and imperfect gold truth

52.3.1    One joint sampling law

After multiplying outcomes by randomized signed actions, let focal and companion responses
be
                    Fit = β + Ui + Ct + Eit ,  Dit = δ + Vi + Ct + Jit .
Pair effects are iid across pairs; Ct is an independent stationary Gaussian AR(1); cell dis-
turbances are independent. Candidate order persists within a pair. A Bernoulli pair audit
Ri has known q, and its label independently flips with probability e < 1/2. An independent
representative sample of M gold labels estimates e. This is a specific experiment, not arbitrary
multiway dependence.
   Let ξi = 1 for a correct audit label and −1 for a flipped label. At the true e, Wi =
Ri ξi /[q(1 − 2e)] has mean one and second moment a = 1/[q(1 − 2e)2 ]. For d = (β − δ)/2, the
corrected score has decomposition
                          Zit = β + Pi + Ct + Hit ,
                           Pi = (Ui + Vi )/2 + Wi (Ui − Vi )/2 + d(Wi − 1),
                          Hit = (Eit + Jit )/2 + Wi (Eit − Jit )/2.

                 Var(P ) = σp2 (1 + a)/2 + d2 (a − 1),    Var(H) = σe2 (1 + a)/2.

52.5       Temporal discovery: retain the class before answering

52.5.1     A stationary finite temporal law

Let Xt = (Zt , At , Yt )′ satisfy

                                    Xt = rXt−1 + ϵt ,      r ∈ {0, .4, .8},

with invariant Gaussian initialization and iid innovations. Innovation structure is

                    z = ez ,        a = kz + la u + ea ,     y = τ a + cz + ly u + ey .

The latent root and errors are independent. The instantaneous intervention coefficient is τ . In
structural form the lag matrix is r(I − B): a real restriction, not an arbitrary VAR. Unknown
continuous lag and long-run interventions are different questions.
   For every candidate r, form Et (r) = Xt − rXt−1 . At the true candidate these are iid
Gaussian innovations. Nine simultaneous variance bands—three coordinate variances and six
signed pair sums/differences—give covariance inclusion by chi-square inversion and Bonferroni.
Propagate each covariance box through all compatible graphs and union over all lag candidates.
   Only inclusion at the true candidate is needed. Wrong-lag data need not be iid, and no
selected lag is falsely treated as fixed. The finite innovation classes contain the inherited 40
broad latent structures or eight encouragement/sufficiency structures per lag. Graphs are
removed only when necessary restrictions cannot intersect their covariance region. On true-law
inclusion the true graph and effect survive.
   With valid encouragement exclusion, c = 0 and the latent root does not cause Z, so
Cov(Z, Y )/ Cov(Z, A) = τ . Interval ratio propagation imposes no positive first-stage floor
and preserves disconnected or unbounded sets. Broad latent models admit equal-covariance
witnesses with arbitrary effect, giving R. Extra scientific information must exclude those
alternatives; selecting a convenient graph does not.
  Widths are outcome/action units, conditional on finite returned sets. The challenger selects
one lag before propagating its graph class.

52.6      A learner whose code matches its argument
The residualized IV score is

                     E[(Z − mZ (X)){Y − mY (X) − θ(A − mA (X))}] = 0.

Independent-training nuisance errors shift the conditional moment by E[δZ (δY − θδA )]. This
is the inherited orthogonal-score principle Chernozhukov et al. (2018); dependent separation
and actual selection need their own proof.
   The corrected procedure has two outer calendar blocks separated by a gap. Inside each
training block a further separated split selects a shrinking lasso grid. Inner training controls
standardization; selected models are refit using only outer training data. Evaluation labels
never tune penalties. Bartlett products stay within evaluation folds, never across the omitted
gap. Actual feature/support overrides are honored.
   For fixed dimension, a correct linear nuisance, positive Gram eigenvalues and fixed geometric
mixing give root-sample moment/coefficient rates. A finite shrinking grid preserves that rate,
including at selection boundaries. Products are then second order. A sufficiently increasing
gap and growing covariance window supply a conditional asymptotic route. Growing dimension
additionally needs restricted-eigenvalue and approximation/product-rate control. Prediction
accuracy alone proves none of these. The grid has 20 or 60 controls, support three or eight,
640 origins and ordinarily a 40-origin gap.
  Widths are outcome/action units. The challenger fits an unpenalized dense reference on the
same permitted training folds.
