52.7      Operations preserve meaning and evidence
Each A-D result carries actual bounds or a refusal reason, units, assumptions and capability
disposition. Finite intervals, disconnected sets, whole lines, empty sets and unavailable
computations remain distinct. Computed sets without bounds reject. Null endpoints denote
infinity only in the explicit extended-real schema, never zero or absent evidence.
   The full linked method streams both pilot and evaluation pseudo-outcomes. Chronological
pilot halves are compressed into augmented QR factors and online target moments. Validation
uses the same fixed penalty losses, followed by full-pilot refit; bounded passes then compute
estimates and covariance. Twelve dense-equivalence cases span chunks 1/37/257, low audit,
identity rank and persistence. Relative tolerance 10−9 and absolute USD 10−6 assess numerical
equivalence, not bank usefulness.
   Complete workloads include input generation, tuning/refit, inference, serialization and total
process memory. At 120,000 evaluation and 480,000 pilot origins, dense and streamed runs
take about 1.08 and 1.71 seconds, with roughly 409 MiB peak RSS each. The streaming fit is
slower. Input generation dominates memory; reduced auxiliary storage does not imply a large
total RSS reduction. No consistent performance advantage is claimed, and a dense fallback is
retained.
   Recovery binds code/input hashes, seed and request count. Local locking, fsync, atomic
record rename and a final manifest prevent partial publication. Real process deaths during
fitting, a partially written checkpoint and final publication recover the same 12 requests on
restart, replay without duplication and reject changed identities. This is local single-process
evidence; multi-host coordination and bank service levels need their platform operators.


52.8      Economics and the remaining obligations
If ∆L is held-out improvement in bank decision loss over an accepted workflow, then
      Net value = ∆L − Caudit − Ccalendar − Cintegration − Ccompute − Creview − Coperation .
52.8. Economics and the remaining obligations                                                  529


The research supplies synthetic precision and local computing measurements, not bank values
for these costs. Linked histories, correctness labels and full-state audits are different services.
A label count is not a market price; a faster fit is not ROI. Width, availability and decision
loss need matched information and actual prices.
   D01 has a scoped added-identity route; D02 a selected nonlinear fixed-policy route. D03
retains equal-law graph ambiguity. D04 requires authentic assignment, inclusion and truth.
D05 lacks reliable finite joint dependence precision. D06 has a corrected but incompletely
qualified sparse learner and complete local streaming. D07 needs bank scale/recovery evidence;
D08 independent acceptance. D09 exceeds the successful funding/servicing grids; D10 needs
bank precision/loss targets and economics. No gap has satisfied every institutional closure
gate.
   Seven input groups remain: independent reviewer, bank truth/data owners, pilot/prices,
platform operator, interface consumers, workflow/economic owner and sponsor decision. Their
contracts are prepared, but missing people, data and signed judgments cannot be authored
into existence. No external contacts were made.


Evidence and reading guide
The five current studies contain 22,528 final requests: 4,608 funding, 5,632 joint dependence
and 4,096 each for servicing, corrected graph inference and corrected learning. Another 4,096
earlier learner requests remain exploratory. Complete journals reconstruct saved summaries;
15 first/middle/last representative requests are regenerated. Twenty-five master-control tests
pass.
   Primary texts support only stated inherited roles. New derivations, fixtures, synthetic
outcomes and engineering measurements remain project evidence. Genuine local PDFs, source
versions/hashes, inspected anchors and claim limits are recorded in the release audit. Literature
coverage retains the 7 October 2026 cutoff; no exhaustive new search is claimed. Process
corrections and exact continuation steps are in the companion review.
  This extension is combined with the preserved 259-page predecessor in a new reader. It is an
author delivery with selected information-design successes and substantive negative findings,
not a fully qualified, independently accepted or adopted bank product.


From research output to a bounded bank decision
A deployment question must first specify the unit, decision time, available records and loss
from a wrong action. The funding construction requires certified randomization and link
inclusion, plus independent calendars whose economic shocks do not overlap. If those inputs
cannot be supplied, its calibrated synthetic interval is not a substitute for a bank answer. The
servicing construction requires a frozen observable policy, truthful representative state audits
and the actual historical action probabilities; otherwise the reported fixed-policy value has a
different target or can be severely biased.
   For discovery, a bank must specify the scientific restrictions that remove observationally
equivalent intervention effects. If its accepted restrictions still permit the whole real line,
the service should return that set and withhold a directional recommendation. For shared
calendars and dependent learning, the present finite failures require a new variance design or
stronger information before qualification. A platform may transmit these limitations faithfully,
but cannot turn them into positive scientific evidence.
530                                                          Causal analysis for a universal bank


   Finally, independent reviewers must reconstruct each claimed regime and bank owners
must measure useful precision, decision loss and complete acquisition and operating costs.
Only a bounded release meeting those conditions should enter an institutional acceptance and
investment decision. An adverse scientific or economic conclusion is a legitimate output of this
program.
Chapter 53

Persistent audit information and
finite calendar uncertainty

A bank can increase its account count without acquiring an independent observation of a
common calendar shock. It can also add monthly observations without redrawing a persistent
identity audit. These two limitations affect different parts of funding uncertainty. A useful
analysis must first state the joint observation law, then determine which uncertainty can be
bounded from its actual information.
   The construction below is a project derivation for the additive experiment. It gives a finite-
sample confidence set when variance and persistence bounds are supplied, together with an
information counterexample to a uniform precision claim when persistence is unrestricted. The
exact multiplier moments, covariance references and numerical illustrations are reproducible
project calculations; no new random evaluation sample or empirical qualification is used.
(Causal banking research project, 2026z,aa)


53.1      The observation law and the banking target
Retain the previously studied independent persistent pairs, common calendar and separate
gold experiment. For pair i = 1, . . . , N and date t = 1, . . . , T , the signed focal and companion
responses are

                     Fit = β + Ui + Ct + Eit ,         Dit = δ + Vi + Ct + Jit .

   The pair effects Ui , Vi are mutually independent centered Gaussians with variance vp .
The cell errors Eit , Jit are mutually independent centered Gaussians with variance ve . The
independent calendar is stationary Gaussian AR(1) with variance vc , correlation ρ|t−s| , and
|ρ| < 1. Candidate order is fixed within a pair and exogenous. Its sign Ki ∈ {−1, 1} states
whether the first candidate is focal. Randomized observed action signs multiply both recorded
candidate histories; undoing those known signs yields the two candidate responses Xi1t , Xi2t .
   An audit Ri ∼ Bernoulli(q), with known constant q > 0, selects a whole pair history. On
selected pairs the reported order is Li = Ki ξi , where ξi has probability e < 1/2 of being −1.
The error is symmetric, independent of pair outcomes and audits, and persistent across dates.
An independent representative gold sample contains M Bernoulli error indicators with the
same e. Unobserved audit labels remain missing; multiplication by Ri below means their
contribution is zero without imputing an observed label. Endogenous selection, asymmetric
error, shared pair audits and nonrepresentative gold labels violate this law.

53.2      A finite construction with explicit unknown-nuisance
          bounds
Suppose the admissible model supplies finite bounds vp ≤ v̄p , ve ≤ v̄e , vc ≤ v̄c and |ρ| ≤ ρ̄ ≤ 1.
The values inside these bounds are unknown. Taking ρ̄ = 1 is allowed as a conservative

coefficients in kT are positive,

                                                 q                       q

53.3. Why validity need not produce a useful finite interval                                                   533


   Obtain a two-sided exact binomial interval Ce by inverting the gold count S ∼
Binomial(M, e), allocating αe /2 to each tail. For an interior count s, its lower endpoint solves
PeL (S ≥ s) = αe /2 and its upper endpoint solves PeU (S ≤ s) = αe /2, with endpoints zero/one
for the boundary counts. Binomial tail monotonicity shows that excluding the true e through
either tail has probability at most its allocated error. Intersect with the model’s [0, 1/2) to
obtain Cr = {1 − 2e : e ∈ Ce ∩ [0, 1/2)}. This intersection preserves coverage under the model,
but can yield ranks arbitrarily close to zero. It does not justify silently imposing a positive
lower rank.
  Define the observed-data confidence set

           (                                                                                           )

   At the true (d, r), Chebyshev’s inequality bounds the probability of violating the displayed
quadratic inequality by αH , using the variance derived above and its nuisance envelope. This
follows directly by applying Markov’s inequality to (Hb − rd)2 : its expectation is the variance
and is no larger than the numerator divided by N . No independence between the confidence
components is needed. The union bound therefore proves


  P {(b, d, r) ∈ C} ≥ 1 − α,         P {1000β ∈ S} ≥ 1 − α,        S = {1000(b + d) : (b, d, r) ∈ C}.

   This is a finite-sample statement, uniform over the specified nuisance envelope and the
declared observation law. It estimates the gold-error rank through a confidence set and
bounds unknown calendar/pair/cell variances; it does not treat those unknown values as
known oracle constants. The construction is feasible in the mathematical sense that all
inputs to the inequalities are observed summaries or declared bounds. A numerically certified
implementation must still project over a continuum of r; a grid that misses a feasible component
would not inherit the theorem. Analytic quadratic roots or interval outer bounds, including
empty, disconnected and unbounded sets, are suitable implementation routes. A raw point
estimator is optional.
   If independent pilot data supply simultaneous upper confidence bounds on the variances
or persistence instead of deterministic bounds, their joint failure probability must receive
an additional budget. Coverage follows on the event that the bounds are valid, with that
event’s failure probability added by the union bound. Independence is not required for this
composition argument, although it can simplify the pilot proof. Supplying bounds calculated
from the same data without a validity argument would merely move the missing uncertainty
problem into another function.


53.3      Why validity need not produce a useful finite interval
For fixed candidate rank r, multiply the numerator inequality by αH and collect powers of d.
The leading quadratic coefficient is

                                   a(r) = r2 (αH + N −1 ) − (qN )−1 .

   If a(r) < 0, sufficiently large positive and negative d satisfy the inequality. If a(r) = 0, the
inequality is linear or constant and can produce a half-line, the whole line or an empty set.
534                                                             Causal analysis for a universal bank


If a(r) > 0, it gives a bounded interval or an empty set at that rank. A sufficient uniform
condition for bounded numerator projection is that every feasible rank exceed

                                        2            1
                                       rmin >               .
                                                q(N αH + 1)
   Merely checking a positive leading coefficient at the estimated rank is insufficient when
smaller ranks remain in Cr . Even when each individual rank gives a finite interval, approaching
a zero leading coefficient can make their union unbounded. A strict common margin is what
supplies the useful bound.
   For illustration, take the previously studied error probability e = .08, so r = .84, and allocate
αH = .02. At N = 100, q = .4, the leading coefficient is −479/125000; this construction has
unbounded tails even if the rank were known exactly. At N = 320, q = .4, it is 17009/2000000 >
0 at that rank. With N = 100, q = .1, the threshold exceeds one, so no allowable rank can
supply a positive leading coefficient. Exact rational arithmetic reproduces these facts. This
is a limitation of the conservative Chebyshev construction, not an impossibility theorem for
every sharper mixture or randomization method. A bounded interval obtained by clipping its
tails would abandon the proved coverage statement.
  Calendar uncertainty has a different dimension. With ρ = .95, stationary calendar standard
deviation .6, and T = 40, the standard deviation of the calendar average is about .4494; at
T = 160 it is .2776. Increasing N does not change either number. An assumed persistence
cap may improve a bound, and genuinely independent calendars may supply new information.
Neither benefit follows from creating more account-date rows within the same calendar.


53.4      An information counterexample for unrestricted persis-
          tence
Consider the favorable submodel with exact audits, no pair or cell noise, and β = δ = b.
Every signed focal and companion history equals the same b + Ct . Thus even infinitely many
observed pairs leave only one Gaussian calendar path. Let the calendar variance vc = σ 2 > 0
and correlation ρ be known in this submodel, making inference easier than in the intended
unknown-nuisance problem. For T ≥ 2, the precision matrix of a stationary AR(1) correlation
matrix is tridiagonal. Summing its entries gives the mean information

                                                   T (1 − ρ) + 2ρ
                                 IT = 1⊤ Σ−1
                                          T 1=                    .
                                                      σ 2 (1 + ρ)
   The matrix identity is independently checked by exact rational inversion for small T , and
the general formula follows by summing its two endpoint diagonals, T − 2 interior diagonals
and 2(T − 1) off-diagonal entries. For fixed |ρ| < 1, IT grows with T . But along the admissible
stationary sequence ρT = 1 − T −2 , it converges to σ −2 . Thus no increasing information about
the common mean is guaranteed uniformly over all persistence values below one.
  The limitation is not confined to unbiased estimators. Compare the laws with means zero
and ∆, the same known covariance, and ∆ = σ. Their total variation distance is
                                                    √ !
                                                 |∆| IT
                               TV(P0 , P∆ ) = 2Φ        − 1.
                                                    2

  To see this, whiten the two Gaussian laws and project onto their mean-difference direction.
53.5. What additional information would change the decision                                     535


The likelihood-ratio threshold lies halfway between the two projected means, leaving the stated
difference of normal tail probabilities. Along ρT , the distance tends to 2Φ(1/2) − 1 ≃ .3829.
  For any confidence set ST with coverage at least 1 − α at both means, the definition of total
variation gives

                               P0 (∆ ∈ ST ) ≥ 1 − α − TV(P0 , P∆ ).

  Combining this with P0 (0 ∈ ST ) ≥ 1 − α shows

                         P0 {diam(ST ) ≥ |∆|} ≥ 1 − 2α − TV(P0 , P∆ ).

  At 95% coverage the lower bound tends to about .5171. An honest confidence set therefore
cannot have uniformly vanishing diameter over this persistence sequence, even with known
covariance and exact identity. This counterexample does not contradict pointwise asymptotic
normality for a fixed correlation, and it does not prove impossibility at the previously studied
specific fixed value .95. It rules out a stronger uniform precision promise that lacks a persistence
margin or independent calendar information. In the monetary target, the diameter scales by
1000 with no additional information gained.


53.5      What additional information would change the decision
The finite region separates valid uncertainty from useful precision. Bounds on unknown
variances and persistence supply a model under which the probability statement is established,
but the resulting set can still be unbounded. For a generated prototype those bounds may be
stipulated and tested as assumptions. For a later bank claim their scientific origin must be
established, or their estimation must receive its own valid uncertainty budget. A successful
calculation cannot certify them.
   The earlier 5,632-request study of the additive pair/calendar/gold law found finite under-
coverage in scarce-information and persistent-calendar regimes despite favorable balanced-case
results. Those fixed findings motivate this alternative construction; they do not validate it.
The same study’s wrong-inclusion, shared-audit and endogenous-label cases remain outside the
law used here. A valid set under independent symmetric audits cannot be transported to those
mechanisms by changing a covariance estimator. (Causal banking research project, 2026ab)
   There are three distinct next routes. A conservative region can serve as a transparent
reference in a generated prototype, with exact quadratic and set-projection checks. A sharper
mixture-likelihood or test-inversion method might retain validity with less conservative bounds,
but it must account for the unknown variances and dependence parameters. A changed
information design can add independently audited pairs, independent representative gold labels
or genuinely independent calendar clusters. Each addresses a different part of the uncertainty.
More gold labels alone cannot remove a shared-calendar obstruction, while more dates alone
do not make a persistent audit independent.
  A prototype should preserve unbounded and disconnected results, measure the cost of
certified projection, and compare these information choices under the same scientific target.
The comparison can initially use generated mechanisms without costly bank data. A later
bank experiment is justified when its information could narrow a decision-relevant ambiguity
enough to change an action. The present argument supports that conditional choice; it does
not promise a universally precise funding estimate.
Chapter 54

Servicing policies with estimated
action and observation probabilities

A servicing team wants to compare an assistance rule with ordinary collection. Its historical
action probabilities may not have been retained, and some customers disappear from the
analytical records before their next repayment is measured. These are two estimation problems
only after a more basic scientific question has been answered: did the recorded history include
enough information to remove action and observation selection? A highly accurate model of
recorded actions cannot answer that question on its own.
  This chapter develops a restricted route with estimated probabilities, a policy selected
on separate training histories, and an explicit finite-sample confidence statement. It also
constructs two observationally indistinguishable worlds in which that route answers different
causal questions. The confidence construction and finite examples are project derivations.
The longitudinal treatment/observation identification principle is inherited from Hernán and
Robins; the importance of independent policy evaluation and cumulative, rather than current-
action, ratios is also explicit in Jiang and Li. Their results do not themselves prove the
composition below. (Hernán and Robins, 2020; Jiang and Li, 2016; Causal banking research
project, 2026ad,ae)


54.1     The servicing information clock and the eligible popula-
         tion
Fix a finite horizon T . An independently sampled customer has a complete potential history
with pre-action information Ht , binary assistance At , and subsequent net contribution Rt ,
for t = 0, . . . , T − 1. History contains every recorded past variable used by the rule or
the assignment mechanism, including earlier rewards when relevant. A finite table, or an
explicitly sufficient finite summary, indexes the probability models. Arbitrary discretization of
a continuous history does not establish sufficiency.
   Let O−1 = 1. Among records still observed at date t, the bank first records Ht , then selects
At , then the observation indicator Ct determines whether the following reward and next history
are recorded. Set Ot = Ot−1 Ct . Dropout is absorbing. Thus Ct = 1 denotes retention here,
the opposite coding from a conventional censoring indicator. Define

                      et (a | h) = Pr(At = a | Ht = h, Ot−1 = 1),
                       gt (h, a) = Pr(Ct = 1 | Ht = h, At = a, Ot−1 = 1).


                                              536
54.2. Identification with action and retention prefixes                                            537


   The stipulated observation law has four substantive restrictions. First, consistency connects
the recorded actions to the defined assistance intervention. Second, conditional on Ht , action
selection is independent of subsequent potential histories under the candidate policies. Third,
conditional on Ht , At , retention is independent of the subsequent complete history; dropout
merely hides records and does not change repayment. Fourth, all histories reachable under the
candidate policies satisfy known floors et (a | h) ≥ ce > 0 for both actions and gt (h, a) ≥ cg > 0,
with ce ≤ 1/2. Infeasible actions must instead be removed from both the declared policy class
and the support requirement.
   The independent sampling unit is the whole customer history. Dependence within that
history is allowed. Independent training and evaluation cohorts follow the same complete-
history, assignment and observation law. Distinct customer identifiers do not guarantee this
condition when common calendar shocks, household links or shared staff information remain.
The construction does not qualify those sampling regimes.
  The target is

economic outcome is not automatically analytical dropout. Treating it as missing information
would change the target. The present example assigns neither a currency value to customer
welfare nor a bank-specific loss threshold.

54.3      A finite table permits an explicit probability error budget

observation to a given dated cell.

54.5      Policy comparisons preserve the selection target
For K prespecified policies, or K rules constructed only from training, replace αE by αE /K.
The nuisance event already covers all their table cells. This gives simultaneous intervals
[Lk , Uk ], intersected with the value range, without asserting independence between policy
scores on the same customers.

   If any component interval is empty the family result is flagged incompatible. Simultaneous
coverage allows selecting a member after inspecting these intervals, provided every candidate
was fixed before evaluation and all were covered. Adding candidates after viewing evaluation
outcomes needs a new argument. For an individual paired contrast, one may instead bound
the paired score and its nuisance error directly; treating separately fitted values as independent
loses their covariance. Neither approach turns a finite candidate class into unrestricted policy
optimization.


54.6       Exact small references and the cost of conservatism
A two-decision example uses observed stress St ∈ {0, 1}, with initial probability 1/2. Historical
assistance has probability .3 + .4St . Next stress has probability .2 + .5St − .15At , retention
probability is .9−.1St −.1At , and dated contribution is 2−3St+1 −.25At . These are hypothetical
utility units; their coefficient signs express an assistance cost and an improvement in future
stress. Every path probability is rational. Retention uses a draw independent of the next
stress innovation given current state and action.
   No assistance, always assist, and assist only when stressed form a fixed finite policy
class. Exhaustive path sums under interventions are compared with a separate backward
value recursion. Summation over observed prefixes reproduces the same values with true
denominators. Perturbing action-one probabilities by +.04 and retention probabilities by −.03
verifies the fitted-law bias expression and its conservative envelope. A deliberately incorrect
current-action/retention shortcut is kept as a negative reference. The program enumerates
all paths; it draws no final evaluation sample and measures no empirical coverage. (Causal
banking research project, 2026ae)

                                                                Bias from the specified fitted
  Policy                           Exact intervention value                    denominators
  No assistance                                       1.3750                           +.21997
  Always assist                                       2.0000                            -.22321
  Assist when stressed                                1.6625                           +.20834


   The common worst-case bias envelope is 1.37243 utility units, exceeding every realized bias
in the table. That conservatism is the price of using probability error bounds without favorable
outcome cancellation. These perturbations illustrate the error propagation formula; they are
not estimates learned from an executed training sample.
   Even with Bt = 2, ce = .25, cg = .65, T = 2, n = 1000 and αE = .025, the evaluation radius
alone exceeds eight utility units. The entire stipulated value range is only eight units wide. A
mathematically valid bound can therefore be unsuitable for choosing assistance. Increasing
the nominal confidence level or adding more rare history cells makes this tradeoff harder. This
is a reason to seek shorter questions, stronger information, sharper variance-sensitive bounds
or a reviewed sequential regression construction; it is not a reason to remove the error budget.
   Sequential doubly robust scores offer a substantive alternative when continuation values
are useful. They require a separate analysis of fitted action/retention models, value-function
errors and sampling dependence. The known-logger variance reduction in Jiang and Li does
not automatically establish estimated-logger finite coverage. The earlier synthetic collection
results already show that mean protection and normal-interval reliability differ. (Jiang and Li,
2016)
54.7. Observational equivalence prevents a hidden-state repair by prediction                    541


54.7      Observational equivalence prevents a hidden-state repair
          by prediction
Consider a single decision with no censoring. In world E, action is a fair independent coin
and Y = A with probability .8, otherwise Y = 1 − A. The intervention values are VE (1) = .8,
VE (0) = .2. In world H, private hardship U is a fair coin, Y = U , and Pr(A = 1 | U ) = .2 + .6U .
Here VH (1) = VH (0) = .5.
  Both worlds have exactly the same observed joint probabilities:

                        Observed pair (A, Y ) (0, 0) (0, 1) (1, 0) (1, 1)
                        Either world                .4     .1     .1      .4


   Even the private-state assignment in world H has overlap: its probabilities are .2 and .8.
Infinite recorded data estimate Pr(A = 1) = .5 and E[Y | A = 1] = .8 perfectly in both worlds.
Weighting by that observed probability returns .8, while the hidden world’s value is .5. No
fitted logger, extra evaluation data or language-model interpretation of these same records can
distinguish the worlds. The effect is .6 in one and zero in the other.
   Observation selection has a separate obstruction. Suppose half the cohort is observed and
half of those observed have Y = 1. One full-data world assigns zero to every missing outcome;
another assigns one. Both yield the same observed records and retention probability .5, but
their cohort means are .25 and .75. Accurately estimating the retention probability does not
recover the unobserved outcome law. The complete-case mean .5 answers neither world’s
population question.
   An additional randomized action design, a truthful relevant-state audit, or a validated prox-
y/instrument model can distinguish some such worlds. Each adds information or restrictions.
The existing proximal and partial-observation treatments explain specific routes and their rank,
exclusion and policy-information requirements; they do not authorize arbitrary hidden-state
inference. (Bennett and Kallus, 2023; Tennenholtz et al., 2020)


54.8      What the proposal can recommend after this derivation
The preserved selected17 study used truthful representative state audits and supplied action
probabilities. It passed its selected valid cells, while wrong probabilities covered only one of
512 requests and policy leakage returned no finite outputs. The present finite-table route
makes estimated-probability uncertainty explicit after restricting to sufficient observed histories.
It removes no hidden-state requirement from that predecessor and claims no new repeated-
sampling qualification. (Causal banking research project, 2026af)
   The separate proposed continuous-state servicing experiment has Gaussian innovations and
a quadratic reward. Its rewards are unbounded and its history table is not finite. Consequently
it cannot use this bounded-table theorem as written. A prospectively declared bounded utility
would define a different target; alternatively, a valid tail/moment bound and a continuous-
model estimation argument are needed. Quietly capping realized losses after evaluating the
results would answer a changed question.
  For the proposal, the executable next comparison is a declared finite-state generated
demonstration with known evaluator truth, estimated training probabilities, independent
evaluation and adverse hidden/censoring cases. Its useful-width screen must be chosen in utility
units before final draws. A broad interval or correct refusal is an informative demonstration
542                                                        Causal analysis for a universal bank


outcome. A claim about real servicing remains conditional on an information audit and a
justified dependence law, and an unknown optimal policy remains a separate research question.
These distinctions make a prototype experiment worth designing without pretending that a
bank trial or a universal hidden-state theorem has already been supplied.

Continuous temporal uncertainty
and an informative intervention

55.1      The banking question and the observation law
A bank can observe a stable association between an offer and a subsequent outcome yet remain
unable to price the effect of changing the offer. The missing information can persist even
with an exactly known observational distribution. This chapter develops a restricted temporal
confidence construction and shows what an additional direct intervention would contribute.
The mathematical construction and exact calculations are project derivations, not a fitted
bank result. Causal banking research project (2026ah,aj)
   In the preserved temporal graph study, all valid cells covered and retained their declared
true graph in 512 of 512 requests. Weak relevance and unrestricted latent observation each
produced 512 whole-line sets. The persistent cell produced 507 finite sets and five whole-line
sets. Under false exclusion, the true graph was retained zero times despite numerical effect
coverage. These findings distinguish numerical coverage from informative effects and from a
valid causal restriction. Causal banking research project (2026ak)
  Let Xt = (Zt , At , Yt )′ satisfy
                                         iid
                 Xt = ρXt−1 + εt ,     εt ∼ N3 (0, Σ),   Σ ≻ 0,   ρ ∈ I ⊂ (−1, 1).

Here I is a declared closed interval, not an estimated selected lag. Initial observations
have the invariant distribution N3 (0, Σ/(1 − ρ2 )), independently of future innovations. We
observe X0 , . . . , Xn , with n ≥ 2. The scalar lag common to all coordinates and the Gaussian
independent innovations are substantive restrictions. A general lag matrix, unknown lag order,
nonstationarity, hidden temporal state, selection and measurement errors are outside this law.
  A structural innovation model is

                     εZ = EZ ,        εA = kεZ + U,      εY = τ εA + cεZ + V,

where EZ is independent of the jointly Gaussian pair (U, V ). Dependence between U and V
represents latent action/outcome confounding. The target τ is the contemporaneous response
to changing At while holding the past fixed. In observed-coordinate structural equations, the
lag matrix is ρ(I − B), where B contains the contemporaneous coefficients. It is not permissible
to change that lag matrix to ρI in the structural equations and claim the same target/law.
 The declared graph family may include the exclusion model c = 0 and a broad latent
model with unrestricted c. In the former, ΣZY = τ ΣZA . In the latter that equality need

                                                543
544                                                                     Causal analysis for a universal bank


not hold. An exclusion is a scientific restriction, not a conclusion from fitting a favorable
covariance. The construction below accommodates a finite declared family through a union
over graph/parameter pairs; it does not claim an exhaustive search over unrestricted causal
structures.


55.2      A feasible region with continuous unknown lag
For every candidate r ∈ I, form residuals Et (r) = Xt − rXt−1 . Use the nine fixed directions

          V = {e1 , e2 , e3 , e1 + e2 , e1 − e2 , e1 + e3 , e1 − e3 , e2 + e3 , e2 − e3 },   K = 9.

For each direction, let Sv (r) be the ordinary sample variance of v ′ Et (r), with divisor ν = n − 1.
At the true lag only, νSv (ρ)/(v ′ Σv) is the sum of squares of ν independent standard normal
variables. To see this, scale the vector of independent normal residuals by its population
standard deviation and apply an orthogonal matrix whose first row is the normalized all-ones
vector. The remaining ν coordinates are independent standard normals, and their squared
norm is the centered sum of squares. Consequently

                          E[Sv (ρ)] = v ′ Σv,        Var(Sv (ρ)) = 2(v ′ Σv)2 /ν.

For a declared rational tolerance 0 < t < 1, Markov’s inequality applied to the squared relative
error gives
                                                               2
                               P {|Sv (ρ)/(v ′ Σv) − 1| > t} ≤ 2 .
                                                              νt
If 2K/(νt2 ) ≤ αO , the union bound supplies simultaneous coverage at least 1 − αO for

                                  Sv (r)            Sv (r)
                       Lv (r) =          ≤ v ′ Σv ≤        = Uv (r),            v ∈ V,
                                  1+t               1−t
evaluated at r = ρ. Dependence between the nine directions is harmless for this bound.
Residuals at an incorrect lag need not be independent.
  Define CO to contain every tuple (r, G, λ, Σ) for which r ∈ I, G is in the declared family, its
parameters λ generate Σ ≻ 0 under the stated innovation law, and all nine inequalities hold.
All nuisance coefficients and the continuous lag remain in the region. Let

                                  SO = {τ (G, λ) : (r, G, λ, Σ) ∈ CO }.

On simultaneous variance inclusion, the true tuple belongs to CO ; hence its effect belongs to
SO . Thus P (τ0 ∈ SO ) ≥ 1 − αO , provided the declared family contains the true structural
model. No multiple-testing penalty over the continuum of candidate lags is required: this
proof uses a single coverage event at the fixed true lag, and the union includes that lag. It
does not declare every wrong-lag confidence calculation valid or justify discarding the true lag
by a separate selector.
  The construction is deliberately conservative. With t = 1/4, K = 9 and αO = .02, it needs
ν ≥ 14,400. The predecessor used 240 transitions; this particular finite bound cannot give it
the displayed two-sided relative band. At smaller sample size this profile returns the whole line
and a bound-insufficient disposition, rather than inserting an invalid finite interval. The exact
chi-square pivot above offers a sharper candidate using suitably certified quantiles, but its
numerical implementation would need separate validation. No improvement in cost or useful
width is claimed from replacing a lag grid with this conservative continuum argument.

disconnected components unless they overlap; never replace a pair of rays by a finite interval.

55.4      An equal-law witness and what an exclusion actually buys
Let Z, U, E be independent standard Gaussian innovations and set

               εZ = Z,    εA = Z + U,     εY = τ εA + (2 − τ )Z + (1 − τ )U + E.

For every real τ , the observed innovation is exactly (Z, Z + U, 2Z + U + E)′ , with covariance
                                              
                                      1 1 2
                                Σ = 1 2 3  ,         det Σ = 1.
                                           
                                      2 3 6

The confounded disturbance has variance 1 + (1 − τ )2 and covariance 1 − τ with U ; its
conditional noise variance is always one. Every world is a coherent positive-definite Gaussian
law. Attaching the same scalar lag and invariant initialization makes the entire observed
temporal law identical for every τ , while a contemporaneous intervention on A changes Y at
slope τ . The equality is algebraic for all real effects, not merely an equality across the finite
checked examples.
   The restriction c = 0 reduces this family to τ = 2; strong observed relevance ΣZA = 1 then
gives the familiar ratio. But relevance alone does not establish exclusion: all other worlds
have the same strong observed correlation with Z. Merely observing more of this law, using a
different discovery optimizer or asking an LLM to orient an edge cannot choose among these
effects. No theorem here rules out all additional measurements; it states exactly what the
declared observational law omits.
   At zero relevance, even exclusion can leave every effect feasible. Take εA = U and εY =
τ εA + (1 − τ )U + E = U + E, with Z independent. Now c = 0, ΣZA = ΣZY = 0, and the
effect is still arbitrary. A weak-instrument ratio that quietly deletes zero cannot solve this
information problem.


55.5      A direct intervention that separates effects without iden-
          tifying every edge
Consider independent experimental episodes at a common fixed pre-action history. Replace
the action equation by A = a0 + δR, where δ > 0 is known and R ∈ {−1, 1} is assigned with
m episodes per arm independently of innovation roots. Keep the other structural equations
unchanged. Under the restricted linear Gaussian model and an invariant τ , the outcome has
the form
                                            iid
                       Y = µ + τ δR + ξ, ξ ∼ N (0, σI2 ),  σI2 > 0.
The unknown µ absorbs the fixed history and baseline action; the unknown variance absorbs
the remaining contemporaneous causes. The episodes must be independent; taking adjacent
dates from one continuing customer trajectory does not satisfy this experiment. Identical
variance in the two arms and a common transported effect are additional model assumptions.
55.6. Precision, costs and the exact remaining scope                                          547


  Let τbI = (Ȳ+ − Ȳ− )/(2δ), and let Sp2 be the usual pooled within-arm variance with νI = 2m−2
degrees of freedom. Orthogonal Gaussian projections within each arm make its sample mean
independent of its centered residuals. Hence

This conservative alternative avoids unverified numerical tail quantiles. A sharper Student
pivot interval is possible with certified quantiles. Nonpositive pooled variance or insufficient
degrees of freedom produces a refusal/whole-line result under the declared algorithm, never
zero-width certainty. A nonnormal outcome model needs another uncertainty argument. If
input numbers are enclosed rather than exact, enclose the arm means and pooled variance as
well before projecting these endpoints.
   Under a common effect parameter, report S = SO ∩ SI . The two component coverage
events need not be independent: the union bound gives at least 1 − αO − αI . Using outer
numerical supersets preserves this inclusion proof. An empty intersection is a retained
inconsistency/failure event, not an invitation to change the error budget or delete a graph
after seeing the result. If no observational restriction is defensible, use SI alone under its own
experiment and target assumptions.
   In the equal-law family, intervention changes the arm mean difference to 2δτ . Distinct
effects are now distinguishable, although several graphs can remain compatible. Identifying the
decision-relevant effect does not require identifying every edge. Randomizing a variable that
merely encourages the action is a different experiment: exclusion, compliance and relevance
then need their own argument.


55.6      Precision, costs and the exact remaining scope
For a binary offer, take a0 = δ = 1/2. A planning illustration with m = 200 per arm,
αI = .03, a reported effect of twenty dollars and Sp2 = 100 dollars squared gives b2 = 9950/297
                p
and half-width 9950/297, approximately 5.788 dollars. The exact reference uses a rational
upward square-root enclosure. These are supplied planning summaries, not observations from
a completed trial.
   For 3,000 eligible customers and fifteen dollars incremental implementation cost per offer, the
point scenario has fifteen thousand dollars net benefit. Its conservative interval still includes
a small loss. Scaling an effect by population does not remove uncertainty, and changing the
intervention or customer population may invalidate transport. A genuine next-experiment
proposal should ask whether resolving this decision is worth the experiment’s cost, compare a
cheaper operational alternative, and include delayed outcomes, noncompliance and treatment
costs in the estimand. No measured bank ROI is inferred from this illustration.
   What is resolved is the mathematical route for one continuous scalar-lag Gaussian family, a
certified enclosure strategy, exact information counterexamples and a separating intervention
with an explicit finite bound. What remains is a resource-profiled implementation and prospec-
tively registered study, tighter useful uncertainty, justified input and model assumptions,
548                                                            Causal analysis for a universal bank


actual interventions/measurements if the proposal advances, and the general unknown-lag-
matrix/latent-state/non-Gaussian/heterogeneous-effect problem. This argument establishes no
general temporal-graph capability, bank validation or independent acceptance. The computa-
tional and information routes are concrete enough to design the next bounded public/generated
experiment.


55.7      When a valid temporal region is still an unsuitable study
          design
The restricted continuous-lag argument separates mathematical coverage from decision-useful
precision. At the true common scalar lag, invariant Gaussian initialization and independent
innovations justify the projected variance argument. A union over candidate lags need only
retain the true lag on that event; incorrect lags need not themselves produce independent
residuals. This is a useful restricted result. It does not establish a confidence procedure for
an arbitrary lag matrix, unknown order, nonstationary hidden histories or a general learned
partial ancestral graph. These differences also determine whether a proposed numerical study
is worth conducting Causal banking research project (2026ai).
   Consider the displayed Chebyshev construction with nine variance directions, relative
tolerance t = 1/4 and observational error allocation αO = .02. For a Gaussian sample variance
with ν residual degrees of freedom, the relative variance is 2/ν. Chebyshev and a union bound
therefore give
                                                                        18
                       Pr(at least one relative deviation exceeds t) ≤ 2 .
                                                                       νt
To make this bound at most .02 requires ν ≥ 14,400, or 14,401 transitions under the stated
residual convention. With 240 transitions and 239 degrees of freedom, the untruncated
expression is approximately 1.20502 and gives no useful coverage bound. The specified whole-
line fallback is honest about this limitation. Increasing the number of Monte Carlo replications
cannot make that per-request fallback decision-useful Causal banking research project (2026ai).
   A sharper pivot is a concrete development route. At the restricted true lag, an exact chi-
square variance pivot can replace the Chebyshev band while preserving the continuous union.
Ordinary development quantiles at 239 degrees of freedom and the nine-way .02 allocation
give variance multipliers approximately [.76731, 1.34533]. These values indicate potential
improvement; they are not certified release endpoints. The implementation must enclose the
tail quantiles, observable inputs and propagated covariance constraints, preserve conservative
fallback under timeout, and profile the continuous-lag calculation. Sampling a lag grid or
accepting a point optimizer’s failure does not certify the whole continuum Causal banking
research project (2026ai).
   The preserved finite-lag study also requires a precise reading. Its persistent cell returned 507
finite sets among 512 requests, so 507/512 = .990234375 passes the original raw finite-fraction
threshold of .99. The five whole-line answers remain visible, but do not justify declaring
that particular threshold failed. Weak relevance and the unrestricted latent observational
cell each returned zero finite sets and still fail it. False exclusion retained the true graph in
zero requests, despite wide effect sets covering the numerical effect. These findings concern
different obligations: availability, effect coverage, and scientific validity of the graph class
Causal banking research project (2026ai).
   A lower confidence-bound rule for availability would be a different criterion. At family error
.05 across sixteen comparisons, the one-sided lower bound for 507/512 is about .97130; even
512/512 gives about .98880. The historical study used a lower-bound screen for coverage,
55.7. When a valid temporal region is still an unsuitable study design                      549


but a raw fraction for finite availability. They should not be interchanged retrospectively. A
prospective successor may justify different criteria, provided it states them before final data
and keeps the predecessor’s outcomes under their original definitions Causal banking research
project (2026ai).
   The coverage screen has its own design-power issue. With 512 independent final requests per
cell and error .05/16, at least 500 successes are required for the exact one-sided lower bound
to exceed or equal .95. Exact binomial-tail calculations give per-cell passing probabilities
approximately .001849, .234929, .770054 and .997670 when true coverage is respectively .95,
.97, .98 and .99. Thus a nominal .95 method is very unlikely to certify a lower bound of .95
using this screen. More replications improve discrimination above the boundary; they do not
create high power at the boundary while retaining the same error control. No product of these
per-cell powers is a joint power calculation without an across-cell dependence argument Causal
banking research project (2026ai).
   Useful precision also requires an information distinction. In the unrestricted equal-law
latent family, every real effect can produce the same observed temporal law. No numerical
improvement can create a uniformly finite informative effect set from those unchanged obser-
vations. A direct assigned-action experiment changes the information available. The proposed
Gaussian episode argument assumes independent episodes, a common transported effect and
equal arm variances. Adjacent records from one trajectory or encouragement in place of the
action require different assumptions and derivations Causal banking research project (2026ai).
   The supplied-summary example makes the planning distinction concrete. At 200 episodes per
arm, reported effect 20 dollars, reported pooled variance 100 dollars squared and the specified
conservative bound, the half-width is about 5.78806 dollars. For 3,000 eligible customers and
an incremental cost of 15 dollars per offer, the net-benefit lower endpoint is approximately
−2,364.19 dollars. Holding the same reported variance and effect fixed, 268 episodes per
arm first reduce the half-width below 5 dollars, while 400 give about 4.08761. In a future
experiment both the estimated effect and pooled variance would vary. These are conditional
arithmetic screens, not prospective power or recommended bank sample sizes Causal banking
research project (2026ai).
  The next restricted study therefore needs a certified executable and input-enclosure policy,
measured resource limits, a fixed final grid of observational and added-information regimes, and
an explicit useful-width or loss criterion. A generated experiment can develop these elements
now. It should preserve strong, weak and zero relevance, false exclusion, latent equal-law cases
and all interval topologies. Final seeds, replication budgets and stopping rules must follow
the design review. General hidden-state, non-Gaussian, selection and heterogeneous-transport
questions remain unresolved beyond the restricted claim; public observations alone cannot
decide among observationally equivalent causal worlds Causal banking research project (2026ai).
Chapter 56

Learning with an explicit error
budget before a dependent
evaluation

Consider an encouragement to take a bank offer. The bank observes information X before
the encouragement Z, the eventual action A, and its subsequent value Y . Flexible prediction
is useful because accounts differ in their pre-existing circumstances. It also creates a second
estimation problem: removing predictable variation imperfectly changes the instrument moment.
When the residual response to the encouragement is small, that change can be large relative
to the information identifying the effect. A narrow interval computed after fitting a good
predictor need not describe the uncertainty in the bank’s causal decision.
   This chapter develops a restricted alternative. Learn on an independent pilot, obtain
an explicit bound on each prediction error, and carry that bound into a joint region for
two observable moments. Evaluate those moments on a bounded sequence with a known
dependence range. Project the region into the effect, retaining disconnected and unbounded
answers. The construction is a project derivation with exact numerical references, rather than
an implemented general learner or a new repeated-sampling qualification (Causal banking
research project, 2026c). Its restrictions are substantial; explaining them is part of deciding
whether the proposed product merits a larger experiment.


56.1      What the repaired predecessor did and did not establish
The preceding sparse-learning experiment already has a repaired version. Its first version
selected penalties using evaluation outcomes, standardized with all observations, included
covariance products across an omitted calendar gap, and ignored some scenario dimensions.
The repaired version uses training-only nested selection, training-specific scaling, within-fold
Bartlett covariance, and the actual registered dimension and support. The original results
remain exploratory. They do not establish the performance of that repaired procedure.
   For the repaired learner, the high-dimension and larger-support scenarios covered respectively
499/512 and 493/512 requests. Their simultaneous lower coverage bounds, 0.949140 and
0.933851, fell below the frozen 0.95 threshold. The nonlinear omitted-nuisance scenario covered
0/512. The weak-instrument scenario covered 512/512, but its median interval width was
3.836470 in the synthetic effect units. These were nominal 99% intervals, so comparisons with
the original 95% intervals cannot isolate the effect of repairing the code. Failure to pass a
certification screen is distinct from proof of universal undercoverage; complete finite availability

                                                550
56.2. The structural target and its observable moment                                          551


is also distinct from useful precision. These results remain the relevant negative baseline.
   An independent pilot removes one source of dependence between fitted functions and
evaluation scores. It cannot make a misspecified dictionary correct, turn a weak instrument
into a strong one, or make repeated calendar observations independent. A successor therefore
needs a statement for each of those issues.


56.2     The structural target and its observable moment
The imposed partially linear model is

                          Y = θ0 A + g0 (X) + ϵ,        E[ϵ | X, Z] = 0.                  (56.1)

The conditional moment excludes a remaining direct effect of the encouragement and unmea-
sured causes associated with its residual after conditioning on X. It is a scientific assumption.
A prediction fit or source hash cannot verify it. Here θ0 is a constant structural coefficient,
expressed in outcome units per unit of action. Interpreting it as an unrestricted heterogeneous
average effect would require a different argument.
  Let m(X) = E[Z | X], r(X) = E[A | X] and ℓ(X) = E[Y | X]. Define residuals
vZ = Z − m(X), vA = A − r(X) and vY = Y − ℓ(X), and moments

                               M = E[vZ vY ],      Q = E[vZ vA ].                         (56.2)

Equation (56.1) implies M = θ0 Q. A nonzero Q identifies the scalar coefficient from this
relation. If Q = 0, the relation can be uninformative even when the observations themselves
are measured exactly.
  The residualized score (Z − m(X)){Y − ℓ(X) − θ(A − r(X))} is the inherited partially linear
IV score in Chernozhukov et al. (2018, Section 4.2, equation (4.8)). That source states its
moment, nuisance-product and nonzero-slope conditions. Its independent-sample theorem
does not supply a result for arbitrary serially dependent bank rows. The following finite
construction instead proves its own statement for a declared observation law.


56.3     An observation law that makes separation meaningful
The pilot contains mP independent draws from the marginal law of W = (X, Z, A, Y ) and is
independent of the entire evaluation sequence. The evaluation observations W1 , . . . , Wn are
stationary and d-dependent: collections separated by more than d dates generate independent
sigma fields. The integer d is supplied and justified by the design. Uncorrelated residuals or a
small sample autocorrelation are insufficient to establish this property.
   Assume known almost-sure ranges |Z| ≤ BZ , |A| ≤ BA , and |Y | ≤ BY . Clip predicted
conditional means into the respective ranges. Since the true conditional means lie there,
clipping predictions cannot increase their squared error. Clipping the observed outcome is
different: it can change the target and cannot be introduced silently to make a bound available.
   The features ϕ(X) ∈ Rp are fixed before the pilot, with |ϕk (X)| ≤ K. A feature learned
from data needs a separate design sample and conditional versions of these assumptions. A
constant feature can represent an intercept, but the derivation below penalizes its coefficient
too. It does not silently inherit the previous implementation’s unpenalized intercept or its
data-dependent scaling.
  These choices exclude the unbounded Gaussian AR experiment in the predecessor. They
can describe a bounded generated benchmark or a justified collection of finite-dependent
552                                                                  Causal analysis for a universal bank


observations. They do not describe an arbitrary bank panel. An extension to geometric mixing
requires a proved coupling or concentration bound, with an explicit additional error allocation.
Unknown dependence remains an information requirement.


56.4     The nuisance error enters as two products
Condition on the independent pilot, so the fitted functions are fixed. Write δZ = mb − m,
δA = rb − r and δY = ℓb − ℓ. Expanding the product, then conditioning on X, eliminates the
linear error terms because E[vj | X] = 0. Thus

                   Mfit = E[(Z − m)(Y
                                 b    − ℓ)
                                        b | pilot] = M + E[δZ δY | pilot],                        (56.3)
                   Qfit = E[(Z − m)(A
                                 b    − rb) | pilot] = Q + E[δZ δA | pilot].                      (56.4)

If a simultaneous certificate supplies ∥δj ∥2 ≤ ej , Cauchy–Schwarz gives

                         |Mfit − M | ≤ eZ eY ,          |Qfit − Q| ≤ eZ eA .                      (56.5)

Consequently the score bias at a candidate θ is bounded by eZ (eY + |θ|eA ). The encouragement
prediction error is essential to this expression. An outcome–action product alone does not
describe the IV score. Nor does an error norm of exact order n−1/4 automatically suffice: two
such errors can leave a root-n scaled remainder of order one.
   The bound is exact in its conditional decomposition and conservative in its norm inequality.
It needs neither an estimated effect in the denominator nor a claim that the remainder is
negligible. Those features allow a finite construction that remains honest when a nuisance
certificate is wide.

56.5.1     What must actually be certified

The cone bound is a substantive requirement. A full Gram condition number is not a sparse
cone certificate when p exceeds the pilot size. A small fixed dictionary can use a certified
minimum eigenvalue. A high-dimensional construction needs a justified sparse certificate or a
generated-design guarantee. If certification fails, the result must declare the bound unavailable
or use an explicitly wider fallback. The theorem cannot assume that a returned regression
coefficient certifies its own rate.
  The minimization also needs a numerical specification. An approximate optimizer adds
a basic-inequality error that must be propagated. A small KKT residual does not by itself
554                                                                    Causal analysis for a universal bank


prove equation (56.14). The exact reference uses a 32-row, four-feature orthogonal design,
support two and penalty 0.1. Soft thresholding gives coefficients (0.4, 0.15, 0, 0); a separate
nonnegative-variable convex optimization agrees. Population squared error is 0.02, below the
selected bound 0.18. This checks the algebra and the small optimization reference; it supplies
no certificate for an arbitrary pilot.


56.5.2    Why a proved bound may still be economically unattractive

Table 56.1 evaluates the formula under the hypothetical certified constants K = Ej = κj = 1,
Aj = 0, and error allocation 0.005 for each score and Gram event. These are planning inputs,
not fitted properties of the predecessor. Even favorable assumed geometry gives a loose bound
at small pilot sizes. A deterministic range cap could reduce the largest numbers, but would
not make them a useful precision claim.

                            E[(Tj − fbj (X))2 | pilot] = ∥fbj − fj ∥22 + E[ϵ2j ].                  (56.15)

across all requests; it does not establish the same conditional coverage among only those
requests whose certificates pass, or a minimum fraction of informative results.

56.9      An exact explanation for the nonlinear failure
The repaired predecessor adds h(X) = 0.6(X12 −1) to the encouragement and outcome equations.
For a standard Gaussian coordinate, E[h] = 0 and E[h2 ] = 0.72; the term is orthogonal to
the linear Gaussian features. Even with unlimited pilot data, a linear dictionary therefore
leaves h in the encouragement residual and leaves θ0 kh + h in the outcome residual, where k
is the encouragement coefficient in the action equation. With unit encouragement-innovation
variance, the residualized numerator and denominator obey
                   Mlinear = θ0 k(1 + 0.72) + 0.72,           Qlinear = k(1 + 0.72).                 (56.22)
For k = 0.8, the ratio converges to
                                  0.72             45
                       θ0 +                 = θ0 +    ≃ θ0 + 0.523255814.                            (56.23)
                              0.8(1 + 0.72)        86
This is a population approximation-error explanation, not an exact prediction of the saved
finite-sample lasso bias. It explains why more observations alone need not cure the failure.
Prespecifying the quadratic feature removes this particular population omission, but finite
estimation and dependence still need their own analysis. Under this Gaussian example the
omitted feature is unbounded, so the earlier bounded approximation theorem does not apply
unchanged.
56.10. The proposed next experiment and its limits                                          557


56.10      The proposed next experiment and its limits
A useful bounded prototype would compare a small fixed dictionary, the certified sparse pilot,
and the independent calibration route on the same declared target. Its full resource record must
include feature preparation, training, tuning, certificate construction, calibration, dependent
evaluation, set projection and retained refusals. A faster optimizer is of little value if the
required pilot or confidence width makes the decision uneconomical.
   Before final draws, choose a bounded mechanism with an explicit dependence range and a
separate pilot, freeze the dictionary and approximation bounds, review the cone and numerical
certificates, and profile complete costs. Then freeze sample sizes, error allocations, adverse
cases, alternatives, fresh draws, stopping rule and useful-width criterion. The old failed
outcomes cannot become the new evaluation data. No final successor study is registered by
the argument in this chapter.
   The route is now explicit for this restricted family. General unbounded dependent learning,
unknown approximation error, unverified instruments, arbitrary learners and useful weak-IV
precision remain open. Where the certificate is too costly or too wide, narrowing the question
or changing the information design is a substantive product recommendation.
Chapter 57

Investment, adoption and the
independent product

A common causal product earns its cost by improving repeated scientific work. The appropriate
alternative is a capable quantitative team composing the same open-source methods with
ordinary engineering, documentation and review. Such a team can produce good causal studies
without a new platform. The investment question is whether the shared representations and
qualified operations reduce the cost of equivalent work or enable additional valuable decisions,
after construction, support and adoption are included.


57.1     Define equivalent output before pricing reuse
An equivalent completed study has a reconstructed population and observation clock, a clear
intervention and financial outcome, a defensible identification argument or useful nonidentifi-
cation conclusion, appropriate inference, reproducible artifacts and review. The comparison
must include negative results. An early finding that a requested target is unidentified can save
substantial work; forcing every study to return a numerical effect would reward scientific error.
  The proposed product owns repeated semantic work: availability-aware histories, target-
preserving conversions, graph/identification traces, inference contracts, policy information
and reconstruction of evidence. It reuses external numerical methods where their qualified
contracts fit. A host application still supplies product-specific behavior, its economic account
and decision constraints. This division creates possible reuse without assuming that a mortgage
equilibrium, an individual collections policy and a macro shock all have one estimand.
   Comparator costs should include the same required outputs and review quality. Reduced
effort from omitting uncertainty or failing to investigate weak support is not a saving. Con-
versely, building a generic model interface for a one-off study can cost more than a small,
clearly documented expert analysis. The portfolio of genuinely repeated requests, not the total
number of database rows, determines the economic opportunity.

The first term already counts workflow savings. Released analyst time must not be added

  At 24 annual studies the illustrative cost premium requires about USD .246 million of
additional constant annual decision value. The adoption ramp requires about USD .980 million.
The size of a bank’s balance sheet does not establish either amount. The expert comparator
may already identify the same profitable policy or reject the same loss-making offer.
   The deposit study illustrates the attribution problem. Finding a negative contribution
can prevent a loss only if the finding changes what would otherwise have been done. The
prevented loss cannot be credited to the product merely because its report contains the
estimate. Likewise the simulated collections gain is a property of the declared environment;
it supplies no observed revenue to this investment account. Latent-state research can be
worthwhile even while operational value remains uncertain.
   Costs and gains also mature on different clocks. Data access, implementation and review
are paid before customer outcomes are observed. A six-month retention measure may mature
during an early evaluation; credit losses or a persistent pricing response may not. A continuation
model supplies a conditional forecast for those outcomes, not an observation. Report the cash
timing and model dependence explicitly.


57.4                                          Measure the common-product hypothesis
The complete-workflow measurements in Section 45.7 refine the resource account but do
not estimate its labor terms. A response workflow over 3.85 million versioned records takes
about 3.38 seconds on the recorded host; a 3,200-customer latent workflow with 19 bootstrap
refits takes about 48.27 seconds. Both the product and expert-composition arms can use
these same numerical operations. Pricing one arm from a bare estimator call and the other
from reconstruction plus inference would be an unequal-output comparison. The illustrative
per-study dollar inputs above therefore remain unchanged pending matched measurements of
preparation, review and rework.
  The first tranche should compare matched tasks in the intervention, sequential-decision
57.5. A staged construction budget and stopping rules                                        561


and dynamic-systems workspaces. Agree their outputs, scientific scope and reviewer rubric
before measuring effort. Give the expert-composition arm the same sources, data access and
expertise, and allow sensible reusable templates. Counterbalance task order where possible to
reduce learning effects.
  Measure analyst and reviewer hours, calendar delay, machine cost, failed starts, rework and
unresolved material findings separately. Ask a second analyst to reconstruct the population,
target and financial conclusion from the exported artifacts. Deliberately introduced clock,
weight and sign errors can test whether review finds the defects. This tests the proposed
product’s specific value proposition, rather than whether a polished interface is pleasant.
  A planning target of 30% lower median analyst/reviewer effort can be useful if review quality
and output scope are held fixed. It remains a hypothesis until measured across repeated uses
and teams. A successful first-author demonstration is insufficient evidence of institutional
reuse. Conversely, more early rejections can be a benefit if they correctly avoid expensive
unidentified studies.
  Progression can be written as

                          nusable
                           t      = nstarted
                                     t       pdata
                                              t    pdesign
                                                    t      pexecution
                                                            t         preview
                                                                       t      ,

where each probability conditions on reaching the preceding stage. This is the chain rule, not
an independence assumption. It separates volume aspirations from usable output and makes
adoption bottlenecks visible. Charges for unsuccessful studies remain in the cost account.


57.5     A staged construction budget and stopping rules
An illustrative first tranche assigns six people for six months: one product/economics lead, two
causal/econometric scientists, two data/platform engineers and one application engineer. At
USD 25,000 per loaded person-month, staff cost is USD 900,000; USD 50,000 compute/tooling
and 20% contingency give USD 1.14 million. This tranche is included in the illustrative USD 4
million initial product cost, not added to it. Data-owner, independent validation, security
and application-owner participation are unpriced and must be estimated consistently for both
alternatives before a bank funds work.
   The tranche should implement the shared observation/request/evidence objects and qualify a
narrow adjusted/cohort and observed-history policy path. Controlled-state fitting and temporal
discovery should enter the architecture immediately through finite, explicitly conditional
research operations. Six people cannot qualify every method in the 44-project survey for
production in six months.
   The next tranche depends on concrete outcomes. Continue if repeated requests share
observation and scientific contracts, reviewers can reconstruct results, the required estima-
tors/inference pass their acceptance exercises, and measured effort supports the economic case.
Narrow the scope if most work remains application-specific. Retain expert composition when
reuse is low. Stop a particular policy analysis when its data cannot distinguish materially
different decisions and additional evidence is not worth its cost.
  These are different decisions: discontinuing an unidentified analysis, deferring a numerical
adapter, and declining investment in the shared product should not be collapsed into a single
project-failure flag. The source archive and scientific representations remain useful even if one
deployment case is rejected.
562                                                         Causal analysis for a universal bank


57.6     An independent offering must price institutional variation
An independent product can distribute the scientific core as an embedded library and provide
the three workspaces with deployment, support and upgrade services. A design-partner
engagement is a plausible first commercial form: a named study portfolio, paid integration
scope, reproducible evidence export and a recurring support boundary. No willingness-to-pay,
sales-cycle or customer-retention estimate is established by this proposal.
  Each institution adds semantic mapping, legal-entity structure, observation systems, sci-
entific review and operational requirements. Code reuse reduces some common work but
does not remove those costs. A commercial comparison should price onboarding, customer-
specific adapters, method maintenance, support and validation participation, and state which
customizations remain owned by the customer.
   Procurement should compare products on the same reconstructed studies, supported identi-
fication routes, uncertainty objects, data-locality requirements and export/replay obligations.
Repository activity or an enterprise demonstration is not evidence that these scientific oper-
ations are available. The source review establishes open-source construction alternatives; it
does not assert uninspected private-vendor capabilities or prices.
   For a banking group, the defensible first investment is therefore a bounded common
scientific layer tied to named repeated decisions. Its expansion should follow measured reuse
and preserved analytical quality. The mathematical distinctions developed throughout the
monograph determine which work can be shared and what the investment is actually buying.
Chapter 58

Public evidence for a causal banking
proposal

The immediate deliverable is a product proposal: a defensible account of the decisions a
shared causal library could improve, the methods and software worth assembling, a bounded
prototype, and the experiments worth funding next. A bank deployment, accepted integration
and measured commercial return are later milestones. Requiring private assignment logs,
independent bank audits and production owners before completing this proposal reverses the
investment sequence. Those expensive inputs should be requested only when less expensive
evidence has established both technical promise and a consequential uncertainty that they can
resolve.
   Public data can provide much of the evidence for that first decision. It can expose realistic
variable definitions, missingness, reporting clocks, financial magnitudes and computational
workloads. Public experiments can exercise estimation under a documented assignment design.
Semi-synthetic data can combine empirical covariates with generated treatment assignments
and potential outcomes, making error measurable. Entirely synthetic histories can isolate
feedback, confounding, graph equivalence and observation errors. These sources complement
one another because no single source supplies realistic bank operations, observed counterfactual
truth and unrestricted reuse at once.
   The proposal therefore replaces a premature demand for authentic bank qualification with
a public-evidence portfolio. It does not replace an unknown bank effect with the effect from
another population. The claim being evaluated changes from “this system improves this bank’s
decisions” to “these capabilities are technically credible, reproducible and sufficiently promising
to justify this specific next experiment.” A negative comparison, a useful refusal, or a narrowed
capability can be a successful research deliverable when it changes that investment decision
honestly.


58.1      What constitutes evidence
Let S = 1 denote membership in a public study and S = 0 membership in the future bank
population. A public randomized study may identify

                                  τ1 = E[Y (1) − Y (0) | S = 1].

   It does not by itself identify τ0 . One possible transport argument would require comparable
interventions and outcomes, sufficient effect modifiers X, overlap between populations, and

                                               563
564                                                            Causal analysis for a universal bank


stability of the conditional causal response. Under those additional assumptions,

              Z
       τ0 =       {m1 (x) − m0 (x)} dP (x | S = 0),   ma (x) = E[Y | A = a, X = x, S = 1].

   The expression explains the later data requirement: a target population distribution and
a credible account of effect modification. It is not a finding that these assumptions hold. A
banking example makes the distinction concrete. Learning how advertising holdouts support
an incremental-conversion estimate can validate treatment coding and an estimator’s workflow.
It does not show the deposit value of a bank telephone campaign, whose product, population,
contact policy and financial payoff differ.
  Five evidence classes are kept distinct throughout this survey.
