   For an observational file, a fitted model is not an assignment mechanism. For a randomized
experiment, the difference in sample means is an estimate with uncertainty, not the true
individual treatment effect. For a semi-synthetic file, both potential outcomes may be available,
but they were generated. These distinctions determine which metrics are meaningful: prediction
accuracy for a repayment label, interval coverage only when truth or a valid evaluation
construction is available, and effect identification only under explicit substantive assumptions.


58.2      Survey method and coverage
The survey inspected 24 dataset families using custodian descriptions, author-maintained
benchmark documentation, data dictionaries and selected loader/generator source. It covers
funding and bank panels; household finance and marketing; lending and mortgage histories;
experimental and semi-synthetic estimation; discovery; linkage; and language-model reasoning.
A source register preserves exact downloaded bytes, SHA-256 identities, inspected passages,
supported claims and access limitations. Dataset documentation supports dataset descriptions;
this survey does not infer a scholarly result from a paper title or repository abstract.
58.3. Evidence already available                                                              565


   The publication cutoff is 7 October 2026. Eight benchmark documentation files and the
CFPB historical schema are pinned to repository commits at or before that cutoff. Other
web pages are acquisition snapshots from 12 October; their current text is not represented
as an archived 7 October page. Older survey and data releases described by those pages
remain candidates, but their exact selected files must be frozen before analysis. The SCF
page provides a concrete trap: some summary extracts were updated on 9 October 2026, after
the cutoff. Those extracts are excluded from a cutoff-respecting study until a prior version is
recovered. The full 2022 dataset is described separately with an earlier release date (Board of
Governors of the Federal Reserve System, 2026b).
   This is a structured, bounded survey. It is strongest for US regulatory and mortgage data,
two commonly used non-US bank datasets, and public methodological benchmarks. It is not
an exhaustive international census. China-specific supervisory and household panels, European
credit registers, financial inclusion and microcredit trial archives, and detailed commercial
panel providers need separate custodian and access reviews. Their absence does not establish
that no suitable public source exists. No registration-gated mortgage account was created,
no commercial data agreement was accepted, and no linked external benchmark code was
executed during this survey.


58.3     Evidence already available
The repository already contains a reproducible public 401(k) analysis and a quarterly monetary
analysis, alongside its synthetic banking studies. The 401(k) extract contains 9,915 households,
eligibility, participation, financial assets and nine declared controls. The existing analysis
distinguishes an eligibility average effect from a participation instrumental-variable target
and compares score algebra with DoubleML under identical fitted inputs. The extract lacks
survey-design fields sufficient to establish design-valid covariance; conditional exchangeability,
instrument assumptions and bank transport are unresolved. These are informative prototype
limitations, not reasons to discard the example (DMLonGitHub application-data repository,
2026).
  The monetary example uses 203 quarterly observations from 1959Q1 through 2009Q3. It
reproduces local-projection coefficients and Bartlett covariance against a numerical reference,
and makes the information-clock ambiguity explicit. An aggregate money-stock response to a
Treasury-bill rate change is not a bank’s deposit-offer effect. It is nevertheless a useful public
demonstration of time-series conventions, dependence-aware computation and sensitivity to
period and control choices (statsmodels dataset contributors, 2026).
   A new descriptive inspection downloaded the UCI Bank Marketing archive, checked its
four CSV files and preserved their identities. The two full datasets contain 41,188 and 45,211
observations; their smaller files contain 4,119 and 4,521. The 41,188-row version has 4,640
subscriptions and 36,548 non-subscriptions. Its default field contains 8,597 unknown values
and education contains 1,731. Empty-cell counts alone would therefore conceal missing
information. The full and smaller versions overlap and must not be used as independent
replications (UCI Machine Learning Repository, 2026a; Causal banking research project,
2026an).
   That inspection is a completed data-profile exercise. It is not a new treatment-effect
estimate, a fitted benchmark or a preregistered experiment. It establishes that an openly
licensed, modest-size financial dataset is immediately usable for schema, timing and refusal
demonstrations.
Chapter 59

Dataset choices and their causal
roles

59.1      Funding responses and bank panels
1. FDIC Summary of Deposits. The custodian describes an annual survey of branch-office
deposits as of 30 June. Institutions with branches submit the survey; institutions with only a
main office are exempt from that reporting requirement. The natural observational unit is a
branch-year, nested within an institution and local market. This makes the source attractive
for deposit concentration, branch-network histories and a proposed event-study workflow.
Before estimation, the chosen release must establish identifiers, ownership changes, deposit
units and coverage. A branch closure or merger is not automatically an exogenous treatment:
local demand, financial distress and strategic selection can drive both the event and deposits.
Annual June observations cannot recover a daily customer offer response. Decision: shortlist
for a public panel prototype, with causal event-study claims conditional on a separately justified
design (Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation, 2026b).
   2. FDIC Bank Data API financial and structural series. The inspected API
specification exposes institution, financial, historical-change and deposits routes. This gives an
acquisition route for an institution-time dataset and the structural history needed to avoid
treating a merger as organic growth. Financial fields and history must be joined using a frozen
field dictionary and defensible continuity rules. First compare accounting identities, dates
and missingness; then examine a declared event or exposure. Bank and calendar dependence
belong in the uncertainty design. No bank-quarter dataset or causal effect was downloaded or
estimated in this survey. Decision: pair with the deposits source after a bounded schema
and vintage inspection; do not pool institution, holding-company and branch units without an
explicit aggregation map (Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation, 2026a).
   3. Federal Reserve FR Y-9C. The report collects consolidated holding-company balance
sheets, income statements and supporting schedules quarterly. The official description says
microdata are public with exceptions. The unit is a consolidated holding company, which is
different from an insured bank or a branch. It can support funding composition and institution-
level stress examples when thresholds, reporting changes and consolidations are accounted for.
It is not a customer-level dataset and does not supply the bank’s internal pricing decision.
Decision: reserve as a second panel source; prefer one coherent institution panel initially and
add holding-company aggregation only for a question that requires it (Board of Governors of
the Federal Reserve System, 2026c).
  4. Federal Reserve H.8. H.8 supplies estimated weekly aggregate commercial-bank


                                               566
59.2. Households, acquisition and credit decisions                                          567


balance sheets and bank-group series, with downloadable data routes. It is inexpensive context
for system-wide deposits, credit and common-calendar shocks. The aggregation is useful for a
forecasting or conditional-response example, but it removes customer and institution assignment
information. Group composition, revisions and seasonal adjustments need attention. Decision:
adopt as a contextual and time-series workflow source; require a separately documented shock
design before attaching a structural causal interpretation (Board of Governors of the Federal
Reserve System, 2026a).
   5. Archived macroeconomic extract. The existing 203-quarter dataset is already
local and has an executed, bounded projection study. Its advantages are a fixed historical
snapshot, small resource requirements and an existing independent numerical comparison.
Its limitations are age, aggregation and unresolved policy information. Decision: reuse this
baseline now; a newer series can be a versioned extension, with release vintages and units
preserved. Replacing it merely because newer numbers exist would not supply an identification
argument (statsmodels dataset contributors, 2026).


59.2      Households, acquisition and credit decisions
6. SIPP-based 401(k) extract. Eligibility, participation and financial wealth yield a compact
financial example with two distinct estimands. The existing workflow can show adjustment-
set declarations, orthogonal scores, overlap diagnostics and why a participation effect needs
stronger assumptions than an eligibility contrast. Unknown survey design and variable
timing remain explicit. Employer selection and saving preferences are plausible unmeasured
confounders. Decision: retain as the principal existing public household-finance example; add
sensitivity and target-definition tests without relabeling observational assumptions as verified
randomization (DMLonGitHub application-data repository, 2026).
   7. Survey of Consumer Finances. The 2022 public file is described as 4,595 families
represented by 22,975 rows across five implicates. The Federal Reserve supplies separate
replicate weights and warns that ignoring both imputation and complex sampling yields
incorrect standard errors. This is valuable for wealth, debt, balance-sheet heterogeneity
and the product’s treatment of uncertainty across completed datasets. It is normally a
triennial cross-section, not a customer transaction panel. A credible exercise would reproduce a
published descriptive quantity with proper imputation and survey variance before attempting
an assumption-dependent causal example. Decision: shortlist for observation construction and
household heterogeneity, selecting a documented pre-cutoff file; do not concatenate implicates
and count them as independent families (Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System,
2026b).
   8. UCI Bank Marketing. The data concern telephone campaigns at a Portuguese bank
and term-deposit subscription. The full additional version has 20 inputs, 41,188 examples
and a documented date ordering from May 2008 to November 2010; the older full version
has 45,211 rows. The custodian states CC BY 4.0 terms. Contact duration is an especially
clear timing test: it is not available when deciding whether to place the call. The files do
not establish a random treatment policy, a representative uncontacted group or an entity key
sufficient for a repeated-customer causal panel. “The client subscribed” is an outcome; it is
not itself an intervention. Decision: adopt immediately for data profiling, business-question
translation, leakage detection and principled refusal. Reject a claimed incremental campaign
effect from this file alone (UCI Machine Learning Repository, 2026a; Causal banking research
project, 2026an).
  9. UCI Default of Credit Card Clients. This 30,000-row Taiwan dataset has 23
predictors, including credit limits, payment status, bills and payments over April–September
568                                                            Causal analysis for a universal bank


2005, followed by a default label. The custodian states CC BY 4.0. The histories are useful for
checking feature clocks, censoring assumptions and the distinction between a repayment and a
bank action. A payment is partly a customer’s response, not an assigned servicing treatment.
The file does not disclose the complete sequence of contact, limit-change or relief decisions and
their logging probabilities. Decision: use as an openly reusable credit-history and prediction
baseline; use its admissible covariates in a clearly labeled generated-action study if desired. It
cannot establish the causal effect of a collection policy (UCI Machine Learning Repository,
2026b).
   10. Public HMDA application records. The inspected CFPB historical public schema
includes lender identity, year, geography, application action, loan amount, income and pricing
fields. It supports a lending-funnel example: application, denial, origination and conditional
loan terms are distinct objects. Conditioning a rate analysis on origination changes the selected
population. Public disclosure transformations, missing fields and policy-specific coverage
require the selected year’s dictionary. The current publication endpoint returned HTTP 403;
the accessible, cutoff-pinned historical schema is evidence about that schema, not proof of the
2024 file’s contents. Decision: shortlist for application and selection analysis after current-year
access is resolved. Do not present it as a monthly repayment panel or individual discrimination
ground truth (Consumer Financial Protection Bureau, 2026).


59.3      Loan servicing and repeated outcomes
11. Freddie Mac Single-Family Loan-Level Dataset. The official page describes
origination and monthly performance data, including prepayments and credit events, and
directs users to register and sign in. It also states that data are unaudited and subject to
change. Free noncommercial, academic/research and limited uses remain subject to terms;
commercial redistribution requires an agreement. Longitudinal loan histories can demonstrate
competing events, outcome horizons, cohort splits and incomplete observations. Modification
flags do not supply the full decision state, all feasible offers or known action probabilities.
Decision: strong conditional candidate for realistic servicing histories. Review the permitted
use and a small fixed cohort before committing resources; use an unrestricted synthetic history
route meanwhile (Freddie Mac, 2026).
   12. Fannie Mae Single-Family Loan Performance Data. The custodian describes
selected fixed-rate loans with origination and dynamic monthly performance, alongside a
HARP mapping between original and refinanced loans. Its stated population excludes several
mortgage categories, so it is not the entire mortgage market. Registration is required; third-
party redistribution and external commercial uses are restricted without written consent. The
HARP mapping is valuable for discussing how an apparent loan termination may be a linked
refinancing, but it does not resolve endogenous refinancing selection. Decision: alternative
to Freddie Mac, not a mandatory second acquisition. Select one source by access, variable
coverage and cohort quality; retain the other as a robustness extension only when it answers a
consequential question (Fannie Mae, 2026).
   13. NHEFS observational follow-up. The inspected causallib loader distinguishes a
smoking-cessation/weight-change analysis and a survival variant with follow-up and censoring.
It explicitly records optional exclusion of missing outcomes and uses cessation as the exposure.
This is an adjacent-domain teaching example for baseline treatment, observation restrictions and
survival semantics. It is not a series of randomized bank servicing decisions. Decision: keep
as an optional inexpensive survival comparison after checking upstream data terms and cohort
construction. Use a generated sequential decision process for time-varying treatment feedback
rather than pretending this baseline-exposure example supplies it (causallib contributors,
59.4. Experimental, panel and semi-synthetic benchmarks                                    569


2026).
  For a sequential policy, histories Ht , actions At , subsequent states and censoring need a
declared order. Identification by a longitudinal g-formula requires consistency, positivity and
sequential exchangeability given the available history. Monthly rows satisfy none of those
assumptions merely by being longitudinal. An observed modification may follow a private
hardship assessment absent from the release. Therefore the first servicing prototype should
combine realistic public outcome histories, where access permits, with generated actions and
outcomes whose causal law is fully declared. Its empirical and generated components must
remain separately labeled.


59.4     Experimental, panel and semi-synthetic benchmarks
14. NSW experimental job-training extract. The causaldata documentation describes
nsw_mixtape as a 445-row experimental extract with earnings and baseline covariates. A
small public earnings experiment is useful for effect-versus-prediction semantics and a design-
based baseline. Before claiming an identified effect, recover the original assignment and
sample-selection description and bind the exact version. A public mirror of the data was
acquired here, but no fitted study or new trial validation was performed. Decision: preferred
small experimental candidate, conditional on those provenance and rights checks (causaldata
contributors, 2026).
   15. MatchIt LaLonde comparison sample. The similarly named lalonde file docu-
mented by MatchIt contains 614 observations: 185 treated observations from NSW and 429
PSID comparison observations. It is not the all-randomized experimental comparison. This is
a valuable adverse example for an agent asked to “load LaLonde and estimate the RCT effect”:
the response must disambiguate the dataset first. Decision: retain as a selection-bias and
dataset-identity challenge, not the randomized baseline (MatchIt contributors, 2026).
   16. ACIC 2016. The inspected author documentation specifies 4,802 empirical covariate
rows and 58 covariates from the Collaborative Perinatal Project. Its generator creates a
treatment mechanism, response surfaces and observations, and can return both potential
outcomes, conditional means and propensities. The package describes 77 settings and 100
indexed seeds in its example; an evaluation must state the chosen grid rather than quietly
select easy settings. The code package states GPL terms, but empirical input-data rights need
their own review. Decision: preferred standardized semi-synthetic estimation benchmark.
Freeze a modest scenario grid spanning overlap, nonlinearity and heterogeneity, then compare
a simple baseline and the proposed method with identical inputs. Error against generated
truth is meaningful within that generator (ACIC competition maintainers, 2026).
   17. IHDP benchmark distributed with CEVAE. The inspected documentation
explicitly says the benchmark contains generated treated and control conditional means and
factual/counterfactual outcomes. It also warns that its legacy code is unmaintained. The
name of an original intervention study must not turn a generated benchmark into observed
counterfactual truth. Decision: secondary semi-synthetic robustness option; prefer ACIC
initially because adding a legacy software stack contributes little to the first proposal. Read
data in a supported environment if this option is later used (CEVAE authors, 2026).
   18. did county teen-employment panel. The documented mpdta example has 500
counties from 2003–2007, 2,500 rows and a first treatment year associated with state minimum-
wage changes. Its treat indicator is ever-treated, not period-specific exposure. This offers
a compact staggered-adoption example and a concrete treatment-clock test. Parallel trends,
anticipation, state-level assignment and limited assignment clusters need discussion; observed
570                                                            Causal analysis for a universal bank


adoption is not randomized. Decision: use as an adjacent-domain panel adapter/reference
example, with comparisons across appropriate estimands. A future bank panel needs its own
design (did contributors, 2026).
   19. Criteo uplift data. The custodian describes advertising incrementality tests in
which a random subset is withheld from targeting. Its page specifies 25 million users, 11
features, a treatment indicator and visit/conversion labels. Feature projection and population
adjustments mean the original incrementality level cannot be recovered. The displayed license
is CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. Decision: useful randomized large-data candidate, but deferred for
this commercial product proposal until permitted use is established. A free download is not
sufficient. A small generated randomized campaign with known propensities can exercise the
same interface without this dependency (Criteo AI Lab, 2026).


59.5      Discovery, observation construction and language models
20. CausalBench perturbational gene-expression data. The documented benchmark
offers observational, partially interventional and fully interventional regimes on large biological
datasets. It is attractive because intervention labels allow evaluations that pure observational
graph recovery cannot supply. Nevertheless, perturbations are biological operations, measured
expression is an imperfect system representation, and validation resources do not amount to a
complete known causal graph. Different auxiliary resources carry different licenses, including a
noncommercial component. Decision: optional external-domain discovery challenge after a
small declared synthetic graph suite. Use held-out intervention prediction or explicitly scoped
reference metrics; do not call a learned biological network banking graph truth (CausalBench
authors, 2026).
   21. FEBRL linkage datasets. The inspected loader describes synthetic identity records
and returns known links reconstructed from generator identities. FEBRL1 has 500 originals
and 500 duplicates; FEBRL4 has two tables of 5,000 records each with known correspondences.
These can test duplicate handling, blocking recall, false matches and propagation of uncertain
identity. Generator IDs that encode correspondence must be hidden from matching features.
A financial outcome or transaction history added to these names is an additional synthetic
construction. Decision: preferred optional linkage benchmark once data-specific terms are
checked; existing project-generated identities remain sufficient for an immediate prototype.
Neither establishes the error rate of a real bank audit (Python Record Linkage Toolkit
contributors, 2026).
  22. PaySim. The author description explains that mobile-money transactions are generated
by a simulator, initially from a service schema and later using aggregate transaction information.
Realistic financial-looking records are still synthetic. This source is useful for workload shape
and event-stream concepts, but its fraud labels do not identify the effect of a bank intervention.
Code and linked dataset terms need separate checks. Decision: optional engineering fixture,
deprioritized because the existing project simulator already provides transparent decision and
observation mechanisms (PaySim authors, 2026).
   23. CLadder. The benchmark documentation describes 10,112 balanced generated
causal questions, underlying model metadata and variants with ordinary, counterintuitive and
nonsense variable names. Those variants help distinguish causal reasoning from memorized
domain associations. Public model metadata can support a logical reference; it cannot be
allowed into the evaluation prompt when it contains the answer. Decision: shortlist for offline
task design and later bounded live evaluation after dataset terms and contamination controls
are fixed. Public benchmark performance is a diagnostic, not evidence that the model owns
the business assumptions (CLadder authors, 2026).
59.5. Discovery, observation construction and language models                           571


   24. Corr2Cause. The documented generator builds graphs, conditional-independence
statements and verbalized causal-relation questions; a three-class supplement distinguishes
entailed, underdetermined and contradicted claims within an equivalence class. Variable
renaming and paraphrases offer useful robustness contrasts. Decision: pair selected tasks
with CLadder and new controlled banking briefs. Require the system to retain equivalent
diagrams and request missing identifying information instead of forcing a direction. Source
review is complete for these descriptions; no live-model scores were produced (Corr2Cause
authors, 2026).
  The surveyed datasets cover concrete components of discovery, but none establishes a
universal “business text to true causal graph” route. A useful graph prototype should return
candidate structures, provenance for asserted edges, explicit temporal restrictions and the
consequences of ambiguity for the requested intervention. On generated examples, structural
metrics can be scored against the generator. On empirical observations, equivalence and
uncertain measurement must survive into the effect analysis.

A bounded public-data prototype
portfolio

60.1     Selection rather than accumulation
Acquiring every dataset would create cost without proportionate evidence. The recommended
portfolio has six study families, each tied to a product decision. Documentation, assumptions,
a runnable baseline and an explicit failure result are more valuable than an impressive count
of downloaded files. A source that is registration-gated or unsuitable for one estimand must
not block another family.

                                             572
60.2. P1: demonstrate that the problem is correctly formulated                               573


results must be labeled synthetic where appropriate. Using public covariates in a simulator
improves distributional realism but does not validate its action or response law. A proposal
can include a live-model evaluation design before paying for it; a claimed live-model capability
requires an actual identified backend and held-out execution.


60.2     P1: demonstrate that the problem is correctly formulated
The first study asks whether the prototype preserves the scientific question as data move
through it. For 401(k), write two briefs: the effect of eligibility on assets and the effect of
participation. The reference specification distinguishes their assumptions and estimands. For
Bank Marketing, ask for pre-contact subscription prediction and the incremental effect of
making a call. The former can be a prediction exercise with an explicit information cutoff.
The latter requires the system to identify absent assignment/control information and propose
a design.
   The baseline is a reviewed template plus deterministic schema/timing checks. The proposed
assistant must output the population, unit, time zero, feasible action, outcome horizon,
available covariates, candidate diagrams, adjustment or instrument assumptions, and missing
evidence. Score each field separately and record whether uncertainty is retained. Do not score
an invented graph as correct merely because it looks economically plausible. A deliberately
misleading brief that proposes controlling for call duration should trigger a clock objection.
   The completed archive profile provides an input fixture, not final task performance. Freeze
the briefs and reference alternatives before evaluating a model or agent. Public benchmark
text may be familiar to a model; use disjoint graph templates and new names/numerical
mechanisms for the held-out portion. Record prompted assistance and reviewer intervention
in the denominator of workflow cost.


60.3     P2: make dependent financial computation reviewable
Retain the existing macroeconomic result as an inherited baseline. For an FDIC extension,
first select a release window whose final included publication predates the cutoff, a bounded set
of institutions and a documented event definition. Acquire field dictionaries, structure changes
and release information before fitting. Separate branch-level deposits from consolidated bank
financials. Entity continuity, mergers and geography should be reproducible transformations
rather than unrecorded analyst choices.
   The first result should reproduce descriptive totals and a declared conditional panel asso-
ciation. A causal event study is an additional design: define event time, comparison units,
anticipation, interference, common shocks and the identifying assumption. A conventional
two-way fixed-effect coefficient and a group-time effect can target different weighted objects
under staggered adoption; matching only the formula name is insufficient. Include a falsification
or negative-control design where justified, but do not interpret a nonsignificant pretrend as
proof of parallel trends.
   Evaluate numerical parity, retained sample/unit counts, missingness, memory, elapsed time
and recovery from an interrupted local job. These metrics support engineering feasibility.
Bank service levels and network recovery remain future target-platform questions. The local
workload must preserve the complete calculation, including reconstruction and uncertainty,
rather than reporting only a fast inner reducer.
574                                                           Causal analysis for a universal bank


60.4     P3: check effect estimators against the right reference
Begin with a generated randomized experiment that has a declared assignment probability
and known response law. Compare a difference in means, a prespecified regression adjustment
and the proposed score estimator. Under unequal assignment, a naive mean contrast can
remain interpretable under the actual design, while precision comparisons must account for the
allocation. In observational semi-synthetic cases, require the declared adjustment information
and vary overlap, response nonlinearity and heterogeneity.
  For ACIC, preserve real covariates and simulated quantities as separate objects. Report
ATE error, heterogeneity error when conditional truth is supplied, interval availability, width,
repeated-sampling coverage, overlap and runtime. Never tune on evaluation potential outcomes.
Use the same scenarios, training information and splits for each method, and retain failures as
outcomes. The NSW extension should report uncertainty for the experimental estimate and
preserve the exact extract identity; its estimate is not a noiseless label for another method.
  Select scenarios and replication counts prospectively from the precision needed to distinguish
meaningful failure. For example, at nominal coverage 0.95, 400 independent repetitions give a
Monte Carlo standard error near 0.011; that is a planning calculation, not proof that observed
94% coverage is acceptable. A simultaneous acceptance rule across the selected scenarios must
be specified before final runs. Current open calibration findings are not erased by switching to
a public benchmark with unknown truth.


60.5     P4: distinguish realism from sequential identification
A servicing prototype should represent a fixed policy and a policy learned on independent
training histories. At each decision time, disclose the available state, chosen action, action
propensity, subsequent outcome and censoring. Include an adverse case with a private hardship
variable that affects both actions and repayment, and a case with weak support for the proposed
policy. A useful result may be a refusal, a broad identified set or a warning that an off-policy
value cannot be estimated reliably.
   Real mortgage histories, if lawfully acquired, improve the realism of delinquency and
termination clocks. They should initially support descriptive transitions and competing-event
handling. If actions are then generated conditional on recorded histories, label the resulting
policy comparison semi-synthetic; if future outcomes are also generated, disclose that response
law. Policy value under that law is a simulation result. The proposed bank experiment is
justified only when an unresolved assumption about genuine actions or response materially
changes the policy recommendation.


60.6     P5: carry ambiguity through graph and identity opera-
         tions
For discovery, use small graphs where observational equivalence classes can be enumerated. The
baseline returns the entire compatible class; a discovery method or language model must not
receive credit for an unjustified single orientation. Evaluate orientation precision, valid-class
retention and the resulting intervention-effect set, including empty, disconnected or unbounded
answers when they are mathematically appropriate. Add interventional information in a
separate condition to test whether it resolves the intended ambiguity.
  For observation construction, start from known entity histories and then corrupt identifiers,
60.7. P6: evaluate the assistant as part of a workflow                                       575


timestamps or links. Keep the hidden generator mapping outside the analysis interface.
Compare exact-oracle, hard-match and uncertainty-aware routes. Report missed candidate
pairs, false matches and the change in a downstream financial target. High pairwise matching
accuracy does not guarantee a small monetary bias when the rare high-value records are the
ones mismatched. FEBRL can add a public fixture; it cannot supply the error distribution of
the future bank’s audit process.


60.7      P6: evaluate the assistant as part of a workflow
Use public data and controlled problems for the sequence from business brief to diagram,
identification query, tool execution and explanation. The baseline should be a competent low-
cost workflow: a reviewed form, a deterministic graph/identification solver where applicable,
and the selected statistical package. The proposed agent should be evaluated for improvements
over that workflow, including errors it introduces and time spent correcting them.
   Measure invalid assumptions, clock violations, unsupported orientations, identification
mistakes, tool/schema failures, hallucinated results, uncertainty fidelity, successful abstention
and end-to-end completion. Record calls, tokens, elapsed time and human review effort only
when they are actually measured. Live backend identity, version, budget and custody are
necessary for a live performance claim; they are not prerequisites for the literature survey,
offline fixtures, architecture proposal or protocol. If a live evaluation is unaffordable, narrow
the claim and retain a costed protocol rather than fabricating results.


60.8      Common study controls
Each new final study needs a prospectively frozen question, input hashes, methods, splits,
scenarios, estimands, assignment/observation assumptions, numerical tolerances, resource limit
and stopping rule. Exploratory profiles such as the UCI row inspection remain exploratory
and may inform that registration. Existing fitted results cannot be relabeled fresh evaluation
data. A source-access failure blocks only the affected dataset branch.
  An initial resource envelope should be modest: local public files, one selected data source
per role, no paid API by default, bounded CPU jobs and recorded memory/time. Exact limits
should be set after an input-profile pilot, before final outcomes are examined. The plan does
not attach invented calendar dates or currency costs to unmeasured work. A baseline that
performs as well as the proposed component is evidence to reuse the baseline, simplify the
design or reject that component.
Chapter 61

When a bank experiment becomes
worth its cost

61.1     Proposal acceptance and later qualification
Proposal acceptance means the scholarly argument is coherent, source-grounded and sufficiently
complete; the software and agent landscape has been compared seriously; the integration
design is concrete; the public/synthetic demonstrations are reproducible within their claims;
and the next investment decision follows from an explicit comparison and cost model. Open
research can be retained with a scoped conjecture, failure result and next test. A general
theorem is not promised where only a restricted construction is known.
   The three major manuscript repairs remain obligations: systematic software coverage and
reuse/commercial comparisons; the developed treatment of language models and agents; and
CLI, MCP, library and workspace integration. The public-data survey supplies their evaluation
substrate. It does not finish those chapters or automatically close any scientific gap. The
software and language-model page/depth commitments also remain; pages in this public-data
section are not counted twice toward them.
   Later bank qualification asks a different question: do the assumptions, precision, workflows
and economics hold for a specific institution? That stage may need genuine offer histories,
logging information, independent labels, owner-reviewed semantics, production constraints
and prospective outcomes. The relevant input should be requested only for the capability and
target population under test. An internal bank pilot is not required to demonstrate that the
proposal has a reproducible public baseline and a sensible experiment design.


61.2     A value-of-information decision
Let d ∈ {stop, build, pilot} denote an investment choice, θ unresolved technical and economic
conditions, and U (d, θ) its net value. Let E denote current public/prototype evidence and Z
the possible result of a proposed experiment. A planning expression for the expected value of
sample information is
                                                    
                EVSI = EZ|E max E{U (d, θ) | E, Z} − max E{U (d, θ) | E}.
                                  d                        d

   An experiment merits consideration when its expected decision improvement exceeds its
full incremental cost, including data preparation, customer burden where relevant, security

                                             576
61.3. Conditions for moving to expensive evidence                                             577


review, labeling, analyst time and opportunity cost. This is a project decision framework, not
an empirically estimated ROI. Where a probability model for θ is unjustified, use a scenario
table and sensitivity bounds instead of a precise-looking EVSI number.
   A simple illustrative calculation shows the sequencing. Suppose, purely for planning, a
small bank study costing 20,000 could avert an unsuitable 200,000 build in 20% of scenarios,
with no other benefits or costs. Its gross avoided-spend value would be 40,000 and its net
would be 20,000 under those assumptions. If the study changes the build decision in only 2%
of scenarios, the same gross value is 4,000 and it is not justified on that ground. These are
stipulated arithmetic examples, not quotations, bank probabilities or forecasts.
   The decision should identify the uncertainty that matters. If a public benchmark shows
repeated action-clock mistakes, improve the formulation layer before requesting confidential
data. If a correct estimator is too slow on modest data, fix or replace it before commissioning
a platform pilot. If all plausible effects lead to the same action, a costly precision improvement
may have little value. If policy value reverses when a missing hardship variable is plausible,
a carefully scoped bank measurement study can have high value even when the public-data
implementation is technically sound.


61.3     Conditions for moving to expensive evidence
An actionable next-experiment recommendation specifies the proposed intervention, target
population, candidate baseline, decision-loss threshold and the smallest information addition
that could alter the decision. It also states an explicit stop or redesign outcome. A bank
experiment should not be recommended merely to fill a missing-evidence cell.
   For funding, the missing addition may be time-stamped offers and an assignment mechanism,
not more aggregate deposits. For servicing, it may be feasible-action and hardship information
at each decision time. For discovery, it may be one feasible intervention that distinguishes
competing graphs. For observation construction, it may be a representative independently
resolved sample of uncertain identities with known inclusion probabilities. Public data help
design each measurement and estimate its computational burden, while the bank supplies the
later population-specific truth.
  Authentic institutional approval, independent acceptance, actual workflow prices and pro-
duction service levels remain future qualification requirements. A proposal can be complete
without them. It cannot honestly claim those outcomes without obtaining them.


61.4     Remaining survey and prototype gaps
The survey has established a usable portfolio and a concrete public-data acquisition/profile,
not six executed new studies. Current-source web snapshots still need exact data-file vintages
for future analyses. Several benchmark datasets need data-specific rights checks. Mortgage
histories require registration and use review; the HMDA publication endpoint was inaccessible
in this run. The Criteo license is a material constraint for a commercial proposal. These affect
individual options; project-generated alternatives and the already local public data keep the
prototype work moving.
   No inspected public financial source supplies the complete logged bank servicing action
process or independent real-bank linkage truth. That finding is limited to the surveyed sources.
It calls for transparent semi-synthetic experiments now and a justified targeted measurement
later, rather than a claim of impossibility. Public reasoning benchmarks also cannot establish a
578                                                           Causal analysis for a universal bank


live agent’s quality without an actual controlled run, nor resolve the business owner’s normative
choice of outcome and feasible intervention.
   Finally, public data do not repair the open mathematical arguments for persistent depen-
dence, hidden states, graph-equivalence effect sets or arbitrary learning procedures. Those
questions remain scoped research obligations. The proposal can present negative findings and
restricted supported regimes, compare alternatives and describe what evidence would change
the recommendation. That is a strong proposal standard without pretending that an accepted
bank product already exists.
